title: Steelers' Yahya Black says he weighs 370 in mic'd up talk with 340-pound Tristan Wirfs
summary: Buccaneers offensive tackle Tristan Wirfs doesn't often come across people bigger than him, but he did on Sunday, when he played against Steelers defensive tackle Yahya Black.
full_text: Buccaneers offensive tackle Tristan Wirfs doesn't often come across people bigger than him, but he did on Sunday, when he played against Steelers defensive tackle Yahya Black. Wirfs was mic’d up for NFL Films , which revealed an on-field conversation with Black about their respective sizes. The discussion went like this: Black: "What they got you weighing at?" Wirfs: "340. What about you?" Black: "370" Wirfs: "I knew it. You look huge." Black: "Thank you. I try." Wirfs: "No, I mean, you look great. You look like an absolute unit." Wirfs and Black both played at Iowa, though not together. Wirfs' third and final year at Iowa was 2019, when he was a first-team All-American and won the Big Ten's lineman of the year award. Black's first year at Iowa was 2020, and Wirfs told teammates in the Buccaneers' huddle on Sunday that he visited Iowa after his rookie season in the NFL and met a younger and much smaller Black. "When I went back to train after my rookie year, he was a freshman. He was not that big," Wirfs said in the Bucs' huddle. "He's, like, doubled in size." Later, Wirfs complimented Black on his apparel when he attended a recent Iowa game as a spectator, and wondered where men their size can get clothes that fit. Wirfs: "Where did you get your overalls for the Iowa game?" Black: "Bro, I just walked into a shop downtown." Wirfs: "No way!" Black: "4X, baby." Both Wirfs and Black have gained weight while in the league. Wirfs weighed in at 320 pounds at the 2020 Scouting Combine. Black weighed 336 at the 2025 Scouting Combine.
author: Michael David Smith

title: NFL business partners aren't pulling punches as to the handling of Jalen Hurts
summary: The Eagles' handling of quarterback Jalen Hurts and his blood clot in Week 5 has sparked plenty of criticism of both the team and the league, which has been in lockstep with the team.
full_text: The Eagles' handling of quarterback Jalen Hurts and his blood clot in Week 5 has sparked plenty of criticism of both the team and the league, which has been in lockstep with the team. And some of that criticism has come from the NFL's business partners. The NFL owns 10 percent of ESPN. That hasn't stopped some at ESPN from offering sharp criticism of the league and the Eagles for the situation. On Wednesday's First Take , for instance, Chris "Mad Dog" Russo went off on the situation. (Stephen A. Smith and others had sharp criticism of the situation on Tuesday's show, too.) "One thing if I may about this whole thing with Hurts, the Eagles did a horrendous job , OK?" Russo said. "And I'm gonna believe the NFL now? That doesn't have grass fields, that didn't do anything with CTE until they were forced to. That wants to play an eighteenth game for the safety of the players, when they want to play another game. "So the NFL now is saying, 'Well, they didn't do anything wrong. . . . The Eagles were great with this.' I don't trust them. Furthermore, the Eagles throwing Sirianni out there to meet the media. That is ridiculous. I mean, he doesn't know. I mean, he's not the — put a trainer out there. Put a team doctor. You made the poor guy answer questions with a hungry media in Philadelphia. That was a disgrace. "And the NFL can't sit there and [say] they care about safety. They care about safety, why are we going for an eighteenth game? They add it to a seventeenth game. Here's the guy that had a blood clot, that got back to the hotel at 3:00 a.m., played the football game, they came back to — flew across the country, came back and said, 'Well, he's gonna miss this week against Carolina.' Then they came back and said, 'He's gonna miss four games.' And then they came back and said, 'He's gone for the year.' That's ridiculous. . . . Now, come on. Literally, come on." The NFL also has a content partnership with The Athletic , posting items from the New York Times subsidiary at NFL.com. That didn't stop Mike Silver of The Athletic (a former employee of the league who has talked openly about certain subjects being off limits when he worked for NFL Network and NFL.com) from going all-in with his criticism of the Eagles and the league . "Imagine medically evaluating an employee on an off-site work assignment, subjecting him to well-documented risk factors that could exacerbate the condition — and then having his symptoms worsen to the point where they are potentially life-threatening," Silver wrote in a column posted on Wednesday. "Then imagine proclaiming to the world that you are in no way culpable, and that any suggestion that you could possibly have handled the situation differently is an affront to logic and decency. Throw in a touch of indignant condescension, and voila: You are the National Football League." Silver specifically targeted Tuesday's effort by NFL chief medical officer Allen Sills to downplay the situation. "Now the NFL, whose medical officials were in the loop when Hurts’ initial blood clot was discovered the night before the game, is in full cover-your-ass mode," Silver wrote. "That’s a curious strategy, given the dots that qualified physicians might connect, made worse by the assertion that none of us — even experts in the field — are qualified to question any of it." The secrecy, disguised as "patient privacy concerns" (despite multiple statements that spell out Hurts's diagnosis, treatment, and prognosis in full detail), has only added to the interest in getting answers. On Tuesday, Sills insisted that the handling of Hurts was " very conservative, very patient-focused and appropriately guarded in every step ." Devin McCourty, a 13-year NFL veteran, appearing on Wednesday's PFT Live (NBC is a broadcast partner but not a business or content partner with the league), raised an excellent question. Wouldn't a "very conservative, very patient-focused and appropriately guarded" approach to a player who spent most of the prior night in a hospital for diagnosis and evaluation of a blood clot in his leg have resulted in a decision that he should not play a full-contact pro football game hours later? Seventeen years ago next week, the NFL was forced by Congress to take brain injuries seriously, 15 years after the formation of the decidedly unserious "Mild Traumatic Brain Injury Committee," which delayed the concussion reckoning for as long as it could. The avoidance of the worst-case scenario as to Hurts has prompted the league to attempt to delay a different sort of reckoning regarding the treatment of serious health conditions not involving the brain. Fortunately, several of the media companies that are in direct business with the league are resisting the effort to avoid answering fair and tough questions about a lingering culture that could have gotten Jalen Hurts killed.
author: Mike Florio

title: Roger Goodell on Jed York suspension: "We saw a violation and we dealt with it"
summary: 49ers owner Jed York attended the league meeting this week upon the conclusion of his six-game suspension.
full_text: 49ers owner Jed York attended the league meeting this week upon the conclusion of his six-game suspension. NFL Commissioner Roger Goodell defended that suspension as an appropriate consequence of York violating the same personal conduct policy that applies to players and everyone else in the league. York pleaded no contest to two misdemeanors after he was arrested in a prostitution sting in East Palestine, Ohio. Goodell said at the league meeting that the personal conduct policy "applies to owners, commissioners, everybody else, players." That's true, but the $500,000 fine York paid is a pittance compared to what players can lose if they receive a comparable suspension. A player who is suspended six games loses one-third of his salary for that season; $500,000 is nothing remotely close to one-third of what York or any other owner makes in a season. "We went through a full process, obviously, to understand the facts, understand the issues. Looked at it under the context of our personal conduct policy," Goodell said. Goodell said the league stands by its personal conduct policy and that the discipline York faced was appropriate for the violation he committed. "It's something we feel strongly about," Goodell said. "We think we need to represent ourselves and our organizations properly. We saw a violation and we dealt with it from a discipline standpoint. That concluded now, so he'll be back representing the 49ers."
author: Michael David Smith

title: Dolphins are raising all season ticket prices for 2027
summary: For the 0-5 Dolphins, who have yet to take the lead in any game this season, the phrase "better luck next year" already applies.
full_text: For the 0-5 Dolphins, who have yet to take the lead in any game this season, the phrase "better luck next year" already applies. So does the phrase "better get ready to pay more money next year." Via Barry Jackson of the Miami Herald , the Dolphins will be raising season ticket prices " across the board in 2027 ." The team attributes the increase to hosting nine regular-season games next season. In 2026, the team increased prices for none of the season tickets — and dropped the prices for some of them. Per Jackson, most tickets will increase by three percent. Some of them (specifically, in the shade on the home sideline) will be bumped a "bit more." In two home games played so far this year, the Dolphins have averaged 58,719 attendees. That ranks 31st in the league, ahead of only the Jaguars — whose ongoing renovations have reduced capacity to 42,000 for 2026. Last year, the Dolphins averaged 65,687 in eight home games, with the ninth played in Spain.
author: Mike Florio

title: Matthew Stafford hopes fans see injuries for more than just the impact on fantasy teams
summary: "Everybody sees these and they're on their fantasy team or whatever," Stafford said. "We're like, 'That guy's worked his ass off for eight months to get this opportunity.'"
full_text: Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford wants fans to understand what player injuries really mean. Stafford said he personally felt the impact from learning Rams receiver Davante Adams will miss most of the rest of the season, and it means a lot more than just his impact on fantasy football teams. "Like Davante, disappointed for those guys," Stafford said. "Everybody sees these and they're on their fantasy team or whatever, and they're like, 'I gotta trade a guy in and out now.' And we're like, 'That guy's worked his ass off for eight months to get this opportunity and it's unfortunate he doesn't get to do what he loves to do.' So I feel more for our guys than I do for anybody else, and I know the work that they put into it, to be out here doing what they love. So that hurts me for them." Stafford said one of the things motivating him to play hard in the weeks ahead is wanting the Rams to still be in playoff contention when Adams, Myles Garrett and other injured teammates return. "I feel even more a responsibility to be as good as I can to be help us continue to win," Stafford said. "Some of those guys, they're gonna have opportunities to hopefully come back and play for us, make sure that when they come back and play for us it's meaningful." Stafford said he hopes people realize the true impact of injuries is on players like Adam, who desperately want to be able to play and currently can't. "Disappointed for him," Stafford said. "I know how hard he works to be out there for us, and when he's not able to do that it tears him up."
author: Michael David Smith

title: JC Latham on incident with Jordan Elliott: It was just an unfortunate situation
summary: The Titans released defensive lineman Jordan Elliott on Tuesday after an incident at the team facility.
full_text: '' The Titans released defensive lineman Jordan Elliott on Tuesday after an incident at the team facility. An argument with teammate JC Latham last Thursday prompted Elliott to etrieve a gun from his car. Latham discussed the incident Wednesday. “It was just an unfortunate situation ," Latham said, via Terry McCormick of titaninsider.com. "It was heat of the moment, and shit happens. I don’t really have too much to say about it. . . . There ain’t never been no bad blood between us two. We were here on the summer getting treatment. Before that, we hung out whenever we were in the same city together. We actually had never had an argument leading up to it. "So I actually think mental health is extremely important, and that’s just one of those situations where you just pray for a guy like that.” Elliott was dealing with personal issues, per McCormick, when he stormed out of the locker room to the players' garage. Teammate John Franklin-Myers followed Elliott and de-escalated the situation, getting Elliott to put the gun away, McCormick reports. Latham was grateful to Franklin-Myers. "I told him I appreciate it," Latham said. "I was still on the field, apparently, . . . so I just told him how much I appreciate him for that."
author: Charean Williams

title: In their SoFi Stadium incident, Troy Aikman's position to Joe Buck was: "You f—ked me over!"
summary: New report adds details to the tension in the MNF booth.
full_text: The 25-year partnership between Joe Buck and Troy Aikman is moving toward a conclusion, and more details have emerged regarding last week's tipping point at SoFi Stadium. Dylan Byers of Puck adds some color to the prior report of tension between the Monday Night Football broadcaster team. “There had been weeks of Troy becoming increasingly cold, difficult, short, making comments,” a source with direct knowledge of the situation told Byers. “Joe finally snapped,” the source told Byers, in reference to the Week 5 incident at the Bills-Rams game. “He basically said, 'Dude, are we really going to do this?' And Troy’s position was: You fucked me over!” Said another unnamed source to Byers, “They exchanged some very direct and honest feelings." Byers, who says he spoke to more than a dozen sources, writes that Aikman "felt like a lot of people had fucked him over." It came down to Buck cutting a deal on his extension, with the understanding that he may have a new partner in 2027. But Aikman also had been trying to do his own deal; per Byers, one of Aikman's agents pegged his value at $30 million per year — a sizable jump over his current rate of $18 million. Aikman "saw it as the ultimate act of betrayal,” an unnamed source told Byers. “They cut this deal in May and put it in a drawer. ESPN didn’t tell him, Joe didn’t tell him.” Ultimately, it's everyone for themselves. Aikman asked for too much. Buck made a more realistic demand. If it had been the other way around, Aikman would have his deal and Buck would be waiting for an offer that, at this point, may never come. Byers reports that, on the most recent Monday night in Santa Clara, Buck apologized to Aikman and the entire production team for losing his cool. Buck's message was, per Byers, "We’re all adults, we’ve all got jobs to do, let’s move forward, let’s have a great year.” Aikman reportedly added nothing after Buck said what he had to say. The whole thing is odd, to say the least, if not unprecedented. At this point, it seems like Aikman will be leaving, likely for CBS or Prime Video. And Buck, armed with his new contract, will be sticking around. Through it all, they'll be working together for the rest of a season that culminates in ESPN's first Super Bowl. At a time when ESPN is trying its best to relentlessly hype the February 14 event, the Aikman-Buck situation becomes a potential distraction. Or maybe it adds a little extra sizzle, given the possibility that their tenuous relationship could lead to an on-air incident at some point between now and the final game of the 2026 season.
author: Mike Florio

title: UFL has a stadium issue in St. Louis for 2027
summary: St.
full_text: St. Louis has been one of the UFL's success stories, with fans packing the stadium where the Rams previously played. But there's a problem for 2027, as explained by UFL co-owner Mike Repole in a lengthy post on Twitter. As Repole puts it, the available dates at their home stadium mean that the BattleHawks "would play FOUR straight home games, followed by FIVE consecutive road games, and potentially return home for Week 10." "FOUR HOME GAMES. FIVE ROAD GAMES. Sorry, but that just DOESN’T WORK FOR US !!!!" Repole said. Repole added that it doesn't mean the UFL is leaving St. Louis. Really, why would they go? They have a strong following there. He didn't identify the scheduling conflicts, and it's odd that the local authorities would load up the weekends in which it knew, or should have known, that the UFL would be playing. Regardless, Repole has opted to take the issue public. Whether that changes things remains to be seen.
author: Mike Florio

title: Commanders-49ers attracts 17.9 million viewers for Monday Night Football
summary: Only 315,000 watched the McAfee alt cast.
full_text: Monday night's game between the Commanders and 49ers started as a blowout. The road team eventually turned a 23-3 deficit into a 23-17 nail biter. The end result, for ratings purposes, resulted in 17.9 million viewers to the various Disney-controlled networks: ABC, ESPN, ESPN2, NFL Network, and ESPN Deportes. The release from ESPN includes no information regarding the audience to the debut of the Pat McAfee alt cast or the Next Gen Stats broadcast on NFL Network. (Last week, ESPN disclosed that 1.1 million watched the ESPN2 ManningCast and the NFL Network Next Gen Stats presentation, without specifying the audience for either network.) Andrew Marchand of The Athletic reports that the McAfee alt cast attracted a mere 351,000 viewers , which equates to 1.96 percent of the total audience. That's far less than the ManningCast attracts, even as the Peyton and Eli show continues to slump. Which brings us back to the overriding question about all alt casts: Why? With the exception of the broadcasts aimed at getting kids to watch by turning the game into a collection of cartoon or video-game characters, there's no reason to siphon viewers from the primary broadcast. The people who watch the alt casts meant for adults will watch the primary broadcast, in the absence of the alt cast. It's ultimately a pointless exercise that only wastes time and money.
author: Mike Florio

title: After two years rehabbing, Tank Dell overwhelmed, anxious and excited to play again
summary: Texans wide receiver Tank Dell has not played a game since Dec. 21, 2024, when he tore multiple ligaments and dislocated his kneecap in a game against the Chiefs.
full_text: Texans wide receiver Tank Dell has not played a game since Dec. 21, 2024, when he tore multiple ligaments and dislocated his kneecap in a game against the Chiefs. The gruesome knee injury threatened his career. " I’m blessed ," Dell said, via DJ Bien-Aime of ESPN. "I want to thank God for getting me back in this position. But I don't think I'm overwhelmed. I'm anxious, of course, but I don't think I'm overwhelmed. I'm anxious to get back out there and play some football." The Texans opened Dell's practice window on Oct. 5, and he returns to game action on Sunday against the Giants. "I know it's a lot of questions, like, 'How he gonna look when he gets tackled?'" Dell said. "I don't care about none of that. I'm ready to get tackled. I'm gonna be joyful. Y'all gonna see the passion I have after I had that first catch." Dell, a third-round pick in 2023, will likely be on a snap count Sunday. That doesn't matter to him or to the Texans. "It's just getting Tank back out there after missing two years of football," Texans coach DeMeco Ryans said. "That's the main thing. Him just going out playing ball. I don't care how many reps he gets. But I'll have my Tank Dell jersey on." Dell has 98 receptions for 1,376 yards and 10 touchdowns in his career.
author: Charean Williams

title: NFL fines Mike Vrabel, Aaron Glenn, Nick Sirianni $250,000 each for conduct toward officials
summary: Fines are currently being held in abeyance, and could be repealed.
full_text: The NFL isn't messing around when it comes to behavior toward game officials. With an asterisk. Albert Breer of SI.com reports that the NFL has fined Patriots coach Mike Vrabel, Jets coach Aaron Glenn, and Eagles coach Nick Sirianni $250,000 each for conduct toward game officials. The discipline may be more performative than substantive. Breer explains that "the fines are in abeyance, meaning they’d be on hold, and could be repealed with good behavior." It's not entirely clear where things stand, and what it would take to avoid the fines. Also, the amounts are borderline cartoonish. In 2012, former Patriots coach Bill Belichick was fined only $50,000 for confronting and grabbing the arm of a replacement official. Recently, 49ers owner Jed York was fined a mere $500,000 to go along with a six-game suspension after a prostitution-related arrest. These fines seem over the top, especially since the specific behavior that prompted the fines has not been identified. In Week 4, Vrabel was flagged for his comments to an official after a disputed call. “I told him it was a terrible — I’m not going to say effing — call,” Vrabel said after the game. “I’ve said that 87 times since I’ve been a head coach. It was nothing derogatory. You’d have to ask him. I think he was a little sensitive .” The league was more than a little sensitive. But it's not as if the $250,000 will be collected. All in all, it feels like an olive branch to the NFL Referees Association, after a pair of suspensions were imposed on officials for interactions with players in Week 5.
author: Mike Florio

title: NFL could embrace replay review transparency by the end of the current season
summary: Transparency apparently is coming, thanks to the UFL, the ACC, and the Big Ten.
full_text: ' In July, Broncos coach Sean Payton predicted that the NFL will adopt UFL-style officiating transparency within the next two to three years. It could be coming sooner than that. A Wednesday item from Albert Breer of SI.com includes this nugget: "[P]lanning is underway for more transparency. I’m told the NFL has watched closely at how the ACC and, after the Michigan–Western Michigan debacle, the Big Ten have started televising their replay review process. The idea of doing something similar to show the public replay reviews is being discussed, and work is being done to implement something similar to what we’ve seen in college football very soon, potentially in the coming weeks, and certainly (some in the league office hope) before the end of the regular season ." It would be stunning if it happens during the current season. The NFL rarely makes significant change while a season is unfolding. Regardless, it's better sooner than later, and later than never. The NFL needs to follow the lead of the UFL, the ACC, and the Big Ten. It's the NFL that's supposed to be the leader when it comes to football innovation. It's already behind the times, and the lack of transparency fuels conspiracy theories. If the league does it, the question becomes whether the league can do it properly. The only thing worse than no transparency would be transparency into a flawed process. So, yes, be careful what you wish for. Seeing the sausage get made could potentially cause you to swear off eating it.
author: Mike Florio

title: Cardinals RB Jeremiyah Love remains out of practice
summary: Cardinals running back Jeremiyah Love is improving, Mike LaFleur said.
full_text: Cardinals running back Jeremiyah Love is improving, Mike LaFleur said. Love, though, did not practice Wednesday. Love has not practiced since Oct. 9 due to a lingering ankle injury. He injured the ankle in Week 4, played 36 of 73 snaps in Week 5 and missed the Week 6 win over the Rams on Sunday. The Cardinals also practiced without safety Budda Baker (groin/illness), defensive lineman Walter Nolen III (ankle), offensive lineman Isaac Seumalo (rest), outside linebacker Josh Sweat (rest), cornerback Garrett Williams (knee), offensive lineman Jedrick Wills Jr. (illness) and safety Andrew Wingard (knee). Rookie quarterback Carson Beck (back), cornerback Max Melton (knee) and safety Wydett Williams Jr. (concussion) were limited.
author: Charean Williams

title: Josh Jacobs: I'm just trying to play ball, learn from this mistake and move forward
summary: The Packers running back returned to the team this week after missing six games on the Commissioner's Exempt List.
full_text: ' Packers running back Josh Jacobs practiced Wednesday and has a chance to play Sunday. Jacobs missed the first six games on the Commissioner Exempt List. He opened his first media session since his May 26 arrest with a statement. "First, I'm excited to be back with the team, with the guys," Jacobs said, via video from Ryan Wood of USA Today . "I want to say thank you to the organization, really for supporting me throughout this whole process and how everything played out. With that being said, I can't get into things, like specifics of things, but obviously, man, I'm remorseful and sorry for putting this team in this situation. Sometimes when you go through life, situations occur, and four-second, three-second decisions can alter your life honestly. With that being said, man, still a human being, man. Still trying to learn. Still trying to grow from the whole process. Actually learned a lot throughout this process, legally and just personally. Yeah, man, going forward, man, just trying to get better." Jacobs remains under investigation by the NFL for Personal Conduct Policy violations stemming from his misdemeanor battery charge. On Sept. 10, he pleaded no contest to charges of battery and criminal destruction of property. He was convicted of battery and fined $1,000 and agreed to a deferred judgment agreement on a charge of damage to property. The original criminal complaint said surveillance video of the altercation shows at least part of the incident, but Jacobs and the victim filed suit to have the evidence permanently sealed. The NFL has left open the possibility of further punishment based on not being privy to exactly what's on the video. Jacobs, though, was happy to be back with his teammates this week. "I’m not trying to win nobody back, and that’s just me being all the way honest because at the end of the day, like I said, I know what happened," Jacobs said. "And if you feel some type of way, obviously I feel bad because it’s still a situation that occurred, and it should’ve never even happened. So that’s something that I still will understand if people feel some type of way about it, but like I said, all I can do is keep showing up and being who I am, being a leader for this team, being a leader in this community and that’s really all I can control.” The NFL placed Jacobs on paid leave Aug. 30, but he said he never doubted he would play again. "I wasn't overly concerned about that, because in my heart I know what happened and what didn't happen, and I just trusted the legal process," Jacobs said. "For me, I was never overly concerned of not playing again. It was just a matter of time of when." He also intimated that he disagrees with the league's decision to sit him for six games, which is the baseline punishment for domestic battery. “I think six games was a lot, honestly, but that’s not really up to me to decide," Jacobs said. "I’m grateful to be playing, so that’s not even something I’m like arguing or petitioning with. I'm just happy to be back on the team.” Jacobs said he isn't concerned about how anyone outside the locker room feels about him after the May 23 incident with a woman at his home. "I know for some people, this might be a stain on me and my character. I feel like I don't have to really speak on my character. A lot of people that know me in this locker room or that have been around me, I'll let them do that. But for me, man, I'm just trying to come back in here and play ball, learn from this mistake and move forward." But he also said the time away from the game gave him an opportunity to reevaluate his life. "Obviously you never want to be in this situation," Jacobs said. "But just me being honest, it was probably one of the best things that's ever happened to me. It gave me a chance to sit down and reevaluate what's important and what I want my life to look like and what do I want people want to know me for. When they think of me, what [are] they going to say?"
author: Charean Williams

title: Senator Lisa Blunt Rochester seeks answers from Roger Goodell regarding the Jalen Hurts situation
summary: The NFL and the Eagles hope to run out the clock as to the Jalen Hurts situation, in the hopes that the media and fans will turn their attention to the next story that grabs our collective attention.
full_text: The NFL and the Eagles hope to run out the clock as to the Jalen Hurts situation, in the hopes that the media and fans will turn their attention to the next story that grabs our collective attention. It may not be easy, because the issue has gotten the attention of Congress. Via Tim McManus of ESPN, Senator Lisa Blunt Rochester (D-Del.) has sent a letter to Commissioner Roger Goodell with specific questions about the manner in which the Eagles and the league handled Hurts's blood clots: "1. Does the NFL have a league-wide protocol for the detection, prevention, and treatment of [deep vein thrombosis] and [pulmonary embolism]? Which medical guidelines were consulted in developing this protocol? "2. What standards and processes govern a player's clearance to participate when a clot is suspected or diagnosed? Does the NFL have a league-wide Return-To-Participation Protocol? "3. What education is provided to players, athletic trainers, and coaches on how to identify the signs and symptoms of DVT and PE? "4. What specific measures has the League put in place to reduce blood clot risk, including, but not limited to, those associated with long flights? "5. Will the League conduct a thorough review of the Eagles' handling of this specific situation, including who cleared Mr. Hurts to play after staying awake overnight, and cleared subsequent air travel on a transatlantic flight back to the U.S. from London? If so, what is the timeline?" Someone also should ask whether the league will implement a protocol for blood clots and other potentially serious health conditions, similar to the procedures utilized for diagnosing concussions and clearing players to return to play. The league has used an unaffiliated neurotrauma consultant in such situations for 17 years, in order to counter the inherent biases of doctors hired by the various teams. The NFL Players Association has requested a full investigation . Under the Collective Bargaining Agreement, it has the absolute right to initiate one . Congress, through its oversight powers as to an industry that enjoys a federal broadcast antitrust exemption, also has the ability to investigate. Given the league's effort to sweep this one under the rug and move on, anyone with the power to force the NFL to answer for the Hurts situation absolutely should.
author: Mike Florio

title: Jonathon Cooper: Nobody's perfect, but no excuses; I do hold myself accountable
summary: Broncos outside linebacker Jonathon Cooper returned to practice Wednesday after spending the first six weeks on the Commissioner's Exempt List.
full_text: Broncos outside linebacker Jonathon Cooper returned to practice Wednesday after spending the first six weeks on the Commissioner's Exempt List. Cooper was arrested twice in seven days in June on domestic violence charges, prompting the paid leave of absence. Cooper would not answer specific questions about his case, which is scheduled for a March 2 trial, during his first media session since his June 4 and 11 arrests. " Nobody’s perfect , but there's no excuses,'' Cooper said, via Jeff Legwold of ESPN, "and I do hold myself accountable and things are going to sort themselves out. I promise that.'' Cooper is facing five charges after two disputes with his ex-girlfriend that began with a fight over a cell phone. The most serious charge is felony second-degree assault/strangulation. The NFL has left open the possibility of further punishment for Cooper once his legal matter is resolved. He was asked what he would say to people, particularly female fans. "Honestly . . . that's hard," Cooper said. "I feel like relationships are difficult, [but] no excuses on my end. I do apologize for anybody's feelings, truthfully, because you have to be associated with me. I'm a grown man. I'm able to take things on the chin, and I understand the concern, the awareness, how serious these matters are. The legal matters will take care of themselves." A seventh-round pick in 2021, Cooper has 31.5 sacks in 81 career games with the Broncos.
author: Charean Williams

title: Roger Goodell: NFL is "comfortable" with Steve Tisch participating in league, team activities
summary: Steve Tisch supposedly has given up his ownership interest in the Giants.
full_text: Steve Tisch supposedly has given up his ownership interest in the Giants. He's still acting as if he partially owns the team. And the NFL is fine with that. On Wednesday, Commissioner Roger Goodell was asked about Tisch's presence at the NFL's quarterly ownership meetings. "I think we're comfortable with him participating as the Giants suggest," Goodell said. Although Tisch no longer holds equity in Giants (his interest was transferred to his children's trust), he continues to serve as the team's chairman of the board. He was present in the team's draft room. He has been at games. Tisch's role came into question once the Epstein files revealed a series of emails between Tisch and Jeffrey Epstein. Subsequent reporting raised questions regarding whether Epstein was arranging dates for Tisch, and whether Tisch was possibly using his influence in the film industry to leverage an exchange of favors . Goodell, in March, cited Tisch's exit from ownership when discussing the NFL's investigation of Tisch. Goodell has repeatedly said it has no evidence of wrongdoing by Tisch. There's no evidence, however, that the NFL has attempted to gather any such evidence. It's possible the league simply hoped to run out the clock and wait for the topic to change. As it often does. Regarding Tisch, the league hasn't done anything. At this point, it likely won't. The emails alone were enough to get the league to nudge Tisch to the sideline. The league, Tisch, and the Giants seemed to believe that Tisch giving to his children now the equity they would have inevitably inherited was enough to end the issue. As long as Tisch continues to be conspicuous when it comes to league and team events, the issue remains.
author: Mike Florio

title: Cowboys-Packers generates 24.656 million on Sunday night
summary: The latest installment of the Cowboys-Packers did not yield an exciting game.
full_text: The latest installment of the Cowboys-Packers did not yield an exciting game. It nevertheless delivered in the ratings department. Via Nielsen, the game generated 24.656 million viewers on NBC. It snaps a streak of two straight Sunday night games that averaged fewer than 20 million viewers. The game was lopsided, with the Packers leading 17-0 at the half. It was never less than a two-score game from the moment the Packers' lead went to 10-0 in the second quarter. Via NBC, the audience peaked at 28.7 million in the 9:15 p.m. to 9:30 p.m. ET window. This week, the Seahawks host the 5-0 Chiefs on Sunday night in a game featuring the return of Super Bowl LX MVP Kenneth Walker III to Seattle.
author: Mike Florio

title: J.J. McCarthy on feeling more ready to start: Experience does wonders
summary: McCarthy will make his first start for the Giants this week.
full_text: J.J. McCarthy was drafted 10th overall in 2024 to be the quarterback for the Vikings, but his path to a long run as a starter in the NFL now goes through New Jersey. McCarthy will make his first start for the Giants in Sunday's game against the Texans and he could have an 11-game run to show the entire league what he's capable of doing. McCarthy said on Wednesday that he sees the move to the first team as "a chance to prove yourself" and that he feels more prepared for the job than he was when he took over as the Vikings' starter at the start of last season. McCarthy said that he gained knowledge about "the nature of NFL football" in 10 starts between injuries for the Vikings and is confident he'll be able to handle things better despite only being with the Giants for a few weeks. "I believe just experience does wonders," McCarthy said, via a transcript from the team. "Being able to be in that same situation where you might have made a mistake the last time, this time you're just going to react better and make a more well-rounded response decision in that situation. Just being around great talent and great coaches, absolutely love everyone on the offensive side of the ball and the defensive side of the ball does a tremendous job of just giving us opportunities and always making sure we stay in the game and fight to the last seconds of each game." Jaxson Dart is still the long-term plan at quarterback for the Giants, but there will be a market for McCarthy if he shows the skills that made him a top pick two years ago and he now has to make the most of his chance to display them.

title: Davante Adams will have a "cleanup" procedure on his hamstring

title: Former Cowboys DB, Broncos scout Cornell Green dies at 86
summary: The Cowboys announced that former defensive back Cornell Green died Wednesday.
full_text: The Cowboys announced that former defensive back Cornell Green died Wednesday . He was 86. Green grew up in California as an elite basketball player, earning all-state honors. He went to Utah State, where he earned All-America honors in 1961 and '62. His 1,067 rebounds still stand as the school's career record, and he is Utah State's sixth-leading scorer with 1,890 points. He had planned to join the NBA after the Chicago Zephyrs drafted him in 1962, but the Cowboys offered Green an invite to training camp. Despite only one year of football experience — his junior year of high school — Green made the Cowboys' roster. Green never missed a game over the next 13 seasons, starting 167 of 168 games after his rookie season. He played cornerback his first eight seasons. Green led the Cowboys in interceptions four times, earned three Pro Bowl invites and garnered two first-team All-Pro honors. In 1970, Green moved to safety, where he was named a Pro Bowler again in 1971 and '72. He played in two NFL Championship Games and Super Bowl V before helping the Cowboys win the Lombardi Trophy with a 24-3 victory over the Dolphins in Super Bowl VI. Green retired after the 1974 season and went into scouting. He worked for the Cowboys and Broncos, earning NFL Scout of the Year in 2010. Green's 34 career interceptions are tied for fifth in the team record book.
author: Charean Williams

title: Jameis Winston on losing his starting job: I understand where I am now
summary: The Giants benched Jameis Winston just 23 days after trading with the Vikings for J.J.
full_text: The Giants benched Jameis Winston just 23 days after trading with the Vikings for J.J. McCarthy. McCarthy will become the third quarterback to start for the Giants, following Jaxson Dart and Winston. Dart tore the MCL and meniscus in his left knee in Week 2, ending his season. Winston started the past four games, going 2-1-1. He was only 14-of-26 for 152 yards with a touchdown and two interceptions on Sunday, leaving with the Giants trailing 34-10 in the fourth quarter. McCarthy rallied the team, going 11-of-21 for 243 yards, a touchdown and an interception and gave the Giants a chance for a miracle comeback. That's why Winston accepts returning to a backup role. "Last game it wasn't what it was capable of being ," Winston said, via video from SNY Giants. "Every single week, you're defined off of the last time you stepped foot on the field. So I believe based off last game, my job is to lead the New York Football Giants to a win, and that didn't happen. That being said, I understand where I am now." Winston has spent most of the past seven seasons as a backup, so he's familiar with the role. "Just focusing on one day at a time," Winston said. "I'm extremely grateful that I still get to do what I love, and that's play football at a high level for the New York Football Giants. Being able to accept roles and understand like, 'What is your significant role? How can I be the best at my role with this team?' is one of the things you have to adjust to in this league."

title: Kendal Daniels practicing today, three days after being taken off the field on a stretcher
summary: Falcons rookie linebacker Kendal Daniels was stretchered off the field on Sunday with what looked like a serious neck injury.
full_text: '' Falcons rookie linebacker Kendal Daniels was stretchered off the field on Sunday with what looked like a serious neck injury. But it turns out that Daniels is just fine. Coach Kevin Stefanski said before today's practice that Daniels is cleared to practice and is not in the concussion protocol. "Doing a lot better. He will practice today, he'll move around. We'll see how it goes this week," Stefanski said. The injury happened when Daniels tackled Bears tight end Colston Loveland, and Daniels’ facemask collided with Loveland’s knee. Daniels stayed down and got medical attention for several minutes, while teammates knelt and were visibly upset. Eventually Daniels was put on a stretcher and taken off the field on a cart. His jersey was cut off by the medical personnel on the scene and his neck was immobilized. He appeared to be conscious and moving a hand. The Falcons quickly announced that he was out of the game with a neck injury. Given that, it's remarkable that Daniels is ready to go three days later. But he's on the practice field today.

author: Myles Simmons

title: Super Bowl stock report for Week 7: Caleb Williams puts Bears back in contention, Rams devolve into disaster
summary: We assess the NFL title race after Week 6 and identify three upcoming games that could reshape the Super Bowl picture
full_text:
There might not be a better encapsulation of the topsy-turvy nature of the NFL than the fact that the Los Angeles Rams own two fewer wins than a Cleveland Browns squad most expected to be in contention for the top pick in the 2027 draft. The Rams are an utter disappointment through six games and will fall well short of delivering on their title of preseason Super Bowl favorites if they do not turn their season around in the next few weeks.
With the Rams out of the top tier of contenders for now, the door is open for someone else to take command of the championship race. Perhaps the Chicago Bears can be that team now that Caleb Williams is healthy and is back to leading a seemingly uncontainable offense.
The season is a month and a half old, so early-season noise is beginning to clear up. The real Super Bowl threats are emerging from the rest.
Here is how the championship race shapes up heading into Week 7.
Odds via DraftKings , +2000 or better
Going 2-1 without Caleb Williams manning the offense was crucial for the Bears. Avoiding a dreaded early-season slump kept all of their goals intact and left them primed to compete at the top of the crowded NFC North upon his return. The Week 5 drubbing against the rival Green Bay Packers amplified the need for Williams to get back into the lineup, though, and he delivered an emphatic response to that embarrassing loss upon his reinsertion into the offense with a monster individual performance in a 31-23 win on the road over the Atlanta Falcons .
It was the Bears' highest-scoring game since Week 1, which showed just how much Williams elevates this team. He completed his first 12 passes against a Falcons defense that has been surprisingly competitive this season en route to the sixth 300-yard effort of his career. His +12.4% completion percentage over expected was his second-best mark to date, and the 83.3% total completion rate was both a career high and the best by any Bears quarterback with at least 30 pass attempts in franchise history. The hamstring seems just fine.
This looks like a breakout season in the making for Williams. All he needs to do is stay on the field. So long as he is available, Chicago seems likely to boast a top-tier offense.
The season-opening loss in Australia was chalked up as a travel-related fluke. The defeat in Denver was a hard-fought battle between two playoff hopefuls. The shootout loss to the Buffalo Bills was a high-variance game against perhaps the best team in the NFL. At face value, each of those results was understandable. Frustrating, yes. But understandable. Then came the stunner in Week 6. Dropping a home game to the Arizona Cardinals completely recontextualized all of the previous losses. If the Rams are capable of losing to that kind of team, then maybe they just are not that good after all.
The most concerning part of this 2-4 start is that there are more reasons for worry than there is room for optimism. Sure, the schedule ahead is far more manageable than what the Rams faced in the season's first month and a half. But dropping a game to the Cardinals means that Sean McVay's crew is capable of losing to practically anyone else it sees during the softer part of its slate. The injury situation makes it all the more likely that the Rams suffer another devastating loss, too, because without Davante Adams , Poona Ford and Kobie Turner (who all landed on injured reserve this week), the floor just got a whole lot lower.
Special teams remains a complete disaster; the defense is solid, but clearly misses Myles Garrett, and Matthew Stafford's decline from his 2025 MVP form handicaps the offense. The Rams need to stack wins in the next four weeks against the Las Vegas Raiders , Los Angeles Chargers , Washington Commanders and Cardinals in order to dig themselves out of last place in the NFC West. If they do not, they might legitimately be in danger of missing the postseason entirely.
The Super Bowl is quite clearly a stretch for the Browns, but should they really hold the sixth-longest odds to win it? They are far more likely to reach the playoffs than some of the other teams in this range, considering they lead the AFC North through six weeks (for the first time since 2014, no less). That 2014 squad ended up at 7-9 and finished last in the division, so if history is any indication, then it makes sense as to why the market is still so low on this team. But at the same time, there are reasons to believe their 4-2 start is for real.
For one, they continue to play excellent defense in the post-Myles Garrett era. Cleveland ranks in a tie for seventh in points allowed per game with second-year star Carson Schwesinger leading the charge. And on the other side of the ball, Deshaun Watson remains above water while his rookie wide receiver tandem of Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion has the makings of a long-term dynamic duo. In his first year as coach, Todd Monken keeps getting the most out of all those pieces and more.
The "Who have they beaten?" argument is fair given the lack of elite opponents and Lamar Jackson's absence for the Baltimore Ravens last week, but three of the four victories came against teams with winning records. The Browns can only play the teams on their schedule, and there are not many daunting challenges on the road ahead, so the wins might just keep piling up. The playoffs are within reach if this train keeps rolling at its current pace.
Sunday, 8:20 p.m., NBC, stream on Fubo
When the Seattle Seahawks line up across from the Kansas City Chiefs on "Sunday Night Football," will they be wishing Kenneth Walker III was still on their side instead of the other? These teams are trending in opposite directions, and their trajectory changes coincide exactly with the Seahawks declining to re-sign Walker and instead watching him land in Kansas City. Zach Charbonnet could make his season debut for Seattle this week, which ought to be a boon to an offense that desperately needs an infusion of rushing ability.
Sunday, 1 p.m., CBS, stream on Paramount+
If Lamar Jackson cannot play with his ankle injury, the Ravens will be in danger of dropping their second consecutive divisional game. This is a prime opportunity for the Cincinnati Bengals to leap past their rivals, especially since they had an extra week to prepare. Every game is critical in a division where three teams stand at 4-2 and the Bengals are only a half game back of the logjam at 3-2.
Thursday, 8:15 p.m., Prime Video
Week 7 opens with a gem. Williams vs. Drake Maye is a spectacular showdown between two elite young quarterbacks who are presently playing their best football of the season. This intra-conference clash provides an excellent opportunity for a couple of Super Bowl hopefuls to see where they stack up against playoff-caliber competition. Chicago might hold an edge due to the injuries on New England's offensive line and at wide receiver, but Maye is back in the kind of form that could be good enough to will the Patriots to a few touchdowns regardless of his supporting cast. The Patriots scored at least 26 points in each of their last three games and likely need to keep that streak alive to keep up with Ben Johnson's high-octane unit.
author: Carter Bahns

title: NFL Week 7 upset alert: Can Giants upset Texans with JJ McCarthy at QB? Can Falcons beat 49ers?
summary: Baltimore and Denver are two other teams firmly at risk of being upset
full_text:
The NFL is funny sometimes. Just when you think you have everything pegged, the league will rip the carpet right out from under you before you even realize it. On a week-to-week basis, any team appears capable of winning, no matter how bleak things may seem from the outside looking in.
Take the Cardinals-Rams games for instance. Los Angeles was dubbed a superteam coming into 2026 and the prohibitive favorite to win the Super Bowl . All the while, Arizona was pinpointed as one of the worst teams in the league and possibly earmarked for the No. 1 overall pick. What happened on Sunday? The Cardinals rolled into SoFi Stadium and handed us arguably the biggest upset of the season. The only thing that stung about Arizona's stunning victory was that we didn't highlight it in last week's post. I had the Cardinals coverering in my weekly picks column , but that was thinking more along the lines of hitting the backdoor cover late.
While we weren't able to sniff out that upset, we did put you on to the Texans taking down the Jaguars in London and the Tennessee Titans taking down the Colts in Indy in last week's piece. We nearly had the Bucs as we win as well, but they couldn't outlast the Steelers in overtime.
That's enough looking back at Week 6. Now, it's time to set our sights on Week 7 and identify a handful of favorites that are officially on upset alert.
All lines via DraftKings ; All times ET
The Rams are reeling. Not only are they 2-4 to begin the season and in last place in the NFC West, but the injury bug is starting to take massive bites out of the roster. Following the loss to Arizona, head coach Sean McVay announced that star receiver Davante Adams ruptured his hamstring and is out for 6 to 10 weeks. On top of that, newly signed kicker Blake Grupe tore his ACL and is out for the year, as is defensive tackle Poona Ford (ruptured triceps). Fellow defensive tackle Kobie Turner is also going to miss at least a month with a groin injury. And that's not even mentioning Myles Garrett (knee), who is still sidelined. That is a lot of bodies piling up for the Rams, which -- as we started to see last week -- makes them vulnerable to just about any club.
That includes a Raiders team that is currently looking to stop a three-game losing skid after beginning the year 3-0. While they've come back down to earth a bit, two of those losses ( Chiefs and Bills ) were by a field goal. Both of those games were played at Allegiant Stadium. Special teams issues have plagued the Rams this season, and they have the worst special teams EPA in the NFL. It's mistakes on that side of the ball that create a perfect concoction for an upset. Moreover, Matthew Stafford hasn't looked like the MVP version of himself from a year ago, ranking 16th in EPA per dropback and 13th in pass success rate. He could be further thrown off his axis when squaring up against Maxx Crosby , who has the second-most pressures (35) in the NFL this season.
Welcome to the J.J. McCarthy era in New York. I'm genuinely curious to see how this goes for the former Vikings first-round pick, who made his debut last week in the fourth quarter. In that brief showing, McCarthy largely played well, throwing for 243 yards, a touchdown, and an interception. Does this give the Giants a boost? McCarthy will have weapons at his disposal in Malik Nabers and Isaiah Likely , and it's possible his rushing ability ignites what has been a lackluster ground attack thus far. Meanwhile, these aren't exactly last year's Texans when it comes to the defense. Coming into Week 7, Houston ranks 20th in scoring defense (23.8). They're also forcing teams to go three-and-out just 14.1% of the time, the third-lowest rate in the NFL. Conversely, the Giants are allowing the fifth-fewest passing yards per game (190.2) in the NFL this season, so maybe they cool off C.J. Stroud .
It's important to note that the Texans will also have a slight rest disadvantage here. While they may be home, Houston is fresh off a game in London last Sunday, which could be a factor in this contest. For what it's worth, the Giants are 4-0 (ATS and SU) in their last four games against Houston.
At some point, the injuries to San Francisco's wide receiver room have to matter, right? When Mike Evans (Achilles) didn't return for the second half of Monday's matchup against the Commanders , the Niners offense mustered a field goal on the opening possession of the third quarter and then punted three straight times (all three-and-outs) to end the game. With the Week 8 bye right in front of them and San Francisco playing on a short week and on the road, it may behoove them to keep Evans sidelined for this game, with hopes of a two-week break being the remedy for the stretch run. If that turns out to be the case, we got a quick sample of an Evans-less offense for the 49ers , and it wasn't the prettiest.
When Evans is on the field, the 49ers have 0.29 EPA per play compared to a -0.03 EPA per play without him. Translation: That's going from the best offense in the NFL to the 16th-ranked offense in the NFL. That brings San Francisco down much closer to Atlanta's level and makes them a live home dog.
It's borderline irresponsible to back the Broncos right now because their offense is totally lost. Bo Nix is averaging just 4.9 air yards per attempt this season, which is the fewest through six games by any player in the last 20 seasons. They won last week in spite of his performance and the defense taking advantage of some questionable throws by Sam Darnold . Now, they head out on the road to face a Cardinals team that has been pesky this season. Most recently, they held Matthew Stafford and the Rams offense to 16 points in a road win. If that's the kind of defensive effort Arizona is going to bring, why should we think the Nix-led Denver offense will fare any better than L.A. from what we've seen out of them through six weeks? I have confidence in Jacoby Brissett , Trey McBride , and the rest of the Arizona offense to get in the low-to-mid-20s on Sunday, which should be enough against Denver.
Seattle will have the home-field and rest advantage over Kansas City after playing last Thursday. However, do you want to know where the Chiefs have the advantage? Quarterback. Sam Darnold was actively putting Seattle behind the eight ball last week in their loss to the Broncos, throwing two interceptions on the final three drives of the game. Turnovers have been a problem for Darnold so far this season, and his 1.4 interceptions-per-game average is the most among players with at least four starts this season. If that persists in this matchup, you're giving Mahomes and old buddy Kenneth Walker III short fields that they'll almost certainly take advantage of to stay undefeated this season. Kansas City is 24-5 in interconference games since 2020 (best in the NFL) and is 8-2 in its past 10 Sunday night road games.
author: Tyler Sullivan

title: NFL Week 7 injury report: Ravens' Lamar Jackson limited, Jets' Breece Hall a non-participant
