author: Shanna McCarriston

title: NFL trade deadline 2026: Saquon Barkley to Seahawks among 10 moves that need to happen
summary: These needle-moving deals would define the trade deadline
full_text:
The closer the NFL calendar creeps to the Nov. 10 trade deadline, the clearer it becomes which teams are buying and which are selling. Three weeks out, there is already a divide between contenders and pretenders, so playing the role of matchmaker provides a myriad of potential trade pairings.
A sweep across the league shows how Super Bowl contenders with roster holes, like the Seattle Seahawks and their running back position, match perfectly with downtrodden teams that own tradeable veterans, like the Philadelphia Eagles and Indianapolis Colts.
Sometimes the obvious trade proposals never come to fruition. But in a lot of cases, if it makes sense on paper, then it makes sense in practice. There are a number of reunions, like Khalil Mack's potential return to the Chicago Bears , that just feel right.
Here are 10 of those trades that feel so fitting that it would be a shame if they did not go through.
The Seattle Seahawks ought to have extreme seller's remorse as they field a bottom-tier rushing attack and watch Kenneth Walker III run wild in Kansas City. Much of their disappointing 3-3 start can be attributed to an offense that ranks second-worst in EPA per rush, which leads one to wonder how much they regret letting Walker go in free agency.
He is very much the missing piece, and they will rely on Zach Charbonnet and Jadarian Price to fill that gap when they return from injured reserve. Neither is an established No. 1 running back, though, so Seattle would benefit from admitting it needs a high-caliber starter, then placing Charbonnet back in his more natural secondary role and allowing Price to develop as a rookie third option.
They would have to pay a hefty price to pry Saquon Barkley away from Philadelphia because of his immense value and his giant cap hit, but with the Eagles poised to watch this season wither away in the wake of countless personnel losses, they should be willing to at least field calls on their superstar running back. Seattle is in as much of a win-now mode as any team in the league and thus is in a position to give up premium draft capital for a player who can help it return to the Super Bowl.
If Jerry Jones cannot turn the Dallas Cowboys into a winning football team, he is at least going to go down swinging. The Joey Porter Jr . trade earlier this season was one big move, but the defense clearly needs more blockbuster additions in order to climb out of the depths. Since Jones addressed the back end of the unit with the Porter deal, it may be time to turn back toward the line of scrimmage and address, again, an edge rusher group that is still lost without Micah Parsons .
While Arizona Cardinals general manager Monti Ossenfort said in August that he has "no interest" in trading Josh Sweat , there might not be a more obvious trade candidate on a team that is not built to contend for anything in 2026. Sweat denied any displeasure with his contract, but there was offseason smoke that he sought a restructured deal or a trade.
He is an expensive veteran for a franchise attempting to build a young core and boasts the kind of perennial sack production and team contract control that a competitive team would pay a premium for. If the Cowboys moved a couple of draft picks to land Sweat, this would be a win-win.
The NFL's stingiest defense is to credit for the Minnesota Vikings ' perfect start. The margins in those five victories were nail-bitingly slim, though, because the offense has only done just enough to capitalize on Brian Flores' coaching masterclass on the other side of the ball.
The passing game is what it is. There is no in-season upgrading over Kyler Murray , and the wide receiver group will always be in good shape so long as Justin Jefferson is there. The main area that needs improvement and, more importantly, can be improved, is the rushing unit. Aaron Jones and Jordan Mason (once healthy) are a serviceable tandem, yet the attack has accounted for only three touchdowns and ranks in the bottom quartile in EPA per rush. An infusion of stardom would take this offense to another level and make the Vikings true Super Bowl contenders.
Enter Jonathan Taylor . Whether the Indianapolis Colts would part with their best player just over two months after they signed him to a two-year contract extension (the third-largest deal for a running back in NFL history) is unknown, but with general manager Chris Ballard fired and coach Shane Steichen potentially on his way out the door , too, this franchise could be headed toward a tear-down. Teams will call about Taylor. Minnesota needs to make sure it is in the conversation.
If there is one trade that is most likely to be completed by the deadline, a Khalil Mack reunion in Chicago has to be at the top of the list. The pairing almost makes too much sense. The Bears need pass-rushing help. Mack remains productive in the latter years of his career, albeit not quite at the All-Pro level of his Chicago heyday. The Los Angeles Chargers are prime candidates to sell expiring contracts, considering their 0-6 record. Everything points to these teams working together to send Mack back to his old home.
The lift Mack would provide for an offense-first team could be a difference maker that sparks a deep postseason run. Now that Caleb Williams is healthy again, the Bears have the potential to score at will. The defense lags behind just enough to warrant a splashy trade deadline move, and this one is just waiting to be completed.
There is a wide receiver injury crisis in Pittsburgh. Aaron Rodgers was on a hot streak until health issues depleted his supporting cast. In order to maximize the supposed last year of his career and stay in contention for the AFC North crown, the Steelers need to plug some immediate help into Rodgers' receiving room.
Michael Pittman Jr. and Roman Wilson are on injured reserve, and Ben Skowronek has a calf issue. It is up to DK Metcalf , rookie Germie Bernard and a couple of practice squad elevations to keep the passing game afloat.
All of that makes the Steelers potentially desperate buyers at the deadline. Chris Godwin Jr. should be on their radar. The Tampa Bay Buccaneers , whom they just defeated in overtime, are drifting further into the abyss and should be ready to sell. His three-year contract makes him an expensive asset who struggles to stay on the field, and that is a profile that the Buccaneers would seemingly want to part with.
He is healthy now, though, and that is what matters to the Steelers. Plus, he should be a tremendous fit next to Metcalf. Godwin spent every year prior to this one on the other side of a towering No. 1 target in Mike Evans , so he would be right at home in the same lineup as a similarly sizable go-to weapon like Metcalf.
The Buffalo Bills are winning games in one way and one way only: Scoring a boatload of points. They have to. The defense is a sieve, specifically in the back end. No matter how much pressure Greg Rousseau and the front provide, opponents are able to pick apart the pass defense to the tune of 285.8 yards per game — the second most in the league. The slot defensive back spot is the biggest weakness, and there is an obvious upgrade potentially sitting on the trade market in Cardinals safety Budda Baker .
Baker is versatile enough to play nickel or fall back deeper into coverage and would immediately be the best player in the Buffalo defensive backfield. He is the Cardinals' highest-paid player and remains under contract through 2027, but he carries a dead cap hit of only $3 million for next year, so moving on from him would not put Arizona in a long-term financial bind. That is an attractive proposition for a rebuilding team.
Jauan Jennings was in a 49ers uniform less than a year ago and would be a perfect fit back in one this season. He led all San Francisco wide receivers in catches and yards in 2024 and 2025 and knows the Kyle Shanahan offense front and back, so with the 49ers fighting through a litany of wideout injuries, why not…
author: Carter Bahns

title: Sam LaPorta sounds off about contract situation with Lions: 'I break my f-----g back for the team'
summary: LaPorta is not a happy camper right now
full_text:
Sam LaPorta is taking a unique approach in terms of his contract situation.
Instead of keeping things in-house, LaPorta has chosen to publicly voice his displeasure . A former Pro Bowler, LaPorta is in the final year of his four-year, $9.47 million rookie contract. He is slated to earn $5.78 million in cash earnings this season.
LaPorta, based on his comments, is clearly not happy that he has yet to receive a contract extension from the Lions.
"I think the combination of like getting your heartstrings twisted, as well as the violent sport that we play, you know, it sucks and it's disappointing that you go out there every week and you bear the risk of getting hurt," LaPorta said on Pardon My Take . "You know, like last year, whatever it was week nine, week 10. I break my f-----g back for the team, and then I'm going out there this year, and I'm balling, and maybe they're not showing the love.
"Yeah, it sucks. I'm going to continue to be a pro, and you know, I just a lot of that to my agent, and he handles that great. ... So I'm going to continue to go do my thing and ball out. And in three months, if I don't get to wear the Honolulu blue and play for the Lions anymore, it's gonna be all good. Yeah, I'll get paid somewhere else. So whatever."
As he alluded to, LaPorta will likely have a big payday this offseason, whether it's with the Lions or someone else. His current market value is a three-year, $45.1 million deal, according to Spotrac .
A former second-round pick, LaPorta has been a valuable part of the Lions' offense since he was drafted back in 2023. He made the Pro Bowl as a rookie and has caught 213 passes and 23 touchdowns in 47 regular season games. During the Lions' 2023 playoff run, he caught 21 of 27 targets for 176 yards and a score.
LaPorta has bounced back this season after a serious back injury sidelined him for the second half of the 2025 campaign. He's been especially good over the past two games; he caught eight passes for 84 yards and a touchdown against the Panthers in Week 5 and caught each of his five targets for 88 yards and a score during last week's win over the Cardinals .
It's very possible that the Lions -- and other potential teams that might be interested in his services -- are turned off by his decision to be so vocal about his contract status, especially with the Lions getting ready for a big showdown against the rival Packers .
Talent, however, usually tops anything else in the NFL . As long as LaPorta continues to produce, he will surely have a robust market if he becomes a free agent this offseason. He has certainly made it clear that he is comfortable with the prospect of becoming a free agent for the first time this offseason if he and the Lions do not come to terms on a long-term deal.
author: Bryan DeArdo

title: Giants plan to start JJ McCarthy vs. Texans in Week 7
summary: McCarthy is set to make his first career start for Big Blue
full_text:
The New York Giants have apparently made a decision on who their starting quarterback will be for this weekend's game against the Houston Texans.
The plan is for JJ McCarthy to get the start, with Jameis Winston backing him up. McCarthy, who was traded from Minnesota earlier this season, is in line to make his first career start for the Giants, who are currently sitting atop the NFC East division with a 3-2-1 record.
John Harbaugh confirms that J.J. McCarthy will start on Sunday for the Giants pic.twitter.com/h7Y9z2W6QR
The Giants initially turned to Winston after Jaxson Dart suffered a season-ending injury in Week 2. As he is known to do, Winston had both good and bad moments over the past five games. He played well enough, though, to post a 2-1-1 record as the Giants' starting quarterback.
Winston struggled on this past Sunday, and he was replaced in the second half by McCarthy, who engineered three fourth-quarter scoring drives. The comeback fell short, however, as the Saints left New Jersey with a 34-27 win.
"I thought Jameis has done a tremendous job, won us games, played well. As we go forward here, this is going to be our direction. We think it gives us some good options on offense,'' John Harbaugh told reporters.
Harbaugh chose McCarthy, who has displayed flashes of the player that compelled Minnesota to take him with the 10th overall pick in the 2024 draft. Injuries and inconsistent play, however, prevented McCarthy from having more success with the Vikings , who are off to a 5-0 start this season with Kyler Murray at quarterback.
"I think he's a strong, young quarterback, has some experience in the National Football League," Harbaugh said of McCarthy shortly after the Giants traded for him. "Obviously, was a very high draft pick, very talented player and is going to make us a stronger football team."
In 12 career games, McCarthy has completed just 57.2% of his passes with more interceptions (13) than touchdown passes (12). He has five touchdowns on the ground and an impressive 5.1 yards-per-carry average.
"I think the last couple weeks, they've (the players) had a chance to see him practice and they're pretty fired up about it,'' Harbaugh said on Wednesday.
Sunday's game was a microcosm of McCarthy's career up to this point. Despite having an underwhelming stat sheet, he was nonetheless able to engineer several successful scoring drives that got the Giants back in the game.
McCarthy will face a Texans team that is finding its rhythm after a slow start to the season.
J.J. McCarthy says he feels "extremely comfortable" with the Giants' playbook: "Great teachers in this building, Jameis has helped me out from the get-go since I got here. Coach Nags, Coach Callahan, they've been doing a tremendous job of just making sure I'm up to speed." pic.twitter.com/ungFAm8rZu
The Texans, after a 0-4 start, have won two straight games after they defeated the Jaguars on Sunday in London. While this season hasn't been their best, the Texans have talented players on defense, especially pass rusher Will Anderson, who leads the NFL with 7.5 sacks. While McCarthy's mobility may be an asset, his lack of experience running the Giants' offense could also hold the Giants back.
Quarterback isn't the only position the Giants need to solidify.  They also need to figure out who the starting running back is after Cam Skattebo — the Giants' starter on paper — inexplicably received zero carries during Sunday's loss to the Saints. Harbaugh said afterward that he is waiting for one of his running backs to earn the job. That player will not be Najee Harris , who was released on Tuesday.
author: Bryan DeArdo

title: Agent's Take: Chris Ballard's Colts tenure might look much different had he made this blockbuster trade
summary: Indianapolis was among Stafford's preferred destinations in 2021, but Ballard chose a different path and never solved the franchise's quarterback problem
full_text:
The Indianapolis Colts dismissed general manager Chris Ballard one day after losing 26-20 to the previously winless Tennessee Titans . The Colts dropped to 2-4 with the loss.
Ballard is the first head coach or front office executive to be fired during the 2026 NFL season. His nearly 10-year tenure as Colts general manager was hindered by an inability to find a long-term solution at quarterback after Andrew Luck's surprising retirement shortly before the 2019 regular season started.
The Colts haven't made the playoffs since going 11-5 in 2020 with a 39-year-old Philip Rivers , who signed a one-year, $25 million deal in free agency. Rivers retired following a 27-24 wild-card playoff game loss to the Buffalo Bills , who lost to the Kansas City Chiefs in the AFC Championship Game.
There's one bold move Ballard could have made in 2021 that would have ended the revolving door at quarterback that has plagued the Colts and changed the franchise's trajectory. The Detroit Lions were accommodating Matthew Stafford's trade request. The Colts were on Stafford's short list of teams, along with the Los Angeles Rams and San Francisco 49ers . Stafford mentioned during a March 2025 episode of Jason and Travis Kelce's "New Heights" podcast that he searched for houses in Indianapolis on Zillow before his trade to the Rams.
The Lions received a 2022 first-round pick, a 2023 first-round pick, a 2021 third-round pick and Jared Goff , who was thought to be a throw-in "bridge quarterback" because of his hefty contract, from the Rams for Stafford. After a rocky start in Detroit, Goff has proven to be the answer at quarterback, earning a four-year, $212 million contract extension, averaging $53 million per year in 2024. A Ballard offer the Lions couldn't refuse would probably have been somewhere between the actual Stafford acquisition cost and the two quarterback trades made the following year, in 2022, for Deshaun Watson and Russell Wilson .
The Seattle Seahawks dealt Wilson and a 2022 fourth-round pick to the Denver Broncos for multiple players (tight end Noah Fant , defensive lineman Shelby Harris and quarterback Drew Lock ), 2022 and 2023 first-round picks, 2022 and 2023 second-round picks, and a 2022 fifth-round pick in March 2022. The Washington Commanders reportedly offered the Seahawks three first-round picks, but Wilson's no-trade clause, which he waived for the Broncos, gave him control over his destination.
Watson's trade from the Houston Texans to the Cleveland Browns followed shortly thereafter. The Browns received Watson and a 2024 sixth-round pick for 2022, 2023, and 2024 first-round picks, a 2022 fourth-round pick, a 2023 third-round pick and a 2024 fourth-round pick.
Perhaps, a trade based around Ballard giving up 2021 (21st overall), 2022 and 2023 first-round picks for Stafford would have gotten the deal done. The Rams didn't have a 2021 first-round pick because of a trade with the Jacksonville Jaguars for cornerback Jalen Ramsey during the middle of the 2020 season.
Ballard subsequently demonstrated he could take big swings in an attempt to improve the Colts' roster. At last year's trade deadline, Ballard went all in on the 2025 season when the Colts were 7-2 by obtaining All-Pro cornerback Sauce Gardner from the New York Jets for a 2026 first-round pick, a 2027 first-round pick and wide receiver Adonai Mitchell .
That type of aggressiveness by Ballard in 2021 to stabilize the most important position on a football team, quarterback, would have prevented the failed Carson Wentz experiment. Wentz was acquired from the Philadelphia Eagles for a 2021 third-round pick and a conditional 2022 second-round pick that became a 2022 first-round pick because his 2021 season offensive playtime reached 75%. He was reunited with Frank Reich, who coached the Colts from 2018 until nine games into the 2022 season. Reich was Wentz's offensive coordinator for Wentz's first two years in the NFL with the Eagles, 2016 and 2017.
The salary cap wouldn't have been an impediment to getting Stafford. He had two years remaining on his $43 million contract, earning $20 million in 2021 and $23 million in 2022. Wentz had four years for $98.4 million left on his deal before reworking his contract, where $5 million of his $25.4 million in 2021 compensation was moved to 2022 for additional contract security.
The reunion was short-lived. Wentz's poor play down the stretch in 2021, particularly during the regular season finale against the 2-14 Jaguars, when the Colts controlled their own playoff destiny but failed to secure a postseason berth, led to his departure. Colts owner the late Jim Irsay called acquiring Wentz a mistake shortly after he was dealt along with a 2022 second round pick (47th overall) and a 2022 seventh round pick to the Commanders for a 2022 second round pick (42nd overall), a 2022 third round pick and a conditional 2023 third round pick in March 2022. The 2023 selection didn't upgrade to a 2023 second-round pick since Wentz didn't take at least 70% of Washington's offensive snaps in 2022.
An aging Matt Ryan was acquired in March of 2022 for a third-round pick. The Colts anticipated Ryan being the quarterback for two years, as his contract was restructured with $12 million of his 2023 salary becoming fully guaranteed. Father Time caught up to a then 37-year-old Ryan in 2022. Instead of contending for a playoff berth, the Colts finished 4-12-1 in 2022. Ryan was released in March 2023. He made $36.7 million for his one-year stint in Indianapolis.
Reaching for Anthony Richardson with 2023's fourth overall pick wouldn't have occurred either. Richardson was a boom-or-bust quarterback prospect with a low floor and a high ceiling. The Colts were enticed by his great arm strength and tremendous athleticism, overlooking his raw, inexperienced nature. Richardson had 13 starts in his three years at Florida.
The Colts hedged their bet on Richardson by signing Daniel Jones to a one-year, $14 million contract worth up to $17 million through incentives in March 2025. Going with Jones, who was benched by the New York Giants 10 games into the 2024 season before his request for a release was granted, at quarterback in 2025 was initially more of an indictment of Richardson than anything else.
Jones was having a surprising career resurrection when he tore his right Achilles late in the 2025 season. A 7-1 start turned into a stunning collapse where the Colts finished with an 8-9 record.
Jones was given the seldom-used transition tag for $37.8 million before quickly signing a two-year, $ 88 million contract worth up to $100 million through incentives, with $60 million in guarantees, of which $49.49 million was fully guaranteed at signing in March. He has struggled so much this season that a benching isn't out of the question.
Stafford paid immediate dividends for the Rams. After going 10-6 and being eliminated in the divisional playoffs in 2020, the Rams won Super Bowl LVI. Stafford arguably had the best season of his career to that point. He completed 67.2% of his passes for 4,886 yards with 41 touchdowns and 17 interceptions to post a 102.9 passer rating. Stafford finished in the NFL's top 10 for touchdown passes, passing yards, passer rating, and completion percentage, ranking second, third, sixth and 10th, respectively. More importantly, Stafford elevated his play in the postseason. Stafford's 2021 season was subsequently topped in 2025 when he was named NFL MVP.
There's no guarantee the Colts would have duplicated the Rams' success with Stafford in 2021. The Colts surely would have made the playoffs with the upgrade at quarterback and challenged the Titans, who were 12-5 in 2021, for the AFC South crown. After all, the Colts went 9-8 with Wentz and were 11-5 in 2020. It's conceivable that the two-game win regression from 2020 could have resulted in no drop off in wins or at least a one-game win increase with Stafford at quarterback.
The 2021 Colts had a strong offensive line anchored by…
author: Joel Corry

title: Jonathan Taylor mock trades: How Giants, Bengals could target Colts star RB after Chris Ballard's firing
summary: The Colts need to replenish their draft assets, and dealing their three-time Pro Bowl running back could produce a significant return
full_text:
After a loss to the previously winless Titans dropped the Colts to 2-4 on the young season, Indianapolis fired GM Chris Ballard . It was the first firing by Colts owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon, and it might not be the last. Shane Steichen has zero postseason trips in four seasons as the Colts' coach, and while he's still leading the way for now, there's no doubt his seat is and has been warm. How much warmer it became after Ballard's firing is unclear, but it's clear Irsay-Gordon expects better than what the Colts are producing.
It's also clear that the Colts aren't close to getting to the level Irsay-Gordon expects. Daniel Jones has been a turnover machine, and the defense is below average, with issues rushing the passer and defending the run. The Colts are 28th in yards per play allowed and 26th in net yards per attempt allowed.
Sometimes it has to get worse before it gets better, and that may be the case for the Colts. Indianapolis is already down a 2027 first-round pick, traded to the Jets at the 2025 trade deadline, but the Colts could be sellers -- and maybe major sellers -- this year.
The biggest name would be star running back Jonathan Taylor . He had 20 touchdowns and nearly 2,000 yards from scrimmage last year, and he's on his way to another big season, but the Colts are stuck going nowhere once again. He's 27 and has played in just one playoff game -- as a rookie in 2020. In fact, Taylor headlined Jordan Dajani's list of five players we want to see moved by the Nov. 10 deadline.
Taylor would have plenty of suitors if made available, and the situation isn't too dissimilar from what the Panthers were going through with Christian McCaffrey in 2022. McCaffrey is a more versatile player than Taylor in the passing game and was younger than Taylor is now when that deal happened, but he had also been injured. In the deal with the 49ers in 2022, Carolina received second-, third-, fourth- and fifth-round picks.
With that in mind, here are five teams who could come calling about Taylor and what a mock trade might look like:
Giants receive: RB Jonathan Taylor Colts receive: RB Cam Skattebo , 2027 second-round pick, 2028 fourth-round pick
The Giants used a four-running-back committee Sunday against the Saints and then released Najee Harris (who didn't exactly love the rotation). In between, John Harbaugh explained his rationale, saying he "would love" to have a " Derrick Henry circumstance or a 'Saquon Barkley circumstance." Whether he meant to or not, it was surely a bummer for Giants fans to hear Harbaugh mention his running back from last year and a former Giants running back in the same sentence. Regardless, Taylor could be that type of workhorse. The Colts getting two high draft picks over the next two years, plus Skattebo, who showed promise as a rookie but didn't have a single touch Sunday, on a cost-effective deal, would be a solid start. The Giants are leading a historically bad NFC East, and even if it doesn't finish that way, having Taylor next to Jaxson Dart next year would be an enticing prospect.
One thing to note, though, is that Harbaugh comes from one of the most patient, draft-and-develop franchises in Baltimore. This would be a significant departure from that.
Bengals receive: RB Jonathan Taylor, 2027 fourth-round pick Colts receive: RB Chase Brown , 2027 second-round pick, 2027 fifth-round pick
This would be similar to the package the Panthers got for McCaffrey, but instead of a third-round pick, the Colts would get Brown. At 26, he's younger and has less wear and tear than Taylor. He's also an accomplished player and productive pass catcher who has handled a bell-cow workload before. A change of scenery could do him good, as he has struggled to get going early this season. For the Bengals , this would be a second major win-now move in just over six months; they sent the No. 10 pick to the Giants in April for Dexter Lawrence . The Bengals have tried to work in more under-center looks, but are among the worst teams using it. Taylor could change that single-handedly. Cincinnati also has an extra third-round pick, which helps make giving up so many picks easier to swallow.
Broncos receive: RB Jonathan Taylor, 2027 fifth-round pick Colts receive: RB J.K. Dobbins , 2027 second-round pick, 2027 fourth-round pick
The Broncos traded a first-round pick for an upgrade at wide receiver in Jaylen Waddle this offseason (though it hasn't really worked out yet). Would they make another big deal for an upgrade at running back in Taylor? The Broncos have struggled to muster much on the ground, exacerbating quarterback Bo Nix's struggles. Dobbins is on a two-year deal, though there's an out after this year should the Colts choose to use it.
Seahawks receive: RB Jonathan Taylor Colts receive: RB Jadarian Price , 2027 second-round pick
It'd be rare to see a team move on from a first-round pick so quickly, but the Seahawks are in a rare position as the first team to lose a Super Bowl MVP in over two decades. Seattle very much misses Kenneth Walker III and is struggling to find much of anything on the ground without him. Price is on IR, and Emanuel Wilson and George Holani have had devastating fumbles. Offensive coordinator Brian Fleury has been with the 49ers since 2019, so he knows the value of a great top running back. Indianapolis would get a good young running back and ample future picks.
Vikings receive: RB Jonathan Taylor Colts receive: RB Jordan Mason , 2027 second-round pick, 2027 fifth-round pick
The 5-0 Vikings have shown signs of an improved run game this year, and Mason is on his way back from a thumb injury that had him on IR, but Taylor would be a game-changer, and combining him with a mobile quarterback in Kyler Murray would be a treat for Kevin O'Connell. Mason, meanwhile, is a good player on his own accord. Plus, the Vikings have draft capital to spare, with an extra third, two extra fifths and two extra sixths.
author: Zachary Pereles

title: Quenton Nelson trade destinations: Five contenders that should call as Colts begin rebuild
summary: Nelson is Pro Football Focus' highest-graded guard in 2026, and he is a pending free agent whose general manager just got fired
full_text:
Indianapolis Colts owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon just signaled to the rest of the NFL that they are set to undergo a rebuild after firing general manager Chris Ballard .
Irsay-Gordon ended Ballard's regime six games into his 10th year in charge. Indianapolis reached the playoffs twice (2018 and 2020), going 1-2 in those two trips under Ballard. The Colts' 72-82-1 regular-season record under his management ranked 17th in the league, middle of the pack, during Ballard's tenure. Indianapolis' five missed playoffs in a row represent the Colts' longest such streak in four decades. Indianapolis never won an AFC South title under Ballard.
Now, the Colts are set to start over in 2027 with a teardown and rebuild ahead under a new front office. The pro of starting a rebuild now is that the 2027 NFL Draft is widely regarded as one of the most talented in years. The con is that the Colts don't have a first-round pick, thanks to trading their 2026 and 2027 first-round draft choices, along with wide receiver Adonai Mitchell , to the New York Jets last season in exchange for All-Pro cornerback Sauce Gardner .
So who could Indianapolis trade away to recoup first-round pick or second-round pick value? Well, Quenton Nelson , an eight-time Pro Bowler, is set to become one of the NFL's most desired free agents ahead of his 31st birthday. This year, Nelson is Pro Football Focus' highest-graded guard with an 89.2 offensive grade.
He is a coveted, win-now asset who could net Indianapolis a second-round pick or maybe a first-round choice if the bidding for him heats up by the trade deadline on Nov. 10, just a few weeks away. The issue with a potential compensation package for the Colts is that Nelson would be a rental or command a top-of-the-market extension for whoever trades for him.
So who could line up to be Nelson's new NFL landing spot?
Record: 3-2-1 (First in NFC East)
It appeared as though the New York Giants ' 2026 season was cooked with Jaxson Dart and Brian Burns going down in the first three weeks of the season. Fast forward to the end of the first third of the year, and the Giants remain in first place in the NFC East because it's the NFC Least. This year's NFC East became the first division ever to go winless in consecutive weeks .
That means even with J.J. McCarthy starting , the Giants still have a chance to win the division. With Dart still on his rookie deal for two more seasons in 2027 and 2028 before hitting his fifth-year option in 2029, the Giants could take a swing for Nelson in an attempt to win now and begin wooing him for the long haul ahead of his free agency next spring.
Do you know the last time a Giants interior offensive lineman made the Pro Bowl? It was all the way back in 2012 that guard Chris Snee earned the honor, when the world was a much, much different place. Trading for Nelson could be a perfect fit for New York to fix a long-time weakness, and they could structure an extension for him in a way that perfectly lines up with Dart's rookie deal. It doesn't hurt that Nelson is a New Jersey guy, starring at Red Bank (N.J.) Catholic before he enrolled at Notre Dame.
Record: 5-0 (First in NFC North)
The Minnesota Vikings ' offense needs a boost. Their 5-0 start has almost nothing to do with what they're doing on that side of the ball. They have scored the fewest touchdowns, nine, in a 5-0 start since the 2003 Carolina Panthers , per CBS Sports Research. Their 283.0 total yards per game, which ranks as the sixth-fewest in the NFL this season, is the worst team offense in a 5-0 start since the 1977 Denver Broncos , according to CBS Sports Research.
They could be interested if they want to upgrade their offense and move off of undrafted free agent Joe Huber at left guard, with Donovan Jackson out for the season with a torn meniscus. Minnesota will have a phenomenal opportunity to scout Nelson in Week 7 when he and the Colts come to town to play the Vikings.
Record: 4-2 (Second in NFC North)
The Green Bay Packers , a team that has been playing mix-and-match with an injury-plagued front, have stabilized their offensive line with the same starting five combination for the last three weeks. That has been a game-changer for them, as that stabilization coincides with their current three-game winning streak. But they could be in the mix, since they're rolling with aging veterans they signed off the street to start for them. Guard Laken Tomlinson , 34, is in his 12th NFL season, and 2024 sixth-round pick guard Travis Glover likely isn't a long-term solution.
Nelson is, and when the Packers can protect quarterback Jordan Love and prevent him from being pressured in the pocket, he is a markedly better quarterback. Green Bay is also quietly in an all-in window the next three years, given the structure of Micah Parsons ' four-year, $186 million contract with $136 million guaranteed. Yes, the Packers don't have a 2027 first-round pick because of their trade of Parsons, but they do have the rights to their 2027 second- and third-round picks. Plus, they own their top five picks in 2028, so they could muster up a competitive package of picks to trade for Nelson.
Record: 6-0 (First in NFC West)
The San Francisco 49ers could make an all-in trade for Nelson. Quarterback Brock Purdy is playing like the best quarterback in football through the first six weeks of the 2026 season despite a litany of wide receiver injuries. With many of San Francisco's best players on the wrong side of 30 years old, the time is now for the 49ers to contend.
They are armed with all of their 2027 draft picks through the first five rounds of the draft, and they currently have the most remaining camp space in the entire NFL this season at $41.3 million. San Francisco could get creative with the structure of a potential extension for Nelson. Investing in Nelson could also prolong the career of 2023 NFL Offensive Player of the Year running back Christian McCaffrey , who is now 30 years old with plenty of tread on his tires.
Record: 2-4 (Third in AFC South)
If the Houston Texans (2-4), winners of two in a row, continue to climb, perhaps they would be interested. However, their asking price from the Colts could be higher since they're a fellow AFC South team. Being able to replace Ed Ingram , Pro Football Focus' No. 26-graded guard with a 69.1 offensive grade, with PFF's No. 1 guard could be a major boon for ascending quarterback C.J. Stroud . He ranks second in the NFL in passing yards (1,714), third in touchdown-to-interception ratio (9-1), 11th in passer rating (100.9), and tied for first in 20-yard completions (25) for a Texans squad that has now won two in a row after an 0-4 start. Imagine how much higher he and Houston could soar with Nelson blocking for him in pursuit of a third AFC South title in four years.

title: Titans release DT Jordan Elliott after incident with firearm at team facility, per report
summary: The veteran defensive tackle appeared in five games this season after following Robert Saleh to Tennessee from San Francisco
full_text:
The Tennessee Titans released defensive tackle Jordan Elliott on Tuesday following an "incident" at the team facility last week. The Titans offered no further details in a statement , saying only there was an incident on Thursday, Oct. 15, and that Elliott was no longer part of their team.
Elliott became frustrated with a teammate on the practice field. He was later seen storming out of the locker room and went to his vehicle to grab a firearm, according to A to Z Sports . However, the situation was de-escalated before anything tragic happened. ESPN confirmed this report , saying that Elliott was upset with right tackle JC Latham , and that the firearm never left Elliott's parking spot. The Metro Nashville Police Department told A to Z Sports that no reports had been filed. Reports indicated fellow defensive lineman John Franklin-Myers helped de-escalate the situation, something that was confirmed by Titans head coach Robert Saleh during his Wednesday press conference.
Saleh told reporters that Elliott is a good man who has never committed a crime in his life. He gave credit to the Titans organization and the league for "pausing," and asking why would a "great man" and "great father" do something like this? Saleh also said he viewed this as a "call for help" more than a "criminal act."
"I will stand on the table for Jordan's character," Saleh said. "Unfortunately, rules are rules with regard to guns on property. And sometimes it's far greater than the knee-jerk reaction of kicking somebody when they're down. My message to 31 other teams would be if you need a hell of a run-stopping D-tackle that can help you on a playoff run, give me a call, I'll tell you everything you need to know about him. He's a good man. Had a terrible lapse in judgment that I recognize as a call for help more than a criminal act. It's unfortunate the way it went down. But as far as Jordan's concerned and the locker room and all that, I think people see it differently here than the knee-jerk reaction of the world."
Clip of #Titans coach Robert Saleh standing up for Jordan Elliott despite a “terrible lapse in judgment.” Saleh notes players recently have taken their own lives. While not saying Elliott is in that mindset, Saleh is mindful this could’ve been a “cry for help.” 🎥 @Titans pic.twitter.com/FlrcEz4V67
Elliott has played in five games this season with one start, and has recorded 11 tackles. He was inactive this past Sunday against the Indianapolis Colts , with Saleh telling reporters Elliott was "dealing with personal stuff." Elliott had followed Saleh over from the San Francisco 49ers , as he spent the past two seasons out in Santa Clara, making 29 starts in 31 games played.
Elliott's release is not the only strange occurrence the Titans are dealing with, as the team also made starting cornerback and $58 million free-agent addition Alontae Taylor inactive in Week 6. They didn't just bench him; they took his uniform away. It was described as a coach's decision, and Saleh has refused to elaborate on the situation.
"We'll discuss it as a staff and make a decision that is best for the team moving forward," Saleh told reporters on Monday.
The Titans return home this week to host the 4-2 Cleveland Browns , who currently lead the AFC North.

title: Eagles will not be punished for how team handled Jalen Hurts' blood clots situation, NFLPA responds
summary: The NFL concluded the process to clear Hurts for Week 5 in London was handled appropriately
full_text:
The Philadelphia Eagles will not face any punishment from the NFL regarding how they handled Jalen Hurts ' medical situation, according to The Athletic . On Monday, the team announced that Hurts is expected to miss the rest of the 2026 season after blood clots were discovered in his lungs.
The league has reportedly concluded that the process that led to Hurts being cleared to play in Week 5 vs. the Jacksonville Jaguars in London with a superficial blood clot "was handled appropriately." The league will not levy any punishment on the franchise for how it handled its medical process, or for Hurts not being given an injury designation ahead of the game.
On Tuesday, the NFL released a statement providing more information on what it knew regarding Hurts' situation and the medical professionals treating him. The league says it was in contact with the Eagles during the tests, going back to the first one in London. The league also clarified what it called "misinformation" regarding reports that Hurts did not sleep for 36 hours ahead of their international game.
Here is the full statement from the league:
"The league had been in contact throughout the process with the Eagles medical personnel, and the Cleveland Clinic in London where the tests were conducted. The league's Chief Medical Officer Dr. Allen Sills arranges for medical resources with leading providers in every international market with approval from the NFL Players Association. Medical care for players is provided by club medical staff in coordination with independent doctors. There was also misinformation regarding Jalen not sleeping for 36 hours before the game. That was not true and no one told him not to sleep because of his situation. The club told all players, coaches and personnel to try to stay awake as long as they could on Saturday as the team was returning back home after the game in London. The team did not have a bye week and like other NFL teams that travel to London and back, they were trying maintain as much of a normal routine as possible."
The NFL Player's Association (NFLPA), released a statement on Tuesday night responding to reports that the NFL will not punish the Eagles for the handling of the situation. They claim the league informed the union that they didn't plan to look further into the management and treatment of Hurts' health. The NFPA is asking the league to launch a full investigation.
Here is the full NFLPA statement :On
"The NFLPA is not aware of any NFL investigation into the medical care provided to Jalen Hurts. In fact, the league previously informed the union that it did not plan to review the care he received. Before conclusions are drawn about how this situation was handled, there must be a full investigation into what occurred. Determining the facts is essential to ensuring players receive the highest level of care and protection going forward."
Wednesday, NFL commissioner Roger Goodell said the league would welcome an investigation.
He later added, "I think our protocols were incredibly good there" and said the NFL has the "greatest medical advisors and people that are working on the health of our players," per NFL Network .
Roger Goodell on the @NFLPA ’s request for an investigation into the Jalen Hurts situation: “We welcome that.” pic.twitter.com/m67z3DkyjK
On Thursday of last week, the Eagles issued a statement saying that a superficial blood clot in Hurts' calf experienced movement, leading the team to rule him out for their Week 6 matchup against the Carolina Panthers . The Eagles also revealed that the NFL was made aware of the situation last week. It was the first of several confusing developments that led to more questions than answers.
Just days after Hurts' blood clot diagnosis became public, it was reported that the team did not plan to place him on injured reserve. Hours later, Hurts was being placed on injured reserve. Then came the bombshell on Monday, when a follow-up scan revealed Hurts' superficial vein thrombosis had developed into deep vein thrombosis, including "bilateral pulmonary emboli," meaning blood clots were now in both of Hurts' lungs.
It's not exactly clear why Hurts was allowed to play a football game and take a long international flight with a superficial blood clot, or whether the Eagles' decisions made his situation more serious. But the NFL has concluded that the team took the appropriate steps in handling the issue.
Jonathan Jones offered additional reporting to help clear up some misconceptions about this wild story.
There was a report that Hurts was told by doctors not to sleep as a precaution due to his blood clot, so he didn't sleep for 36 hours before playing against the Jaguars. The NFL specifically targeted this rumor in their statement, making it clear that the team was encouraged to stay up late to remain on Eastern time.
Hurts was not told to stay awake because of his medical condition. He returned to the team hotel around 2:45 a.m. local time on Sunday and slept until around 10 a.m. Hurts also took a nap at the stadium before kickoff.
Tom Pelissero eventually walked back this reporting, saying Hurts' agent clarified that while the quarterback was up until early Sunday morning being evaluated at a hospital, he was able to sleep before the game.
Saturday, Oct. 10: Superficial blood clot discovered in Hurts' calf during a visit to the Cleveland Clinic in London following a team walk-through.
Wednesday, Oct. 14: Follow-up appointment in Philly reveals superficial blood clot had moved, causing Eagles to shut down Hurts indefinitely. He undergoes further testing.
Monday, Oct. 19: Eagles and Hurts' agent, Nicole Lynn, issue a joint statement laying out the updated diagnosis of deep vein thrombosis. Here's the full statement:
"Over the last few days, Jalen Hurts has received comprehensive medical evaluations by physician experts. In the interest of transparency, we are providing additional information on the diagnosis and treatment plan related to his condition.
"Jalen was initially diagnosed by specialists in London with a left calf superficial vein thrombosis. After further testing and monitoring, the current diagnosis is a deep vein thrombosis, as well as bilateral pulmonary emboli. He is clinically stable and has no significant functional limitations. His treatment should only involve anticoagulation (i.e. "blood thinners"). During this time, he will not be allowed to participate in any contact activities, including football.
"Jalen's prognosis is very good, and we expect a full recovery. We anticipate that he will have the opportunity to resume contact football activities when off the blood thinners. In the meantime, he will remain active around the team and continue to condition. More importantly, we anticipate that he will have no long-term effects."
author: Jordan Dajani

title: NFL trade deadline: 5 players we'd like to see get a change of scenery, including Jonathan Taylor
summary: These blockbuster moves probably will not happen, but stars like Jonathan Taylor and Jeffery Simmons deserve a chance to play for true contenders
full_text:
The NFL trade deadline is right around the corner, and you're probably familiar with a few names that may or may not be on the trade block. Pass rushers Khalil Mack and Josh Sweat could be on the move. Fans are interested to see what happens with Jacksonville Jaguars wide receiver Brian Thomas Jr ., and maybe Tennessee Titans running back Tony Pollard is shipped off to a contender.
The trade chatter is usually more entertaining than the deals that actually take place before that Nov. 10 deadline, but we've been surprised before. Remember when the Jaguars sent cornerback Jalen Ramsey to the Los Angeles Rams in 2019? Or when the Carolina Panthers dealt running back Christian McCaffrey to the San Francisco 49ers in 2022? Those two players definitely needed a change of scenery. Who are some current NFL stars who could use one as well?
Below, we will break down five players who more than likely won't be dealt at the trade deadline but whom we would like to see moved. Let's begin with a star running back.
Jonathan Taylor is still one of the best running backs in the NFL, but his Indianapolis Colts are struggling. Indy just lost to the previously winless Titans, which led to the firing of general manager Chris Ballard on Monday.
Quarterback Daniel Jones has really struggled this season. He threw for 269 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions on Sunday while registering a QBR of 24.5. Jones is averaging 215.0 passing yards per game and has thrown four touchdowns compared to six interceptions. At what point do you consider throwing Anthony Richardson back in the lineup?
Taylor, on the other hand, has racked up 655 scrimmage yards and seven touchdowns through the first six games of the season. He just became the fastest player to reach 8,000 career rushing yards since Adrian Peterson , and he should be carrying the rock for a team with Super Bowl aspirations.
Where could he fit? Seattle Seahawks , New England Patriots , Minnesota Vikings
Jeffery Simmons has been the best interior defensive lineman in the NFL for two seasons now. The casual fan probably doesn't see much Titans football on "RedZone," but Simmons is a one-man wrecking crew for a terrible team.
Simmons led all defensive tackles with 11.0 sacks and 17 tackles for loss last season, which earned him first-team All-Pro honors. He's on a similar trajectory this year, having recorded 4.0 sacks and six tackles for loss through six weeks.
Simmons got to the quarterback twice this past Sunday in Indy, and logged SEVEN pressures from the interior. On the first play from scrimmage of the second half, he stripped Jonathan Taylor of the ball and recovered it himself.
Big Jeff doing it all on that turnover 📺: @NFLonFOX pic.twitter.com/k62Fe0nPYK
Simmons is the longest-tenured Titan and the emotional leader of this team. He just signed a three-year, $105.8 million extension four months ago. It doesn't seem likely that he's moved, but Simmons would be talked about like one of the best players in the NFL if he were wrecking games for a contender.
Where could he fit? Chicago Bears , New England Patriots
The Los Angeles Chargers are 0-6, and there's little hope this team can turn it around. Offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel is on the hot seat — the same could be said for head coach Jim Harbaugh — and now, injuries are beginning to mount. If quarterback Justin Herbert couldn't figure it out with Ladd McConkey , Rashawn Slater and Joe Alt healthy, what's it going to look like with all of them out/injured?
Herbert leads the NFL in interceptions this year with eight and is averaging a career-low 190.2 passing yards per game. He became the first quarterback in NFL history to start a season 0-6 while throwing an interception with at least two sacks taken in each game. It's been a disaster.
Justin Herbert is not Josh Allen or Lamar Jackson . He can't be leading the Chargers in rushing yards like he did against the Kansas City Chiefs on Sunday, and he can't power a team to success by himself. Herbert needs a more comfortable situation — maybe one that includes a Brian Flores defense and Justin Jefferson .
Where could he fit? Minnesota Vikings, New York Jets , Philadelphia Eagles
Budda Baker has been a star for the Arizona Cardinals ever since he was selected No. 36 overall in the 2017 NFL Draft out of Washington. He made the Pro Bowl as a rookie — the first of what have turned into eight Pro Bowl appearances. Not many players have made 1,000 tackles before age 30. Just Bobby Wagner , Roquan Smith , Luke Kuechly , Lavonte David , Ray Lewis, Fred Warner and ... Budda Baker.
Baker is still a stud, as evidenced by the Cardinals' upset win over the Rams on Sunday. He recorded six tackles, one sack, two tackles for loss and one pass defensed. He stopped at least one touchdown from being scored, and he was effective in blitzing the quarterback and stopping the running backs. Someone come get him.
Where could he fit? Buffalo Bills , Cincinnati Bengals , Jacksonville Jaguars
We thought Maxx Crosby got the change of scenery he was after in March, when the Baltimore Ravens agreed to send two first-round picks to the Las Vegas Raiders for their star pass rusher. However, the Ravens backed out of the deal after their doctors allegedly found something worrisome during their in-person physical.
Crosby is one of the most aggressive and well-rounded pass rushers in the NFL. Not only does he get after quarterbacks, having recorded four double-digit sack seasons, including in 2025, but he plays a high percentage of defensive snaps each year and is effective against the run as well. No player has recorded more tackles for loss (135) since Crosby was drafted in the fourth round of the 2019 NFL Draft.
I don't know if Crosby still wants out of Vegas. Maybe he viewed the canceled trade as divine intervention signaling he was always meant to don the silver and black. The Raiders are more competitive this year than they have been in quite some time, but I would still like to see Crosby on a winning team.
Where could he fit? Chicago Bears, Detroit Lions
author: Jordan Dajani

title: Former NFL security committee member details how league operates amid civil unrest in Paris before Week 7 game
summary: Amy Trask, the former CEO of the Oakland Raiders, served on the NFL's security committee
full_text:
The NFL will expand its international footprint on Sunday when the Pittsburgh Steelers and New Orleans Saints kick off from the Stade de France just north of Paris. This will mark the league's first ever game in France. However, the international contest does have the backdrop of ongoing civil unrest and protests occurring throughout the country sparked by the rising cost of living and poor school conditions.
Demonstrations throughout Paris and the rest of the country descended into riots as violent groups have looted shops, burned property, and battled with authorities. More than 2,800 people have been arrested, according to CBS News .
Naturally, with the NFL on Paris' doorstep, security concerns surrounding the teams, players, fans, and anyone else involved in the events of the league have been raised.
"The league takes extremely seriously security matters irrespective of the location of the game and irrespective of whether it is a game or ancillary activities surrounding a game," Amy Trask, former CEO of the Oakland Raiders , former member of the NFL's Security Committee and current CBS Sports analyst, said in a one-on-one interview about the upcoming game in Paris. "I can tell you from experience on the league's security committee, the preparation and the planning is extensive. It is tremendous, and that, again, is the case whether this is a game internationally, in the United States or whether it's an event other than a game."
Given the unrest in the city, the outside-viewing public has questioned if the game would need to be moved out of Paris and back to the United States. Internally, however, NFL Executive VP of club business, international and league events Peter O'Reilly said Tuesday that there was never a point that the game was in danger of not being played at the Stade de France. That said, the league will have heightened security in the wake of these demonstrations.
When asked about the game day security measures the league takes, Trask highlighted the several layers of security that are involved in a game within the United States, ranging from "local authorities, local law enforcement, state authorities, state law enforcement, national authorities, and national law enforcement." Those layers only increase when factoring in the international component.
"That is something that was a focus when I was on the security committee," Trask said. "You've got security on site the moment people are approaching the venue. In other words, the security is not simply at the gate when people are entering the venue. There is security well outside of the venue. There is security before you even enter the parking lot, so there will be security throughout the area. Some of the security will be noticeable, recognizable. Some of the security will be undercover, meaning simply not in uniform, not dressed in a manner where you will immediately notice it is security. It was my experience that there is ample security at the NFL events.
"... As I noted, when the games are in the United States, that's local security, municipal security, state security, national security. Now you will add to this Parisian security, French security as well."
While the matchup between Pittsburgh and New Orleans is the marquee event, there will be other satellite events to complement the game that players could be involved in as the NFL attempts to endear itself to the international audience. On top of that, there will likely be some time for the players to explore, which brings with it added security questions. The Steelers know this firsthand, as former quarterback Skylar Thompson was jumped and robbed before last season's game in Dublin, Ireland.
"Teams handle things differently," Trask noted when asked about how clubs communicate with players about how to spend time outside of the facility and possibly attending league-sponsored events or other activities. "I don't think there is one answer for every team. ... When I communicated with the team, I emphasized the importance of the fans. Yes, a team is there to play a game, but there are, as you referenced, satellite events, and you do want your players to understand the importance of the fans that are attending these satellite events that are participating.
"Now, the most important thing for the players is to be ready for the game. There are curfews, and there are rules put in place for the players by the head coach, by the organization so that their primary focus is the game or, as the gentleman from my work would say, 'Just win, baby.' That said, you do want players involved to the extent possible in satellite events."
The Steelers and Saints will kick off from Stade de France on Sunday at 9:30 a.m. ET and 2:30 p.m. local time.

title: Joe Thuney trade revisited: How Bears, Chiefs both came out as winners
summary: Chicago acquired the stabilizing force its offense desperately needed, while Kansas City turned the draft capital into a potential star
full_text:
When Ben Johnson took the Chicago Bears job two offseasons ago, all questions centered around Caleb Williams , naturally. The former Heisman Trophy winner and 2024 No. 1 overall pick had endured a brutal rookie season in a brutal offensive ecosystem. He had taken 68 sacks -- tied for third-most ever -- and his offensive coordinator got fired mid-season. His coach got fired two and a half weeks later, also midseason.
So Johnson needed stability, not only from his quarterback but for his quarterback. He and GM Ryan Poles went to work quickly and nailed one of their first moves as a duo: acquiring guard Joe Thuney from the Chiefs . Ahead of the Bears' "Thursday Night Football" showdown against the Patriots -- for whom Thuney played for five years and won two Super Bowls -- we revisit a move that helped kickstart Chicago's turnaround.
The Chiefs didn't move on from Thuney due to a decline in play. Even in his age-32 season, Thuney was producing at a high level. He was a first-team All-Pro for the second straight year and, amid injuries and underperformance along Kansas City's offensive line, even kicked out to left tackle and played serviceably. In fact, he finished 10th in Offensive Player of the Year voting.
Rather, the Chiefs were running into a financial crunch. They had franchise-tagged right guard Trey Smith . Right tackle Jawaan Taylor carried a massive cap hit. Center Creed Humphrey's extension was starting to kick in, as was defensive tackle Chris Jones '. There were high-priced veterans across the board. Thuney was due an extension -- he got two years and $35 million from Chicago two months after the trade -- and the Chiefs weren't going to be the ones to deliver it.
That's the price of success. The Chiefs had also prepared to lose someone up front. They drafted Kingsley Suamataia in the second round in 2024 and Wanya Morris in the third round in 2023, and after Thuney left, they drafted Josh Simmons in the first round in 2025.
The Bears were a natural landing spot. Johnson had worked with an excellent offensive line in Detroit and expressed it as a priority in his introductory press conference. While tackles often get the most credit and recognition along the offensive line, Johnson knew he had to fortify the interior, too. His interior lineman when he was the Lions ' offensive coordinator -- Jonah Jackson , Graham Glasgow , Frank Ragnow and Kevin Zeitler -- was arguably the NFL's best. In fact, a week before the Thuney trade, the Bears traded for Jackson, another move that bore fruit immediately.
Thuney was the headliner, but the Bears overhauling their entire offensive line was massive for making the Johnson/Williams partnership work.
2024 Bears offensive line: LT Braxton Jones , LG Teven Jenkins , C Coleman Shelton , RG Matt Pryor , RT Darnell Wright 2025 Bears offensive line: LT Theo Benedet or Ozzy Trapilo , LG Joe Thuney, C Drew Dalman , RG Jonah Jackson, RT Darnell Wright
Thuney was not only a Pro Bowler and first-team All-Pro again in 2025 (his third straight year earning both honors), but he won the inaugural Protector of the Year award. He finished first among guards in ESPN's Pass Block Win Rate and third among guards in ESPN's Run Block Win Rate. He was the face of a drastically improved unit overall.
Dalman, a free agency add, was a Pro Bowler before abruptly retiring this past offseason. Jackson solidied the right guard position, and Wright lept from promising youngster to second-team All-Pro. The Bears as a whole finished first in pass block win rate and fifth in run block win rate. Williams went from taking 68 sacks to 24. The Bears went from 5-12 with one of the league's worst offenses to 11-6 with one of the league's best offenses.
Thuney continues to play well this year, though not quite at the level he was last year, per the win rate metrics. Part of that could be the absence of Williams, who hurt his hamstring in Week 2 and missed Weeks 3, 4 and 5. Still, he has proved to be a crucial part of Chicago's sudden turnaround and remains a vital cog for a team looking to make it back-to-back postseason trips.
The Chiefs ended up sending the 2026 fourth-rounder acquired in the Thuney trade plus a 2025 third-rounder (No. 95 overall) to the Patriots for the No. 85 pick in 2025 and using that pick on cornerback Nohl Williams.
Williams is looking like a stud -- and potentially a star. Out of 78 players who have been the primary defender on at least 25 passes this year, Williams ranks ...
It doesn't get much better than that, and considering 2026 first-round pick Mansoor Delane has been similarly awesome, the Chiefs might have found their top cornerback duo for the foreseeable future already. It's the latest secondary success story for a team that continues to draft cornerback gems -- Williams, Trent McDuffie (2022 first round), Jaylen Watson (2022 seventh round), L'Jarius Sneed (2020 fourth round).
Of course the Chiefs would have loved to keep Thuney. Offensive line was a major issue last year, when Patrick Mahomes got hurt and the Chiefs missed the playoffs for the first time since 2014. But Suamataia has stepped in ably this season, and the Chiefs are 5-0 and looking like a Super Bowl contender once again. This is what good teams do: They adapt, they identify and develop talent, and they keep going.

title: Russell Wilson has one bold trade target that could make the Chiefs unstoppable
summary: Russell Wilson explains why adding Kenneth Walker has made the Chiefs even more dangerous and why Garrett Wilson could be the next piece
full_text:
The Kansas City Chiefs are the last remaining undefeated team in the AFC and one of just two undefeated teams in the league. The hosts of CBS Sports' "Set Hut" want you to put Super Bowl-level respect on their name. The Chiefs are tied with the Buffalo Bills for the second-best odds of winning it all (+750), behind the also undefeated San Francisco 49ers (+540), per DraftKings Sportsbook .
Hosts Russell Wilson and Kyle Long discussed why this year's Chiefs are different than past years and what they can add at the trade deadline to level up even further. It starts with game-changing free agent signing Kenneth Walker. Walker is the defending Super Bowl MVP and joined the Chiefs from the Seattle Seahawks this offseason. The Seahawks have 643 total rushing yards, 107.2 yards per game. Walker has them beat in total yards despite playing one fewer game, with 665 yards (113.0 per game). The running back also leads the NFL in forced missed tackles (52) and in yards (183) and touchdowns (six) against stacked boxes, meaning eight or more defenders.
Wilson calls Walker "dynamic" and says, "Every time he touches the ball, there's a chance he may score." When discussing whether the Chiefs should be a Super Bowl favorite, Wilson says Walker is a main reason why that answer is "yes."
"Walker is bringing something they've never had before, [Mahomes] never had a 1,000-yard rusher," Wilson said. "... Kenneth Walker is changing the game for Patrick Mahomes. Walker has brought toughness that I feel like they've always had, but there's a different type of toughness and just physical nature that he's bringing to the game."
But what's next for the Chiefs? The NFL trade deadline is fast approaching, and Andy Reid's offense could become even more powerful with one bold move on the minds of both Wilson and Long.
MR. UNLIMITED PLAYER OF THE WEEK: Kenneth Walker III @DangeRussWilson pic.twitter.com/GCnrDniI76
"If I'm the Chiefs, I'm gonna go get [ New York Jets ] Garrett Wilson ," Russell Wilson said. " ... Because I believe that Garrett Wilson down the field, with his ability, he's a smart guy, he learns quickly, he'd be great in an Andy Reid-style offense," the Super Bowl champion said, adding that they've "never had a receiver like him."
Garrett Wilson to Chiefs? @DangeRussWilson thinks the Chiefs should trade for Garrett Wilson pic.twitter.com/PRHRrVVLpq
As Long is saying, Garrett is a player who wants to win. Russell interrupted to declare the young receiver "deserves to win" and that winning doesn't seem to be happening with the Jets in the near future.
"[Garrett Wilson] don't waste your youth, go get that Lombardi, there's a guy waiting for you to throw the football," Long said.

title: Predicting the full 14-team NFL playoff bracket entering Week 7: NFC East produces a surprise winner
summary: With Jalen Hurts sidelined and the NFC East in disarray, fresh playoff projections reveal who claims the division and which teams make a Super Bowl run
full_text:
The NFC East has been the worst division in the NFL this year and it hasn't been close.
The division has been so bad that it actually made NFL history in Week 6. With the Commanders losing to the 49ers on Monday night, the NFC East became the first division in NFL history to have all four teams go winless in back-to-back weeks (0-6-2), and this somehow happened even though two NFC East teams played each other in Week 5.
Last week, we projected the Eagles would win the division, but that was before we learned that Jalen Hurts is expected to miss the rest of the season due to blood clots . With Hurts out, that has created a wild open race.
At this point, you might be wondering who's actually going to win the NFC East, and fortunately, we might have the answer for you here. To help us figure out who's going to win each division and who's going to make the playoffs, we had our analytics expert, Stephen Oh, simulate the rest of the 2026 season. We also have an analysis on why each NFC East team could take the division .
There are 179 games left on the regular-season schedule, along with 13 playoff games, and Oh simulated all of them. Not only did he project the 14 teams that will end up making the playoffs, but he also crowned a Super Bowl champion. And yup, he also projected who the winner of the NFC East will be, since someone has to win that division.
With that in mind, let's get to the projections. And just as a reminder, we're projecting what the NFL playoff field will look like at the end of the season. This is NOT the current playoff standings.
For the first time all season, there are no changes to the AFC playoff field. The seven teams projected to make the playoffs this week are the same seven that we had last week. The only difference is that the Patriots and Bengals have switched seeds, with New England now one spot ahead of Cincinnati after being behind them last week.
Here's the projected AFC playoff field (with each team's current record): 1. Chiefs (5-0) -- AFC West champion 2. Bills (5-1) -- AFC East champion 3. Jaguars (4-2) -- AFC South champion 4. Ravens (4-2) -- AFC North champion 5. Broncos (4-2) 6. Patriots (4-2) 7. Bengals (3-2) JUST MISSED: Steelers , Texans
When you look at the teams that didn't make the cut here, the Steelers and Texans are definitely the most notable. The Texans have won two games in a row since starting 0-4, but in the end, our computer thinks they dug themselves too deep of a hole to start the season. We have them finishing at 9-8, which would mean that Houston goes 7-4 over its final 11 games. As for the Steelers, we have them projected to finish in the AFC North at 9-8, which leaves them one game out of the postseason.
For you Browns ' fans, our projection has them finishing 8-9 and out of the playoffs.
The Giants are on top of the NFC East heading into Week 7, and surprise, surprise, our computer actually has them holding on to WIN the division. In what might go down as one of the ugliest division races of all time, our computer has the Giants finishing 8-8-1 and stealing the division from the 8-9 Cowboys . That's right, New York's Week 5 tie with the Commanders could end up deciding the division.
Here's the projected NFC playoff field (with each team's current record): 1. 49ers (6-0) -- NFC West champion 2. Vikings (5-0) -- NFC North champion 3. Panthers (3-2) -- NFC South champion 4. Giants (3-2-1) -- NFC East champion 5. Lions (3-2) 6. Seahawks (3-3) 7. Packers (4-2) JUST MISSED: Bears
The problem with being in the NFC is that there's a chance we could see two teams make the playoffs with losing records this year: the winner of the NFC East and the winner of the NFC South. That leaves just five spots for the other teams, which is how the Bears end up being the odd man out, despite finishing with a 10-7 record in our projection.
As for the Rams , our projection has finally given up on them: They have just a 24.6% chance of making the postseason. To put that in perspective, the team in the final wild card slot (Green Bay) has a 65.8% chance of getting in.
Now that we know who's in the playoffs, let's see who's going to make it to Super Bowl LXI.
And now, we're down to our final eight teams.
If you're scoring at home, we are now down to four teams: Two teams that have never won a Super Bowl (Bills and Vikings) and two teams (49ers and Chiefs) that have faced each other in two of the past seven Super Bowls.
We've been doing a projection every week since the start of the season, and here's a look at the projected Super Bowl each week.
There really has only been one consistency over the past few weeks and it's that the Chiefs are inevitable. This is the fifth straight week we've projected them to make the Super Bowl.

title: NFL Week 7 picks, odds: Vikings and Chiefs stay undefeated, while Cardinals pull off another upset
summary: Tyler Sullivan picks every game on the Week 7 schedule, including five locks against the spread
full_text:
Aaron Glenn, you just made the list.
We nearly went 4-1 with my Locks of the Week for Week 6, but we endured a tough beat in the final seconds of the Jets-Patriots matchup in Foxborough. Down 10 and just 36 seconds remaining in regulation, Glenn sent out the field goal unit to cut New England's lead to a single possession. Jason Sanders trotted out onto the field and easily netted the 36-yard field goal to make it a 26-19 deficit.
The ensuing onside kick was unsuccessful, and that brings us to our final, with the Patriots failing to cover the 7.5 spread by the hook. Ouch.
🚨BREAKING: THE NEW YORK #JETS KICKED A FIELD GOAL WHILE TRAILING BY 10 POINTS WITH JUST 30 SECONDS REMAINING. THE BETTING SPREAD WAS 7.5 POINTS, AND THE FIELD GOAL CUT THE DEFICIT TO 7. GAMBLERS WHO BET ON THE #PATRIOTS TO COVER ARE FURIOUS. WOW 😳😳😳 pic.twitter.com/Q0XhLeCGJz
As brutal a beat as that was, I get it. If you kick the field goal and you recover the onside kick, you're a Hail Mary away from tying the game. It's not the most likely of outcomes (as we saw), but it was a sliver of a chance that Glenn had to take, so it's hard to blame him. Even if it does sting on the gambling front.
That brought us to a 3-2 ATS record with my five locks for Week 6, and that was truly the lone bright spot of a slate where I went 5-9 ATS and 6-8 SU overall. I'll look to stabilize that record in Week 7, and that begins, as always, with my five locks.
Note : Buffalo, Los Angeles ( Chargers ), Washington, and Jacksonville are on the bye in Week 7.
We told you last week that the Colts were nowhere near being a 7-point favorite against anyone, including the Titans . That proved to be right on the money as they lost outright, which helped lead to the firing of GM Chris Ballard. I'm not sure if a GM getting fired has the same effect as when a coach gets fired, and you see a galvanized effort the following game. That's especially true when the Indy offense continues to look lost with Daniel Jones at the helm and is now set to face Brian Flores' top-notch Vikings defense.
This season, Minnesota leads the NFL in blitz rate at a blistering 69.8%. Jones has largely checked down against the blitz this season, with his air yards per attempt falling to 5.2 against the blitz compared to 9.5 without it. In my view, that just means even less of a threat for explosive plays on the Colts' end, which helps keep things in check. The Vikings defense, which will be well rested after being on the bye, is No. 1 in the NFL in third-down and red-zone efficiency. That's a nightmare matchup for the Colts' offense, which is averaging just 4.7 yards per play.
Meanwhile, I'm encouraged by Kyler Murray as he's coming off his best performance of the season. So far, his passer rating and yards per attempt have improved in each game this season. With the rest and home-field advantage, Minnesota should leave Indy in the dust.
Projected score : Vikings 33, Colts 19 The pick : Vikings -6.5
Yes, we put Aaron Glenn in the crosshairs in the lede, but let me give you a quick life lesson -- Don't let yesterday impact tomorrow. Sure, the Jets burned us last week, but that shouldn't mean we look at them any differently in Week 7, especially with a fantastic matchup against the winless Dolphins . New York was competitive with the Patriots last week, and they've been a team we've backed several times already in 2026.
The offense is a concern, as they have the worst red-zone efficiency (38%) in the NFL and rank 27th in points per game (18.7). However, I'm not sure how much that'll matter against a Dolphins offense tied for the fewest points in the NFL (14.0). New York is allowing just 20.3 points per game this season, which is tied for the seventh-fewest in the league. So, it might not be too heavy of a lift for Geno Smith and company to jump out in front of the Dolphins and clear the number.
Projected score : Jets 23, Dolphins 16 The pick : Jets -4.5
Tennessee notched its first win of the season last week by taking down the Colts, but I don't think this is a sign they're about to crawl out of the basement. The Titans have made incremental improvements, but they were outgained by 213 yards last week despite the win. As I wrote about in last week's picks column, taking the Titans to cover was more about Indianapolis than anything else, and that remains true, which is why we're fading them this time around.
The Browns are ... good? They pulled off an upset win over the Lamar Jackson-less Ravens last week and, remarkably, stand in first place in the AFC North heading into Week 7. Deshaun Watson has been clutch this season, as he has four game-winning drives where he's been money. In that window, Watson has completed 75% of his passes (18-of-24), thrown for 179 yards, and has two touchdowns with zero interceptions. To his credit, Cam Ward has also popped in the fourth quarter this season as well, but Tennessee is also tied for the fewest points scored in the NFL over the first three quarters. If that persists, Cleveland has a defense capable of snuffing out any late Ward comeback attempt.
Projected score : Browns 24, Titans 17 The pick : Browns -1.5
The Broncos offense is broken. More specifically, Bo Nix appears to be broken. Yeah, they beat the Seahawks last week, but they did that in spite of their quarterback play. Nix averages 5.6 yards per attempt, along with just 4.9 air yards. That air yards per attempt average is the shortest through six games in the past 20 seasons. Overall, the offense is 26th in points per game and 31st in total yards per game and yards per play. Nothing about that screams road favorite.
Arizona is coming off its second upset win of the season, slaying the Rams with a strong defensive effort. The Cardinals just held Matthew Stafford and Co. to 16 points. If that even remotely carries over, it's going to be another quiet showing for the Denver offense. Of course, there are concerns about the Cardinals offense, especially after going 0-5 in the red zone last week, but I have way more faith in that unit than what the Broncos are producing currently. I'll take the points and sprinkle on another upset.
Projected score : Cardinals 23, Broncos 20 The pick : Cardinals +4.5
There's still no word as to whether Lamar Jackson will, in fact, return for this game, but the line suggests he will. Even assuming that No. 8 will be under center for Baltimore, I like the Bengals here as they are fresh off a bye in Week 6. Joe Burrow doesn't have the best head-to-head splits against Jackson in their careers, but the Bengals QB was playing well entering the break and currently ranks second in completion percentage and seventh in passing yards per game.
I also believe this week's game will highlight Cincinnati's interior defensive line and expose a weakness for Baltimore on the interior of its offensive line. The Bengals have the second-most sacks in the NFL by defensive tackles through Week 6, while the Ravens have had a rotating door at center. This game could be one of the key examples as to why Cincinnati traded for Dexter Lawrence this offseason.
The Bengals are also 10-3 ATS in their last 13 road games after a win that Burrow starts.
