title: Who will win the NFC East: Panel of experts states case for each team
summary: The Giants currently sit atop the NFC East, but the Cowboys, Commanders and Eagles all have arguments for emerging from the NFL's most chaotic division race
full_text:
Move over NFC South, because here comes the NFC East. This division has been the most disappointing over six weeks and has just become the first division ever to feature back-to-back winless weeks with at least four games played. We even had two division rivals play each other, and they TIED.
The Philadelphia Eagles are 2-4, and unfortunately, just lost quarterback Jalen Hurts for what looks like the remainder of the season after blood clots were discovered in his lungs. The Dallas Cowboys were a hot pick to win the NFC East this year with the additions they made on defense, which included new coordinator Christian Parker. However, Dallas is also 2-4, and this defense still ranks third-worst in the NFL . The Washington Commanders were a sleeper to some. Jayden Daniels was back healthy, and he led this Commanders team to the NFC Championship game as a rookie. But Washington resides in fourth place at 1-4-1.
Then there are the New York Giants , who lead the NFC East at 3-2-1. Jaxson Dart, unfortunately, went down with a season-ending knee injury in Week 2, so in stepped Jameis Winston. However, the Giants also traded for J.J. McCarthy , who is on the verge of taking over the offense.
So, which one of these four teams is going to win the division and host a playoff game? Our panel of four writers made their case for each squad.
Odds courtesy of DraftKings Sportsbook
SportsLine's chances to win division: 27%
Yes, the Dallas Cowboys' offense has slumped in consecutive prime-time defeats the last two weeks, but that unit is just a few subtle tweaks -- more motion, more under-center looks, and more play-action passing -- away from hitting its stride. The Cowboys have by far the most talented offense in the division, featuring Dak Prescott, Javonte Williams, CeeDee Lamb, George Pickens and a young, ascending offensive line.
Sure, their defense continues to have problems, but that unit has shown some signs of relative improvement, by their low standards, the last two weeks. If Brian Schottenheimer can tighten up his scheme, there is no reason why Prescott and company can't just outscore the Philadelphia Eagles, Washington Commanders and the New York Giants.
That's why the Cowboys can still win the NFC East. Las Vegas feels the same way with DraftKings Sportsbook giving Dallas +130 odds to win the division, the best odds of the NFC East's four teams.
SportsLine's chances to win division: 31.9%
In a division as bleak as this, where every win is a luxury, holding a 1.5-game lead goes a long way. All the Giants need to do is maintain their pace, as modest as it is. That will be easier said than done as the schedule stiffens up in the weeks to come with the Texans , Jaguars , 49ers , Seahawks and Lions presenting the biggest challenges, but banking an early advantage over the rest of the division makes this team the one to beat until further notice. The "Jameis Winston Experience" was its usual roller-coaster ride and delivered a pair of wins, but J.J. McCarthy might be the quarterback with the higher upside. If John Harbaugh commits to him after benching Winston, the offense should look more like it did with Jaxson Dart under center. Cam Skattebo and the run game can return to form in a McCarthy-led system. Isaiah Likely is blossoming into a top-flight tight end, and with Malik Nabers rounding into form as he gets healthier and more confident, there are two reliable weapons who can aid McCarthy in keeping the offense afloat. It does not have to be a high-octane operation, just a decent one, to compete in a weak division.
Remember that McCarthy, for all of his flaws, went 6-4 a year ago in Minnesota. Of course, he had the benefit of playing with an elite defense during his tenure with the Vikings. It is not as if the Giants are a liability on that side of the ball, though. They are firmly in the middle of the pack in yards and points allowed and are a top-five team against the pass.
If New York can simply be a mid-tier team on both sides of the ball, that should be enough to hold onto a slim lead in such a downtrodden division.
SportsLine's chances to win division: 24.7%
OK, I like a challenge. Ignore that Dan Quinn is on the hot seat and that Jayden Daniels hasn't won an NFL game in over a year. Sure, Washington is off to its worst six-game start since 2020, but do you remember what happened in that 2020 season? The Washington Football Team rebounded to finish 7-9 and win the NFC East. Then, WFT legend Taylor Heinicke gave Tom Brady and the Bucs a game in the wild-card round.
It's easy for the casual football fan to overlook this Washington team, but don't. The Commanders beat the reigning Super Bowl champion Seahawks while forcing three turnovers. Then, they were in a position to beat the best team in the entire NFL on the road in prime time Monday night. It looked like we were in for a blowout after the 49ers went up 23-3, but this Commanders squad didn't give up, and outscored San Francisco 14-0 while outgaining Brock Purdy and company 201 yards to 7. SEVEN YARDS. The 49ers racked up a grand total of seven yards in the fourth quarter as Washington fought back.
Washington isn't going to finish No. 2 in total defense as it did in 2020, but the Commanders definitely have some pieces. Daron Payne is a former Pro Bowl defensive tackle, and there's still time for Odafe Oweh and K'Lavon Chaisson to live up to their contracts. Both made big plays Monday night! Then, there's rookie Sonny Styles , who is absolutely an ascending talent next to Frankie Luvu . Sure, there are some questions in the secondary. Let's hope Trey Amos can get back to 100% -- but the point is that the Commanders don't need an elite defense to win this stinky division.
The "Daniels magic" has to reappear -- and soon. We all saw him rack up 4,000 passing yards and 1,000 rushing yards through the playoffs as a first-year player. It's not like he has zero help either. Losing Terry McLaurin is tough, yes, but Stefon Diggs has proven he can still make plays. He was the leading receiver for a team that made the Super Bowl last year. Versatile tight end Chig Okonkwo needs more looks on offense. He led the Tennessee Titans in receiving just last year. I would make the same argument for rookie wideout Antonio Williams . He caught four passes or 64 yards and a touchdown in his NFL debut. He's capable of doing more. So is Treylon Burks . The touchdown catch he made against Denver last year is on a poster in my room.
The Eagles are already turning their attention to 2027, the Cowboys don't have a defense and their offense is worse than it was last year, and the Giants are banking on J.J. McCarthy to save them. It's going to be the Commanders standing atop the NFC East when it's all said and done. Keep your left hand up.
SportsLine's chances to win division: 16.5%
Everyone keeps pointing to the Eagles as sellers at the trade deadline, especially after this four-game losing skid and Jalen Hurts being sidelined for what is presumed to be the rest of the season due to blood clot issues. Anyone from Saquon Barkley to Dallas Goedert to Big Dom (probably) has been surmised as a possible trade chip for Howie Roseman as he sells off parts to retool for tomorrow. But when has Roseman ever done what we've expected of him? What if he zigs when everyone in the NFL expects him to zag?
Even at 2-4, the division is very much in play for Philadelphia, especially with three straight NFC East contests ahead. If they emerge from this stretch with at least a 2-1 record, that may only further embolden Roseman to buy at the deadline, which comes right after the club's Week 9 matchup against the Giants.
For all the injuries they've endured this season, the Eagles still have a secondary with top-tier talent, headlined by Cooper DeJean and Quinyon Mitchell . Meanwhile, Jalen Carter solidified the defensive line, so there are pieces for this defense to improve on the 5.4 yards per play allowed and 363.8 total yards per game allowed…

title: Prisco's Week 7 NFL picks: Patriots upset Bears, Lions edge Packers
summary: Pete Prisco reveals all of his Week 7 picks, including the Chiefs over the Seahawks in Kenneth Walker's revenge game
full_text:
What's a good Halloween costume to hide a face? I need it.
After last week's picks, I need to go into hiding. It was awful. When you can't get over .500 with the straight-up picks, you know it's a bad week.
I went 6-8 straight up and 3-11 against the spread. I could flip a coin and do better. Maybe my cats will make my picks next week.
My season records are now 54-38-1 straight up and 37-54-2 against the spread. That is vile.
Time to turn it around, so I am going to the dogs. Let them bark.
All lines via DraftKings ; All times ET
This is a big game for both teams, a tough one for the road team on a short week. Both teams can score, which should make this a fun one to watch. I think the Patriots have the better defense and that will be the difference. They overcome the road to win a much-needed game.
Pick: Patriots 28, Bears 27
These two are both coming off road victories and now have a long trip to play this one. The Steelers have been the more consistent team this year, but the Saints looked good last week against the Giants . This will be tight, but the Steelers take it.
Pick: Steelers 27, Saints 26
The 49ers are rolling as the league's best team, especially on offense. But losing Mike Evans will hurt. The Falcons couldn't stop the Bears last week, so what's to think they will slow down Brock Purdy ? They might not. But the Falcons will keep up. It's close.
Pick: 49ers 30, Falcons 28
The Browns are 4-2 after beating Baltimore last week, while the Titans beat the Colts last week. Neither team is doing much on offense, which suggests this will be a low-scoring game. I think the Browns have a better defense, which will be the difference. They win it again on a late field goal.
Pick: Browns 17, Titans 16
The Vikings are off a bye, while the Colts are off a terrible home loss to the Titans. That led to the firing of general manager Chris Ballard. Maybe that gives the Colts a bump. Beating the Vikings' defense will mean a lot of Jonathan Taylor . I think we see that as the Colts keep it close, but just miss out on the upset.
Pick: Vikings 21, Colts 18
The Dolphins are off their bye in search of their first victory, while the Jets lost to the Patriots last week. The Jets have the better team and their defense should be able to limit the Miami offense. But the Dolphins play hard and will also play well on defense. It's close.
Pick: Jets 19, Dolphins 17
The Bucs might have Baker Mayfield back for this one. That would be big. The Panthers are rolling on offense as Bryce Young is in the MVP conversation. It will stay that way, but the Bucs will hang around.
Pick: Panthers 24, Bucs 23
The Bengals are coming off a bye, while the Ravens are coming off a loss to the Browns. They could have Lamar Jackson back from an ankle injury here, which certainly changes things. Even if he's back, I think Joe Burrow will have a big day throwing it. The improved Bengals defense will do the rest. Upset.
Pick: Bengals 24, Ravens 23
Who starts at quarterback for the Giants? It should be J.J. McCarthy , but we will see. No matter who starts, the Texans ' defense is having issues. The Giants will move the ball. But they won't stop C.J. Stroud . He's on fire and that gets the Texans the victory.
Pick: Texans 27, Giants 23
The Cardinals are coming off a big road upset of the Rams , while Denver beat Seattle last Thursday. The Denver offense has been lifeless so far this season. But the defense is still sticky. I think that defense will come up big, while Bo Nix finally makes some plays. It's close.
Pick: Broncos 24, Cardinals 21
The Lions are coming off a bye, which they needed, while the Packers are coming off consecutive victories. They are playing much better on both sides of the ball. The two defenses will be challenged here, but the Lions will be the better offense at home coming off the bye. Lions win it by a tiny margin as both quarterbacks light it up.
Pick: Lions 34, Packers 33
This is a must-win for both teams, as they are on losing streaks. The Rams have a lot of injury issues, which have really impacted their team. They still have Matt Stafford. He can light up a defense, which he will do here. But the Rams will give up some big plays to the Raiders , who hang around.
This is a revenge game for Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker , who was the Super Bowl MVP for Seattle last February. And let's not forget the Chiefs have Patrick Mahomes . Seattle is good on defense, but their offense is turning the ball over. That matters here. Chiefs take it.
Pick: Chiefs 23, Seahawks 17
The Eagles are a mess with all the injuries, including quarterback Jalen Hurts being out for the year. The Cowboys have struggled on offense the past two weeks, which isn't a good look. This is desperation time for these two. The Cowboys will win it, but it's close.
Pick: Cowboys 21, Eagles 20

summary: We assumed it was coming, and today the NFL announced that Arizona Cardinals kicker Chad Ryland was named the NFC Special Teams Player of the Week for his performance against the Los Angeles Rams in the Cardinals week six victory. From the team: This is Ryland’s first career selection as Player of the Week and […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - OCTOBER 18: Chad Ryland #38 of the Arizona Cardinals leaves the field after his team's 18-16 win against the Los Angeles Rams at SoFi Stadium on October 18, 2026 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Luke Hales/Getty Images) | Getty Images We assumed it was coming, and today the NFL announced that Arizona Cardinals kicker Chad Ryland was named the NFC Special Teams Player of the Week for his performance against the Los Angeles Rams in the Cardinals week six victory. From the team: This is Ryland’s first career selection as Player of the Week and he becomes the ninth kicker in team history to be selected as the “NFC Special Teams Player of the Week.” He is the second Cardinals player to earn “NFC Special Teams Player of the Week” honors this season after Simi Fehoko was selected following the Cardinals Week 1 win at the Chargers. It is the first time since 2015 that the Cardinals have had two different players each named NFC Special Teams Player of the Week (David Johnson, Chandler Catanzaro). Ryland accounted for all 18 points in Arizona’s 18-16 victory, connecting on all six field goal attempts. His final field goal of the day was a 43-yard game-winner as time expired in regulation. Ryland’s six field goals and 18 total points are both career highs. Only once in franchise history did a player make more field goals in a game than Ryland did on Sunday (7 by Jim Bakken on 9/24/67 at Pittsburgh). His six field goals in Los Angeles are the most in a single game in the NFL this season and the 43-yarder was his fifth career game-winner. He became the first NFL player to have 6+ field goals in a game since Houston’s Ka’imi Fairbairn on 1/4/2026 (6 FG) vs. Indianapolis. Ryland is tied for 3 rd in the NFL in made FGs (14) and 4 th in the NFL in total points (54) in 2026. Congratulations to Ryland for his incredible performance.

title: Billboards are going up asking Cardinals management to sell the team
summary: The Arizona Cardinals are a member of the National Football League (NFL). There are 32 member clubs. The Cardinals are the oldest continuous NFL team, beginning in 1898. In the 128-year history of the franchise, the team has won a grand total of two titles, in 1925 and 1947. Next season will be the 80th […]
full_text: The Arizona Cardinals are a member of the National Football League (NFL). There are 32 member clubs. The Cardinals are the oldest continuous NFL team, beginning in 1898. In the 128-year history of the franchise, the team has won a grand total of two titles, in 1925 and 1947. Next season will be the 80 th anniversary of the 1947 championship season. The 1925 title wasn’t actually won by the Cardinals, but the league took the title away from the Pottsville Maroons and then gave it to the second-place club, which was the Chicago Cardinals. RELATED: THE STORY OF HOW THE BIDWILL FAMILY BECAME OWNERS Last year, the Cardinals under head coach Jonathan Gannon lost the most games in a single season with 14. The final two seasons netted 26 losses, and Gannon was sent packing. In the franchise’s history, the team has played in three league championship games, winning one. They have competed in 18 playoff games. The NFL did not begin a postseason system until 1933, which means Arizona will average playing in a playoff game every 5.1 seasons. After moving to Phoenix from St. Louis in 1988, the club has found limited success, winning three division titles, playing in 12 playoff games, and losing to the Pittsburgh Steelers in Super Bowl XLIII after the 2008 season. Since the 2016 season, the Cardinals have played in just a single playoff encounter, a 34-11 loss to the Los Angeles Rams after going 11-6-0 in 2021. Since 2016 (with divisional finish): 2016: 7-8-1 (2 nd ) 2017: 8-8-0 (3 rd ) 2018: 3-13-0 (4 th ) 2019: 5-10-1 (4 th ) 2020: 8-8-0 (3 rd ) 2021: 11-6-0 (2 nd ) 2022: 4-13-0 (4 th ) 2023: 4-13-0 (4 th ) 2024: 8-9-0 (3 rd ) 2025: 3-14-0 (4 th ) Longtime fans still remember the 1974 and 1975 seasons under head coach Don Coryell, in which the franchise won back-to-back division crowns, but lost in their first playoff games. In 1976, the team went a respectable 10-4-0 but didn’t make the playoffs, and then in Coryell’s final season, finished 7-7-0. Or the magical Super Bowl year with QB Kurt Warner, when the team held the late lead only to have it snatched away. The following year, both under head coach Ken Whisenhunt, the franchise won their division but fell hard in the playoffs 45-14. The NFC Championship Game loss to the Carolina Panthers in 2015. Fans have vivid memories of these exceptional Cardinals teams. But here’s the rub: all of that was so long ago. What about now? Here it is 2026, and the roster is still devoid of an accomplished quarterback, with defensive struggles, and high-round draft picks that have fizzled out and traded away for almost nothing. What about now? Most points to the ownership group, which consists of five Bidwill family members. Michael Bidwill, is listed on the team’s website as the owner. Michael represents the fourth generation of the Bidwill family as sole owners of the club. It began in 1932 when Charlie “Blue Shirt” Bidwill bought the Cardinals while on a yacht he owned, and had guests on board for a classy dinner. One of the guests was Dr. David Jones, who owned the Cardinals and was complaining about the team and the everyday toil. Charlie, on the suggestion of his wife Violet, agreed to purchase the Cardinals. When Charlie passed away in the spring of 1947, his wife inherited the team and became the first woman to own a professional football team. Since then, the team has been owned by Charles Bidwill, Jr. and his brother Bill, then Bill Bidwill as the primary owner, then Bill and Michael Bidwill, and now Michael as principal owner. Bill Bidwill had five children: Michael, Bill, Jr., Tim, Patrick, and Nicole. While Michael is listed as the principal owner, he shares the ownership group lineage with his siblings, representing the third generation of the Bidwill family running the franchise. No other Bidwill family member is on staff with the Cardinals. Not happy There is a contingent of the Cardinals fanbase that is just sick of losing seasons. They believe that the team doesn’t spend on high-priced free agents during the free agency period, which could come in and make a difference right away. Every year, the franchise gets a bump in its evaluation on the Forbes list. In 2024, the team was valued at $4.8 billion; the following year, that jumped to $5.5 billion. What happened to make such a jump? A Super Bowl appearance? Best quarterback in the league? The club signed the league’s best head coach? Nope. Nothing. The franchise vaulted in value just for existing. And in 2025, the Cardinals made $571 million. So, the owners of the team got $700 million extra in value, plus took home $571 million in profit. All in one swoosh. The Cardinals fanbase is asking why the front office isn’t using some of that cash on big-name players. Go after them, and pay them handsomely. Show them the advantages of not playing in a cold city, and every game is inside a climate-controlled dome. Keep in mind, the Cardinals are just one of many ventures that Michael has found success in. His portfolio, identified as “Bidwill Family Holdings,” extends to luxury real estate developments, premium hospitality ventures, and hospitality-focused private equity funds. Petitions have circulated asking any disgruntled Cardinals fan to sign. These petitions aren’t for better restroom facilities at the stadium, or to lower their ticket prices, or asking about why the beer costs so much on game day. Nope. These petitions are asking for the Bidwill family to sell the team. Get totally out of the football business. And now, another group began a GoFundMe and spent the money on billboards, asking the same questions and pleading for a new ownership group. On social media, the hashtag #BIDWILLOUT has grown with a simple statement: Sell the team. A total of $7,000 was raised in just two days for a series of digital billboards. The message: MICHAEL, PLEASE SELL THE TEAM. Signed, the Fans. One billboard is in Surprise, another in Mesa, while the other is near Tempe Marketplace. Another is planned for downtown Phoenix. The reality The NFL is comprised of 32 member franchises. Each is wholly owned by people and corporations. Two things: The NFL is not going to ever oust an ownership group as long as it hasn’t done anything illegal, and #2: there isn’t a number two. The Bidwill family can keep their franchise for as long as they want. They are already in their fourth generation of owners. And their team increases in value every single year, regardless of, well, anything. Just for existing. Just look at the franchise’s value for the last five years: 2022: $3.2 billion 2023: $3.8 billion 2024: $4.3 billion 2025: $5.5 billion 2026: $8.6 billion Just look at the franchise’s earnings for the last five years: 2021: $467 million 2022: $467 million 2023: $546 million 2024: $560 million 2025: $571 million Keep in mind, a great percentage of these earnings come from the collective of the NFL. For every Cardinals jacket you buy, it is split 32 ways. So, when someone purchases a New York Football Giants cap, Arizona gets 1/32 of the profit. The same goes for the current TV packages. Each team makes over $400 million annually, regardless of whether anyone shows up for home games or not. Then there are other national sponsors such as Oakley, Ford Motor Company, Verizon, Ticketmaster, Pepsi, Toyota, Bank of America, Coca-Cola, Bud Light, and AT&T. With each of these corporate sponsors, the Cardinals are paid an equal share of the profits. Do not for one second think that a fan boycott will solve this. The team will still rake in millions. Look at the pandemic year. Fans weren’t allowed to attend NFL games. How many NFL teams folded? I have never been more proud of the Arizona Cardinals fans! Cardinals Fans United is the most powerful force in the NFL! Do not stop keep it up! Love you guys! #MontiOut #BidwillOut #RallisOut #selltheteam — Justin Sane (@JustinS54965881) October 16, 2026 This year, Arizona is averaging 62, 079 per home game. Last year, it was 63,524. Pretty much, fans are…

Cox/Getty Images) | Getty Images Offense LT Jake Matthews: 55 LG Matthew Bergeron: 55 C Ryan Neuzil: 55 RG Chris Lindstrom: 55 RT Jawaan Taylor: 55 QB Michael Penix Jr.: 55 WR Drake London: 55 WR Jahan Dotson: 47 RB Bijan Robinson: 43 TE Kyle Pitts: 43 WR Olamide Zaccheaus: 30 WR Zachariah Branch: 19 TE Charlie Woerner: 16 RB Brian Robinson Jr.: 10 TE Austin Hooper: 7 TE Nick Muse: 3 WR Chris Blair: 2 Here’s a sobering stat for a player I like quite a bit: Zaccheaus has just 4 receptions on 11 targets for 17 yards, versus 9 receptions on 10 targets for 55 yards for Branch. OZ can be a sparkplug, but hasn’t been yet this season, and yet is handily outsnapping a player (144 snaps to 89) who is a more dangerous receiving threat in Branch. His starting spot may very well be in jeopardy when A.J. Terrell and C.J. Henderson are back, but Jeff Ulbrich appears to be fond of Hughes and may give him a longer leash. Kevin Stefanski on Mike Hughes: pic.twitter.com/88Iu4b0JEi — Daniel Flick (@ByDanielFlick) October 19, 2026 This was a day where the team’s preferred run defenders played a heavy role, with Kendal Daniels getting a ton of snaps before his scary injury, Sydney Brown getting extended run, and big snaps for London. It worked in the sense that the Falcons allowed under 100 rushing yards to the most productive rushing attack in the NFL, but Caleb Williams killed them through the air, so… Special teams DeMarcco Hellams: 27 Mike Ford: 27 Josh Woods: 27 Jammie Robinson: 25 Harold Perkins Jr.: 21 Nick Muse: 20 Sydney Brown: 15 Chris Blair: 12 Olamide Zaccheaus: 10 Kendal Daniels: 9 Maason Smith: 8 Gervon Dexter: 8 LaCale London: 8 Robert Longerbeam: 7 Liam McCullough: 7 Zachariah Branch: 6 Billy Bowman Jr.: 6 Xavier Watts: 6 Mike Hughes: 6 Austin Hooper: 5 Nick Folk: 5 Divine Deablo: 2 Mike Jerrell: 1 Matthew Bergeron: 1 Kyle Hinton: 1 Cameron Thomas: 1 Ryan Neuzil: 1 Corey Levin: 1 Jake Matthews: 1 I’ve been hard on Mike Ford, so credit where it’s due: Aside from a ticky-tack penalty for going out of bounds with some help from Chicago, he did nice work on special teams Sunday. Perhaps they’re rounding into form. What was less great? The return game, where Zachariah Branch fumbled twice and the team’s returners continued to make baffling decisions with the ball. Is it worth fielding a kick inside the 10 when it might bounce into the end zone if you’re only going to pick up 15-20 yards, as Brian Robinson and Olamide Zaccheaus did? Should you bother fielding punts at all if you’re feeling uncertain and muff them (Branch) or simply lose a yard (Zaccheaus)? The Falcons’ offense has its own suite of problems, but having the league’s second-worst average starting field position is making their life much harder.

UPDATE: Monday, 4:13 p.m. ET Kevin Stefanski spoke to the media on Monday and shared an update about Daniels’ condition, saying it was “all positive news” and that Daniels was in the building with the team. “Feel very, very fortunate that he got the treatment he got and we feel really good about where he is,” Stefanski said, per ESPN’s Mark Raimondi. Stefanski: All positive news on Kendal Daniels. He's here back in the building today. … Feel very, very fortunate that he got the treatment he got and we feel really good about where he is. #Falcons — Marc Raimondi (@marcraimondi) October 19, 2026 UPDATE: 6:06 p.m ET Kendal Daniels has apparently been released from Grady Memorial Hospital and returned to the Falcons’ locker room postgame. According to Will McFadden of AtlantaFalcons.com, Daniels was walking on his own, which is a relief considering how dangerous the injury looked. While we were wrapping up with Bijan Robinson in the locker room after the game, rookie linebacker Kendal Daniels came in with a couple of trainers. He was walking on his own, which is obviously a good sign after the scary scene today. — Will McFadden (@willmcfadden) October 18, 2026 UPDATE: 3:53 p.m. ET The Falcons released a statement on Daniels. Atlanta Falcons linebacker Kendal Daniels is alert and has movement in all his extremities. He was taken to Grady Memorial Hospital for further evaluation. Falcons linebacker Kendal Daniels was carted off the field in the third quarter of the Falcons’ Week 6 matchup against the Bears. The top of his head collided with another player during a tackle on Bears TE Colston Loveland, and he immediately reacted like he was in intense pain. Daniels’ injury comes after fellow linebacker Divine Deablo left the game with an arm injury. Deablo has been ruled out for the remainder of the matchup. Losing both of these players is a blow for sure, but I have to think it’s especially to focus after seeing a player who’s been so central to what this defense does well go down with such a scary injury. Prior to leaving the field, Daniels was secured to a backboard. Prior to the medical staff getting involved, right after the hit, Daniels did appear to be moving his arms and hands, so hopefully that’s a good sign. Daniels has been a fantastic fit for Jeff Ulbrich’s defense, and he’s very quickly developed as a leader on the field. When Deablo went down with the arm injury, it was the rookie Daniels who took over the green dot. Josh Woods swapped out his helmet while the medical team was attending to Daniels to take over the green dot, according to The Athletic’s Josh Kendall . The Falcons defense has been hit hard with injuries of late. In addition to Daniels and Deablo, cornerback AJ Terrell is on injured reserve, and his counterpart CJ Henderson is out Sunday with a groin injury. We will update this post as more information becomes available, and we’re wishing Daniels all the best.

title: Week 6, 3 Up and 3 Down: standout performances on both sides of the spectrum
summary: The Atlanta Falcons fell behind early to the Chicago Bears and couldn’t recover. A late push created highlights for some, but a few obvious lowlights put them in the hole to begin with. Here’s the Week 6, 3 up and 3 down. 3 up Kyle Pitts The tight end led the Falcons 4th-quarter resurgence with […]
full_text: ATLANTA, GEORGIA - OCTOBER 11: Kyle Pitts Sr. #8 of the Atlanta Falcons celebrates after a receiving touchdown against the Baltimore Ravens in the second quarter of a game at Mercedes-Benz Stadium on October 11, 2026 in Atlanta, Georgia. (Photo by Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Atlanta Falcons fell behind early to the Chicago Bears and couldn’t recover. A late push created highlights for some, but a few obvious lowlights put them in the hole to begin with. Here’s the Week 6, 3 up and 3 down. 3 up Kyle Pitts The tight end led the Falcons 4th-quarter resurgence with some fantastic individual efforts. For years, fans have complained about Pitts’ engagement, but this season he’s definitely played hard every snap regardless of the score. His YAC ability has flashed on limited touches, and he’s one of the team’s best answers for dealing with pressure. Unfortunately, he just isn’t getting the looks, and he’s gotten opportunities only during mop-up duty. Pitts has earned the chance to be a priority; Tommy Rees and Michael Penix Jr. have to make it happen. Just an absurd individual effort from Pitts here. Bails out Penix's bad decision. Elijah Hicks read this all the way and was waiting for that out breaking route, times it perfectly and Kyle just muscles the ball out of the DBs hands. Bears sideline couldn't believe it. pic.twitter.com/CcnK6zXQP0 — Tre’Shon (@tre3shon) October 19, 2026 Jessie Bates III Bates cracks the list two weeks in a row after forcing a fumble that helped turn the tide late in the game. A few weeks ago, Bates was in the down column due to him overextending himself too often, but he’s tightened up since then, and the play-making opportunities are coming his way. Bates had a couple of nice run fits in the box and prevented anything from going over the top. Credit to Caleb Williams for executing the death-by-1000-paper-cuts strategy, but Bates did his job on Sunday. Jared Ivey Ivey played under 20 snaps, but he made the most of them. He finished as PFF’s highest-graded Falcons defender , and the film backs up that grade. He made multiple stops at and behind the line of scrimmage against the run and pressured Williams a handful of times. He can play from 3-tech to wide 9, making him a versatile depth piece, and while he is a noticeably stiff player, his hustle is undeniable. This game tied for his 2nd-greatest number of snaps for the season, and I wouldn’t be surprised to see a slight increase against the San Francisco 49ers. 3 down Olamide Zaccheaus The WR had a brutal outing and was a constant negative for the Falcons offense. He’s been unreliable as a blocker and hasn’t given anyone a reason to trust him as a receiver. Among WRs who’ve run at least 50 routes in 2026, Zaccheaus has the second-worst Total EPA (-0.92) and EPA/Target (-0.08) per SumerSports . He dropped a 3rd-down conversion on the game’s second drive and was later immediately accused by Michael Penix Jr. of giving up on his route. OZ was never cut out to be a WR3 this season, and it’s time to shrink his snaps. 2nd drive of the game. 2nd down: If you want to establish a screen game get WRs who can block in. OZ gets blown up at the LOS and this thing is dead immediately. 3rd down: sure lets reward the guy who just killed us on 2nd. Penix makes the correct read, low ball right at the… pic.twitter.com/aCwn7fMdfd — Tre’Shon (@tre3shon) October 19, 2026 Zachariah Branch This performance hurt, mainly because it had nothing to do with his WR ability; he was positive in his very limited snaps. However, Branch has been inconsistent as a returner this year, and his two turnovers Sunday cost the Falcons big time. The muff on punt team was partly due to a technique known as the “ Banana Ball ,” but the main issue is that he’s trying to field a punt inside the 10. OZ did the same thing when he was put in later, and that’s a massive red flag for this coaching staff. That said, you can’t turn the ball over. It was good to see the vets rally around Branch, but a break from return duties and more WR work might help. Pass Protection No one person or unit is responsible for the Falcons protection woes; they’re failing as a family. Penix has to get better at diagnosing the blitz pre-and-post-snap and work through his progression. Tommy Rees has to actually give Penix something to progress through. There’s a lack of answers in the short game, and some of these route concepts take too much time. The offensive line has to get better at passing off stunts from center to guard and from guard to tackle. They also need to be on the same page when navigating the blitz, especially Bijan Robinson, who struggled a lot with DBs this weekend. This will be the biggest issue for the offense until they prove they’ve learned from their mistakes. https://t.co/mkMHPrjqv9 pic.twitter.com/ezTMPpJYwT — Tre’Shon (@tre3shon) October 19, 2026 Not the result fans or the team wanted, but the sky isn’t falling. You can’t turn the ball over on special teams; if those plays go the other way, we’re looking at a very different game. Pass protection is the biggest area of improvement, and Rees better figure it out because the 49ers defense is humming.

title: Ravens QB Lamar Jackson returns to practice
summary: The Baltimore Ravens are dealing with a laundry list of injuries entering Week 7, but Wednesday’s injury report included positive updates on several key players. Chief among them was quarterback Lamar Jackson’s return to practice after a two-week absence due to an ankle injury. Head coach Jesse Minter twice used the word “preparation” when referring […]
full_text: ATLANTA, GEORGIA - OCTOBER 11: Lamar Jackson #8 of the Baltimore Ravens looks on from the sidelines during the first quarter against the Atlanta Falcons at Mercedes-Benz Stadium on October 11, 2026 in Atlanta, Georgia. (Photo by Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Baltimore Ravens are dealing with a laundry list of injuries entering Week 7, but Wednesday’s injury report included positive updates on several key players. Chief among them was quarterback Lamar Jackson’s return to practice after a two-week absence due to an ankle injury. Head coach Jesse Minter twice used the word “preparation” when referring to Jackson’s participation, which was officially categorized as limited, and the two-time MVP was not in uniform when leaving the field. Taken together, those signs suggest that he is preparing to play but is not physically ready. Minter maintained his previous stance that the team was taking Jackson’s injury “day by day.” Jackson’s preparation could have included taking snaps from Cam Jurgens as the two work to develop their chemistry and communication at the line of scrimmage. Wednesday was their first shared practice since the former Eagles center arrived in Baltimore via trade two weeks ago, as well as his first day of full participation with his new team. Jurgens spoke to reporters after practice, an excellent sign towards his availability for his Ravens debut on Sunday against the Bengals. The Ravens listed 13 other players on their first injury report of Week 7. Here is the full list ( * denotes new injury): Full participation TE Mark Andrews (full) OLB Trey Hendrickson (finger) C Cam Jurgens (concussion) Limited participation WR Rashod Bateman (shoulder) S Jaylinn Hawkins (knee) * TE Matthew Hibner (hand) G/C Vega Ioane (ankle) * LG John Simpson (groin) LT Ronnie Stanley (non-injury related/rest, toe, ankle) CB T.J. Tampa Jr. (knee, designated to return from injured reserve) RG Andrew Vorhees (foot) DT Broderick Washington (ankle) Did not participate DL Calais Campbell (non-injury related/rest) OLB Tavius Robinson (pectoral) Robinson’s injury is by far the most alarming. He leads the defense with 3.5 sacks and has been a crucial run-stopper off the edge. An absence would elevate undrafted rookie Ethan Burke into a larger role; he had two pressures in three pass-rushing snaps on Sunday in Cleveland. The Bengals are coming into their trip to Baltimore much healthier after their bye week. Cincinnati reported just one injury on Wednesday: safety Kyle Dugger, who was limited with a quad injury. He appeared in the team’s first three games before going down with 41 snaps on defense and 49 on special teams.
author: Nikhil Mehta

title: Ravens Week 7 film review: rookie WR Ja’Kobi Lane makes strong return
summary: The Ravens’ disappointing 13-10 loss to the Browns in Cleveland still featured some strong performances from individual players. Despite the offensive struggles, we saw two rookies step up and contribute in the passing game, while Kyle Hamilton set the physical tone for what was arguably the defense’s best performance of the season. Ja’Kobi Lane returned […]
full_text: CLEVELAND, OHIO - OCTOBER 18: Ja'kobi Lane #6 of the Baltimore Ravens plays against the Cleveland Browns at Huntington Bank Field on October 18, 2026 in Cleveland, Ohio. (Photo by Gregory Shamus/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Ravens’ disappointing 13-10 loss to the Browns in Cleveland still featured some strong performances from individual players. Despite the offensive struggles, we saw two rookies step up and contribute in the passing game, while Kyle Hamilton set the physical tone for what was arguably the defense’s best performance of the season. Ja’Kobi Lane returned from injury and provided Tyler Huntley with a reliable, quarterback-friendly target, Josh Cuevas flashed his ability to create yards after the catch, and Hamilton reminded everyone why he is one of the most versatile defensive players in football. WR Ja’Kobi Lane 31 snaps | 22 receiving | 9 run blocking | 1.82 yards per route run Third-round rookie Ja’Kobi Lane missed the last several weeks after suffering a wrist injury in Week 1 against the Colts, but his return against Cleveland gave Baltimore an immediate boost in the passing game. Lane finished with 4 receptions for 40 yards on 5 targets, tying Josh Cuevas for the second-most targets on the team. More importantly, his performance gave us a glimpse of how his physicality, catch radius, and ability to work back toward the quarterback can translate to the NFL level. One of my biggest concerns with Lane coming out of USC was how he would handle press coverage and physicality at the line of scrimmage. Against Cleveland, we started to get an encouraging answer. Lane aligned on the boundary for 20 of his 22 receiving snaps and faced several press looks throughout the game. On one rep, he did an excellent job using his frame to create separation, initiating contact with the defensive back before working back toward the football. His physicality was also evident over the middle, where he secured several tough catches despite defensive backs and linebackers punching at the ball and delivering contact at the catch point. Ravens WR Ja’Kobi Lane | 4 catches | 40 yards | 1.82 YPRR Lane made some tough catches into traffic this week, unphased by nearby defenders. Also showed great physicality through his routes, using his large frame to create separation by pushing off on one. pic.twitter.com/cQebyURg1L — Yuri (@Yuri_Ravens) October 19, 2026 What stood out most was how quarterback-friendly Lane made himself throughout the game. He consistently maintained his positioning and worked back toward Huntley when plays broke down, providing a reliable outlet during scramble situations. That ability should translate particularly well once Lamar Jackson returns, considering how much of Baltimore’s passing offense can be generated through his ability to extend plays. My initial comparison for Lane coming out of the draft was former Ravens tight end Isaiah Likely, largely because of his ability to make himself available and create opportunities outside of structure. We could start seeing Lane develop into a similar off-script weapon while also providing Baltimore with a physical possession receiver who can consistently work the middle of the field. S Kyle Hamilton 63 snaps | 24 run defense | 4 pass rush | 35 coverage | 6 stops Kyle Hamilton led the charge in what was arguably Baltimore’s best defensive performance of the season, setting the tone with his physicality against the run and his ability to diagnose plays near the line of scrimmage. Hamilton finished with 7 tackles and 3 tackles for loss, consistently disrupting Cleveland’s rushing attack and screen concepts. His usage this season has been heavily concentrated around the box, and against the Browns, we saw exactly why Jesse Minter continues to deploy him in that role. Hamilton’s ability to diagnose plays and attack downhill was on full display throughout the game. On one rep, he immediately recognized a screen, worked through a blocker, and secured a tackle for a negative gain. On another, he attacked off the edge and penetrated into the backfield to bring down the ball carrier. What made his performance particularly impressive was how consistently he combined his instincts with physicality. Hamilton also delivered a massive shoulder-led hit on a Browns running back in space, setting the standard for what became an extremely physical afternoon for Baltimore’s defense. Ravens S Kyle Hamilton 7 tackles 6 stops Absolute enforcer in the box. Click to close. 3 receptions for 7 yards in coverage pic.twitter.com/Bkrki0by6Y — Yuri (@Yuri_Ravens) October 21, 2026 Hamilton’s versatility continues to be one of the most valuable components of this defense. His ability to function as a box defender, attack the line of scrimmage, and disrupt underneath passing concepts gives Minter flexibility in how he structures his defensive looks. Against offenses that rely heavily on screens, quick passes, and manufactured touches, Hamilton’s ability to recognize concepts and close downhill becomes even more valuable. Baltimore will need that same level of physicality and consistency from him down the stretch, particularly as the defense looks to build on its strongest performance of the season. TE Josh Cuevas 23 snaps | 14 receiving | 9 run blocking | 4 receptions | 44 yards | 1 touchdown With rookie tight end Matthew Hibner sidelined by a hand injury, Josh Cuevas received an opportunity to take on a larger role in Baltimore’s offense and made the most of his limited workload. Cuevas finished with 4 receptions for 44 yards and a touchdown, providing one of the few bright spots in an otherwise disappointing offensive performance. His ability to find space underneath, create yards after the catch, and align in multiple positions stood out against Cleveland. One of the more interesting aspects of Cuevas’ performance was how offensive coordinator Declan Doyle utilized his positional versatility. On his touchdown reception, Cuevas aligned in the backfield as a fullback before releasing into open space for Baltimore’s first and only touchdown of the afternoon. Cuevas has consistently shown a natural feel for finding openings in coverage and settling into areas where the quarterback can deliver the football. On another rep, he aligned near the left guard before releasing into a route and turning the reception into a substantial gain, flashing the straight-line speed and yards-after-catch ability that made him an intriguing developmental prospect coming out of college. Ravens rookie TE Josh Cuevas Yac monster, finds soft spots in zone and can line up anywhere pic.twitter.com/0iYwiUijyZ — Yuri (@Yuri_Ravens) October 21, 2026 Cuevas’ ability to contribute from multiple alignments gives Baltimore another element of flexibility at the tight end position. With Mark Andrews struggling to consistently produce and injuries beginning to affect the depth of the room, Cuevas could find himself with an increasingly important role down the stretch. His ability to operate as a receiving option from the backfield, create separation underneath, and generate additional yardage after the catch makes him an interesting weapon for Doyle to incorporate into the offense. As Baltimore looks to generate more consistency in the passing game, Cuevas has an opportunity to establish himself as a legitimate contributor rather than simply a developmental depth piece.
author: Yuri

title: Ravens discussion: silver linings coming out of loss to Browns
summary: The Baltimore Ravens are 4-2 after their loss to the Cleveland Browns with a tough slate of opponents on the docket. Before we turn the page on Sunday’s game, let’s grab a few positives out of the defeat to take into Week 7. Nikhil Mehta Kyle Hamilton has been the Ravens’ primary nickel defender this […]
full_text: Oct 18, 2026; Cleveland, Ohio, USA; Baltimore Ravens tight end Josh Cuevas (85) celebrates after a touchdown in the first quarter against the Cleveland Browns at Huntington Bank Field. Mandatory Credit: Scott Galvin-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Baltimore Ravens are 4-2 after their loss to the Cleveland Browns with a tough slate of opponents on the docket. Before we turn the page on Sunday’s game, let’s grab a few positives out of the defeat to take into Week 7. Nikhil Mehta Kyle Hamilton has been the Ravens’ primary nickel defender this year, but between his versatile deployment and Jesse Minter’s use of dime personnel, the team still needs a reliable slot corner. Second-year UDFA Keyon Martin won the job out of training camp, but was benched after an up-and-down Week 1 showing. Fifth-round rookie Chandler Rivers’ performance was even more of a rollercoaster, leading to Martin’s return in Week 6. He practically shut down one Browns drive on his own with a PBU and a sack, and he did not deserve the pass interference flag that set up Cleveland’s game-tying touchdown in the fourth quarter. Martin also downed a Ryan Eckley punt at the one-yard line. Dustin Cox The silver lining for me coming out of the Ravens’ loss to the Browns was the pass rush. Seeing Trey Hendrickson and Nnamdi Madubuike playing at a high level on the field together was an encouraging sign of what the pass rush can look like going forward. Getting Mike Green going at the same time as Hendrickson is the dilemma now, as both appear to be most effective rushing from the right side of the defense. Hendrickson and Madubuike are the two highly-paid stars up front, though, and they certainly played like it on Sunday with 11 pressures. Zach Canter My biggest silver linings was how well the defense played, only allowing 13 total points with five sacks and 10 quarterback hits, and the return of Ja’Kobi Lane. The defense only allowed one touchdown all day, which was practically gift wrapped to the Browns. A Derrick Henry fumble gave them possession at the Ravens 35 and then an excellent Keyon Martin 3rd down stop was inexplicably called a pass interference, giving the Browns the ball inside the 10 with a fresh set of downs. They were nails all game, until the final drive where a great play call from Cleveland’s head coach Todd Monken against Minter’s Tampa 2 put them in field goal range. While it sucks they gave up the final points, only allowing 13 is an excellent performance in today’s NFL. Ja’Kobi Lane was another bright spot, finishing with 4 catches for 40 yards. The offseason hype machine was put on hold after an early Week 1 injury put Lane on IR for four weeks. But he came back and immediately showed himself as a quarterback friendly target with the hands that made him special. Hopefully we’ll get to see some highlight reel plays downfield thrown from Lamar Jackson soon. Frank Platko A silver lining from the Ravens’ defeat in Week 6 was the performance of rookie pass-catchers Ja’Kobi Lane and Josh Cuevas. Lane was essentially making his season debut again having only played the first half of Week 1 and made an immediate impact. He made four catches for first down conversions and looked comfortable over the middle of the field as a space-eater. Lane should be a fixture in the passing game from here on out. Cuevas took on an elevated role with Matthew Hibner sidelined and had a season-best performance. He caught four passes for 44 yards, with a long 29-yard snag and fourth-down touchdown as well. With Mark Andrews on a declining trajectory and Durham Smythe out for the year, the Ravens will need their young tight ends to quickly acclimate into big roles. Cuevas showed a lot of promise against the Browns as a receiving threat moving forward.
author: Frank Platko

Backup Tyler Huntley managed to steal an overtime win in Atlanta in his first start, but he could not move the ball against the Browns last Sunday. A 1-1 record in two games without one of the most impactful players in the entire sport is not a bad outcome, especially if the rest allows Jackson to be closer to full-strength for the Ravens’ tough stretch of upcoming opponents. Next up are the Bengals, who enter the week as 2.5-point underdogs for their trip to Baltimore ( via FanDuel Sportsbook ). Cincinnati has their usual explosive, pass-heavy with a middling defense outside of one of the league’s best pass rushes. These matchups often turn into shootouts, which will not be sustainable with Huntley under center. Jackson opens up the playbook and helps the run game by forcing defenses to respect his arm and contain his legs. Jackson’s status on the Ravens’ first injury report of Week 7 could swing this line later on Wednesday afternoon. Injury updates on other key players, including trade acquisition Cam Jurgens, may not move the market, but they will still be plenty relevant on Sunday. In his Ravens debut, Jurgens will face the Bengals’ strong defensive tackle duo of Dexter Lawrence and Jonathan Allen, provided he can clear concussion protocol in time to play. If Jackson misses another game, Ravens head coach Jesse Minter will have his toughest test yet slowing down Joe Burrow, Ja’Marr Chase, and Tee Higgins, who have tortured Baltimore in the past and will be looking for revenge for last year’s shutout. In the last two games, his “best at our best when the best is needed” mantra has really showed up. In Atlanta, the Ravens decisively won the game’s last four drives to come back from an eight-point deficit for the third time that night and win in overtime. In Cleveland, the offense opened the fourth quarter with a missed field goal and a fumble and squandered subsequent redemption opportunities with three-and-outs. The defense dominated for most of the game, but could not keep the Browns out of the end zone after of the fumble and gave up a 33-yard completion on third-and-five to set up the game-winning field goal. Cincinnati’s season average of 25.6 points feels like a tough target for Huntley unless Baltimore’s new-look O-line gels right away. If Jackson plays, well, he’s Lamar Jackson. title: NFL trade deadline: Buffalo Bills trade candidate – Brian Thomas Jr.
summary: Could the Buffalo Bills actually address the receiver position before the NFL trade deadline? Right now it very much feels more likely that if a trade occurs, it’ll be for a defensive player, but you never know. Today, let’s highlight Jaguars receiver Brian Thomas Jr., a young, naturally very gifted wideout who’s fallen on hard […]
full_text: Could the Buffalo Bills actually address the receiver position before the NFL trade deadline? Right now it very much feels more likely that if a trade occurs, it’ll be for a defensive player, but you never know. Today, let’s highlight Jaguars receiver Brian Thomas Jr., a young, naturally very gifted wideout who’s fallen on hard times and out of favor in Jacksonville’s passing game after a tremendous start to his professional career. This article is the second in the trade-candidate series I plan to sprinkle onto the site until the actual trade deadline until November 10, which is 20 days from now, and lands after Week 9. Past installments in this series: Derwin James Age: 24 At this stage, any and almost all of the BTJ intrigue directly stems from his rookie season in 2024, when he caught 87 passes for 1,282 yards with 10 touchdowns. That year, he had a gaudy 2.45 yards-per-route-run figure and a drop rate of just 6.5%. Last season, Thomas had a YPRR of 1.45, and his drop rate jumped to 13.5% on 90 targets. Through six games in 2026, his YPRR is a pedestrian 0.95, and his drop rate is 25.0%. 2026 snap splits Wide: 71.6% Slot : 28.4% Regarding his snaps, BTJ has appeared on 43.1% of the Jaguars offensive snaps this season. He’s fourth on the team in targets. A season ago, he was on the field for 63.4% of the offensive snaps. As a rookie, Thomas’ snap rate was 79.4%. How he’d fit with Bills At just under 6’3” and 209 pounds with 4.33 speed, Thomas boasts prototypical size and speed to serve as a vertical-threat X on the outside in the Bills offense. That spot is currently held by DJ Moore. However, even if he’s built to be the downfield burner X he demonstrated he could be in 2024, resorting to the off-the-line Z wideout — the other outside receiver — would be most sensible for Thomas if the Bills were to trade for him. Yes, Keon Coleman has appeared at Z in some instances this season and has had reasonable success there. But the Z is the role Josh Palmer has most predominantly played. It’s the wideout whose main responsibility is to take the lid of the defense to free underneath space and occasionally make a big play down the field. Thomas can absolutely do that. This move would likely (see: almost assuredly?) be subbing Thomas into Palmer’s spot on the field and the roster. Financial obligation for Bills to trade for him 2026 salary: $1.07M If the Bills trade for Thomas after Week 9, they’d be on the hook for $537k in prorated base salary. His 2027 salary is $2.79M. As a former first-round pick, he’d be eligible for the fifth-year option after that, in 2028. The time remaining on his rookie deal remains the pillar of BTJ’s trade value. He’s incredibly cheap on the books now and in coming years. Projected cost to acquire Using Syndicate32.com’s trade machine , given Thomas’ clear downward spiral in productivity, the projected cost to trade for the receiver is a late Round 2 pick in 2027. That feels ever-so-slightly high simply because Thomas is now well into his second season as a woefully ineffective receiver and he’s clearly not a big part of Jacksonville’s offensive plans. While that rookie year is a distant memory in the NFL world, it still exists, and his age and contract situation may very well support the Jaguars asking for an early Day 2 selection for the receiver. Should the Bills trade for Brian Thomas Jr.? For as much of a fan as I was of Thomas as a draft prospect, I don’t think at this date and time I could strongly advocate the Bills sending a second-round pick for him. If Coleman’s mini-emergence wasn’t ongoing, that would be a different story. I absolutely believe he’s in dire need of a change of scenery, especially considering the GM and coach who drafted him in Jacksonville are long gone. Then there’s the LSU connection. I can’t ignore that here. While Joe Brady of course didn’t coach BTJ in Baton Rouge, it wouldn’t be crazy to assume the Bills head coach still has some LSU-based connections who could provide intel on what makes Thomas tick and how to get the best out of him in a new locale. For as much as I’m always on the WR Train, I have accepted that the Bills need to trade for defensive help before anyone on offense. BUT, Thomas is a youthful, cost-controlled tantalizing talent playing what I believe is the the game’s second-most important position, a spot that directly impacts Josh Allen. If Thomas can be acquired for a third-round pick, along with a late-round throw-in, I think the Bills should seriously consider making that move. What are your thoughts on BTJ?

title: Drives that feature a sack are different for Josh Allen
summary: Normally in the NFL, a sack is a death knell for an offensive drive. Not for a Josh Allen drive. Earlier this week, this tweet circulated from Thursday Night Football Prime Vision analyst Sam Schwartzstein that showed a staggering Allen statistic: The actual rates are 72.7% and 36.4% — there was a sack nullified by […]
full_text: Normally in the NFL, a sack is a death knell for an offensive drive. Not for a Josh Allen drive. Earlier this week, this tweet circulated from Thursday Night Football Prime Vision analyst Sam Schwartzstein that showed a staggering Allen statistic: Crazy Josh Allen stat. The Bills have 12 drives that have a sack. They have a 75% Score Rate, and a 42% TD Rate. League average is 29% Score Rate and 10% TD Rate per @NextGenStats — Sam Schwartzstein (@schwartzsteins) October 19, 2026 The actual rates are 72.7% and 36.4% — there was a sack nullified by penalty on an eventual touchdown drive that Sam miscounted — but the point still remains. With the sample-size difference in mind, I wanted to determine how absurd those rates were relative to historical data. From 2001 – 2025, all drives — and there were over 27,00 of them — that featured a sack ended with a touchdown 7.6% of the time. Field goals occurred 13.5% of the time. That means any type of score for an the offense that endured a sack happened on 21.1% of those drives. Unsurprisingly, this Allen-led attack is far ahead of those averages. The next logical question in my mind centered around how Allen’s offenses have performed in this niche drive-conversion scenario overall in his career, since 2020, and when compared to the game’s other elite quarterbacks. In his full career to date, the touchdown rate on Allen drives with a sack is 12.9%. The Bills field goal rate is 19.6%. The scoring drive rate is 32.5%. That’s more than 15 percentage points above average. The only quarterbacks with had at least 100 such drives whose offenses have managed better scoring rates in their careers entering Week 7 are Lamar Jackson (33.1%) and Patrick Mahomes at 38.4%. (Brock Purdy currently sits at 35.0%. Drake Maye is at 35.3%. They’ve had 80 and 82 such drives respectively). If we start at 2020, the Allen-led touchdown rate in those scenarios increases to 14.0%. Buffalo’s field goal rate is 20.7%. That adds to a scoring rate of 34.7%. Goodness. That means, since the beginning of the 2020 campaign, the touchdown rate for Allen’s offenses on a drive that also featured a sack is just about double the NFL average. His team’s field goal rate is more than seven percentage points higher. And his offense’s scoring rate is more than 13 percentage points higher than the collective average. And he’s absolutely blowing those averages out of the water to date in the 2026 season. Yet ridiculous Allen stat. What else is new?

title: Examining Buffalo Bills 3rd down defense woes
summary: The Buffalo Bills haven’t had any difficulty whatsoever when it comes to scoring points. Which is wild, because us fans have seen them leave meat on the bone (a Cardinal WNY sin when it comes to wings). Yet at 5-1, they’ve won nailbiter after nailbiter thanks to a defense that doesn’t seem to particularly enjoy […]
full_text: The Buffalo Bills haven’t had any difficulty whatsoever when it comes to scoring points. Which is wild, because us fans have seen them leave meat on the bone (a Cardinal WNY sin when it comes to wings). Yet at 5-1, they’ve won nailbiter after nailbiter thanks to a defense that doesn’t seem to particularly enjoy sitting on the bench. It’s kind of them to allow Josh Allen to catch his breath, but would another third down stop here or there kill them? I mean, it’s bad. Real, real bad. And getting worse rather than better… Some stats to ponder I think all football fans can agree that whenever possible, it’s preferable for your favorite team to get a stop on third down. If you can believe it, there’s a good correlation between third-down stops and points allowed by NFL defenses. Therefore third down stops are a good thing as they help your team prevent points which is of course correlated with winning. Complicated math lesson aside, let’s set a baseline and then stack up some Bills numbers. The current NFL average 39.29% for allowing third down conversions. We’ll call that the perfect average (aka the “mean”) for purposes of discussion. If we treat “average” as a cluster of teams and apply my rule of four so I can skip all sorts of calculations I don’t care about doing tonight, the average line is anything below 43.371% (set by the Green Bay Packers in the 9th worst spot for the metric). OK then. That means you don’t want to allow greater than 43.37% or risk me saying you’re bad or terrible. Where do the Bills currently sit? They’re the fifth worst team in the league at 45.00%. That’s already bad, but I have worse news. They’re getting worse! Against the Houston Texans they allowed 43.75%. Against the Detroit Lions, they allowed 36.36%. Against the Los Angeles Chargers it was 40.00%, then 41.67% against the New England Patriots, then 50.00% against the Los Angeles Rams, and most recently 58.33% against the Raiders. Want even worse news? No one allows more third downs than the Dallas Cowboys, and even they only do so at a 54.67% rate. Sure I’m comparing the Bills’ worst day to Dallas average day, but it helps add perspective on just how bad it was against the Raiders. Bills fans expected growing pains, but the idea is that it leads to improvement over the course of the season and in this key metric, it just ain’t happening so far this year. Let’s check the film then! What we have is every single third down the Raiders faced against Buffalo. The official stat sheet has them going 7 of 12 to get that 58.33% conversion rate noted above. That said, the one by penalty and the one field goal are not counted in those totals. Do with that information what you will. pic.twitter.com/KHl8pskmjv — Kuebiko (@Kuebiko_Kami) October 21, 2026 I don’t have the time tonight to break down every single play in narrative format without jeopardizing my ability to do my fulltime job due to sleep deprivation so here’s my short version… There’s a little bit of hope. Remember that it’s NORMAL to give up around 40% of conversions. The 22.22% the Minnesota Vikings allow would of course be great, but we don’t need exceptional right yet as we’re setting our sights on “mediocre” first. To get to that level, Buffalo would have needed two less conversions allowed in this game. Honestly, I think they were close on a few. There are several lowlights in that short, depressing, awful film I have above that are due to a bit of confusion which created reaction lag. A little more time and understanding of the system could pay off. We also have Tre’Davious White to look forward to. If he sees the field, I do think recognition of the play could be a major advantage compared to what we see in the clips. Physical speed is great, but as we see on plays like the 3rd & 8 about a quarter of the way into the video, it’s the confusion that can kill. Even with the growing pains, there are several play in this game where small improvements give the defense a chance at a stop. If they can make those little changes, perhaps they can reverse the decline and get back to their middling ways .

title: Carolina Panthers 2027 NFL Draft Prospect Profile: Greg Johnson
summary: The 2027 NFL Draft feels like forever away, and we’re all caught up in the start of the NFL season. Regardless, it’s never too early to look ahead to the Draft. This weekly series will take a closer look at some of the prospects the Carolina Panthers could select in the 2027 iteration of the […]
full_text: SEATTLE, WA - SEPTEMBER 26: Greg Johnson #65 of the Minnesota Golden Gophers looks on during a game between the Minnesota Golden Gophers and Washington Huskies on September 26, 2026 at Husky Stadium in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Henry Rodenburg/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The 2027 NFL Draft feels like forever away, and we’re all caught up in the start of the NFL season. Regardless, it’s never too early to look ahead to the Draft. This weekly series will take a closer look at some of the prospects the Carolina Panthers could select in the 2027 iteration of the Draft. In this series, we’ll only be looking at prospects the Panthers could seriously consider. This week our profile will focus on Minnesota Golden Gophers interior offensive lineman Greg Johnson. Bio Johnson (6’6”, 325 lbs.) has been a jack-of-all-trades lineman for the Gophers since arriving on campus. He started at left guard as a true freshman before becoming the starting center during his sophomore campaign. He moved back to guard last season and even played some snaps at both tackle spots when needed. Johnson was slated to stick at guard this season, but injuries have forced him back to the center spot. His versatility and effectiveness across the line earned him an Honorable Mention All-Big Ten nod last year. Strengths/Weaknesses Johnson has elite size for an interior lineman. He’s tall and long, giving him a rather sizable reach advantage against most opponents. He’s an incredibly smart player, able to fill in admirably at all five positions on the offensive line and his tape inside and outside are both impressive. According to PFF, Johnson has allowed only one pressure this season in 202 opportunities, earning a quality 80.3 overall grade so far. Johnson’s durability is also a major positive as he has yet to miss any time in college due to injury. This is especially impressive given how often his cohorts on Minnesota’s line have succumb to various ailments. Johnson’s size, weight, and strength should profile much better than they do in the run game. He has a good run blocking grade from PFF this year (81.1), which shows some improvement in one of the areas of concern. Continuing to show this improvement will be a major boon to his draft stock. Another potential issue is his lack of a home on the offensive line making him a master-of-none type of player. Projection Greg Johnson is an incredibly versatile and effective lineman that every NFL team covets at least as a depth piece. His improvement in the run game has helped elevate him as high as the middle of the first round on most mock drafts, consistently being taken on day one of the Draft. He could immediately slot in anywhere on the interior and/or be a swing tackle off the bench. For a team like the Panthers, the fit makes sense. Robert Hunt could be a cap casualty, and current do-it-all lineman Brady Christensen can’t stay healthy. Unless they want more Toricelli Simpkins III tape, the Panthers might invest a high pick on someone like Johnson. Johnson could even slot in as the starting center if Sam Hecht doesn’t take firm control of the position as the season moves on. As Taylor Moton and Damien Lewis begin to age out of the league, Johnson will be hitting his prime and could take the mantle as leader of the offensive line. What do you think, Panthers fans? title: Discussing where the Panthers stand after the first third of the season
summary: The NFL used to have this super convenient way to break the season up. Every team played 16 games, so it was natural to break that up into four quarters, just like you would a singular game. Now, it’s 17 games played across 18 weeks. There’s literally no way to divide 17, but we can […]
full_text: The NFL used to have this super convenient way to break the season up. Every team played 16 games, so it was natural to break that up into four quarters, just like you would a singular game. Now, it’s 17 games played across 18 weeks. There’s literally no way to divide 17, but we can divide 18 weeks into three equal segments. Maybe we could even call them periods. They provide nice checkpoints to reflect on how the season’s going and what’s to come in the next segment. Through six weeks, the Carolina Panthers sit at 3-2 with a substantial 1.5 game lead in the NFC South, which looks to be its usual mediocre to bad self. The two losses came with some grave concerns for their own distinct reasons, but all three of the wins brought equal of not more reason for optimism. MY TAKE: I’ve come away from these first six weeks very happy about where the Panthers currently stand. The Bears loss made the defense look like a train wreck, but they’ve gotten back on track since then. It’s possible that it’s an okay unit that got overwhelmed by the weirdness of Week 1. The Browns loss looked like Bryce Young turned back into a pumpkin, but he bounced back with one of the best games of his career while the Browns have gone on to prove that they might be legitimately good, particularly on the defensive side of the ball. The wins over the Falcons and Eagles came against backup quarterbacks, but that doesn’t discredit them. Teams are supposed to comfortably win games against backup quarterbacks. The Panthers are two for two doing that this year. The other win came against Jared Goff and a healthy Lions offense. Bryce Young and the offense won the shootout, and they did so on Sunday Night Football, which has been a house of horrors for the Panthers in the past. The Panthers set in the drivers seat in the NFC South. Bryce Young is playing like a franchise quarterback, and a good one at that. The defense has steadied after a bad start. And a lot of key players are set to return before the season ends. I don’t see much to complain about. What say you? How would you grade the Panthers in the first third of the season? Was it better or worse than you would have predicted?

title: Chicago Bears Pass Protection Analysis on the Sacks Allowed vs Falcons
summary: In his first game back after injuring his hamstring on September 20, Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams put together one of his most efficient games, completing 30 of 36 passes for 305 yards and a touchdown. The game plan featured a quicker passing game and fewer rollouts, likely to ease pressure on his hamstring. His […]
full_text: ATLANTA, GA - OCTOBER 18: Samson Ebukam (52) of the Atlanta Falcons grabs Caleb Williams (18) of the Chicago Bears during the Sunday afternoon NFL game between the Atlanta Falcons and the Chicago Bears on October 18, 2026 at the Mercedes-Benz Stadium in Atlanta, GA. (Photo by David J. Griffin/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images In his first game back after injuring his hamstring on September 20, Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams put together one of his most efficient games, completing 30 of 36 passes for 305 yards and a touchdown. The game plan featured a quicker passing game and fewer rollouts, likely to ease pressure on his hamstring. His average air yards per attempt (3.6) was his career-low, and his average time to throw (3.02) was the fifth-lowest since working with Ben Johnson. He scrambled just once for 2 yards, and his usual elusiveness never shifted into top gear as he took four sacks. Just speculation on my part, but it seemed the Bears may have asked him to scale back the running a bit. Let’s get down to the nitty-gritty! Sack 12: 2nd Quarter: 2-9-CHI 21 (:41) (Shotgun) C.Williams sacked at CHI 12 for -9 yards (G.Dexter) Caleb takes the shotgun snap, settles, and has some quick pressure up the middle to deal with. Center Garrett Bradbury didn’t handle the defensive tackle twist well, and he’s not in position to slow Brandon Dorlus (#54). Williams shakes that sack off, but former Bear Gervon Dexter Sr. is there to clean it up. Left guard Joe Thuney had decent position on Dexter, but when Caleb moved up, Thuney lost leverage, and Dexter slipped the block. Dorlus was the catalyst to this sack, so let’s give this one to Bradbury. Sack 13: 3rd Quarter: 1-10-ATL 31 (1:40) (Shotgun) C.Williams sacked at ATL 40 for -9 yards (B.Dorlus) Dorlus missed the first one, but he got home rushing off the Bears’ right edge here. Williams was flushed backward, so when right tackle Darnell Wright thought he was pushing Dorlus past the pocket, he actually took him right to the sack. But I can’t give this one to Wright. He was doing what he thought was correct by pushing Dorlus wide. Williams feels some pressure in his face from another former Bear, LaCale London (#94), who was working on right guard Luke Newman. But I can’t give this one to Newman either. Williams has Kalif Raymond (right slot) on the quick curl because D’Andre Swift took the linebacker with him towards the sideline. It would have been a really quick pass, but Raymond was there. Williams then looks to Cole Kmet down the left sideline, and a back shoulder throw probably gets it done here, but I don’t know how often these two have practiced that, which may have caused the hesitation. Regardless, Raymond would have been an easy 5 yards on first down, so this one is on Caleb. Sack 14: 4th Quarter: 1-10-ATL 39 (14:32) C.Williams sacked at 50 for -11 yards (L.London) This play action looks like it could have had a bootleg out to the left, but instead, Caleb set up in the pocket to throw. With the entire offensive line stepping right to sell the zone run in that direction, London recognizes the pass and scrapes to get in the backfield. Center Logan Jones tried to peel back and pick up any late-leaking defenders, but London got through the line too quickly. Jared Ivey (#51) had a good angle of pursuit on Caleb, who was cocking to throw before fading back, but London came in from behind. Since he was out of the pocket, Williams could have chucked it out of bounds to avoid the loss in yards, so I got to put this one on the quarterback too. I do think that if Caleb wasn’t in his first game back from the hamstring, he would just outrun Ivey’s angle toward the sideline, but given the game situation, he was probably content to take the sack. Sack 15: 4th Quarter: 3-5-CHI 29 (4:20) (Shotgun) C.Williams sacked at CHI 23 for -6 yards (Z.Smith) This one is on Williams too. The pocket got a bit muddy, but he didn’t need to bail as quickly as he did. And just like the last sack, he could have thrown this one out of bounds. But Za’Darius Smith (#55) closed the angle and tripped him up. Here’s the individual Sackwatch tally after six games: Caleb Williams – 3.5 Sacks happen – 3 Garrett Bradbury – 3 Theo Benedet – 1.5 Jonah Jackson – 1 Colston Loveland – 1 Tyson Bagent – 1 Darnell Wright – 1 Here are the total Bears’ sacks allowed through 6 games in the Sackwatch era: 2010 – 31 Martz 2011 – 21 Martz 2012 – 25 Tice 2013 -11 Trestman 2014 – 17 Trestman 2015 – 13 Gase 2016 – 13 Loggains 2017 – 17 Loggains 2018 – 16 Nagy 2019 – 19 Nagy 2020 – 15 Nagy 2021 – 26 Nagy 2022 – 27 Getsy 2023 – 27 Getsy 2024 – 20 Waldron 2025 – 11 Johnson 2026 – 15 Johnson
