title: Patriots at Bears Q&A: The Battle of 2024 QB Supremacy
summary: The Bears have a quick turnaround this week, playing Thursday night against the New England Patriots. Both the Patriots and Bears are playing good football right now as they both sit at 4-2. The last time these two teams played was in 2024. A game where the Bears’ offense looked so inept that it ended […]
full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - NOVEMBER 10: Caleb Williams #18 of the Chicago Bears and Drake Maye #10 of the New England Patriots interact after a game at Soldier Field on November 10, 2024 in Chicago, Illinois. The Patriots defeated the Bears 19-3. (Kara Durrette/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Bears have a quick turnaround this week, playing Thursday night against the New England Patriots. Both the Patriots and Bears are playing good football right now as they both sit at 4-2. The last time these two teams played was in 2024. A game where the Bears’ offense looked so inept that it ended with the firing of Shane Waldron. The Bears are in a much different place heading into this matchup, and the Patriots are looking like an AFC playoff team following up their Super Bowl appearance in February. To get you set for this big game, we sat down with Taylor Kyles from Pat’s Pulpit (SB Nation’s New England Patriots site) to get you a better perspective of where the Patriots are at. Here’s that Q&A. 1. We know the big topic of this game is going to be the battle of 2024 first-round QBs. Caleb Williams has beaten all his first-round QB-mates except for Bo Nix (hasn’t played him) and Drake Maye after the disastrous game in 2024 that led to Shane Waldron being fired. Are there any lingering concerns about Drake Maye’s poor stretch of play, or is confidence high that he’s all the way back? Drake Maye has done a complete 180 since his ugly three-game stretch to start the season. Through that initial rough patch, Maye was putting the ball in harm’s way due to poor decision-making, and that seemed to shake his confidence and affect his fundamentals. But since turning things around in Buffalo, Maye has returned to MVP-caliber form and done an excellent job maximizing his arm talent and mobility. One of the best examples is his deep passing, where he went from a 0-4 touchdown-to-interception ratio from Weeks 1-3 to a 5-0 ratio from Weeks 4-6, the best mark in the league over that span. Between his improved sense of risk-vs-reward, ability to avoid potential negative plays, and impressive field vision, I think it’s safe to say early concerns have been put to bed. That said, Maye must prove he can replicate this dominance and ball security against the league’s best defenses. 2. The offensive line for New England certainly looks significantly beat up, and I’m sure the short week doesn’t help. How much of an issue is this for the Patriots? C Jared Wilson is the only Patriots lineman to play ever snap for the offense, excluding garbage time. RG Mike Onwenu is on injured reserve with an ankle injury; RT Morgan Moses has dealt with a foot injury for weeks; LT Will Campbell was knocked out of Week 5’s Raiders game with a knee injury; and LG Alijah Vera-Tucker left last week’s Jets game with a hamstring injury. Even Onwenu’s backup Ben Brown, who’d been playing well for a natural center, was knocked out last week with a knee injury. Campbell looked good last week despite his recent injury, and Moses should play on Thursday night, but the Patriots will be starting reserves on the attack: Matt Pryor and LG Walter Rouse. Pryor is a big, powerful veteran who didn’t give up pressure and generated movement in the ground game, but his lateral quickness is lacking, and he struggled to sustain blocks in the ground game. Rouse flashed as a run blocker, but didn’t get any quality pass protection snaps and struggled in that area when he was asked to step in late against the Jaguars. If I’m the Bears, I’m targeting the interior on blitzes and stunts to force a group without much experience together to communicate and be on the same page, specifically to the offense’s left. 3. Can you give us one player on offense and one player on defense that Bears fans may not know but you think can make a significant impact on Thursday night? WR Kyle Williams has been a bit of a one-trick pony for the Patriots since being drafted in the third round last year, but that one trick is catching go-balls for touchdowns. Williams has an excellent release package and the speed to hit home runs at any moment, especially with Maye throwing him the ball. Williams is expected to have a bigger role with Romeo Doubs and Mack Hollins on injured reserve, and he could be a difference-maker given how shaky the Bears’ outside corners have been defending the deep ball. On defense, Elijah Ponder looks like a rising star one year after joining the Patriots as an undrafted free agent, tying for third in the NFL with 5.5 sacks. He’s a big edge defender with the explosiveness and bend of someone much smaller, and he’s provided quality play as a pass rusher, run defender, and occasional coverage player. Ponder beat tackles one-on-one, even if his technique is still a work in progress, but last week he showed he can also win and free up teammates on stunts. I wouldn’t be surprised if he makes it a long night for LT Theo Benedet. 4. What happened to AJ Brown last week? I’m sure he was rusty, but that seemed like someone coated his hands in butter before the game. Any concerns about his performance moving forward for New England? A.J. Brown’s drops were ugly, and they even extended to the onside kick recovery team, where he almost gave the Jets a chance to come back late in the game. That said, he was open on nearly all of his targets, and the egregiousness of his drops led me to believe the receiver was in his head after missing four games with a high ankle sprain. Brown is a professional and one of the best pass-catchers on the planet, so I won’t be worried unless the issue becomes an unshakable habit. 5. How do you think this Super Bowl XX rematch plays out (Sorry, I had to bring it up, you understand)? As a native Chicagoan, I can let that one slide. And there’s no shame in losing to the ‘85 Bears (Rest in peace, Coach Ditka)! I see this game being close early before turning into a good old-fashioned shootout with Drake Maye and Caleb Williams showing why they’re two of the league’s top young talents. I’m predicting Andy Borragales pays off a long drive from Maye and company to win 31-28.

title: Chicago Bears vs. New England Patriots – Week 7 game preview
summary: The Chicago Bears return to Soldier Field to face the Super Bowl runner-up New England Patriots on Thursday Night Football. The Patriots started the season slowly, just 1-2, with losses to Jacksonville and Seattle. Drake Maye was playing bad football, too. He led the league in interceptions with six in the first three games. But […]
full_text: FOXBOROUGH, MASSACHUSETTS - OCTOBER 18: Drake Maye #10 of the New England Patriots drops back to pass during the second half during the NFL game against the New York Jets at Gillette Stadium on October 18, 2026 in Foxborough, Massachusetts. (Photo by Kathryn Riley/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Chicago Bears return to Soldier Field to face the Super Bowl runner-up New England Patriots on Thursday Night Football. The Patriots started the season slowly, just 1-2, with losses to Jacksonville and Seattle. Drake Maye was playing bad football, too. He led the league in interceptions with six in the first three games. But they’ve turned a corner. Maye is playing much better and they come to Chicago riding a three-game winning streak. They upset the Bills, blew out the feisty, upstart Raiders and took care of the Jets. This game creates a test of sorts for the Patriots. Are they the team that beat the Bills and took out the Raiders, Jets and Steelers? Or are they the team that lost to the Seahawks with a back-breaking interception and got trounced by the Jaguars? For Chicago, it’s a step up in competition. They have also been rocky — with comfortable wins over the Panthers and Jets — but ugly losses to the Packers and Vikings. And just last week they did their best to cough up a 31-7 lead in their 31-23 win over the Falcons. But as usual, there are plenty of reasons for those blips. Backup QBs, bad weather and in the case of the Falcons, inserting backup players too soon in a game they led comfortably. Each of these teams wants to establish themselves as a true contender and be mentioned above the best teams in the league. A Thursday night win on national streaming TV could go a long way. Plus, it’s a rematch for two of the top 3 overall picks of the 2024 NFL Draft with Caleb Williams and Drake Maye. It’s sure to be brought up, as well as when they faced off as rookies. That game did not go Caleb’s way. New England Patriots SB Nation site: Pats Pulpit Record: 4-2, 2nd in the AFC East Last week: 26-19 win over the Jets Game day, time, TV: Thursday, 7:15 p.m., Amazon Prime Video Spread: Bears -2.5 Bears all-time record against: 5-11, including postseason (Super Bowl XX that is!) Historical meetings: In week 7 of the 2022 season, Matt Eberflus and the Bears went to New England to face the Patriots on Monday Night Football. Mac Jones was benched after starting 3 for 6 for 13 yards and an interception to Jaquan Brisker. Bailey Zappe didn’t fare much better and was picked by Roquan Smith and Kyler Gordon. Justin Fields and David Montgomery rushed for touchdowns. Fields threw another TD to Khalil Herbert and the Bears won 33-14. It was their last win of the 2022 season Last meeting: Week 10 of the 2024 season. The Bears hosted the Patriots in a game to forget. The Patriots were 2-7, and the Bears laid a total egg. Four Joey Slye field goals and a Ja’Lynn Polk TD from Drake Maye were all the Pats needed to win 19-3. Caleb Williams was sacked nine times, and the Bears mustered only 142 total yards. Patriots won 19-3. Injury report: Eight Patriots were listed on their Tuesday estimated injury report. Did not participate C Ben Brown (knee) CB Carlton Davis III (neck) DT Joshua Farmer (personal) Alijah Vera-Tucker (hamstring) Limited participation WR A.J. Brown (ankle) CB Channing Canada (hamstring) T Morgan Moses (foot) CB Karon Prunty (hamstring) Offense: The Patriots offense enters this week ranked 18th in points but seventh in yards. They are 10th in passing yards and sixth in rushing yards. Drake Maye (63.9 pct cmp./1,463 yds./11 TD/7 INT) rebounded from a rough early couple of games to return to the form he showed last year. Since starting the year with one touchdown and six interceptions over the first three games, he has 10 TDs to just one INT in the last three. With A.J. Brown (6 rec./53 yds/0 TD) missing time, Maye is relying on WR Demario Douglas (20/233/3), TE Hunter Henry (19/225/2 TD), RB Rhamondre Stevenson (15/111/0) and Mack Hollins (15/209/0). Former Packer Romeo Doubs (14/261/3) is the main deep threat. Eli Raridon (9/112/1), Efton Chism III (9/98/1) and Kyle Williams (6/147/1) each have touchdowns, too. On the ground, it’s mostly Stevenson (71 att./263 yds./2 TD), followed by TreVeyon Henderson (49/194/1). Maye (34/185/1) makes some runs, too. Corey Kiner (31/138/0) also gets worked in. Defense: The Patriots enter the week fifth in points allowed and sixth in yards allowed. Their passing defense ranks 11th and their rushing defense ranks ninth. Christian Gonzalez (14 tkls/5 PD/0 INT) became the highest-paid CB this summer and is a true No. 1 corner. With him, Marcus Jones (1 INT/5 PD/27 tkl), Charles Woods (25 tkls/5 PD/1 INT) and our old friend Kevin Byard (26 tkls/2 PD/0 INT) are patrolling the secondary. Craig Woodson (23 tkls/1 FR/2 PD/1 INT) also makes plays. Up front, LBs Robert Spillane (39 tkls/2 QB hits/1 TFL) and Christian Elliss (38 tkls/1 sk/1 TFL/3 QB hits/1 FF/1 PD) lead the Pats in tackles. Elijah Ponder (5.5 sks/7 TFL/10 QB hits/2 FR/1 FF) and Christian Barmore (2 sks/2 TFL/5 QB hits/1 PD) lead the pass rush. Gabe Jacas (1.5 sk/1 INT/1 PD/3 TFL/5 QB hits) and Milton Williams (1 sk/1 TFL/2 QB hits/38 tkls) are also making stops up front. Key matchups: It’ll be interesting to see how Christian Gonzalez is used and how Ben Johnson tries to get his pass-catchers in favorable matchups. Mike Vrabel is a good defensive coordinator, and he’ll throw a lot at Chicago to get the offense off balance and out of sync. Dennis Allen, on the other hand, has to use his disguises and blitzes well against Drake Maye to try and get him looking like the Maye from the Super Bowl and the first three games of the season. Not the Maye from the last three weeks. Key stats The Patriots defense ranks seventh in red zone defense, allowing touchdowns on 50 percent of opponents’ drives. The Bears, after their red zone performance, are scoring on 50 percent of their red zone drives. New England ranks ninth in blitz percentage, sending extra pressure 31.9 percent of the time. However, they rank 13th in pressure percentage, getting pressure 23.9 percent of the time. Chicago ranks fourth in pressure percentage at 30.2 percent. The Pats are allowing the ninth-worst completion percentage to opposing QBs at 66.1 percent. QBs have a 90.3 rating against their defense. New England has the second-most turnovers on offense with 13. Seven interceptions by Maye and six lost fumbles. The Patriots have 11 fumbles on the season and have lost six of them Can the Bears beat the Patriots at home? Which of these teams is the more likely “pretender,” and which one is more likely the “contender?” Let us know in the comments.

title: Bears vs. Patriots: Can Grady Jarrett beat the ailing Pats interior?
summary: It’s a quick turnaround week, which always magnifies the injury report for teams. The Bears are not without injuries, as Kyle Monangai, Jonah Jackson, and TJ Edwards have all been sidelined this week. The Patriots, however, had their OL decimated on Sunday against the Jets. Guards Alijah Vera-Tucker and Ben Brown, and Tackle Morgan Moses […]
full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - SEPTEMBER 28: Jalen Hurts #1 of the Philadelphia Eagles scrambles from Grady Jarrett #50 of the Chicago Bears at Soldier Field on September 28, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images) | Getty Images It’s a quick turnaround week, which always magnifies the injury report for teams. The Bears are not without injuries, as Kyle Monangai, Jonah Jackson, and TJ Edwards have all been sidelined this week. The Patriots, however, had their OL decimated on Sunday against the Jets. Guards Alijah Vera-Tucker and Ben Brown, and Tackle Morgan Moses all had varying injuries Sunday that put their statuses in question for Thursday’s matchup in Chicago. This adds to an already ailing OL in New England with Greg Van Roten, Michael Owenwu, and Marcus Bryant on IR. This leaves the Bears with a golden opportunity — get pressure up the middle, and disrupt Drake Maye quickly. The third year QB currently has his highest career pressure % at 26.2%, an uptick of 5% from last season. Losing three starters isn’t going to help. You have to expect a combination of rookie Caleb Lomu, Matt Pryor, and Walter Rouse to fill in for their teammates’ absences. Lomu and Rouse have about 300 snaps in their careers between them, while Pryor — a vet that Bears fans are very familiar with — has a fair amount of experience and is capable of providing quality starts. Still, this opens up a major opportunity for the Bears. Enter Grady Jarrett. Jarrett, one of the big DL acquisitions in the 2025 offseason, has been more disruptive in 2026 than 2025, despite his numbers still lagging. While he hasn’t yet recorded a sack, he has 5 pressures, 3 hurries, and two QB hits through 6 games this season. Much of his game needs to be seen live, though, as his presence has been felt more often, setting up others for sacks or impact plays. For instance, watch this sack Dayo Odeyingbo has on Jalen Hurts. Grady Jarrett’s stunt and pressure forces Hurts to step up, right into the arms of Dayo: Dayo Odeyingbo comes up BIG for the SACK on Jalen Hurts 😤 pic.twitter.com/XL4pIuvirJ — ClutchPoints (@ClutchPoints) September 29, 2026 This is the type of impact Jarrett is going to have to make on Thursday against a jump start Patriots squad. After starting the season 1-2, New England is on a bit of a tear, winning their last three games by a combined 38 points. Maye is at the center of that, and he has proven to have a propensity for going downfield, as evidenced by his 5th-best 8.0 yards per pass attempt. The Packers game illustrated the Bears’ weakness in covering deep passes, and their need to maintain several defenders in coverage against QBs with a strong deep ball. So getting pressure on four man fronts will be even more critical for the Bears. With Grady Jarrett going up against two potential backups in Matt Pryor and Walter Rouse, he could do some serious damage in limiting Maye’s ability to throw downfield. If the Bears are to win this Thursday, I think that Jarrett needs to create one or two sacks for himself or others. If he doesn’t, it may force Allen to generate some blitzes and Maye could pick them apart.

full_text: The Cincinnati Bengals have been missing a healthy Bryan Cook as he has been recovering from an ankle injury. The veteran safety was in and out of the lineup in the Week 3 loss to the Steelers, then missed the following week vs. the Jaguars. The Bengals dropped both games. While he did return for the Week 5 win at Miami, he struggled to make an impact in the 31-24 victory. As the Bengals prepare for the Ravens offense, having Cook back at full strength will be a welcome sight for Bengals fans. He is also excited to get back on the field after the bye week. Cook spoke with Charlie Goldsmith of FOX 19 this week and had this to say about heading into the week: “I’m excited to really go. You don’t know how well you feel until you really push yourself. It’s like life. When you hit those extremes, you’re alive.” Cook also knows how important it will be to contain Lamar Jackson if he returns after facing him in so many important games with the Kansas City Chiefs. “You have to try to contain Lamar,” Cook said. “He’s a force to be reckoned with. He’s one of the best dual-threats if not the best dual threat of this generation. He’s very explosive. He has a tank in the backfield with 22 (Henry). You try to contain those two. They have a high-powered offense. We have to slow them down, capitalize on missed opportunities, get a turnover, and be physical. It’s the AFC North.” The defense has struggled at times this season, but getting a fully healthy Cook back will be a big win for the safeties group. It will also be a major boost to have a veteran leader on the back end of this defense, especially against an offense that can be one of the most dynamic in the league when it’s clicking. Will be fun to see Cook back on the field at full strength.

full_text: The Cincinnati Bengals lost tight end Tanner Hudson for the season with a pec injury. While Hudson doesn’t play a majority of snaps, he still plays a pretty key role. That being as a second receiving tight end or fourth receiver. He played roughly 69 snaps over four games. However, we saw them adjusting and using him in more creative ways. The most notable was his touchdown catch against the Miami Dolphins when the offense called an audible out of a heavy formation and spread out there tight ends. That is where Hudson easily beat a linebacker in coverage on a timing pattern. The question now becomes who fills that void and tight end coach James Casey seems to have plenty of faith in Erick All Jr. to fill it . The team seems to be missing that Noah Fant presence of a tight end who the team trusts as a blocker as well as a pass catcher to keep from giving away the offense’s intentions. Could All show the ability to pull that off? Bengals News Quick Hits | Joe Knows: ‘It’s Gone Through Baltimore”; Bryan Cook Eyes Re-Match With Lamar And King Henry The importance of this game is not lost on Joe Burrow. Getting to 4-3 rather than 3-3 and 0-2 in the division are two drastically different spots to be sitting in after this Sunday. Ravens’ Lamar Jackson returns to practice but status remains unclear vs. Bengals It may have been promising for Baltimore fans to see Jackson back out there at first, but for the quarterback to bee seen limping in the locker room and after practice is not a good sign at all. Who knows how this trends as the week goes on, but it isn’t a good start. Bengals Get Encouraging Injury News on Key Playmaker Ahead of Ravens Game Another player who is likely to eat up some of Hudson’s snaps is rookie wide receiver Colbie Young who looks to be healthy after getting injured during the team’s Week 3 loss on his first catch of the game. NFL News NFL QB rankings, Week 7: Dak Prescott hits season low; C.J. Stroud eclipses Patrick Mahomes Burrow remains at No. 12 and at the bottom of Tier 2. The craziest move was CJ Stroud to No. 3 overall. That seems quite high even if he has had a couple of good games in a row. He only sits behind Josh Allen and Brock Purdy. Jordan Elliott released by Titans after pulling out gun in parking lot, Robert Saleh says Just an absolutely insane escalation here. Even the player on the other side of the argument said they would hangout outside of team activities prior to this and never had an argument leading up to this. Giants to start J.J. McCarthy at quarterback in Week 7 vs. Texans This move seemed pretty obvious. It does come after some garbage time prevent defense stat padding. However, when a team parts with draft capital for a quarterback mid-season, you are probably going to see them start sooner than later.

full_text: Sunday will be the first chance for the Cincinnati Bengals to face former pass rusher Trey Hendrickson. One of Hendrickson’s Baltimore Ravens teammates is drinking the Kool-Aid on this revenge game with a pretty big prediction: “Trey is a great leader, and he’s a guy who flies around,” linebacker Trenton Simpson said Wednesday. “And man, I am excited to see him against his former team. The things he’s doing in practice, the way he rushed the passer, and just how he’d get off the ball. And I believe that this game for him is about to be like one of those multiple-sack games. So I’m calling it. I’m excited to see the celebration he does, so I’m excited.” Ravens linebacker Trenton Simpson is predicting a multi-sack game for Trey Hendrickson, who is facing his former team in the Bengals. “I’m calling it,” Simpson said. pic.twitter.com/r02Sdm3p0p — Jamison Hensley (@jamisonhensley) October 21, 2026 Hendrickson has missed two games this season with a broken finger that he got surgery on. If he were to have multiple sacks, it would be the first such performance with Baltimore, as he only has two sacks so far. He looked good last week against the Cleveland Browns, getting plenty of pressure on a rookie left tackle and recording a sack. It will be interesting to see how the Bengals scheme up pass protection with Hendrickson. One thing we know is the team will likely be excited to run directly at him. For years, one of the biggest knocks was that you could run at Hendrickson and gain yards pretty easily. It became more obvious as the defense deteriorated around him There is no doubt Hendrickson will be wearing the biggest chip on his shoulder. He was loud and clear about his displeasure with the front office, and he’d tell anyone who would listen about his offseason contract drama. That has clearly left a bad taste in most fans’ mouths. Now, the Bengals will need to keep Hendrickson from having a big day if they are to come out of Baltimore with a W.

title: Bengals Progress Report: Grading the Offense
summary: The Cincinnati Bengals are coming out of their bye week. They’re 3-2, and so far, it’s been a pretty mixed bag so far. They started the season looking dominant against the Buccaneers and Texans (who have won just two games between them at this point in the season), but then suffered frustrating losses to the […]
full_text: The Cincinnati Bengals are coming out of their bye week. They’re 3-2, and so far, it’s been a pretty mixed bag so far. They started the season looking dominant against the Buccaneers and Texans (who have won just two games between them at this point in the season), but then suffered frustrating losses to the Steelers and Jaguars before escaping Miami with an ugly victory over the winless Dolphins in Week 5. So, yeah. Mixed bag. Since there’s no Bengals football to watch this weekend, let’s take a look at how the rushing and passing offenses have performed through the first five games, assign each a grade, and then determine an overall offensive grade. Starting with… Rushing Offense Zac Taylor, once again, entered the season talking a big game about establishing a more balanced offense. The Bengals spent much of training camp working on Joe Burrow taking snaps under center, and they really tried to force the issue through the first few games of the season. It hasn’t exactly worked. The Bengals have the seventh-fewest rushing yards in the league, are averaging just 3.6 yards per carry, and have scored only two rushing touchdowns this season. Perhaps most damning of all, their longest run of the season is just 13 yards, the shortest of any team’s longest run in the NFL. And that run came all the way back in Week 1. Chase Brown has significantly out-carried Samaje Perine so far, 71-27, but that trend shifted somewhat in Week 5 against the Dolphins. The Bengals appeared to abandon their commitment to running with Burrow under center and instead leaned more heavily on running out of shotgun, an approach that seems better suited to Perine. Of course, Brown has also proven himself to be a reliable receiver out of the backfield, so he shouldn’t have much trouble staying on the field moving forward. Meanwhile, it’s become painfully obvious that the Bengals coaching staff has little, if any, confidence in Tahj Brooks. For the first time in Burrow’s career, he has the same five starting offensive linemen in front of him for consecutive seasons. While they’ve done a better job protecting him than in years past, this offensive line was built primarily to keep Burrow upright, not necessarily to open up running lanes. Ultimately, the running game has been a disappointment, but there is one important thing worth pointing out. According to PFF, the four highest-graded run defenses in the NFL belong to the Buccaneers, Steelers, Jaguars, and Texans, with grades of 79.5, 76.3, 75.0, and 74.8, respectively. In other words, four of the Bengals’ first five opponents have been among the league’s best at stopping the run. Meanwhile, Cincinnati’s rushing offense ranks 18th in the NFL with a PFF grade of 70.9. That’s worth considering before completely writing off the running game, but the production simply hasn’t been good enough. Rushing-Offense Grade: 71% (C-) Passing Offense This is the identity of the Bengals’ offense, and it’s not particularly difficult to understand why. Burrow is an elite quarterback, and Cincinnati boasts the best wide-receiver duo in the NFL in Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins, both of whom would be legitimate No. 1 receivers on just about any team in the league. The offensive line was built to keep Burrow clean, and so far, it’s done an okay job. Considering what we’ve seen from Bengals offensive lines in recent years, that’s actually something of a compliment. Chase and Higgins are weapons 1 and 1A. Opposing defenses understandably do everything they can to take them away, which creates opportunities for players like Mike Gesicki, Dohnte Meyers, and Brown coming out of the backfield. Unfortunately, Andrei Iosivas landed on injured reserve after tearing a ligament in his thumb that required surgery. While he’s expected to return at some point this season, his absence has exposed a considerable gap between the Bengals’ top two receivers and the rest of the depth chart. Through five games, Burrow has thrown for 1,361 yards (sixth in the NFL), 11 touchdowns (fourth), and just three interceptions (tied for the second-fewest). Higgins leads the team with 423 receiving yards, while Chase and Gesicki have each caught four touchdown passes. Those are impressive numbers, especially considering the Bengals have struggled to establish any sort of consistent rushing attack. Opposing defenses know Cincinnati wants to throw the football, and Burrow and company have still managed to put up strong numbers through the air. There have been some frustrating stretches, though, and the passing game hasn’t always looked as explosive or consistent as you’d expect from an offense featuring this much talent. Still, if this is what a typical “slow” start looks like for Burrow and the Bengals’ passing offense, there’s reason to believe they could come out of the bye week firing on all cylinders. Hopefully. Passing-Offense Grade: 89% (B+) The Bengals’ offense has as much star power as any unit in the NFL, but far too often, it seems to get in its own way. Taylor’s play-calling can be frustratingly conservative, and at times, the offense lacks the creativity you’d expect from a unit with so many talented players demanding touches. The inability to establish a consistent rushing attack has made the offense increasingly one-dimensional, placing even more pressure on Burrow and his receivers to carry the load. Fortunately, they’re talented enough to do exactly that. But there’s a difference between having the talent to be one of the NFL’s best offenses and actually performing like one week in and week out. Through five games, the Bengals’ offense has been good. Not great, but good. Overall Offensive Grade: 80% (B-)

title: NFL trade deadline 2026: Cincinnati Bengals’ potential trade partners and targets
summary: The Cincinnati Bengals are coming off of their bye week, sitting in last place in the AFC North at 3-2. With everyone else in the division sitting at 4-2, they are right in the mix to still win the division. Meanwhile, there are several teams around the league sitting with just 1 win on the […]
full_text: Tennessee wide receiver Van Jefferson (11) can’t haul in a pass against Los Angeles cornerback Cam Hart (20) during their game at Nissan Stadium in Nashville, Tenn., Sunday, Nov. 2, 2025. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co The Cincinnati Bengals are coming off of their bye week, sitting in last place in the AFC North at 3-2. With everyone else in the division sitting at 4-2, they are right in the mix to still win the division. Meanwhile, there are several teams around the league sitting with just 1 win on the season, along with the Chargers, who are surprisingly 0-6 to start the year. Could the Bengals swing a trade to continue making a push back to the playoffs this year? Most years, I would say absolutely not. After adding Dexter Lawrence via trade for the 10th overall selection, it cannot be completely ruled out. Let’s take a look around the league at some potential players that could be on the trade block for teams that have started out poorly this year. Washington Commanders (1-4-1 record) The Commanders invested heavily in free agency this season, and it has not worked out on the field. One of those additions was tight end Chig Okonkwo. With Tanner Hudson recently going on IR the Bengals could use another receiving threat at the tight end position. Okonkwo is coming off his best game of the season on Monday Night Football. He went for 6 receptions for 69 yards in the Week 6 loss. Unfortunately, Okonkwo is under contract for two more seasons after this one. I can’t see the Bengals actually bringing in a high-dollar tight end to the roster with Jack Endries just sitting on the 53-man roster already. Outside of Okonkwo I don’t see anybody else on their roster that makes sense from a football standpoint who could become available from Washington. Tennessee Titans (1-5 record) Tennessee was able to finally get in the win column this week. They are still a team that looks more in the running for the top overall draft pick than they do a shot at making a run toward the playoffs this year. Linebacker Cedric Gray has been demoted from a full-time starter to a rotational role in the defense after the addition of rookie Anthony Hill Jr. from Texas this season. Gray finished the 2025 season fourth overall in total tackles with 164. He had a 92.7 run defense grade last season. The Bengals’ young linebackers are improving, but it would be nice to add another player in the mix to take snaps from Oren Burks. It would also be better injury insurance over Burks for the current starters. Buying low on a player still on his rookie contract that has played well in the past makes a lot of sense to me. Amani Hooker at strong safety is another player that makes sense from a purely football standpoint. Jordan Battle has struggled, and Kyle Dugger has been injured. Hooker has over 5,000 career snaps, has an 88.5 run defense grade this season, and has recorded 2 interceptions. However, Hooker just recently signed a 3-year contract extension in Tennessee. That could make it unlikely the Bengals have any interest there. Tampa Bay Buccaneers (1-5 record) Tampa Bay blew a 16-3 lead in the second half against the Pittsburgh Steelers this week. With just one win on the season, we might see them decide to unload a few contracts around the trade deadline. The player everyone would love to add to this roster is Bucky Irving. Irving is one of the most elusive running backs in the league. Still on his rookie deal through next season, I can’t see the Buccaneers actually trading him. There is another running back they might part with, and that is Kenny Gainwell. Gainwell had some quality games against the Bengals last season when he was playing for Pittsburgh. He has just 61 rushing yards and 61 receiving yards so far this season. Last year with Pittsburgh he ran for 537 yards, while adding an additional 486 receiving. Gainwell is under contract again for next year with a salary of $7 million. He could be cut with a dead cap hit of $3 million before that season. I don’t know how much interest the Bengals would actually have in Gainwell, but he does seem like a player that is likely to be on the trading block. Miami Dolphins (0-5 record) Miami is in a complete rebuild this season. They have added a lot of young talent via the 2026 NFL Draft, and will be looking to do the same again this year. They are likely to sell off some players for draft capital ahead of the trade deadline. The problem here is that I don’t think anyone they might be willing to part with makes sense for Cincinnati. I could see them letting go of a veteran like Josh Uche or Zach Sieler on the defensive line. For once, that is not a position that the Bengals are in desperate need of. If anything, we have so many guys at that position that it is hard for some of the young guys to see enough snaps this year. Jordyn Brooks would have been a prime target to go after, but the Miami Dolphins decided to give him another contract extension this year. They are planning to have him and rookie Jacob Rodriguez as building blocks for their defense going forward. Los Angeles Chargers (0-6 record) People are going to toss out names like running back Omarion Hampton, safety Derwin James, and pass rusher Khalil Mack. I don’t see any of those being realistic options for Cincinnati to acquire. Hampton is in his second season, and the Chargers are unlikely to give up on him just yet. James has a massive contract and has been constantly injured. Mack isn’t a position Cincinnati really needs help at, along with a hefty contract of his own this year. The one player that I would go after is cornerback Cam Hart. Hart played for Al Golden at Notre Dame. He has great size at 6’2” and 207 pounds. He is having a career year with a 73.8 coverage grade. He is still just 25 years old, and has also recorded 2 interceptions this year. With the Chargers at 0-6 I am making that phone call and trying to acquire Hart. If you added Hart, it would allow Dax Hill to stay in the slot the rest of the year. Hart would start on the outside opposite of DJ Turner. That trio could be one of the best in the league. Shoring up the secondary with the defensive line Cincinnati has would be beneficial for a team looking to make a long playoff run.

title: Bengals News: Zac Taylor Hot Seat Watch
summary: The Cincinnati Bengals are coming out of their Week 6 bye and are set to travel to Baltimore for their second division game of the 2026 season. full_text: The Cincinnati Bengals are coming out of their Week 6 bye and are set to travel to Baltimore for their second division game of the 2026 season. They’re 3-2, but they’ve been a mixed bag so far. The offense, despite the star power, has struggled with consistency. The defense has shown progress in some ways, but they haven’t shown themselves to be among the league’s top-ranked units. After three straight seasons of missing the playoffs following two consecutive trips to the AFC Championship and one Super Bowl appearance, head coach Zac Taylor’s leash may finally be starting to get tight. With the Bengals still very much in the mix in the division, it’s too early to say Taylor could be on his way out, but some think the process could be accelerated with a bad showing against the Ravens . The Bengals under Taylor have been notoriously slow starters. The offense, with Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins, has looked mediocre at times, and the defense, after a good start, has struggled over the last couple weeks. Burrow and the weapons around him have a finite amount of time in the league to win a championship, and they can’t afford to waste any more time. This weekend could tell us a lot about what happens next. Here’s what else is going on: Bengals Get Encouraging Injury News on Key Playmaker Ahead of Ravens Game “He’s looked as good as he’s looked in a long time,” Taylor said. “I think last week he had a good week on what he could handle from a rehab perspective. So this week to get him back involved, he looked good running around today. I think it’s good to finally get him back and feel like he’s closer to 100% health.” Bengals Urged to Trade for 19-Sack Defender “I would say Yaya Diaby because you could extend him and make him a part of your d-line of the future,” said Liscow on why he is so high on the Bengals adding Diaby. “I think that would be one of the more expensive options on the list, especially when you factor in the extension required there. But pairing him with Dexter Lawrence and with Boy Mafe gives you three really good players on that defensive line to build around.” Bengals may have a green light to trade for Colts 3-time Pro Bowler after Chris Ballard’s firing, but an obstacle needs to be addressed There’s no question Taylor is the better tailback compared to Brown, and his production from this season is enough of an argument on its own. Taylor has 492 yards and seven touchdowns on 122 carries through six games. Over 80% of his yardage has come from under center concepts, and he’s averaging 4.4 yards per carry on those runs. He would be an obvious upgrade over Brown as the lead back in Cincinnati’s run game. The Bengals used their bye to look inward. Here’s what stood out “I think certainly we’ve had our moments in all three phases that you feel like this is who we’re going to be,” Taylor said. “And now it’s just putting the complete game together in all three phases.” Who Dey! title: Browns TE not sweating the small things at the moment
summary: Cleveland Browns tight end Harold Fannin Jr. was one of the offense’s few bright spots in 2025.  Fannin led the Browns in receptions (72), receiving yards (731), receiving touchdowns (6), and was sixth in yards per catch (10.2). Through six games of the 2026 season, it appears that Fannin has not been as productive, although […]
full_text: (Photo by Lauren Leigh Bacho/Getty Images) | Getty Images Cleveland Browns tight end Harold Fannin Jr. was one of the offense’s few bright spots in 2025. Fannin led the Browns in receptions (72), receiving yards (731), receiving touchdowns (6), and was sixth in yards per catch (10.2). Through six games of the 2026 season, it appears that Fannin has not been as productive, although there are extenuating circumstances. Heading into this week’s game against the Tennessee Titans, Fannin has 19 receptions (second on the team), 166 receiving yards (third), and three receiving touchdowns (tied for first). However, his yards per catch have declined to an average of just 8.7 yards. Fannin’s targets are down slightly – an average of five per game compared to 6.5 last season – but that is a small difference. So, what gives? For starters, the Browns have more weapons on offense with the addition of rookie wide receivers Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion. In Weeks 1 and 2, Concepcion led the team in receptions. In Week 3, it was Fannin; Week 4 was running back Quinshon Judkins; in Week 5 it was four different players, and in Week 6 it was three different players. Could it be as simple as quarterback Deshaun Watson spreading the ball around according to the way the game is going and not something more complicated? According to Watson, the answer to that question is “yes” : “It depends on how the defense is playing us, and we only have one football. We got a lot of skilled guys that can make plays. (Denzel) Boston, Jerry (Jeudy) been coming along, KC (Concepcion Jr.), and then we got Harold. So, that’s four different guys and one football. So, you got to pick your spots depending on the play call and what the defense is presenting. And you got to find the open guy and find the right guy with the ball. So, it just depends on the game.” One big change from Fannin’s rookie season is that head coach Todd Monken is now calling the plays. But Monken said the offense is focused more on exploiting the defense and not feeding the ball to any one particular player: “Sometimes the matchup’s not great, like when (Baltimore went) dime and that’s Kyle Hamilton. We had some that were designed or that could get to (Harold), and that was Kyle Hamilton covering him. And the game goes sometimes in a way that it doesn’t end up where the ball doesn’t find him. And I thought Harold did a great job blocking. He did a number of things well when we asked him to do that, and he is certainly a weapon that we are trying to get the ball to. “I mean, we would like to get the ball more to Denzel Boston, and we’d like to get the ball more to KC Concepcion, and Harold happens to be one of those others. And so, we just got to do a better job collectively. And then you’ll see those touches will rise.” But what about the man himself? Is Fannin bothered by what some perceive as a slow start to the season? Not so much, because the Browns are winning and because he knows the opportunities will come: “I’m cool with it. It doesn’t really bother me. I’m obviously happy that we’re winning. We’re going to continue to keep coming out with wins whether I have catches or not. The main thing is to go out there and win. I’m going to continue to go out there and do my job to the best of my abilities that I can. If we come out with a win, I come out happy.” As Monken has pointed out numerous times, every week is different in the NFL. Some weeks it will be Concepcion or Boston leading in receiving, some weeks it will be a committee, and some weeks, like against Carolina when he had seven receptions and two touchdowns, it will be Fannin’s turn to shine. At some point, Watson will need to find Fannin in a big spot, and given his track record, Fannin will make the catch. Until then, as Fannin said, everything is cool for the first-place Browns. title: Browns HC Todd Monken’s success is due to choosing respect
summary: Why are the Cleveland Browns 4-2 and successful in HC Todd Monken’s first run as an NFL head coach, despite being called frauds? Is it the defense? Sure, that is part of it. Is it two back-to-back home-run NFL draft classes by GM Andrew Berry? Definitely a part of it. Does QB Deshaun Watson’s fourth-quarter […]
full_text: Why are the Cleveland Browns 4-2 and successful in HC Todd Monken’s first run as an NFL head coach, despite being called frauds ? Is it the defense? Sure, that is part of it. Is it two back-to-back home-run NFL draft classes by GM Andrew Berry? Definitely a part of it. Does QB Deshaun Watson’s fourth-quarter magic play a role? Yes, indeed. Has the Browns roster shown a grittiness that personifies the City of Cleveland? Very much so. Also, have the Browns taken advantage of some teams playing poorly, some luck, and injuries to their opponents? Sure, every good team has a bit of all of that. If you listen to Cleveland radio announcer Andrew Siciliano, the answer to how the Browns are winning is complicated. If you wait until about four minutes into the clip below, you will hear him give Monken a ton of credit, while quoting TE Blake Whiteheart , when he says about Monken, “He’s demanding but not demeaning.” I was wrong about the story of the young NFL season so far, the Browns, @AndrewSiciliano explains the impact that Todd Monken has had and why I should have believed after our incredible spring interview with Monken. Plus Andrew has an AMAZING Monken impression he workshops. pic.twitter.com/2SRbrhkPqp — Kevin Clark (@bykevinclark) October 21, 2026 For anyone in a leadership position of any kind, including as a parent (heck, all of us have also had leaders above us, including parental figures), the balance between having power and using that power in a healthy way is always a fine line. In sports, coaches are often called either “disciplinarians” or “players’ coaches,” with the connotation that the former doesn’t care about the players, just the rules, and that it is flipped for the latter. While winning always helps, the Browns new (but aged) head coach seems to have found the perfect marriage of the two, where he has earned his players’ respect without compromising his expectations. title: Week 7 Browns NFL Power Rankings: Cleveland 1st in division, but last in power rankings
summary: It is Week 7 of the 2026 NFL season, and the Cleveland Browns continued to build some momentum. Overall, the Browns went up by 3.6 spots from week-to-week to have an overall ranking of 16.1 That is an identical reversal from last week, when they dropped by 3.6 spots. The victory did them some good […]
full_text: It is Week 7 of the 2026 NFL season, and the Cleveland Browns continued to build some momentum. Overall, the Browns went up by 3.6 spots from week-to-week to have an overall ranking of 16.1 That is an identical reversal from last week, when they dropped by 3.6 spots. The victory did them some good obviously, but ranking-wise, they are still cumulatively ranked last in the division. People are still respecting the Browns, but not their offense and easy schedule. Here is a summary of how the Cleveland Browns are viewed across mainstream media outlets in NFL Power Rankings heading into Week 7 of the 2026 NFL season. CBS Sports – No. 16 (up 3 spots) Can you believe they are in first place in the AFC North after six games? Amazing. The defense is top-10 in scoring right now. Impressive. ESPN – No. 19 (up 4 spots) Biggest issue on offense: Run blocking Quarterback Deshaun Watson’s poor play in the first three quarters of games can’t be ignored, but coach Todd Monken has acknowledged that an inconsistent run game has placed Watson and the offense in disadvantageous situations. With an entirely new offensive line from last season, the Browns rank 24th in ESPN’s run block win rate metric and last in yards before contact per rush on designed runs (1.29). It’s a big reason they’re averaging the eighth-longest average conversion distance in the NFL (8.9). NFL.com – No. 16 (up 5 spots) Logically, the Browns shouldn’t be able to win in this fashion as often as they have. The formula remains the same: Play stifling defense, weather a few blows and hope the offense finds enough to score more than the opposition. It worked again Sunday, scoring the Browns another key AFC North triumph and securing first place in the division at the latest stage of a season since 2014. That’s a long time, folks, but with a growing collection of creditable wins, we must respect this team even if it doesn’t make perfect sense. Sporting News – No. 16 (up 4 spots) The Browns are allowing on average only 20.3 points per game to opponents, tied with the Seahawks and Jets for No. 7 in the league. Consider with Myles Garrett last season, they allowed 22.3. The defense doesn’t get enough credit for getting better under new coordinator Mike Rutenberg. Yahoo Sports – No. 19 (up 3 spots) The Browns have four very close wins in the final minutes, and the last two victories came in the final 10 seconds. They’re 21st in DVOA. In betting terms, they have the longest odds to win the AFC North despite being in first place right now. This is not sustainable, especially with an offense that is 29th in DVOA, which is why they’re not higher than 19th. But it is a lot of fun right now in Cleveland. One thing that shouldn’t change is the defense will keep the Browns in games. That unit is ninth in DVOA. Linebacker Carson Schwesinger, last season’s NFL Defensive Rookie of the Year, is a star and his forced fumble on Derrick Henry in the fourth quarter led to a Browns touchdown and turned around the game. “It’s been an unbelievable credit to our team, especially our defense,” Browns head coach Todd Monken said, according to the team’s site. “Early on, after 10 points, shutting them out and constantly getting us the ball back and giving us a chance to win.” Bleacher Report – No. 13 (up 4 spots) The Cleveland Browns have developed a formula, leading to the team’s unexpected yet AFC North-leading 4-2 record. Really, it’s rather simple. Cleveland needs to play top-notch defense for three-plus quarters before the team can hand the ball to Deshaun Watson and let the quarterback create a play when it’s absolutely needed. Watson hasn’t played particularly well this season. However, he’s done enough, specifically in crunch time, to help his team establish a winning record. Despite the early success, this approach doesn’t seem sustainable when the Browns eventually face the better teams. For example, Lamar Jackson wasn’t in the Baltimore Ravens’ lineup during Sunday’s matchup. Fortunately, Cleveland’s remaining docket looks rather manageable. In fact, the Browns face only one team with a winning record between now and the start of December. USA Today – No. 14 (up 2 spots) Look who’s in first place at the latest point of a season since 2014. Will a team scheduled to kick off at 1 p.m. ET for the rest of the season get a prime-time flex at some point? title: Browns roster: Key defender that nobody is talking enough about
summary: The Cleveland Browns are doing quite well this season. They just knocked off probably the best team in the AFC North Division, the Baltimore Ravens. Plus, they have beaten the Pittsburgh Steelers for a 2-0 divisional record. That may come into play as the season rolls along. RELATED: MAY NEVER SEE THIS HIGH A PFF […]
full_text: The Cleveland Browns are doing quite well this season . They just knocked off probably the best team in the AFC North Division, the Baltimore Ravens. Plus, they have beaten the Pittsburgh Steelers for a 2-0 divisional record. That may come into play as the season rolls along. RELATED: MAY NEVER SEE THIS HIGH A PFF GRADE ON A BROWNS DEFENDER But keep in mind, except for the Ravens contest, Cleveland hasn’t beaten a team that has a good record. However, as the saying goes, “You can only play who is on your schedule.” The offense this year is a roller coaster. It was billed as being a short passing game with lots of tight end play and predicated on getting the run game going. The run game is almost non-existent ; there aren’t any tight ends on the roster who are good blockers, and the offensive line has had its share of attrition already. But on the other side of the ball, now that’s a different story. For the duration of Jim Schwartz’s tenure as the defensive coordinator with Cleveland, he made many improvements and had this group in the Top-5. When Schwartz was passed over for the head coaching gig and decided not to retain his DC job with the Browns, Mike Rutenberg was hired to oversee Schwartz’s architecture. Immediately, there were quite a bit of questions from the media and Cleveland’s fanbase as to why new head coach Todd Monken would hire a guy to take over the defense who wasn’t a Schwartz disciple. Rutenberg never worked with – or under – Schwartz. And yet Monken stated early that this defense would continue to follow the path that Schwartz laid for the defense. One of the first things Rutenberg did when he accepted the Browns DC position was get GM Andrew Berry to contact the agent for LB Quincy Williams, who just so happened to be a free agent. Williams had spent part of 2025 on IR because of a shoulder injury, and a lot of teams did not have Williams ranked that high a priority. But Rutenberg coached Williams while with the New York Jets for four seasons. Rut knew. And now with the Browns, Williams is balling out. In six games, Williams has 40 total tackles, with a high of 11 against his former team, the Jets, in the Week 5 loss. He has never been a huge sack artist, mainly because he doesn’t blitz much, but he has a single sack this year and 13.5 for his eight years in the league. Both Williams and his partner in crime, LB Carson Schwesinger, are playing at a Pro Bowl level, and it is just one-third into the season. But Schwesinger receives the lion’s share of notoriety and accolades since he was named the “NFL Defensive Rookie of the Year” after his rookie season. Folks know his name, and expect great things from him in every game. But Williams is also having an impressive season, and yet nobody is noticing, or looks at him as “the Browns’ other linebacker.” Schwesinger has natural instincts, a non-stop motor, can recognize the run quickly, and now has a seasoned veteran as a mentor. The two linebackers combined have 96 total tackles. In every single game this season, one or the other has led Cleveland in tackles. In three games, this duo was 1-2 in total tackles. Williams is proving to be a great free agent signing by Berry. According to Pro Football Focus (PFF) , Williams was ranked as the #3 linebacker before the Ravens contest, and afterwards, Schwesinger is now ranked #9. Pre-snap, it is Williams who is moving players around to ensure that they are in the correct positions. It is his experience coming through, and he acts like a coach on the field. He isn’t wearing the green dot, but he is still barking out instructions to his teammates. He saved his best game of the year against his former team and led the Browns in tackles with 11. Williams was able to force the fumble from TE Kenyan Sadiq in the third quarter when New York was on the 11-yard line while Cleveland S Ronnie Hickman recovered. That play was huge. Williams leads the league in forced fumbles with three, all in the Jets matchup. The talented linebacker has great speed (4.59), is a sideline-to-sideline backer, has a never-ending voice on and off the field, and can blitz when needed. Against the Jets, Williams had a PFF grade of 95.7. That is incredible. In some games, he is the best player on the field for Cleveland. He has shown a nose for the ball, and his motor never unwinds. And to think the Browns got Williams for $13 million on a two-year deal is an incredible bargain. And he showed his merit this past weekend against division foe Baltimore Ravens. In the first quarter, Baltimore had a first-and-15 as QB Tyler Huntley threw a short pass in the flats to RB Derrick Henry. As the ball was in the air, Williams was already tracking Henry and nailed him for just a two-yard gain. In Quarter 2, the Ravens had a third-and-eight with 10:06 before the half. Huntley sent a short pass to WR Zay Flowers, who had a lot of real estate in front of him if he could get past Williams. The result was a five-yard gain and a subsequent punt. skies are closed 🙅 pic.twitter.com/RVE7vozimm — Cleveland Browns (@Browns) October 18, 2026 Williams and Schwesinger combined for a zero-gain run by Henry right before the half as the collision rocked the stadium between the three. With 2:13 before the half, Williams’ number was called on a blitz package as he sent Huntley to the turf for the sack. He has brought proven production, experience, and versatility to an already good Browns defense. In just his third NFL season, Williams had 110 tackles. Then he reeled of seasons of 106, 139, and 116 before notching just 83 last year where he sat out multiple games. He was named First Team All-Pro in 2023 after his 139-tackle output paired with 15 tackles for loss and 10 batted passes. Clay Matthews with Tom Cousineau. A duo of great linebackers is in the DNA of the Browns. Schwesinger paired with Williams is just this year’s version. What were your expectations when the Browns signed Williams to replace Devin Bush? How are you feeling about him after 6 weeks?

title: The Browns running game is broken, but it’s not broken beyond repair
summary: A quick story to illustrate how to look at the Cleveland Browns’ run game: As someone who is into the gaming culture (video games to be exact), I never had a reason to buy a personal computer for gaming purposes. Reasons? It’s far too expensive, and it’s just too complex in terms of the technical […]
full_text: A quick story to illustrate how to look at the Cleveland Browns’ run game : As someone who is into the gaming culture (video games to be exact), I never had a reason to buy a personal computer for gaming purposes. Reasons? It’s far too expensive, and it’s just too complex in terms of the technical aspects of it. One of my friends I went to college with bought a PC, but recently he had to get it fixed. Originally, he thought about going to buy another one and spend more money. Instead, he decided to go to Geek Squad to figure out the cause of the problem. To sum it up, he had to buy three new parts instead of buying a new computer. The Cleveland Browns running game has been broken since last year, and head coach Todd Monken has been tasked with fixing it. So far, the running game is still an issue , but to be fair, that isn’t new. However, it isn’t broken beyond repair. LeCharles Bentley recently wrote an article discussing the run game issues in Cleveland and how it can be fixed. The article makes valid points. After doing my own research and watching the All-22 film, Bentley is right: the running game can be salvaged. However, it’s not something that can be fixed overnight. It’s a process. Processes take time; success will not happen instantly. The Browns running game isn’t broken beyond repair; here’s how to fix it: Get rid of Outside Zone run concepts (for now) It’s temporary, but until Cleveland has the personnel to run it, the outside zone running plays should be scrapped from the playbook. The reason for it is that the team doesn’t have another in-blocking tight end on the roster right now (more on that later). Running back Quinshon Judkins doesn’t appear to have his explosiveness back after having surgery on his fibula and ankle. It might take some time for his explosiveness to come back, but when he has enough space on the edge, he can make something happen. It’s only temporary, but the outside zone runs just aren’t working right now. More inside zone, gap runs Looking at the makeup of this current running back room, the room is diverse in terms of the archetypes, but recently the team brought in running back Audric Estime. Estime is more of a north-south runner, and the running game had a bit of a different feel when Estime was in. Re-watching the tape from Sunday, the Browns found some form of success when they decided to run inside the guards and tackles: More inside zone, I don’t ask for much pic.twitter.com/6J3EA33r7H — Curt (@curtiss_brown21) October 20, 2026 Monken’s running game found some success running inside zone because the team can gain consistent yards from running it. The running lanes have to be more consistent in terms of opening holes, but overall the team should lean into more inside zone concepts. Less Under-Center, diversify being in shotgun Monken said this last week about running under center versus operating out of shotgun in terms of the running game: Browns coach Todd Monken gave great insight today on the benefits of running the ball under center versus shotgun. 📹: @AshNoelleTV https://t.co/bll99A8cgv pic.twitter.com/801Z03LZk5 — Daniel Oyefusi (@DanielOyefusi) October 14, 2026 Monken makes valid points. As for quarterback Deshaun Watson, he claims he doesn’t have a preference in terms of what he wants to run but also stated that many QB’s are comfortable running out of shotgun than going under center. Monken and Watson are right in their own ways, but the reality is the Browns need less under center work. Why? It’s simple. Watson has never been comfortable running under center; he’s more tailored to playing in shotgun (which is something he’s thrived in most of his career.). Some would argue that Shedeur Sanders could operate under center better than Watson, but that’s not the case either. Sanders spent most if not his entire career playing in shotgun and found success during his tenure in Colorado. However, his rookie season he struggled playing under center as this was a learning curve for him. Both quarterbacks have their difficulties in processing and neither are proficient in running under center better than shotgun. As far as operating under shotgun, Cleveland needs to diversify. As much as fans disagree with it, the team can operate out of shotgun but the problem is they are predictable. To be less predictable, the Browns should incorporate more motion in their offense and try to make the defense work instead of making their jobs easier. The linebackers are often keying easily on the Browns running game because they are reading the mesh point of the running backs. Trade or sign for a blocker tight end As mentioned earlier, Cleveland does not have a reliable blocking tight end on this roster. Tight end Harold Fannin Jr isn’t the best blocker, but he’s a willing one. Forcing Fannin to block is also keeping him out of pass routes more as well. However, most of the blocking issues stem from Fannin and his lack of focus, along with some physical limitations, as well as Blake Whiteheart being asked to do more than he should. If the Browns want to fix their running issues, trading for or signing a tight end could be beneficial. It would allow the running game to be much more easier to run because you have someone that can help the running offense and it allows you to run under center more effectively. A list of names that the team should look into: Los Angeles Rams TE Davis Allen Houston Texans TE Cade Stover FA TE Will Dissly New Orleans Saints TE Noah Fant ( Editor’s note: Wonder if lining FB Michael Burton up as a tight end or offset wing player more could help?) The Browns had tight end targets that they wanted in the draft but they were sniped by other teams (New Orleans Saints taking Oscar Delp was one of those names they were interested in). In-blocker tight end helps a lot and the Browns need that. Overall, the Browns running game has been broken going back to last season but it’s not broken beyond repair. However, the team can make moves in the short term that can benefit later in the year without having to overhaul the entire scheme. title: 3 Browns players stepping up for the rest of the season would make the biggest impact
summary: The Cleveland Browns have had an exciting start to the season that has exceeded expectations for what they could do as a team. As the season progresses and the team builds on what it has accomplished so far, certain players will need to step up and play a major role in the team’s success. Deshaun Watson […]
full_text: The Cleveland Browns have had an exciting start to the season that has exceeded expectations for what they could do as a team. As the season progresses and the team builds on what it has accomplished so far, certain players will need to step up and play a major role in the team’s success. Deshaun Watson will need to begin to put together more complete games. While he has been successful in several fourth-quarter game-winning drives this season, he has struggled to find consistency in the passing game through the first three quarters. He recorded just 84 passing yards through the first three quarters against the Baltimore Ravens but threw for 94 yards in the fourth quarter alone. The Browns’ run game, both the running backs and the offensive line, will need to keep improving. Cleveland’s leading rusher, Jaleel McLaughlin , had just 9 rushing attempts for 41 yards in the win over the Ravens. With Quinshon Judkins battling an ankle injury, the rest of the Browns’ running backs will need to step up. On the defensive side of the ball, Jared Verse needs to continue to develop his role as a leader within the group. Although he has consistently pressured opposing quarterbacks this season, he has yet to record a sack. It will be important for him to start making big plays and taking over games. Let me know what you think in the comments – Which player needs to step up for the rest of the season?

full_text: Linebacker DeMarvion Overshown is set to make his return to the Dallas Cowboys on Monday, which will give a struggling defense a much-needed boost. Roster upgrades are something that the Cowboys could use, and team owner Jerry Jones is adamant about being active in that regard. Speaking of adding to the roster, Dallas has been linked to Cardinals pass rusher Josh Sweat. Also, a sputtering Cowboys’ offense is searching for answers after consecutive bad performances. With more adversity behind him, DeMarvion Overshown ready to prove himself again – Nick Harris, Fort Worth Star-Telegram DeMarvion Overshown hasn’t played since Week 1 due to a hamstring injury. Now that he’s cleared to return against the Eagles on Monday, he’s ready to get back to making plays. What was initially thought to be a two-to-three week issue turned into five games missed for the season’s starting MIKE linebacker, but Overshown has continued to be the same person he has been during his entire tenure in Dallas: level, measured and carrying a smile on his face wherever he goes. “I’ve been taking it day-by-day, it’s really all you can do with stuff like this,” Overshown said. “I’m blessed. Of course, I want to be out there with my teammates, but then again, it’s just about being thankful about what you do have. What I do have not playing football is a loving and caring family. I do have a team that supports me and understands that I’m doing whatever I can to get back on the field.” A ‘disappointed’ Jerry Jones would like to improve Cowboys’ roster before trade deadline – Jon Machota and Mike Jones, The Athletic The Cowboys are off to a rough start in 2026. Team owner Jerry Jones is willing to make another roster move to assist in turning things around. “I don’t have a specific (trade),” he said, “but certainly I’ll be real clear, I would be active if we could get a chance to help the team this year. So, that’s important, I think.” Is there any scenario where the Cowboys would be sellers at the trade deadline? “No, no, I don’t see that,” Jones said. “But I don’t rule it out now. If somebody comes along and offers you one of those deals, like the one I made a year or so ago, then it’s just too much.” Can Cowboys’ returning defenders help ease pressure on rookies Downs, Barham – Calvin Watkins, Dallas Morning News With DeMarvion Overshown and Cobie Durant returning to the lineup, Jaishawn Barham and Caleb Downs won’t have as much on their plates in terms of responsibility. Barham was thrust into a position he might not be equipped to handle so soon. Yet, the Cowboys have confidence in his abilities to make plays. It seems Overshown will play the weakside linebacker spot upon his return. Barham and Overshown are a better combination at linebacker than Barham and Dee Winters. “I don’t know how it’s going to play out,” Overshown said. “I’m going to be out there, that’s enough for me. title: Why we should continue rooting for the Cowboys to turn things around
summary: The Dallas Cowboys had Super Bowl aspirations entering the 2026 NFL season and that shouldn’t change despite their overall poor play to start the year, which has resulted in a 2-4 record through the first six weeks. This is a team that has the talent to turn things around and every reason to do so […]
full_text: Photo by Patrick McDermott/Getty Images | Getty Images The Dallas Cowboys had Super Bowl aspirations entering the 2026 NFL season and that shouldn’t change despite their overall poor play to start the year, which has resulted in a 2-4 record through the first six weeks. This is a team that has the talent to turn things around and every reason to do so due to the unique situation they find themselves in. First off, the Cowboys are still very much in the playoff race due to the poor state of the NFC East division. For the second week in a row, all four teams in the NFC East failed to win, leaving the division up for grabs. Despite disappointing at every turn so for this year, Dallas is still somehow considered the favorite by many to be the division champs. As long as their playoff hopes are still alive, we can fully expect Jerry Jones and Company to do everything within their power to turn things around. That means another big trade could be in play before the November 10 deadline as well as them sticking with and remaining patient with Brian Schottenheimer, despite his questionable coaching/decision-making. As much as many of us would like to see Schottenheimer replaced after his many coaching gaffs, that seems highly unlikely given the state of the NFC East division and the possibility of the Cowboys coming out on top. After all, who would step in to replace him? Klayton Adams? He is supposedly an up-and-coming HC candidate, but even he’s an unproven one. Another reason to keep rooting for the Cowboys to turn things around and finish strong has to do with draft positioning. They currently hold two first-round selections in the 2027 NFL Draft, but the higher of the two belongs to the New York Jets as part of the trade package for Quinnen Williams. As things stand right now that would be the sixth and 27 th overall picks, the latter of which is from the Green Bay Packers for Micah Parsons. How the Packers end the things is completely out of the Cowboys control. They could continue to string wins together, make the playoffs, or perhaps even the Super Bowl. That would put their first-round pick in the latter part of the round. What they can control is how they finish the season, preferably as a playoff team or even better as a Super Bowl champion. That way the difference between the Cowboys and Packers first-round picks is minimal at best. No one wants to see the Cowboys part with a Top 10 selection as things currently stand. That would just be rubbing salt in an open, festering wound after suffering through in another disappointing season. That would be the ultimate gut punch. While the Cowboys may be disappointing us at nearly every turn so for this year, there is still reason to root for them to turn things around and finish strong. All of the pieces, at least most of them, seem to be in place. It’s up to them to start executing and playing better. For the sake for mental health, all of us are probably hoping they can do so. Where are you on the season? Have you packed it in already? Or are you rooting for the turnaround?

title: Cowboys defense 2nd-half performance vs Packers brings hope
summary: The Dallas Cowboys defense wasn’t the reason the team lost to the Packers on Sunday night. But they still weren’t good enough. Team stats allowed The Cowboys allowed 23 points to the Packers, 17 of which came in the first half. They tightened up after halftime, surrendering just six points on five qualifying drives. Jordan […]
full_text: Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images The Dallas Cowboys defense wasn’t the reason the team lost to the Packers on Sunday night. But they still weren’t good enough. Team stats allowed The Cowboys allowed 23 points to the Packers, 17 of which came in the first half. They tightened up after halftime, surrendering just six points on five qualifying drives. Jordan Love threw for 276 yards with one touchdown and one interception In the first half, the Packers went nine-of-ten on 3rd down. Green Bay held the ball for nearly 15 minutes on two drives in the first half, resulting in 10 points. Individual stat leaders on defense Caleb Downs led the team in tackles with 12, six of which were solo. But many came after giving up a pass reception. Kenny Clark, Quinnen Williams, and Elijah Garcia each finished the game with a sack. Dee Winters secured the Cowboys’ first interception of the season, initially finishing with a pick-six that would eventually be called back and ruled down by contact. Advanced analytics According to SumerSports, the Cowboys finished with their best EPA/play allowed rating of the season at -0.02. This was the first time this season they forced an opponent into a negative EPA per play. Dee Winters, Quinnen Williams, and Justin Barron were the three highest-rated players on the Cowboys defense, per Pro Football Focus. Jordan Love was pressured on 45.5% of his drop backs per Next Gen Stats . Rashan Gary was credited with a career-high 10 pressures against his former team. How’d the rookies look? Caleb Downs finished with a team-leading 12 tackles, but many came after giving up a completion. He was placed in the slot throughout the night and covered Matthew Golden often. Downs is not a pure cover corner and the Packers were unafraid to throw his direction when he was matched up one-on-one in the slot. The first year safety allowed six catches on six targets on the night. Malachi Lawrence had his first career start, replacing second-year edge Donovan Ezeiruaku on the depth chart. He finished with zero tackles and zero sacks, but did record a pass breakup over 20 yards downfield in the endzone. He was part of a unit that recorded three sacks on the night and dealt pressure on the quarterback, but did not show up on the stat sheet. Jaishawn Barham finished the game with four solo tackles. The linebacker missed a key tackle on third-and-twelve on the Packers first drive, resulting in a first down. That was a four-point play, as the Packers would go on to score a touchdown instead of a field goal. LT Overton played 22 defensive snaps but did not show up in the box score. Final grade: C The first half was brutal for the defense, specifically on third down. Because of the continuous barrage of third-down conversions, the Packers had two scoring drives chewing up nearly 15 minutes combined. It didn’t matter how far the first-down marker was, every Green Bay third down was converted until the 6:46 mark in the second quarter. The Cowboys defense did record an interception during that time but unfortunately the pick-six was ruled down by contact and led to zero points. If that first half performance continued into the second half, the grade would have been an F for this week. Maybe even an F- (or lower if possible). But this defense flipped the script in the second half. After the break, the Cowboys defense allowed only two field goals for the remainder of the game. They battened down the hatches on third down, allowing just two conversions. And the Packers gained a total of 83 yards. For comparison’s sake, the Packers gained 90 yards on their first drive of the game. Now maybe you could say the Packers were content with taking their foot off the gas in the second half. There were also some key drops by Packers receivers in or around the endzone. But at the end of the day, the second half performance was night and day compared to the first half. The defense did not lose this game for the Cowboys. They tightened up and got right, allowing the offense multiple opportunities to make a comeback. They recorded three sacks, one interception, and for the first time this season, forced an opponent into a negative EPA/play. For those reasons, they receive a ‘C’ on their report card this week.
