summary: There is a point in every disappointing season when the conversation shifts from how a team can make the playoffs to whether it has any realistic chance of competing at all. After another lifeless start and a 23-13 loss to the Green Bay Packers, the Dallas Cowboys are getting dangerously close to that point. At […]
full_text: Mandatory Credit: Jeff Hanisch-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect There is a point in every disappointing season when the conversation shifts from how a team can make the playoffs to whether it has any realistic chance of competing at all. After another lifeless start and a 23-13 loss to the Green Bay Packers, the Dallas Cowboys are getting dangerously close to that point. At 2-4, with consecutive losses to Tampa Bay and Green Bay, this team looks less like a playoff contender and more like one that could be picking near the top of the 2027 NFL Draft… if they had that pick. Instead, the New York Jets would likely have it for the Quinnen Williams trade unless the Green Bay Packers fall apart and the one Dallas got in the Micah Parsons trade is even higher up. That is a brutal place to be for a team with Dak Prescott, CeeDee Lamb, George Pickens and an offense that entered Week 6 averaging 27.6 points per game. Yet the Cowboys have scored just 29 points combined in their last two games. They were held scoreless in the first half at Lambeau Field for the first time since November 2021, and the offense looked completely out of answers when Green Bay turned up the pressure. Questioning the heart of football players is usually a foolish take. The desire to be a great team, however, doesn’t seem to show up consistently, particularly in the details that separate winning teams from losing ones. The discipline is missing, the adjustments are not translating into better football, and the leaders have not found a way to pull everyone out of this spiral, which feels like it has been going on since the last time the Cowboys made the playoffs in 2023. I wonder who that team lost to? The same mistakes keep showing up Good teams will lose games on the road. The Cowboys faced familiar problems and took extra time to regroup after their defeat in Tampa Bay. On Sunday, Dallas committed 11 penalties for 108 yards against Green Bay, reinforcing a season-long concern about discipline. Penalties extend opposing drives, put the offense behind the chains and erase opportunities for a team that cannot afford to give away free yardage. The defense did show some signs of improvement. Dallas held Green Bay to 57 rushing yards, recorded three sacks and kept the Packers out of the end zone in the second half. Joey Porter Jr. has brought a physical presence to the secondary, and there were stretches when the Cowboys made Jordan Love uncomfortable. But the improvement remains inconsistent, and one of the defense’s biggest problems returned: third-down defense. Green Bay converted 11 of 18 third-down attempts, including nine of its first ten. The Packers repeatedly extended drives that should have ended, controlling the pace of the game and keeping Dallas’ offense on the sideline. On the opening touchdown drive alone, Green Bay converted four third downs, twice overcoming third-and-13. Teams are now converting 50% of 3rd and 9+ attempts against the Cowboys this season. League average is 21.8% @1053thefan — Bobby Belt (@BobbyBeltTX) October 19, 2026 That is how a defense can make individual plays and still fail to do its job. A sack or a tackle for loss means little if the opponent converts the next third down and keeps marching toward the end zone. Porter and the rest of the secondary can provide encouraging individual performances, but coverage and pressure must work together. The Cowboys cannot keep asking their defensive backs to hold up indefinitely while opposing offenses convert in the situations that should favor the defense. There is progress to acknowledge, but progress without consistency does not win games. Brian Schottenheimer has to turn accountability into results Brian Schottenheimer and QB Dak Prescott are starting to sound like broken records after taking responsibility for the offense’s shortcomings. Don’t get it twisted; that is the appropriate response from a head coach and a franchise quarterback. Neither should point fingers at teammates or make excuses for another loss. But accepting responsibility is the first step, not the finish line. It seems the Cowboys have been back to square one for a while now. Schottenheimer’s play-calling continues to raise serious questions. Dallas rushed for just 48 yards on 15 carries, while Prescott attempted 54 passes. After Javonte Williams scored the Cowboys’ first touchdown early in the third quarter, Dallas ran the ball only once more. Schottenheimer acknowledged the imbalance wasn’t part of the plan, but that explanation only reinforces the problem: whatever the plan is, the Cowboys aren’t executing it or adapting effectively when the game changes. Brian Schottenheimer is broken pic.twitter.com/I1hQoHGVFi — Zac (@Zac_LeeDM) October 19, 2026 Some of that imbalance stemmed from Dallas falling behind 17-0 at halftime. That’s important to note, but it doesn’t explain the broader offensive struggles, especially since the team had nearly two weeks of preparation between games and still came out flat. Prescott finished with 258 passing yards, one touchdown and two interceptions. He was pressured 21 times, and his two first-half interceptions helped Green Bay build its lead. The offensive line struggled to protect him; the running game never established itself, and the play-calling failed to provide a consistent answer against Green Bay’s pressure. That fourth-down throw late in the game was another painful example. Facing a fourth-and-11 at the Packers’ 14-yard line, Prescott heaved the ball toward the end zone under heavy pressure, but the pass sailed out of bounds. The situation was desperate, and the pressure was real, but the play ended without giving his receivers a realistic chance to make a play. dak prescott throws it out on 4th down pic.twitter.com/sFUtVM3uhY — wok (@wokdior) October 19, 2026 Prescott does not deserve all the blame for the loss. He was under pressure much of the night, and the offense around him wasn’t good enough. Still, franchise quarterbacks are expected to lead when things get difficult. That means making better decisions, helping the offense settle down and finding ways to keep the team alive when the game is slipping away. The same standard applies to Schottenheimer. A coach can own the mistakes after a loss, but if the same mistakes keep happening, accountability starts to ring hollow. Dallas has heard the explanations. Now it needs to see meaningful changes in the game plan, the execution and the results. This team cannot get all three phases right at the same time The most frustrating part of the Cowboys’ season thus far is how rarely the pieces seem to work together. When the offense is producing, the defense has struggled to stop anybody. When the defense shows signs of life, the offense disappears. Against Green Bay, Dallas’ defense improved after halftime, allowing just six points and generating pressure, but the offense could not capitalize on the opportunity to make the game competitive. The first half was the clearest illustration. Dallas failed to score, Prescott threw two interceptions, and Green Bay built a 17-0 lead. The Cowboys had opportunities to change the momentum, including a defensive interception by linebacker Dee Winters, but the offense immediately gave the ball back, in the red zone no less. It was Dallas’ first interception of the season, a welcome development that nevertheless came amid another frustrating night for the team as a whole. Even the late touchdown did little to change the overall picture. Ryan Flournoy’s six-yard score cut the deficit to 10 points with less than a minute remaining, but the Cowboys failed on the two-point conversion. By then, too many possessions had been wasted and too many mistakes had accumulated. The game had been long over. Green Bay wasn’t flawless, but the Packers made the plays that mattered, and Dallas didn’t. That is the difference between a team that can recover from a rough stretch and one that keeps digging itself…
author: Jorge Guajardo

title: Cowboys trade rumor: Dallas linked to Cardinals pass rusher Josh Sweat
summary: The Dallas Cowboys are being connected to yet another trade rumor. ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler mentioned on Wednesday that the Cowboys could be interested in Arizona Cardinals pass rusher Josh Sweat. It is worth mentioning that Dallas hosts Arizona next Sunday afternoon. The Cowboys might have one more move in them. Perhaps that’s shortsighted, given their […]
full_text: Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images | Getty Images The Dallas Cowboys are being connected to yet another trade rumor. ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler mentioned on Wednesday that the Cowboys could be interested in Arizona Cardinals pass rusher Josh Sweat. It is worth mentioning that Dallas hosts Arizona next Sunday afternoon. The Cowboys might have one more move in them. Perhaps that’s shortsighted, given their 2-4 record. But that might as well be 4-4 in this season’s NFC East climate, where no commodity is proven and Philly’s transitional state has cracked the door open. As one team exec pointed out to me Tuesday, Josh Sweat to Dallas makes a lot of sense. He fits Dallas’ profile, and the Cowboys need edge-rush help. Sweat’s Cardinals won S u nday , but they are not contention-adjacent just yet. Sweat has been linked to the Packers, too, but Green Bay has Micah Parsons returning eventually. Fowler even notes in his report here that the Cowboys executing this move, hypothetically, could be viewed as shortsighted as the Cowboys are a pair of games below .500 this season. All is fair in the crummy NFC East, though. While the Cowboys certainly need help at pass rusher, the other reason this could be viewed as shortsighted may be the more important one. Following their trade for Joey Porter Jr. a couple of weeks ago, the Cowboys are pretty low on draft capital for 2027 . Round 1: The Cowboys own a first-round pick, but it is the worse of theirs and Green Bay’s. Dallas has Green Bay’s by way of the Micah Parsons trade, but they owe the better of the pair to the New York Jets as a result of the Quinnen Williams trade. 2: The Cowboys own their second-round pick. This is the easiest one in the entire discussion. 4: While the Cowboys do own a fourth-round pick, it is not their original one. They own Pittsburgh’s fourth-rounder as it came to them in the Broderick Jones trade. 7: Similarly, the Cowboys do not own their original seventh-round pick. The one that they have came to them by way of the Nate Thomas trade. That deal happened with the Houston Texans, but Houston held the pick by way of the New England Patriots. The Cowboys hardly have assets to give away next season as is, although they could obviously find a way to accrue some more in the offseason. You get the point, though. Should the Cowboys be in on this? Maybe only if they go on a winning streak of sorts? What do you think?
author: RJ Ochoa

title: Cowboys ‘run it back’ attitude on offense is starting to stumble
summary: The Dallas Cowboys are 2-4 through six games, adding reasons for failure and areas of blame faster than they can add wins to the dub column. Losing 23-13 at Lambeau Field on Sunday night to the Green Bay Packers, the Cowboys lost back-to-back games while failing to score at least 20 points in either of […]
full_text: Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images | Getty Images The Dallas Cowboys are 2-4 through six games, adding reasons for failure and areas of blame faster than they can add wins to the dub column. Losing 23-13 at Lambeau Field on Sunday night to the Green Bay Packers, the Cowboys lost back-to-back games while failing to score at least 20 points in either of them (when both games were started by Dak Prescott) for the first time since 2019. The loss puts the Cowboys at risk of potentially going a full calendar year without consecutive wins, last doing so in 2025 on November 17th and 23rd. Right now, this is the defining trend of the Brian Schottenheimer era, and the start of figuring out why this team is falling so short on lofty expectations yet again. Every single team that made the playoffs a year ago had a winning streak of at least three games during their regular season, something Schottenheimer’s done exactly once. Twelve of the 14 teams had a streak of four games or longer. Both Super Bowl participants had the longest streaks in their respective conferences. The last three Cowboys teams to make the playoffs from 2021-23 had streaks of six games, four, and five. As obvious as it may be, there is evidence that measurable consistency is a tangible trait of teams that are contenders not pretenders. All of us likely got ahead of ourselves wanting this team to end the two year playoff drought in 2026, but just showing any consistency would be keeping the horse in front of the cart. Coach Schottenheimer got a bit of a pass on this metric at large from his debut season because Matt Eberflus’ defense was only consistently terrible, and never competitive. This does not excuse the Cowboys from not properly accounting for if Schotty could keep the offense consistently performing while they went “all in” on a defensive makeover, and now the organization is paying the cost of having more holes in the boat than patches – seeing the defense, offense, and special teams all have a hand in ugly losses. More simply put, the Cowboys “run it back” approach to hyping up all 11 starters returning on offense as a huge positive is not working, and this is another thing we’ve seen before as fans. Whenever proper attention isn’t given to any one position group or facet of the game at large in the offseason, they regress to the point of being a problem. To bring in another team for comparison on the “run it back” model, the Denver Broncos under Sean Payton are exhibiting that at a master-class level this season. Jaylen Waddle was literally their only significant offseason acquisition to add to the starting lineup on either side of the ball. The Broncos offense has struggled mightily, but have already made a play-caller change to go back to HC Sean Payton after OC Davis Webb started the year. The Cowboys have only given more and more votes of confidence towards the entire job Schottenheimer is doing, which has included calling the offense since day one even though he never did so as Mike McCarthy’s OC. The Broncos also have a win against a really good Jaguars team on their record, a big comeback win against the Rams, and most recently beat the defending Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks. They’ve overcome obstacles and showed a fight to win the Cowboys just flat out don’t have right now. The scope of just how much Brian Schottenheimer’s scheming, play-calling, and overall managing of the offense this season mattered in the big picture for this team does not feel like something that was handled well in the offseason. The low hanging fruit of a take on the job he did in these areas in 2025 was that everything offensively was under too much fire because of the horrid defense, so all things considered because of that he did alright. Last time out, the Cowboys defense held the Packers to six points in the second half, and the Cowboys still abandoned the run game and didn’t make much noise in a comeback attempt. The Cowboys offense banked on experience to be dominant in 2026, but they’re paying an ultimate cost right now for an underperforming head coach and play-caller dragging the entire ceiling this team has down in a division that’s never, ever been more winnable.
author: Sean Martin

title: Besides 3rd-down issues, the Cowboys defense had some success
summary: The Dallas Cowboys didn’t have what it took to leave Lambeau with the win on Sunday night, falling to the Green Bay Packers, 23-13. While the loss is unpleasant, there were some things we can come out of this game and feel better about. Oddly enough, they’re on the defensive side of the ball. Initially, […]
full_text: Photo by Patrick McDermott/Getty Images | Getty Images The Dallas Cowboys didn’t have what it took to leave Lambeau with the win on Sunday night, falling to the Green Bay Packers, 23-13. While the loss is unpleasant, there were some things we can come out of this game and feel better about. Oddly enough, they’re on the defensive side of the ball. Initially, it was frustrating for the Cowboys defense. They made some great plays on first down, often creating 2nd-and-10 or longer situations, and they would hold up okay on second down. But then, the bottom fell out. Again and again, the defense buckled on the money down, allowing the Packers to convert on third down. It was a total breakdown, and it just kept happening. But they did get better as the game went on. The defense allowed the Packers to convert 9/10 on third down in the first half, but that dropped to just 2/8 in the second half. That’s a significant improvement. While they struggled getting off the field in the first half, the defense as a whole did well in many areas. Their run defense was great. Granted, the Packers are one of the worst run offenses in the league, but the Cowboys shut them down. Even in a favorable game script for them, Green Bay only finished with 57 total rushing yards, and averaged just 2.2 yards per carry. Quinnen Williams was overpowering blockers and shutting down rushing lanes. He and Kenny Clark controlled the interior of the trenches, and both came away with a sack, as did fellow defensive tackle Elijah Garcia. All three of these sacks were aided by pressure created by Rashan Gary. Overall, the pressure from the defensive front was good at times, but when they sent more defenders at Love, he usually found a wide-open target somewhere. Dee Winters came away with the defensive play of the game with the team’s lone interception of the year. He was brought over to Dallas for his coverage ability, and it was nice to see it finally pay off. It’s a shame he was touched, a pick-six could have shifted the momentum a bit. The Cowboys offense then gave the ball right back shortly thereafter. Speaking of coverage, it’s hard not to be pleased with what Joey Porter Jr. has given the team so far. Not only did this no-tackling corner make a great tackle right out of the gate, but he did what he’s touted to do, which is provide smothering coverage and break up passes. He did both of those things. Even Malachi Lawrence showed some unexpected coverage skills by getting downfield and having the ball slightly graze off his hands just enough to cause an incompletion in the end zone. Whether it’s Porter Jr. or Lawrence, that’s two last-second deflections that saved a touchdown. The Cowboys’ improvement resulted in allowing just six points in the second half, and 23 points total. That’s pretty decent. In the second half, the Packers had five drives and two of them resulted in field goals, and one of those happened when Green Bay started in Cowboys territory after the Dallas offense turned the ball over on downs. The other three drives the Packers had resulted in a net yardage total of just five yards. Two of those drives were three-and-outs and netted negative yards. That’s a great second-half showing. There were certainly a lot of plays the defense wishes they could have back, but this group also made more impact plays in this game than we’ve seen in a while. There was a more all-hands-on-deck feel as more players were helping out in the run game, and Porter Jr.‘s play finally gave them some much-needed support in coverage. It was definitely something to build off of going forward. It feels like the Cowboys' defense had more impact plays last night than they've had in all five of their prior games combined. That's a good sign. pic.twitter.com/iypQIrfR2X — Dan Rogers (@DannyPhantom24) October 19, 2026
author: Dan Rogers

title: Cowboys news: Dallas waives former fifth-round pick
summary: The Dallas Cowboys have struggled with health in their secondary all season. On Tuesday, they decided Caelen Carson was no longer in the mix. While it opened a roster spot for Juanyeh Thomas, it could also mean Cobie Durant returns to the field soon. Cowboys sign S Juanyeh Thomas to active roster, waive CB Caelen […]
full_text: Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images | Getty Images The Dallas Cowboys have struggled with health in their secondary all season. On Tuesday, they decided Caelen Carson was no longer in the mix. While it opened a roster spot for Juanyeh Thomas, it could also mean Cobie Durant returns to the field soon. Cowboys sign S Juanyeh Thomas to active roster, waive CB Caelen Carson – Tommy Yarrish, DallasCowboys.com Juanyeh Thomas is officially back on the 53-man roster after a few weeks on the practice squad. Over the course of his three previous seasons with Dallas, Thomas played in 36 games, including starting three in 2025, and posted 62 tackles, five pass breakups and a forced fumble. Most of his work over that time has come on special teams, including 65 snaps there through three games played in 2026. In 2024, the Cowboys drafted Carson in the fifth round of the 2024 NFL Draft out of Wake Forest. Over the course of the last three seasons, Carson played in 17 games and started eight for Dallas. Carson tallied 45 career tackles, a tackle for loss and six pass breakups in that time span. Cowboys have gone away from these key things that once sparked optimism in Dallas’ offense – Joseph Hoyt, Dallas Morning News It’s unsettling how the Cowboys abandoned the run game versus the Green Bay Packers Sunday’s game was never really out of hand from a scoring perspective, however. Still, that didn’t keep the Cowboys from doing something they’ve done a lot this season: abandon the running game. The Cowboys finished with 54 passes compared to 15 running attempts. They had only one rushing attempt in the fourth quarter. Last year, the Cowboys were 16th in rushing attempts. This year, they’re 31st. After Sunday’s game, quarterback Dak Prescott said the Cowboys shouldn’t lose offensive balance when the game is still manageable. Download the SB Nation app today! Fewer ads Seamlessly jump between communities and conversations Faster commenting and posting experience! Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android . DeMarvion Overshown to return vs. Eagles on MNF – Patrik Walker, DallasCowboys.com With Dee Winters expected to miss some time, DeMarvion Overshown’s return is vital for the defense. Expect Overshown to operate on a pitch count as he ramps back up, but he is beyond excited to return with plenty of football left on the Cowboys’ 2026 schedule, and in a wide-open NFC East. “We play on Monday, so now I’ve got to wait an extra day, but I’m excited,” he said. “I’ve definitely taken this rehab, this recovery, very serious. I’ve been trying to get back on the field since the week after I got out. Getting this opportunity to go this week, I’m thankful that I’m still able to get to do what I love.” Eagles cut former Cowboys RB in flurry of roster moves – Johnny McGonigal, PennLive.com Former Cowboys RB Jaydon Blue won’t get his chance at a revenge game on Monday Night Football. The Eagles have waived former Cowboys running back Jaydon Blue, the team announced Tuesday. Blue initially joined Steele and Pierce on the Eagles’ practice squad, where he remained for most of this season. Blue was signed to the active roster after Jalen Hurts landed on IR with blood clots. Blue did not log any carries or offensive snaps in Sunday’s loss to the Carolina Panthers. 5 things to know about the Philadelphia Eagles ahead of Week 7 matchup with Dallas Cowboys – Abraham Nudelstejer, Dallas Morning News Here’s what you need to know about the Eagles and where things stand behind enemy lines. Offense in disarray Sean Mannion is in his first season as the Eagles’ offensive coordinator, and Sirianni has already spoken out in his defense to dispel rumors that he could be fired. At his news conference Monday, Sirianni defended Mannion. “I have a high confidence level in everybody in this building,” Sirianni said. “Sean, that’s why I hired him. Right now, we are in a rough spot, as we know. And so it is about controlling the things you can control in this moment and figuring out what the next steps are. I think we gotta find out what the things are that we have to get better at and what we do well.”

title: NFL picks and predictions: Broncos vs. Cardinals and the rest of Week 7
summary: Welcome back to the seventh installment of Hart’s Picks for the 2026 NFL regular season. For Week 6—I picked just 7 of 14 games right. The only winners I chose correctly were the Patriots, Bears, Panthers, Steelers, Chiefs, Bills, and 49ers. It was a pretty wild slate of games with some major upsets. Let’s see […]
full_text: DENVER, COLORADO - OCTOBER 15: Head coach Sean Payton of the Denver Broncos shakes hands with head coach Mike MacDonald of the Seattle Seahawks after their overtime win in the game at Empower Field At Mile High on October 15, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Andrew Wevers/Getty Images) | Getty Images Welcome back to the seventh installment of Hart’s Picks for the 2026 NFL regular season. For Week 6 —I picked just 7 of 14 games right. The only winners I chose correctly were the Patriots, Bears, Panthers, Steelers, Chiefs, Bills, and 49ers. It was a pretty wild slate of games with some major upsets. Let’s see if I can do any better this week. There are only 14 games again this week with the Bills, Jaguars, Chargers, and Commanders on their bye weeks. New England Patriots at Chicago Bears — Thursday Night Football This is an interesting matchup to start Week 7. The Patriots head to Chicago with a three-game winning streak, but a lot of injuries to deal with. Chicago, now 4-2 on the season, is dealing with their fair share of injuries as well. A tough game to predict, but I’ll be going with the Bears at home. I think their defensive pressure package will force Drake Maye into some bad decisions. Winner: Bears Pittsburgh Steelers at New Orleans Saints — Sunday (Morning Game) This Week 7 matchup for the morning game will be played in Saint-Denis, France. The Steelers are 4-2 and the Saints are 2-4. I’ll give the edge to Aaron Rodgers and Pittsburgh in this one. I think their offense can be more consistent going up against one of the worst defenses in the NFL. Winner: Steelers San Francisco 49ers at Atlanta Falcons — Sunday (Early Game) The 49ers remain unbeaten and the Falcons have dropped two straight. For San Francisco to be undefeated with all their injuries is quite impressive. Wide receiver Mike Evans will miss some time after coming up with an Achilles injury in their win over the Commanders on Monday Night Football . Even so, I think the 49ers will find a way to win. Winner: 49ers Cincinnati Bengals at Baltimore Ravens — Sunday (Early Game) This AFC North matchup has some big implications. Every team has two losses this year, but the Bengals are in pursuit of their fourth win. They struggle to defend the run, which might be an issue facing Derrick Henry, but I think Joe Burrow and his high-powered offense can find a way to topple the Ravens on the road. Winner: Bengals Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Carolina Panthers — Sunday (Early Game) The Panthers sit atop the NFC South with a 3-2 record and the Buccaneers are in last place at 1-4. It’ll be the first divisional matchup for Tampa Bay this season. It’s basically a must-win game to keep any hopes at making the postseason alive. However, I think Bryce Young and the Panthers can do enough on offense to earn their fourth win in front of a hometown crowd. Winner: Panthers New York Giants at Houston Texans — Sunday (Early Game) The Texans started off the season in a 0-4 tailspin, but have reeled off two victories in a row. I like their odds of getting a third straight win taking on the Giants at home. If they can achieve that, the battle for the AFC South will continue to heat up if the Jaguars continue to falter. Winner: Texans Indianapolis Colts at Minnesota Vikings — Sunday (Early Game) Chris Ballard is out as GM of the Colts after their Week 6 loss to the Tennessee Titans who were winless going into that matchup. Meanwhile, the Vikings enter Sunday’s matchup coming off a bye sporting a 5-0 record thanks to a tremendous defense. I’ll be taking Minnesota. Winner: Vikings Miami Dolphins at New York Jets — Sunday (Early Game) This AFC East affair is probably the most boring game of Week 7. The Dolphins are one of two teams (including the Chargers) that remain winless. The Jets aren’t a great team either at 2-4, but I think they will be able to perform well enough to keep the Dolphins from earning their first win of the season. Winner: Jets Cleveland Browns at Tennesee Titans — Sunday (Early Game) The Browns, even with a struggling offense, are finding a way to win football games. They are 4-2 and the current leaders of the AFC North. I certainly didn’t see that coming. The Titans, now 1-5, found a way to topple the Colts in Week 6. However, I think Todd Monken and his squad will find another way to gut out a tough victory. Winner: Browns Green Bay Packers at Detroit Lions — Sunday (Afternoon Game) This is a classic NFC North rivalry matchup. The Packers have been impressive winning three in a row and the Lions are coming off an early bye. Detroit has scored a lot of points, but their defense still has some issues. However, I think the extra week of preparation bodes well for them. I’ll take Detroit at home in this one. Winner: Lions Los Angeles Rams at Las Vegas Raiders — Sunday (Afternoon Game) Things just keep getting worse for the Rams. They lost to the Cardinals last weekend and will be without star receiver Davante Adams for a while after he suffered a hamstring rupture against Arizona. After three straight wins to start the season, the Raiders have dropped three in a row. I don’t trust this pick, but I’ll be taking Los Angeles on the road. They have to find a way to pull it together. Winners: Rams Denver Broncos at Arizona Cardinals — Sunday (Afternoon Game) Both these teams are coming off nail-biting Week 6 victories. The Broncos, even with all their issues on offense, are 4-2 facing a tough slate of opponents to begin the season. I’m optimistic Bo Nix and his teammates can get things going in the right direction against a Cardinals defense that is bottom 10 in the NFL. I’ll take Denver on the road. Winner: Broncos Kansas City Chiefs at Seattle Seahawks — Sunday Night Football The Chiefs are coming off a bye and have one of the best offenses and defenses in the NFL. The Seahawks are coming off a Thursday Night Football loss to the Broncos and are struggling mightily on offense without a formidable rushing attack. I expect Kenneth Walker to have a big game going up against his former team in primetime. I’ll be taking Kansas City. Winner: Chiefs Dallas Cowboys at Philadelphia Eagles — Monday Night Football The Week 7 slate of games finishes with an NFC East rivalry. Even though both teams are 2-4, neither are out of it quite yet in the race for the division title. Prayers up for Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts, who will be out the rest of the season to get treatment for blood clots in his lungs. All things considered, I think Dallas finds a way to win this one. Winner: Cowboys
author: Christopher Hart

title: Sean Payton discusses where Bo Nix can get better
summary: Good morning, Broncos Country. After six weeks, the Denver Broncos have a 4-2 record. That’s a reasonable outcome based on their tough schedule of opponents. It seems a bit better when you acknowledge the fact they haven’t played a complete game thus far. For their Week 7 gridiron matchup, the Broncos head south to battle […]
full_text: DENVER, COLORADO - JANUARY 04: (L-R) Head coach Sean Payton of the Denver Broncos speaks to Bo Nix #10 of the Denver Broncos before the game against the Los Angeles Chargers at Empower Field At Mile High on January 04, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by C. Morgan Engel/Getty Images) | Getty Images Good morning, Broncos Country. After six weeks, the Denver Broncos have a 4-2 record. That’s a reasonable outcome based on their tough schedule of opponents. It seems a bit better when you acknowledge the fact they haven’t played a complete game thus far. For their Week 7 gridiron matchup, the Broncos head south to battle the Arizona Cardinals who are 2-4. The Cardinals coming off an impressive win over the Los Angeles Rams and showed a lot of grit limiting the Rams’ offensive attack. The Broncos are one of five teams in the AFC with a 4-2 record. The hardest part of their schedule appears to be behind them. However, they have a lot of work to do to be playoff contenders. But everything happens one week at a time. This Sunday, Denver has to execute well in all three phases to avoid an upset as road favorites against the Cardinals. Though one area the Broncos desperately need better productivity is offense. There is plenty of blame to go around with that unit. Denver’s rushing attack pales in comparison to how they started off last season. They are one of the bottom five teams in the NFL in rushing yards per game and haven’t had an explosive run over 20 yards. Their offensive line has taken a step back too—with several starters struggling compared to their performances last season. Under the microscope the most is third-year quarterback Bo Nix. He hasn’t performed well to date. It’s true he has struggled early on in his first two seasons, but this year is a bit different. Whether it’s passing efficiency on first down, struggling to convert on third down, or failing to extend plays with his legs—Nix’s production has dropped across the board. Yesterday after practice, Head Coach Sean Payton expressed confidence in Nix’s ability to get back to prior form, but also acknowledged a few key areas he would like to see him improve. “Just relative to third down, finding throws where you guys look at receivers that are more open than maybe you’ve seen. Play design. Last week was a different defense. It was hard to see the down-the-field throws relative to how they played. This defense is a little different, and yet each week there’s a challenge behind that,” stated Paton. The Broncos currently rank as the third worst offense in the NFL when it comes to converting on third downs. Last season, Nix completed nearly 62-percent of his third down throws. His efficiency in passes resulting in first downs was fairly decent at 40-percent. This season? The drop-off has been significant. His completion percentage is an abysmal 48-percent . Moreover, just 26-percent of his third down throws result in moving the chains. It’s hard to sustain drives and score points with those numbers. It’s a big reason why Denver’s offense has failed to take off to greater heights. The numbers back up what Payton has noticed. Denver’s third down endeavors have been disastrous and are a primary reason the team isn’t achieving much on offense. Nix has been the subject to a lot of criticism in the media. Yet he remains confident and focused he will get things back on track. “I just feel strong where I’m at. I’m good mentally. I had a good practice today. I feel good physically. I think it’s going to be there. It’s just in football, you have to get that one game that just gets you going. I think we’ve been playing some really good teams thus far and haven’t gotten that one, but we’re searching for that one game that sort of just puts us right back where we were.” Perhaps this Sunday’s gridiron matchup will be the one that Nix puts together his best game of the season. The Cardinals have forced a lot of turnovers on defense. Though they are in the bottom half of the league with respect to run and pass defense. With a little extra time to prepare after their win against the Seattle Seahawks, I’m hoping that is the case. If not this weekend—when? As always, thank you for reading. summary: The Denver Broncos have a run game problem. Dobbins #27 of the Denver Broncos runs the ball during an NFL football game against the Seattle Seahawks at Empower Field at Mile High on October 15, 2026 in Seattle, Colorado. Denver's run game after contact: #30 in yards after contact per rush at 2.26 #31 in % of runs that gain 5+ yards at 26.5 #31 in longest run at 17 yards #31 in elusiveness rating — Warren Sharp (@SharpFootball) October 21, 2026 Those are catastrophic numbers. J.K. Dobbins is a big part of that, but you have to have a group effort to achieve numbers this bad. Is rookie Jonah Coleman the savior? That is highly to be determined. His sample size is just 10 rushes and he wasn’t lighting the world on fire with those 3.9 yards per carry against the Jacksonville Jaguars. This offense will be a trainwreck until its fixed. Broncos daily recap Broncos at Cardinals preview: Denver aims for three-game win streak The Broncos are coming off a big win over Seattle and the mini-bye for their game against the Cardinals on Sunday. Is the coaching in Denver setting their offense back? In both the run game and the pass game, we’re seeing signs of poor execution. In Seattle, we had two different wide receivers miss run blocks that cost the team a good chunk of yards. We’ve, of course, seen linemen whiff blocks. Potent quotables Sean Payton Opening statement “First day, Wednesday, a pretty normal work week schedule. Any questions?” On his role in supporting OLB Jonathon Cooper over the last few months “It’s been good. All the things that are league protocol relative to what he can and can’t do. He’s in good shape. He’s able to be in the building training. He hadn’t been able to practice, but the six weeks—And we’ve kind of gone through it already, just his steps and his journey. So we’re following that path.” On what OLB Jonathon Cooper needs to show in practice to play this week “I think it’s just getting acclimated, and then if that’s the case, what’s the pitch count? All those things as you come back in.” On if QB Bo Nix’s character helps put him in a better position to get going again “I think he’s seen a lot. I shared this with you guys, and I’ll say it again: I have to be better just relative to in the course of the game. Each game takes on a different feel or style, if you will. Collectively, I think his play will be a byproduct of all of us doing our jobs better.” On the areas he wants QB Bo Nix to improve “Just relative to third down, finding throws where you guys look at receivers that are more open than maybe you’ve seen. Play design. Last week was a different defense. It was hard to see the down-the-field throws relative to how they played. This defense is a little different, and yet each week there’s a challenge behind that.” On how the team has performed over the last two games with him calling the offensive plays “You’re never satisfied. The first half last week felt good with where we were at relative to the game. The second half can be a lot better. So it’s still one of those yellow tape work in progress deals.” On getting back into the rhythm of play calling “I just think that just our focus out here, putting the right plan together. Tonight’s an important night. This is a pressure defense. They give you some looks where they were problematic for the Rams. They were able to take a really good offense and a good quarterback and maybe put them out of rhythm. So we’re going to have to have the right answers.” On adjusting some of the offensive terminology “I think players, coaches, all of us, there’s a language and there’s some things that are easy.” On how much of the terminology did change “It’s immaterial. There are some things that became easier to call, and we continue.” On if any of his other responsibilities have changed since resuming playcalling duties “I think there’s not much different relative to during the week, just in the offensive meetings like we’ve been. It’s just when game time comes, it’s different.” On S Taylor Rapp’s performance last week “Good. He’s smart, tough, loves the game and is one of those players that can come in like he did and transition cleanly. It’s hard to find that. His experience, his football I.Q., all of that shows up on tape, and it’s one of the things that attracted us to him.” On what Arizona’s defense does well “They give you a couple different looks. They’re in their base defense. They have a penny package. You have to I.D. if they’re in that. Then their pressure package from nickel. They affect the quarterback. I think the other thing that stands out is they’re causing more fumbles in their wins. Their takeaway numbers have been really good, and that’s something you see.” On Cardinals TE Trey McBride “Clearly he reminds me a lot of [Raiders TE Brock] Bowers, these unique skill set tight ends that can get matched up on safeties or even corners. He has really good feel, really good transition, and they’re doing a really good job of moving him around. When you just look at the hit numbers, [No.] 85 [Cardinals TE Trey McBride], [No.] 14 [Cardinals WR Michael Wilson]. Then to your original question, there are certain games that unfold a certain way. [Pro Football Hall of Fame Coach] Bill [Parcells] used to always talk about, ‘There’s a way to win each one of these; we just have to know how.’ So there were some important lessons in last Thursday night’s win, just relative to field position, a handful of things.” On how players’ make up allows them to buy into finding different ways to win each game “To your question, that is a strong element to our player procurement, whether it’s free agency, draft, especially with today’s challenges. I think it’s always when the water gets a little rougher that you lean on that.” On the defense’s performance last week “[Seahawks WR] Jaxon [Smith-Njigba] made a number of fantastic plays. It’s interesting, every week there’s a lot of attention drawn to a player like that. Not just him, and yet he’s able to have… I thought we did a pretty good job minimizing the run after the catch, but the turnovers were huge. The pressure and the hits on the quarterback, that has an effect and it was really impressive.” On CB Kris Abrams-Draine’s performance “The ball finds him a little bit, and it did the other night. He really has good ball skills. He has really good football I.Q., and we saw that a year ago even. So I’m glad we have that depth. Again, it would probably go into that work in progress still, and we’ll get that going.” On the potential impact of RB Jonah Coleman’s return “We think it’s a deep room and a talented room. title: Broncos have designated rookie running back Jonah Coleman to return from IR
summary: The Denver Broncos announced on Wednesday evening that they have designated rookie running back Jonah Coleman to return from the injured reserve. The talented rookie suffered and played through a high-ankle sprain during the Broncos’ victory over the Jaguars in Week 2 before being placed on the short-term IR the following week. Coleman returned to […]
full_text: DENVER, COLORADO - SEPTEMBER 20: Jonah Coleman #20 of the Denver Broncos runs the ball during the fourth quarter of a game against the Jacksonville Jaguars at Empower Field At Mile High on September 20, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Lauren Leigh Bacho/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Denver Broncos announced on Wednesday evening that they have designated rookie running back Jonah Coleman to return from the injured reserve. The talented rookie suffered and played through a high-ankle sprain during the Broncos’ victory over the Jaguars in Week 2 before being placed on the short-term IR the following week. Coleman returned to the practice field today and is now eligible to play this Sunday vs. the Cardinals if they activate him off the IR prior to the game. We've designated RB Jonah Coleman for return from IR. 📰 » https://t.co/Q3H7isiaHb pic.twitter.com/3AYdIz5x6F — Denver Broncos (@Broncos) October 21, 2026 As I mentioned, Coleman turned heads during his performance in the Broncos’ comeback victory vs. the Jaguars. He ripped off a few good runs, looked explosive, ran with power, and helped milk the clock late in the 4th quarter to make sure the Jags never had a chance to get the ball back again. He looked like a starting running back and did all this while dealing with a high ankle sprain that would send him to the short-term injured reserve. Now that he is healthy, he should have a big role in the Broncos’ struggling run game. Veteran JK Dobbins has found the end zone in back-to-back weeks, but the overall performance has not been great. The entire offense, including quarterback Bo Nix, has been struggling in recent weeks, and an improved run game could help spark both. I believe Coleman should have a significant role in the offense and the run game moving forward. Pair him with RJ Harvey, who has been the Broncos’ most explosive and consistent playmaker this season and hope your two young backs can spark this offense. However, ever since Sean Payton has retaken the role of play-caller, Dobbins has seen an increased role with the offense, despite the results being sub-par, and I don’t see that changing right away. Still, I hope Coleman does see some snaps and touches this week and his role continues to grow as the season progresses. I believe he will be activated off the IR prior to Sunday’s game, and we will see Jonah Elliss, who Sean Payton said would return this season, placed on the IR to open up a roster spot for Coleman.

Next on the docket is a scrappy Arizona Cardinals bunch that just pulled a huge road upset of the Los Angeles Rams. The good news for the Broncos (4-2) is that they got the mini-bye week before heading to the desert and could get a few players back from injury and the commissioner’s exempt list. Denver looks to extend its winning streak to three games after coming out of a gauntlet to start the season. The Broncos are currently -4.5-point road favorites over Arizona (2-4). The total sits at over/under 43.5 points, with a lean toward the over at -115. Offensive Rankings Denver : Thirty-first in total offense (252.2 yards per game), 26th in rushing offense (84.2 YPG), 28th in passing offense (168.0 YPG), 26th in scoring offense (19.0 points per game). Arizona : Twenty-third in total offense (307.3 yards per game), 22nd in rushing offense (96.3 YPG), 20th in passing offense (211.0 YPG), 24th in scoring offense (21.0 points per game). Defensive Rankings Denver : Twenty-second in total defense (348.3 yards per game), 31st in rushing defense (139.8 YPG), 10th in passing defense (208.5 YPG), tied for 10th in scoring defense (20.8 points per game). Arizona : Twenty-third in total defense (350.5 yards per game), 20th in rushing defense (120.8 YPG), 22nd in passing defense (229.7 YPG), tied for 31st in scoring defense (29.7 points per game). Here are the MHR staff’s keys to Sunday’s game. Win the line of scrimmage on offense The Broncos offensive line has been the definition of “meh” to start the regular season. It’s nowhere near what it’s been the last few seasons, but it also isn’t horrid either. Denver needs to dominate the line of scrimmage on Sunday. Open lanes in the running game and do a better job of pass protection. It’s a cliche, but success on offense starts in the trenches. Getting that could lay the foundation for jump-starting the offense. — Ian St. Clair Bench Bo Nix; Start Jarrett Stidham Just kidding. Ya’ll crazy if you think benching Bo Nix is even remotely the answer. That said, Bo Nix does need to play better, and he isn’t seeing the field well to start the season. He’s had slow starts in every season he’s played, so, for now, I’m chalking this up to another slow start. However, seven games in, I’m hoping to see him take flight a bit now that the hardest part of the Broncos’ schedule is complete. At 4-2, they got through it with a winning record, and that is all we could hope for. — Tim Lynch Pressure the QB The key to this game is the same as it has been every week. Get to the QB. The defense has done a great job this season of causing mayhem in the backfield. Make it uncomfortable for Jacoby Brissett (like the back of a Volkswagen). When QBs are harassed and hurried, they make mistakes. — Adam Malnati Disciplined, execution-based offensive football This team needs to execute at a high level, and it will win this game easily. The defense is already there. If the offense can up its game, this Broncos team will be unstoppable. — Sadaraine Limit the impact of Trey McBride The Broncos defense has performed well this season, aside from a few games. For the most part, they’ve been able to limit the impact of the opposing team’s top player on their offense. This week, they face All-Pro tight end Trey McBride, who is coming off a sensational 2025 season. He is the focal point of Arizona’s aerial attack and gets over ten targets per game. Defensive coordinator Vance Joseph needs to come up with a good game plan that limits his impact on the game. If they can slow him down, Denver will have a great shot at earning their fifth victory of the season. — Christopher Hart What are your keys to Sunday’s game?

title: Discussion: Is Sam LaPorta right to take his contract frustrations public?
summary: This week, Detroit Lions tight end Sam LaPorta went public with his frustrations about his contract situation with the team. In the midst of the final year of his rookie deal, LaPorta and the Lions have cut off extension talks after the two sides have reached a stalemate. And while his initial comments to the […]
full_text: Detroit Lions tight end Sam LaPorta (87) warms up ahead of the Hall of Fame Game at Tom Benson Hall of Fame Stadium in Canton, Ohio on Thursday, July 31, 2025. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co This week, Detroit Lions tight end Sam LaPorta went public with his frustrations about his contract situation with the team . In the midst of the final year of his rookie deal, LaPorta and the Lions have cut off extension talks after the two sides have reached a stalemate. And while his initial comments to the local media weren’t very incendiary, during his podcast appearance on “Pardon My Take” this week, LaPorta didn’t hold back. “It’s disappointing that you go out there every week and you bear the risk of getting hurt. Like last year, whatever it was, Week 9, Week 10, I break my fucking back for this team. And then I’m going out there this year, and I’m ballin’, and maybe they’re just not showing the love,” LaPorta said. He later added that he’s happy to go somewhere else if Detroit doesn’t pay up. “So I’m going to continue to do my thing and ball out, and in three months if I don’t get to wear the Honolulu Blue and play for the Lions anymore, it’s going to be all good. I’ll go get paid somewhere else. So, whatever,” LaPorta said. LaPorta is more than within his rights to feel this way. And I’m sure a lot of people think he’s in the right to be frustrated given everything he has accomplished. Personally, I think the more controversial topic is taking this grievance public. By saying this on a podcast, he is creating drama, distraction, and possibly frustration on both sides of the table. Maybe that’s the goal as a negotiating tactic, but he’s already taking a PR hit, with some fans angry over his attitude. So today’s Question of the Day is: Should Sam LaPorta have taken his frustrations public? My answer: During a break in our Midweek Mailbag podcast, Erik Schlitt and I discussed this topic at length. You can watch that segment below. In short, I’m a little torn. On one hand, I appreciate honesty. Too often, we get boilerplate, safe answers from players who are too afraid to say their peace, because of the potential backlash from the public. We get annoyed when coaches give us coachspeak, yet when anyone dares to say what’s actually on their mind, they’re vilified, too. On the other hand, I don’t think much of anything was gained with these comments, other than LaPorta’s release of frustrations. I don’t think the Lions will take too kindly to these comments, so I reject the notion that this puts pressure on them to get a deal done. I think it’s probably a net negative for LaPorta, too. While he may have experienced some relief for finally saying what he wants, the public backlash is already pretty obvious. Just look at the comment section of our news story on the article , and you’ll find plenty of comments asking to trade him or accusing him of being unloyal, greedy, and tone-deaf. LaPorta is well within his rights to say whatever he wants, whenever he wants. And, again, I admire someone who speaks their truth without being overly disrespectful—and I don’t think he went over the top here. However, I do think more damage than good will come of this. What are your thoughts? Vote in the poll below and share your fuller beliefs in the comment section at the bottom of this page.

Injured list updates C Cade Mays (Wrist, PUP) — Will return to the active roster this week S Brian Branch (Achilles, PUP) — Will return to the active roster this week On Monday, coach Dan Campbell told the media that the plan was to activate both Mays and Branch to the 53-man roster this week, but it was unclear how much either could play against the Packers. Branch is expected to “handle quite a bit,” but he may not be able to play the entire game, while Mays is expected to start based on Campbell’s comments on Wednesday : “We really worked the heck out of Cade yesterday. He got some quality reps, and we would like to give him a go here.” RB Isiah Pacheco (MCL/Back, IR) — expected to be out until December WR Tom Kennedy (MCL, IR) — season-ending injury OL Giovanni Manu (Undisclosed, NFI) — eligible to begin practicing at any time OL Ben Bartch (foot, IR) — eligible to begin practicing in Week 10 LB Devin White (forearm, IR) — eligible to begin practicing in Week 10 S Kerby Joseph (Knee, PUP) — expected to return to play this season S Thomas Harper (Ankle, IR) — eligible to begin practicing at any time Branch’s safety running mate, Kerby Joseph, also got some positive news this week, as Campbell noted on Tuesday that he still expects the All-Pro safety to return to play this season. While there is still no timetable for his return, this was the first positive update we have gotten from coaches surrounding Joseph’s status and was quickly followed up by even more promising videos posted on Joseph’s social media accounts . Additional quick updates: A trio of players was added to injured reserve during the Lions’ bye week: Kennedy will miss the season, while Bartch and White will miss at least four weeks and may need even longer to recover. Manu was seen at practice last week working with trainers, a possible first step towards opening his recovery window. Harper is now eligible to begin his practice window once healthy. Estimated n o practice None As Jeremy Reisman previously reported, all players on the active roster attended Tuesday practice . While he’s no longer in the starting lineup on defense, he’s been a steady contributor on multiple phases of special teams and would boost multiple spots if he could return to game action. title: Detroit Lions TE Sam LaPorta vents frustrations about contract situation
summary: A few weeks back, reports emerged that the Detroit Lions and tight end Sam LaPorta had cut off contract extension talks after negotiations were no longer productive. Days later, LaPorta talked to the media and confirmed that both sides had reached a stalemate. In that media session, he took the high road, noting that he […]
full_text: Detroit Lions tight end Sam Laporta (87) arrives ahead of Cincinnati Bengals game at Paycor Stadium in Cincinnati on Sunday, Oct. 5, 2025. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co A few weeks back, reports emerged that the Detroit Lions and tight end Sam LaPorta had cut off contract extension talks after negotiations were no longer productive. Days later, LaPorta talked to the media and confirmed that both sides had reached a stalemate. In that media session, he took the high road, noting that he feels respected in the building and he wants to be optimistic about a deal eventually getting done. However, LaPorta was a little more open and honest this week when appearing on the “Pardon My Take” podcast . LaPorta vented about the frustration of putting his body on the line every week and not feeling financially supported for it. “I think the combination of getting your heartstrings twisted as well as the violent sport we play—it sucks,” LaPorta said. “It’s disappointing that you go out there every week and you bear the risk of getting hurt. Like last year, whatever it was, Week 9, Week 10, I break my fucking back for this team. And then I’m going out there this year, and I’m ballin’, and maybe they’re just not showing the love.” LaPorta’s back injury last year was one that clearly caused him a lot of stress. Earlier this year, he talked about how thoughts about his career ending because of the injury crept into his head and led to some emotional offseason moments. So, it’s certainly not surprising for that to be at the forefront of his mind when it comes to making sure he’s financially supported. We haven’t heard the Lions’ point of view on why contract issues have hit a snag, but both general manager Brad Holmes and coach Dan Campbell have expressed a ton of public appreciation for what LaPorta does and also made it clear they want him around long-term. “There are always going to be two sides, and you work through these things, and just because there’s a report of that doesn’t mean that that’s some big issue, big deal,” Campbell said two weeks ago. “I love LaPorta. We love LaPorta. He’s a heck of a football player, and I thought he played his best game the other day. His work ethic, his production speaks for itself.” It’s unclear if the two sides will resume talks during the season, or if it will be hashed out in the offseason. Regardless, LaPorta’s letting his agent take care of that, while he remains focused on the current NFL season. That said, it sounds like he’s already at ease if things don’t work out in Detroit. “So I’m going to continue to do my thing and ball out, and in three months if I don’t get to wear the Honolulu Blue and play for the Lions anymore, it’s going to be all good. I’ll go get paid somewhere else. So, whatever,” LaPorta said. The whole interview is definitely worth your time. LaPorta talks about Dan Campbell’s fourth-down mindset and the culture shock of an aggressive offense after playing at Iowa. There’s also talk about blocking for Jahmyr Gibbs, how his back feels, playing on Thanksgiving, and submitting his name for the Italian flag football Olympic team.

title: Kerby Joseph injury update: Lions safety posts promising video of progress
summary: We still don’t have a timeline for the return of Detroit Lions safety Kerby Joseph as he continues to rehab from a serious knee injury, but the positive signs continue to accumulate. On Tuesday, Lions coach Dan Campbell said he still expects Joseph to play at some point this season, and hours later, the All-Pro […]
full_text: Detroit Lions safety Kerby Joseph waves to the crowd ahead of a game against the New Orleans Saints at Ford Field in Detroit on Sunday Sept. 13, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co We still don’t have a timeline for the return of Detroit Lions safety Kerby Joseph as he continues to rehab from a serious knee injury, but the positive signs continue to accumulate. On Tuesday, Lions coach Dan Campbell said he still expects Joseph to play at some point this season , and hours later, the All-Pro safety went to social media to provide even more optimism. Joseph has been relatively quiet over the past couple of months, but on Tuesday night, he posted a compilation of his workouts at the Lions’ indoor practice field, asking viewers “which break was my best.” The video shows Joseph running at near full speed and making quick change-of-direction cuts on both legs. And toward the end of the video, he hints at a comeback in the near future with the following caption: “Dis shii onna way man” Here’s the video: View Link If that isn’t enough, Campbell provided more optimism regarding Joseph’s progress when asked by local radio why he believes the Lions safety will play again this year. “The progression of where he’s come right now in his rehab, the strength that the knee is gaining,” Campbell told 97.1 The Ticket on Wednesday. “We’re working here. I don’t want to give a timeline, but I do feel optimistic that before the season’s out he’ll play for us.” And don’t forget that Lions safety Brian Branch, who will return to action this week, was also very optimistic about Joseph’s eventual return . But Campbell finished his answer with one of those moments in which you can never tell if he’s being even a little serious or not. “And, look, I hope I’m not wrong, but maybe I am, and then you can call me a liar. But I like where he’s trending.”
author: Jeremy Reisman

title: Dan Campbell hints at who will play alongside Brian Branch at safety
summary: We now know that the Detroit Lions plan to play Brian Branch this week against the Green Bay Packers, marking the end of his 10+ month rehab after tearing his Achilles last season. Branch could make an immediate impact on the Lions’ struggling secondary, but Detroit’s coaching staff still has some decisions to make in […]
full_text: Sep 15, 2024; Detroit, Michigan, USA; Detroit Lions safety Brian Branch (32) celebrates after intercepting a pass from Tampa Bay Buccaneers quarterback Baker Mayfield (not pictured) in the second quarter at Ford Field. Mandatory Credit: Lon Horwedel-Imagn Images | USA TODAY Sports via Reuters Con We now know that the Detroit Lions plan to play Brian Branch this week against the Green Bay Packers, marking the end of his 10+ month rehab after tearing his Achilles last season. Branch could make an immediate impact on the Lions’ struggling secondary, but Detroit’s coaching staff still has some decisions to make in terms of personnel. The biggest question is simply: who is going to play alongside Branch? The Lions have gone through a litany of safeties this year, both due to injury and poor play. Avonte Maddox is out for the year with an injury, and Thomas Harper is on injured reserve for the foreseeable future. Meanwhile, the Lions have given significant playing time to Chuck Clark, Christian Izien, and recently rookie Keith Abney. I asked Campbell what he’s looking for besides Branch, and the Lions coach mentioned that Branch is such a good, versatile player, that they can put any type of player alongside him, and the Pro Bowl player will make it work. “Here’s what’s great about getting BB [Branch] back. BB gives you the flexibility is what do you want to do with anybody else?” Campbell said. “Because there are things you’re going to want to do with BB, high, let him play top down, and then there are things you want him to play underneath. And that doesn’t require somebody else playing off of him necessarily. He’ll make it right.” On the surface, veteran Chuck Clark is a better player in the box given his physical limitation at age 32. Abney, while still very new to the position, is an athletic, rangey defender that could play some single-high looks. Unsurprisingly, because the Lions view Branch as capable to fill both roles, Campbell expects to play both Clark and Abney against the Packers this week. “We’re going to use all those guys,” Campbell said. “Chuck has been really steady for us, man. He’s smart veteran guy. He’s going to be where he’s supposed to be. And then I mentioned this about Abney. Abney is worth continuing to invest in. I mean, he’s going to play for us.” Last game, both Abney and Clark were essential in utilizing a game plan to take away Arizona’s top two threat, Michael Wilson and Trey McBride . Detroit faces a much bigger threat in the passing game this week against the Green Bay Packers, and it’ll require an entirely different game plan. Campbell described their options as “pick your poison.” The Packers have two deep-ball threats in receivers Matthew Golden and Christian Watson. But if your plan is to take the top away from both players, Green Bay can punish you over the middle with their Pro Bowl tight end Tucker Kraft. “That’s the danger in it. Wherever you’re having to use some resources, then now you have got to worry about Kraft.” Campbell said. “If you’re going to use it to take the top off on some of this, well now you have got Kraft underneath and you have got to worry about the backs. It does, it creates some issues, man, that you have got to be ready for. And some of it is you better pick your poison. You can’t defend all of it, so you better pick your poison and what you think means the most to you to stop.” Branch could very well be the antidote to Green Bay’s poison this week, but he’ll need help from everyone around him to make the entire defense work in harmony.
author: Jeremy Reisman

title: The Detroit Lions have decided on their starting center vs. Packers
summary: For a few weeks now, we’ve been talking about the crossroads the Detroit Lions are facing at center. Cade Mays signed a three-year, $25 million deal this offseason to take that position, but after fracturing his wrist in training camp, it’s been Juice Scruggs holding down the pivot for the first five games of the […]
full_text: Detroit Lions quarterback Jared Goff (16), and center Cade Mays (64), left, practice next to offensive lineman Juice Scruggs (70), and quarterback Luke Altmyer (2) during training camp at Meijer Performance Center in Allen Park on Thursday, July 30, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co For a few weeks now, we’ve been talking about the crossroads the Detroit Lions are facing at center . Cade Mays signed a three-year, $25 million deal this offseason to take that position, but after fracturing his wrist in training camp, it’s been Juice Scruggs holding down the pivot for the first five games of the season. Mays is set to return to play this week against the Green Bay Packers, but Scruggs has played so well that he’s deserved consideration to keep the job. During his Wednesday radio appearance on 97.1 The Ticket, Lions coach Dan Campbell more or less put the discussion to bed. All signs point to Cade Mays taking over at center this Sunday. “We really worked the heck out of Cade yesterday. He got some quality reps, and we would like to give him a go here,” Campbell said. “… We’d like to just rip this Band-Aid off of Cade. I thought he had some good work yesterday. I thought he looked pretty good.” In his answer, Campbell was sure to give his flowers to Scruggs and the job he’s done thus far. “Juice has done a hell of a job for us,” Campbell said. “I’ve mentioned this before, I’m going to continue to say it: thank goodness we got Juice, man. He’s been outstanding for us.” One out-of-the-box option to ease Mays in would be for him to rotate with Scruggs throughout the game. However, Campbell made it blatantly clear he was not interesting in doing that, as it could disrupt a ton of the offensive operation. “I don’t see us doing that,” Campbell said. “You go around and around, and all these questions come in. It’s different than a guard. Jon, you know that. A guard and a center is totally different. That guy’s touching the ball. The snap count is different. Everything: the snap, the timing, the calls, the quarterback’s comfort with one guy over and over.” So it appears Mays is in line to make his first start for the Lions on Sunday, while Scruggs will be both the primary backup center and compete for time at left guard.

title: 5 Lions vs. Packers thoughts after watching Green Bay’s win over Cowboys
summary: The Detroit Lions face off against the Green Bay Packers this week, and the timing could be tough for them. The Packers have shrugged off an ugly start to the season and are now riding a three-game winning streak. Their last two wins in particular—blowout wins over the Bears and Cowboys—have been impressive. I watched […]
full_text: Oct 18, 2026; Green Bay, Wisconsin, USA; Green Bay Packers quarterback Jordan Love (10) during the game against the Dallas Cowboys at Lambeau Field. Mandatory Credit: Jeff Hanisch-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Detroit Lions face off against the Green Bay Packers this week, and the timing could be tough for them. The Packers have shrugged off an ugly start to the season and are now riding a three-game winning streak. Their last two wins in particular—blowout wins over the Bears and Cowboys—have been impressive. I watched the Packers’ last game against the Cowboys, both live and again on replay, and took some notes as it may pertain to this week’s game against the Lions. Packers have no run game Green Bay let the Cowboys hang around for much longer than they should have, and a lot of that has to do with their lack of a running game. The Packers scored just six second-half points against a terrible Cowboys defense. Removing two Jordan Love kneel-downs, the Packers rushed for just 42 yards on 17 carries in the second half (2.57 YPC). Mind you, this is a Cowboys defense that, even after this performance, ranks dead last in rushing yards allowed (149.8 per game) and 25th in DVOA. For the season, Green Bay is dead last in: Rushing yards per game (59.8) Yards per carry (2.9) Rush EPA (-0.299) 31st in rushing success rate (32.5%) Green Bay will likely get Josh Jacobs back this week, which should help. But there are systemic issues with their running game, including a busted offensive line. If recently added guard Kevin Zeitler makes his first appearance this week, it could have a bigger impact than Jacobs’ return. Green Bay’s safeties are awesome and versatile Watching the Packers deploy Xavier McKinney and Evan Williams in creative and exciting ways made me yearn for the days of a healthy Brian Branch and Kerby Joseph. Both players are so versatile, and defensive coordinator Jonathan Gannon has done an awesome job putting them in positions to make plays. Just watch him hide Williams close to the line, only to have him back out, scream to the opposite side of the field, and pick off a completely unsuspecting Dak Prescott. This is ridiculous. Evan Williams covers so much ground #Packers https://t.co/zgcIk4bp6q pic.twitter.com/RdxMnPIsWd — Cameron Ezeir (@camezeir) October 19, 2026 For the season, the duo has a combined five interceptions, 2.0 sacks, six quarterback hits, and 73 tackles. They will stress both Jared Goff and the Lions’ receivers, making it hard to both attack the deep portion of the field (GB is 11th in EPA per pass on deep balls) and the middle of the field (first in EPA per pass against slot targets). This will put more pressure on Detroit’s boundary receivers to win against what is a pretty mediocre cornerback group in Green Bay. Deep ball merchants While Anthony Balaj put together a nice piece on why the Packers’ deep-ball game may not be as threatening as it seems , it’s still a huge part of what the Packers do on offense. Though Love didn’t connect on a deep shot against the Cowboys, they did benefit from a 37-yard pass interference penalty on a deep shot to Bo Melton. In fact, no one in the NFL has benefited more from defensive pass interference penalties than the Packers through six games, with a league-leading 135 yards gained. No team has more passing attempts of 20+ air yards than the Packers (5.3 per game), although their +0.32 EPA per deep shot only ranks them 19th in the NFL. Meanwhile, the Lions have been horrible against deep shots this year. They’re dead last in EPA/pass (+1.41) and are giving up the second-most yards per game (80.6) on deep shots. Detroit is hoping the return of Brian Branch this week may help stabilize the back end, but this may be their biggest test of the season. Careful blitzing Jordan Love Dallas tried to bring some extra pressure to test a poor Packers offensive line, but Jordan Love had all of the answers before the Cowboys could get home. While Dallas was able to produce a 53.8% pressure rate on those blitzes (eighth-highest of Week 8), Love still torched them on those plays. He went 8-for-12 for 100 yards and one sack against the blitz. He produced the sixth-highest yards per attempt (8.4) and second-highest EPA/dropback (+0.43) against the blitz in Week 6. His season-long stats are a little more tame, ranking 13th in EPA/dropback (+0.03), 12th in yards per attempt (8.1), and 11th in passer rating (104.2) against the blitz. Still, if I were the Lions, I would test my luck trying to create pressure without deploying extra defenders. Love’s statistics are actually much worse with no blitz, ranking: 23rd in passer rating (84.4) 17th in yards per attempt (7.1) 17th in EPA/dropback (+0.05) Given that the Lions are producing the seventh-highest pressure rate without blitzing (35.5%) and the Packers are allowing the sixth-highest pressure rate on non-blitz plays (36.2%), the game plan seems obvious. Well-coached blitzing The Packers dialed up some well-timed and well-disguised blitzes against Dallas that ensured a comeback attempt from the Cowboys never came close to materializing. In total, they had a 35.7% blitz rate (11th-highest of the week). More importantly, it was effective. On blitzes, they were able to produce a 45.0% pressure rate (13th), and it completely disrupted Dak Prescott and what was one of the best passing offenses in the league. Against the blitz, Dak Prescott was just 12-of-20 passing for 79 yards (4.0 yards per attempt — ranking 28 out of 29 qualifying QBs in Week 6). Detroit’s offensive line has been better than expected this year, but the reshuffled unit is still figuring things out when it comes to handling the blitz, allowing the third-highest time to pressure in the NFL against the blitz (2.21 seconds). Thankfully, Jared Goff tends to make things right by getting the ball out quickly and avoiding the negative plays. Despite the quick pressure, Detroit still has the second-highest EPA per pass against the blitz (+0.33).
