title: Detroit Lions scouting report: Green Bay’s wild season is trending up
summary: After a much-needed bye week, the Detroit Lions are back on the field. They kick off their 2026 campaign to reclaim their NFC North crown against the Green Bay Packers in Ford Field in Week 7. After back-to-back road games and a bye week, Lions fans should be going crazy for them on Sunday afternoon. […]
full_text: GREEN BAY, WISCONSIN - OCTOBER 18: Matthew Golden #0 of the Green Bay Packers celebrates a touchdown with fans during the first quarter against the Dallas Cowboys at Lambeau Field on October 18, 2026 in Green Bay, Wisconsin. (Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images) | Getty Images After a much-needed bye week, the Detroit Lions are back on the field. They kick off their 2026 campaign to reclaim their NFC North crown against the Green Bay Packers in Ford Field in Week 7. After back-to-back road games and a bye week, Lions fans should be going crazy for them on Sunday afternoon. The Green Bay Packers have had a wild up-and-down season so far in 2026. Injuries and off-the-field concerns dropped the team to 1-2 after Week 3. Since then, the team is on a three-game winning streak and heads to Detroit with star running back Josh Jacobs back on the field to give the offense a much-needed boost. While this is Detroit’s first divisional game, the Packers are 1-1 in divisional play this season. Let’s take a deep look at the Packers’ season so far ahead of Week 7. Green Bay Packers 2026 season thus far (4-2) Week 1: Lost to Minnesota Vikings, 39-22 Week 2: Defeated New York Jets, 20-17 (OT) Week 3: Lost to Atlanta Falcons, 35-14 Week 4: Defeated Tampa Bay Buccaneers, 17-14 Week 5: Defeated Chicago Bears, 31-7 Week 6: Defeated Dallas Cowboys, 23-13 Offensive stats: The offense has had a more chaotic ride than the defense. At quarterback, Jordan Love has been doing well, throwing for 1,684 yards with 11 touchdowns and four interceptions. He’s had to carry the offense while the running game has struggled. Love has the third-most passing yards in the NFL, but the passing game hasn’t been all flowers and roses, as it ranks in the middle of the pack in DVOA and PFF. With Jacobs returning, expect that part of the offense to take a step forward. MarShawn Lloyd leads the team with 122 yards and two touchdowns, averaging 2.5 yards per carry. The trade for Kaleb Johnson hasn’t worked out as well as fans hoped, with Johnson getting only 104 yards on 3.7 yards per carry. The running game is the offense’s biggest weakness, ranking in the bottom four in multiple categories, from rushing yards to DVOA to PFF grades. When Love has time to throw, he most often finds wide receivers Christian Watson and Matthew Golden. Watson leads the team in yards (538) and touchdowns (6), while Golden leads in catches with 30. The duo has already combined for over 1,000 yards this season, and they could be the passing game’s future one-two punch if wide receiver Jayden Reed can’t return from his neck injury. Newly paid tight end Tucker Kraft has had a slow start, catching 25 passes for 249 yards and a touchdown. Green Bay’s biggest flaw right now is drops, as they lead the NFL with 20, according to Pro Football Reference. One major reason for the running game’s struggles is the offensive line. Injuries have plagued the position group, and the team has made multiple moves, including signing former Detroit Lion Kevin Zeitler to provide immediate help, although he has yet to play. According to PFF, they have the second-worst run-blocking grade (47.8), but it gets worse. They also have the worst pass-blocking grade from PFF (46.8), which explains why, despite Love’s high mark in passing yards, the passing grades and DVOA aren’t high, but they’re enough to carry the offense and make them an average team in EPA. Defensive stats: The Packers defense has been on the calmer side this year, but not in the front seven. Two defensive tackles and a linebacker are on IR, while their star pass rusher and another defensive tackle are still on PUP. EDGE Lukas Van Ness leads the line with 3.5 sacks, while defensive tackle Devonte Wyatt has 2.0 sacks and a forced fumble as the defense tries to hold down the fort until EDGE Micah Parsons returns. The linebacker room lost its best player, Edgerrin Cooper, for the year with a torn Achilles, but Zaire Franklin and Ty’Ron Hopper are doing their best to keep the defense tough. Franklin has 41 tackles, a forced fumble, and a pass deflection, while Hopper has 12 tackles, two pass deflections, and an interception. Green Bay’s secondary has been the strength of the defense, mostly because of the lack of injuries at the position. Safety Xavier McKinney is back to his old tricks, tied for the league lead with three interceptions, and with Evan Williams next to him with two, this safety duo looks like one of the best in the NFL. With a stout secondary, they rank highly in passing defense in DVOA and passing yards allowed, and PFF rates them the NFL’s top coverage unit. While the passing defense has been stellar, this team is struggling to stop the run, which makes sense with how many bodies are out in that front seven, especially on the interior. With the Packers allowing over 110 rushing yards a game, Detroit may try to use the running game to open up the passing game. Injury notes Key players ruled out : RT Zach Bako-Bewele (IR), LB Edgerrin Cooper (IR), WR Jayden Reed (IR), DT Javon Hargrave (IR), DT Jonathan Ford (IR), WR Skyy Moore (IR) Key players to monitor : TE Luke Musgrave (PUP), EDGE Micah Parsons (PUP), DT Jordon Riley (PUP), G Aaron Banks (knee/toe), T Anthony Belton (knee), C/G Jager Burton (back), C/G Jacob Monk (quad), CB Benjamin St-Juste (hamstring) We thought the Carolina Panthers were banged up. Oh man, the Packers blew them out of the water. Their offensive line took a big blow when they lost their top player, right tackle Zach Bako-Bewele, to a patellar tendon tear that ended his season. Several of these injuries are season-ending, but the Packers are dealing with even more issues. Their superstar Parsons is still on PUP, and he won’t be returning to practice this week, but he’ll be on the field soon enough. Another player still on PUP is tight end Luke Musgrave, as the Packers could use all the help they can get on offense. Last week, the Packers added more players to their IR list: defensive tackles Javon Hargrave and Jonathan Ford, and wide receiver Skyy Moore. Additionally, the offensive line has four linemen (two starters) dealing with issues: left guard Aaron Banks is battling knee and toe issues, and the replacement for Bako-Bewele, Anthony Belton, is dealing with a knee injury. Banks missed Week 6, so his Week 7 status is up in the air. Their depth at guard and center has been rough, too: backup interior lineman Jager Burton missed Week 6 with a back injury, and Jacob Monk is dealing with a quad injury. Cornerback took a little bit of a hit, down Benjamin St-Juste, but it’s nowhere near as depleted as the trenches. Biggest strength: Secondary With injuries depleting the front seven, the secondary is taking on the burden of carrying the defense. They’ve allowed the third-fewest yards per passing attempt. Green Bay leads the NFL in interceptions with nine. When you not only limit what offenses can do through the air but also take away the football, you start changing how offenses attack you. Evan Williams Picks Off Dak Prescott, What A Great Play From The Packers. The Packers Secondary Comes Up With A Huge Interception Right There. Big Time. 🔥 pic.twitter.com/r1qvGb4Es5 — SM Highlights (@SMHighlights1) October 19, 2026 The Packers have allowed the third-lowest passer rating (73.9) and only nine passing plays over 20+ yards, tied for second-fewest in the league. We’ve seen what great safety play is like in Detroit when safeties Kerby Joseph and Brian Branch are on the field together, and the Packers are doing the same with McKinney and Williams. The cornerback room isn’t too impressive, but they’ve done their job well, so with the overtop help being as dominant as it has been, the cornerbacks have more opportunities to make plays and do their part. Biggest weakness: Running back Despite Jacobs returning this week for Green Bay, this position has been a huge problem for them this year. It’s uncertain how ready Jacobs will be and how much he’ll play,…

title: Matt LaFleur, Josh Jacobs speak after running back’s reinstatement
summary: Wednesday marked the first day that Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs was able to practice with the Packers since training camp, following his placement on the NFL’s commissioner exempt list for a domestic violence incident that led to Jacobs pleading no contest to charges of battery and criminal damage to property. Jacobs still […]
full_text: (Photo by John Fisher/Getty Images) | Getty Images Wednesday marked the first day that Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs was able to practice with the Packers since training camp, following his placement on the NFL’s commissioner exempt list for a domestic violence incident that led to Jacobs pleading no contest to charges of battery and criminal damage to property. Jacobs still isn’t technically a member of the Packers’ 53-man active roster, as Green Bay has the option to use a one-week exemption on the running back while he’s coming off the commissioner exempt list, but Green Bay Packers head coach Matt LaFleur has already stated that Jacobs practiced with the team on Wednesday, a sign that Jacobs will be up on the active roster soon. Both LaFleur, who had previously stated that he wouldn’t talk about Jacobs’ situation until the league’s investigation (which is still ongoing) was finished, and Jacobs, who hasn’t had the opportunity to talk to the press this year, were asked questions by the media relevant to the running back’s time on the exempt list. Here’s what they had to say on Wednesday. Matt LaFleur I think a lot of times you get into a situation where you might not make the right decision. I think people learn from their mistakes, and I think he’s extremely remorseful. I do believe that he’s a good person. I’ve been around him quite a bit. I believe in second chances. Josh Jacobs Josh Jacobs’ opening statement. pic.twitter.com/gftJyp2oVm — Bill Huber (@BillHuberNFL) October 21, 2026 I’m excited to be back with the team, with the guys. I want to say thank you to the organization, really for supporting me throughout this whole process and how everything played out. With that being said, I can’t get into a lot of things. Like specifics of things, but obviously, man, I’m remorseful and sorry for putting this team in this situation. Sometimes, when you go through life, situations occur. A four-second, three-second decision can alter your life. But with that being said, I’m still a human being, man. I’m still trying to learn. I’m still trying to grow from the whole process. I actually learned a lot throughout this process, legally and just personally. Going forward, man, it’s just trying to be better. For some people, I know this might be a stain on me and my character. I feel like I don’t really have to speak on my character. A lot of people that know me, in this locker room or has been around me, I’ll let them do that. For me, man, I’m just trying to come back in here and play ball, learn from this mistake and move forward. Josh Jacobs said he never doubted he’d play again. What surprised the #Packers RB was it took 6 games. “I think 6 games is a lot, honestly. But that’s not really up to me to decide. I’m grateful to be playing, so that’s not something I’m really arguing or petitioning.” pic.twitter.com/AuQe7HTdvx — Ryan Wood (@ByRyanWood) October 21, 2026 I think six games is a lot, honestly, but that’s not really up to me to decide. I’m grateful to be playing, so that’s not something I’m really arguing or petitioning with. I’m just happy to be back on the team. Josh Jacobs says he understands some fans will think less of him after what happened, but he’s secure in who he is, and what the #Packers think of him. “I’m not trying to win nobody back.” pic.twitter.com/GZvcu9tQDc — Ryan Wood (@ByRyanWood) October 21, 2026 Me, personally, I’m not trying to win nobody back. And that’s me being all the way honest, because at the end of the day, I know what happened. If you feel some type of way, I feel bad, because it’s still a situation occured and it should have never even happened. That’s something that I would still understand if people feel some type of way about it. But like I said, all I can do is keep showing up and being who I am. Being a leader for this team. Being a leader in this community. That’s really all I can control.

title: Packers Injury Report: Jordan Love has a back injury, but it’s not serious
summary: The Green Bay Packers held a walkthrough on Wednesday, so they didn’t have a full practice by any means, but the only player who was estimated to be a non-participant on their injury report today was receiver Bo Melton (back), who was able to finish the game in Week 6 against the Dallas Cowboys. The […]
full_text: (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Green Bay Packers held a walkthrough on Wednesday, so they didn’t have a full practice by any means, but the only player who was estimated to be a non-participant on their injury report today was receiver Bo Melton (back), who was able to finish the game in Week 6 against the Dallas Cowboys. The big news of the day was that quarterback Jordan Love (back) was added to the injury report and was listed as an estimated limited participant. After practice, according to ESPN’s Rob Demovsky , Love stated that he has a sore back, but that there is “no chance” that the injury will keep him sidelined against the Detroit Lions on Sunday. Along with Love, the following players were also listed as limited on the Packers injury report: offensive lineman Aaron Banks (knee/toe), defensive lineman Anthony Campbell (ankle), cornerback Brandon Cisse (shoulder/neck), receiver Matthew Golden (shoulder), defensive lineman Jordon Riley (Achilles), cornerback Benjamin St-Juste (hamstring), receiver Christian Watson (ankle) and receiver Savion Williams (ankle). Cisse is the only player in the group who dropped out against the Cowboys and did not return to action. Banks, Riley and St-Juste never suited up in the game to begin with. On the Lions’ end of the injury report, the only player who was listed as anything less than an estimated full participant was cornerback Rock Ya-Sin (limited, hamstring). Detroit didn’t have a practice today, in part because they practiced on Tuesday coming off their BYE week. Packers held only what they called a job-through today so practice participations are estimated, but only one DNP today. Josh Jacobs not listed so presumably he’s full go. pic.twitter.com/48UYiLmsLy — Rob Demovsky (@RobDemovsky) October 21, 2026

full_text: GREEN BAY, WISCONSIN - OCTOBER 18: Brandon Cisse #2 of the Green Bay Packers breaks up a pass intended for Ceedee Lamb #88 of the Dallas Cowboys during the second quarter at Lambeau Field on October 18, 2026 in Green Bay, Wisconsin. (Photo by Patrick McDermott/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Packers’ defense showed itself to be a bit better than just a unit that beats up on bad quarterbacks on Sunday. What, exactly, Dak Prescott is as a player at this point is open to debate and discussion, but I think most people would agree he’s still a pretty good player — better than Geno Smith and Jalon Daniels and the Tyson Bagent/Case Keenum combo platter, at least. And with weapons like CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens, there was plenty of reason to be wary of the Cowboys’ offense. And the Packers shut it down, despite their ever-growing list of injuries. How? In part because of contributions from a strong rookie class. Brandon Cisse played his best game as a pro against the Cowboys’ terrific receiving duo, earning his first career interception in the process (admittedly a bit of a cheapie, but you take what you can get). Dani-Dennis Sutton, meanwhile, continued to provide regular pressure, shoring up an edge rusher room widely condemned in the national press as being bereft of talent without Micah Parsons. Chris McClellan has continued to provide valuable, if unspectacular, reps on the defensive line, and Trey Smack was perfect kicking field goals and PATs. That’s a pretty good night from a rookie class that’s looking pretty darn good, even without a first round pick in the mix. And to loosely quote Al McGuire, the best thing about rookies is they’ll eventually not be rookies, pointing to good things ahead from this group of players. It’s still a mystery how far the Packers can go this year, but their promising rookies will help them along the way to wherever they end up and beyond, continuing to grow as they figure out what it means to be an NFL player. summary: When the Green Bay Packers and Detroit Lions meet up for their first of two 2026 regular season matchups on Sunday afternoon, nearly every media market in the United States will get to see the game on local television. These two teams have combined for five playoff appearances in the past three years, and both […]
full_text: DETROIT, MI - NOVEMBER 27: Television camera operators for FOX Sports follow the action on the field during an NFL regular season Thanksgiving Day football game between the Green Bay Packers and the Detroit Lions on November 27, 2025 at Ford Field in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Scott W. Grau/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images When the Green Bay Packers and Detroit Lions meet up for their first of two 2026 regular season matchups on Sunday afternoon, nearly every media market in the United States will get to see the game on local television. These two teams have combined for five playoff appearances in the past three years, and both come into Week 7 with a winning record; as a result, FOX made it their late-afternoon game of the week when the NFL announced its schedule in May, and that slot has held up despite some early-season struggles on the Packers’ part. In fact, the Packers have bounced back remarkably from a 1-2 start that saw their game against the Chicago Bears two weeks ago — also initially slated for a large viewership in the 3:25 PM window — get flexed back into the early afternoon. (To be fair, the injury to Bears quarterback Caleb Williams surely factored in as well.) Green Bay now sits at 4-2 and on a three-game winning streak, while the Lions are 3-2 and coming off a bye week. These two teams have combined for some great games in the past few years, though 2025 saw the Packers sweep Detroit for the first time in Dan Campbell’s tenure as head coach of the Lions. Detroit is currently favored by 3 points, but this game very much feels like a tossup, especially if the Lions’ last-ranked passing defense continues to play the way it has to this point in the season. Ready to watch some fireworks? Good, because unless you’re in California and Nevada, you’re getting this game on your local FOX affiliate. The only other game on FOX in this time slot is Rams-Raiders, which will have a very limited local viewing area this week. Packers-Lions is shown in red on this week’s broadcast map below, provided by 506sports.com: As the top game on the network this week, Packers and Lions fans will get the network’s top broadcast tandem of Kevin Burkhardt and Tom Brady. Burkhardt has a day off from his duties as the pregame and postgame panel host for the World Series, but he’s not traveling far — games 1 and 2 will be held in Milwaukee on Friday and Saturday nights, giving him a short flight over Lake Michigan for Sunday’s game at Ford Field before he presumably makes a trip down to Tampa for Monday’s game 3.

title: Jordan Love’s interception against the Cowboys wasn’t his fault
summary: When a receiver doesn’t run to where he’s supposed to, defenders are able to make plays on the football. The Green Bay Packers benefitted from this on Sunday, when Dallas Cowboys receiver CeeDee Lamb slipped on one of his routes, leading to a cornerback Brandon Cisse’s interception. Unless you were paying close attention on Sunday, […]
full_text: (Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images) | Getty Images When a receiver doesn’t run to where he’s supposed to, defenders are able to make plays on the football. The Green Bay Packers benefitted from this on Sunday, when Dallas Cowboys receiver CeeDee Lamb slipped on one of his routes, leading to a cornerback Brandon Cisse’s interception. Unless you were paying close attention on Sunday, though, you probably missed that Packers quarterback Jordan Love’s interception was in part to blame on his target running the wrong route, too. pic.twitter.com/nhDw2PTyYQ — Justis Mosqueda (@JuMosq) October 21, 2026 Earlier this week, Green Bay head coach Matt LaFleur confirmed that receiver Matthew Golden was supposed to run a “Lookie” route from the slot, which makes sense considering the motion that the Packers ran, the matchup they got “on” Golden and the outside target to Golden’s side running a mandatory outside release. pic.twitter.com/0EIG64G12T — Justis Mosqueda (@JuMosq) October 21, 2026 What is a Lookie route? Here’s how it’s described in one of the Packers’ playbooks that I have access to. Essentially, a receiver runs vertical, stutters and then his first option on the route is to run a slant. If the defender on him has hard inside leverage on him (square leverage is a slant, as well as outside leverage), then he’s supposed to convert and run an out route. In the book, the receiver is instructed to “make every effort to cross the defender’s face” for a slant. pic.twitter.com/3MBLZK9d0J — Justis Mosqueda (@JuMosq) October 21, 2026 To make it simple: It’s an option route from the slot (slant or out), which is why the outside receiver is instructed to run an “M.O.R.” in the Packers’ playbook. “M.O.R” means a mandatory outside release. Basically, the outside receiver is just there to clear space for the slot, in case an out route does happen. The Lookie route is also the first read on the play. Teams like to call this when they get an advantageous matchup (like a slot receiver on a non-defensive back), as it gives the route-runner a “two-way go” to make that defender wrong 100 percent of the time — at least on paper. Below is the full play from the interception against the Cowboys. pic.twitter.com/09NIxbwx25 — Justis Mosqueda (@JuMosq) October 21, 2026 What’s interesting about this play is the motion, as Golden goes from what was a trips side to what was the single-receiver side. Because the Packers started out in trips and motioned Golden away from the slot, the slot defender couldn’t travel with Golden, forcing an off-ball linebacker to play “on” Golden. (Note: They were in zone, so no one is truly man-to-man.) Golden ends up square with the linebacker after his stutter, but decided to break outside anyway, which gave the linebacker, who had a flat responsibility in quarters coverage, the opportunity to undercut the football. According to LaFleur, Love expected Golden to run the slant, which is why the ball was a little late on the out route. Certainly, Golden didn’t “make every effort to cross the defender’s face” for the slant. LaFleur also mentioned that something happened on the backside of the play to force the Mike linebacker to squeeze the window tighter than expected too (it was the Will linebacker who was “on” Golden), but Christian Watson, who was in the opposite slot, appears to have run a “China” route, which is common on the backside of Lookie plays. I’m not in the coaches’ room and very well could be wrong (and it would not be my first time), but I would assume that the flub was on the running back. Often, these “Lookie” plays are run out of empty (to stretch the spacing of that Mike linebacker), so it’s possible the back wasn’t even supposed to be on the backfield in that play. pic.twitter.com/l2ka8VsxVS — Justis Mosqueda (@JuMosq) October 10, 2023 The Lookie route is very common in the NFL, and the Packers have been on the wrong end of it before. Notably, it’s how then-Raider Davante Adams got an explosive catch-and-run (out of an empty set) when Preston Smith was split out in space (as a flat defender) a couple of years ago. That is what the play was supposed to look like when Green Bay ended up with Golden “on” a linebacker after the motion. Unfortunately, a wrong decision on an option route can disrupt the timing of a pass and put a defender in a position to make a play on the ball. Hopefully, Golden can learn from this lesson and not repeat his mistake.

title: Houston Texans NFL Power Rankings Week 7
summary: The morning sun rose upon a new day last Sunday, and as the Houston Texans suited up for their week six game against the Jacksonville Jaguars, a fortunate wind blew in their favor. After succumbing to multiple heartbreakers to start the season, the Texans have now won two in a row following a thrilling, nail-biting, […]
full_text: The morning sun rose upon a new day last Sunday, and as the Houston Texans suited up for their week six game against the Jacksonville Jaguars, a fortunate wind blew in their favor. After succumbing to multiple heartbreakers to start the season, the Texans have now won two in a row following a thrilling, nail-biting, tubthumping, eye-popping whale of a game against the Jaguars, capping it off with a 49-yard game-winning field goal by one of the best to ever kick a football: Ka’imi Fairbairn! KA’IMI FAIRBAIRN GAME WINNING FIELD GOAL. 📺: @nflnetwork pic.twitter.com/wjV61KEY8s — Houston Texans (@HoustonTexans) October 18, 2026 That kick may have only been to improve to a record of 2-4, but it meant so much more than just one win for this team. The Texans found themselves in rather uncharted territory starting the season at 0-4, and the journey back to a successful season was going to require a win like this. They had to prove they could beat a good opponent at some point, and now – thanks to the brilliance of the QB CJ Stroud – they have! Stroud had one of his very best games as an NFL quarterback last Sunday, granting the primarily British crowd at Wembley Stadium the opportunity to bear witness to the triumphant return of 2023-era Stroud, the emergence of a true speed demon in WR Jaylin Noel, and, finally, a game-winning drive from the Texans themselves instead of their opponent! They may still be searching for answers on defense, but at least the Texans have finally got the MVP version of Stroud to awaken from his slumber! CJ Stroud is making all the throws look easy, and they are on target. Highest accuracy over expectation and the 3rd-highest completion over expectation. pic.twitter.com/zYZav3JYps — Troy_OTC (@TexansCap) October 20, 2026 Is C.J. Stroud back? Through Week 6, he has the highest PFF grade and EPA efficiency of his career pic.twitter.com/t9urPn50qB — Kevin Cole (@KevinCole___) October 19, 2026 This 34-31 victory was all about Stroud and his ability to pull off impossible throws like he’s pulling rabbits out of his hat. He made full use of his long cast of talented receivers, even hitting TE Foster Moreau for two touchdowns, including one of the most impressive catches you’ll ever see: Despite all the fanfare, the Texans are still just 2-4, and multiple games outside of the AFC playoff race. This may have been an impressive win against a true contender, but the Texans are still working to dig themselves out of the hole they fell in after losing four games in a row. But, this kind of victory, even if it’s just one win on paper, can do a lot to improve the morale of the team going forward. Now, they have captured some amount of the ever elusive, undefinable “momentum” that all football organizations are searching for. Like an ancient artifact, momentum is a concept that is hard to define, yet all football teams yearn for it, even as many claim not to believe in it. The concept of carrying some sort of abstract, positive force from one week of football to the next is something that doesn’t really make any sense, yet seems to have an impact on the NFL season every year, like some sort of invisible hand that guides the best teams to the top of the heap. Have the Texans found their momentum? Well, it certainly feels like they have, but we probably won’t know until the momentum has long passed, so for now, let’s just see where all of those Power Rankings pundits have placed the Texans, now! Here’s where the Houston Texans land after their 34-31 victory over the Jacksonville Jaguars: NFL.COM : 14. Houston Texans (Last Week: 25) Don’t look now, but the Texans are clawing their way back into relevance! Houston’s defense isn’t the shutdown unit it was in years past, but the talent-laden group has inched itself closer to familiarity since DeMeco Ryans took the play-calling reins. Most importantly, C.J. Stroud is playing some of the best football of his career. His performance in London was simply exquisite (save for his late interception in the end zone), and if the Texans can sustain their turnaround, he’ll force his way into the MVP conversation. – Nick Shook ESPN: 16. Houston Texans (2-4) Week 6 result: Beat the Jaguars 34-31 Week 6 ranking: 21 Biggest issue on offense: Lack of a run game The Texans’ passing attack is humming, as quarterback C.J. Stroud ranks second leaguewide in passing yards (1,712), but an effective run game would take this offense to the top tier. They’re averaging 84.8 rushing yards per game (25th) and have 32 rushing first downs on the season (tied for 22nd). Running back David Montgomery , who was acquired via trade in March, is averaging a career-low 2.7 yards per carry and missed Week 6 because of a groin injury . – DJ Bien-Aime SPORTS ILLUSTRATED: 14. Houston Texans (2–4) Last week’s ranking: No. 14 Last week’s result: beat Jaguars, 34–31 This week: vs. Giants Forget about the defense. The narrative heading into the trade deadline should be: How much more help can Houston provide C.J. Stroud, who is playing at a top-10 level over the course of the last month and seeing the field better than he has in two years. My take? Call Philadelphia and see what Saquon Barkley has left in the tank. – Conor Orr BLEACHER REPORT: 19. Houston Texans (2-4) Last Week: 26 Week 6 Result: Won vs. Jacksonville 34-31 (London) The Houston Texans didn’t get their first win of 2026 until Week 5. They’ve now won two in a row and have reentered the AFC South picture with a victory over the rival Jacksonville Jaguars. Houston’s defense hasn’t been nearly as dominant as it was a year ago. However, C.J. Stroud is playing at a Pro Bowl level and leads a balanced offense—when healthy—that will give the Texans a chance to win more often than not. New wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. had just three receptions for 34 yards in his Texans debut on Sunday, but he should help open up the passing attack. Climbing out of a 2-4 hole will be difficult, of course. However, Houston did exactly that last season and made it to the divisional round. This is a team that must be taken seriously moving forward, even if it is still chasing the early playoff field. – Kris Knox CBS SPORTS: 15. Texans (2-4) (Last Week: 23) That was a big-time victory in London over the Jaguars. C.J. Stroud is really playing at a high level, but the defense has to pick it up. – Pete Prisco USA TODAY: 20. Houston Texans (26): They continue to have one of the league’s least-efficient run games. But that defense, QB C.J. Stroud’s inspired play and an upgraded wideout corps − not to mention DeMeco Ryans calling the defensive plays again − suggest this team could go on another long heater. – Nate Davis YAHOO! SPORTS: 17. Houston Texans (2-4, LW: 24) The 2025 Texans started 0-3, blew out a hapless Titans team, then got a 44-10 win against the Ravens and that led to a 12-5 record and a playoff berth. This season’s Texans started 0-4, blew out a hapless Titans team and then got a huge 34-31 win against a good Jaguars team in London. The next four games are vs. Giants, at Chargers, at Browns, vs. Colts. Those teams rank 28th, 31st, 21st and 25th in DVOA. Nothing is guaranteed in the NFL, but there’s an opportunity for the Texans to be 6-4 in a month. The play of C.J. Stroud offers long-term optimism. He led all quarterbacks in EPA per play in Week 6 through Sunday’s games, and did so against a Jaguars defense that was playing well. Stroud has been up and down this season, but has generally been good as long as Nico Collins is in the lineup. If he continues to play well, digging out of an 0-4 hole is very possible. – Frank Schwab THE ATHLETIC: 17. Houston Texans (2-4) Last week: 21 Sunday: Beat Jaguars 34-31 Fantasy focu s : C.J. Stroud Houston’s slow start was not the fault of its quarterback. Stroud, who is in the fourth year of his rookie deal and is headed toward interesting contract negotiations with the Texans, is 16th in the league in fantasy scoring (112.2) and on pace for the best passer…

title: Redrafting Texans 2026 NFL Draft Class Through Six Weeks
summary: The 2026 season isn’t over, but the Texans rookie class has already made their mark on the season. It’s a mixed bag of results thus far with the two second round picks Kayden McDonald and Marlin Klein making little impact on the field. It’s still early, but it’s a fun exercise to see who the […]
full_text: The 2026 season isn’t over, but the Texans rookie class has already made their mark on the season. It’s a mixed bag of results thus far with the two second round picks Kayden McDonald and Marlin Klein making little impact on the field. It’s still early, but it’s a fun exercise to see who the Texans could have selected with each of their picks in the 2026 NFL Draft. Round 1, Pick 26: Austin Barber, RG – Florida (Cleveland Browns) Texans pick : Keylan Rutledge, G – Georgia Tech While Rutledge hasn’t been bad, he hasn’t been exactly as powerful as anticipated. Austin Barber has arguably been the best interior offensive lineman of the entire class and he was considered a reach in the third round. The third rounder has crushed it and elevated the Browns offensive line this season. Houston could use the right guard’s run blocking on their team. Round 2, Pick 36: Denzel Boston, WR – Washington (Cleveland Browns) Texans pick : Kayden McDonald, DT – Ohio State Rookie Kayden McDonald missed the first four weeks due to a high ankle sprain. He’s played in each of the last two games, but has yet to make the impact as Cleveland’s second round pick Denzel Boston picked three selections after McDonald. Boston has been a breakout star for the Browns making plays down the field and stretching the defense with his incredible catch radius. Boston would have complimented Nico Collins, Jayden Higgins, and now Tank Dell extremely well. Round 2, Pick 59: Anthony Hill, LB – Texas Texans pick : Marlin Klein, TE – Michigan ‘Sideline Klien’ is back again… not playing. It’s extremely tough given how much the Texans invested in the versatile tight end. They’re right back to running six offensive lineman sets. Anthony Hill Jr. was the defensive rookie of the month for the Titans. That production would have saved the Texans in multiple games while both Henry To’oTo’o were out. Hill’s long-term development and potential is sky high; we’ll see if that’s the case for Klein. Round 4, Pick 106: Gracen Halton, DT – Oklahoma Texans pick : Febechi Nwaiwu, G – Oklahoma DT Darrell Jackson Jr. was selected three picks before Nwaiwu and would’ve been the selection here, but instead we’ll go with his college teammate in Gracen Halton. The fourth round pick won the starting role after Alfred Collins and C.J. West landed on IR. Nwaiwu has yet to record a snap since week three. The lack of depth at guard hurts this team. Houston could use the defensive line production from Halton, especially in the pas rush game. Round 4, Pick 123: Emmett Johnson, RB – Nebraska (Kansas City Chiefs) Texans pick : Wade Woodaz, LB – Clemson A “my guy” has from this draft class, rookie Emmett Johnson has been a good change of pace back behind Kenneth Walker III. He’s put together 19 carries for 62 yards but its his seven catches for 92 yards that have been impactful. Houston could use his depth and pass catching ability in their offense, especially with David Montgomery out. Woodaz has improved week over week and thrust into a position he wasn’t ready for. While Woodaz will make for a good depth piece, Johnson will be an instant impact asset for the Chiefs moving forward. Round 5, Pick 141: Zakee Wheatley, S – Penn State (Carolina Panthers) Texans pick : Kamari Ramsey, S – USC Just as I predicted when I listed Wheatley as a top “my guy” in the class , he’s earned a starting spot in Carolina’s secondary. He’s an elite athlete with great size. Though Ramsey has been a strong spot player for the Texans, he hasn’t been as immediately impactful as Wheatley. This was the closest one of all the picks so far given Ramsey’s support with both Jalen Pitre and Reed Blankenship out. Round 6, Pick 204: Harold Perkins Jr., LB – LSU (Atlanta Falcons) Texans pick : Lewis Bond, WR – Boston College Between the injuries, positional changes, and inconsistent production, Perkins slid from a first round prospect to a sixth round pick. He has won the starting job at inside linebacker and has dominated right off the bat. His tackling and coverage grades are at the top of this class. With all of the injuries at linebacker, Perkins skill inside and contribution on special teams would have possibly won the Texans a game or two early. Conversely, Lewis Bond, for all the hype, has been a non-factor all season. If anything, his lack of development has directly led to the Texans needing to trade for both Marvin Harrison Jr. and Kayshon Boutte. Round 7, Pick 243: Deion Burks, WR – Oklahoma (Indianapolis Colts) Texans pick : Aiden Fisher, LB – Indiana There’s only 14 players selected after Fisher, but still several compelling options. Burks has stepped up as of late due to injuries in the Colts WR room. He’s been active every game and has three receptions and three carries. He’s used as a downfield option for Daniel Jones and has shown flashes of big playmaking ability. That’s more than we can we can say about Aiden Fisher. He’s played primarily special teams through three games, but hasn’t made the impact that Burks has with the Colts. Which player do you wish the Texans drafted? Comment down below!

summary: Thanks to the nflFastR project, Pro Football Focus for the timely sources of data. full_text: Thanks to the nflFastR project, Pro Football Focus for the timely sources of data. For those of you new to this, I will publish key QB stats each week judging how well the Colts’ QB performed. Yes, O-Line, receivers, and play-calling impact these numbers but they are primarily QB measures. I will probably modify the charts throughout the season. Commentary will be brief but feel free to let me know in the comments that stats aren’t everything. (click charts for larger view) The Colts offense didn’t so much have a problem moving the ball downfield as they did simply holding onto to it. A 72.7% Drive Success rate can win you games but not if you give the opponent the ball 3 times. Daniel Jones was responsible for two of those turnovers, and his anemic second-half passing performance pretty much sealed the Colts’ fate. Let’s read the story from the numbers. HOW WELL? mouseover definitions: arsr , edp , sg% , oz% , pr% , tip , ttt , adot , ay/c , yac , yacoe , yd/c , ac% , cpoe , aypa , drp , scr% , ta% , sck% , aa% , ny/d , ny/p , 1st% , td% , to% , qbsr , epa/p , adj/p Indianapolis got solid production from its running game while using a fairly balanced approach on early downs. ( 11th ARSR; 12th EDP ) Jones faced a fair amount of pressure but generally took longer than average to get rid of the ball, which means he invited a lot of the pressure himself. (13th PR%; 10th TIP; 6th TTT ) Jones attacked downfield aggressively, throwing deeper than almost anyone in the league. However, he had trouble connecting and so his completions came at a much more ordinary depth. Fortunately, the receivers provided strong production after the catch helping generate good overall yardage per completion. ( 2nd ADOT; 16th AY/C; 7th YAC; 8th YCOE; 10th YD/C ) The big problem was that Jones struggled to complete passes consistently, finishing near the bottom of the league in adjusted completion rate. That offset the completion yardage, leaving his passing production per attempt below average. ( 29th AC%; 22nd CPOE; 17th AYPA ) Drops were a big factor, but the biggest problem was sacks. He was sacked six times, taking away a significant amount of potential passing production. ( 8th DRP; 5th SCK% ) Add in throw-aways and scrambles and in total, he abandoned a lot of passes. Those lost plays dragged down the passing game’s overall yardage production, leaving Jones well below average in net yards per dropback. ( 24th TA%, 11th SCR%, 8th AA%, 21st NY/D ) With poor yardage, Jones couldn’t generate first downs and he managed only one touchdown. ( 19th 1ST%; 23rd TD% ) Turnovers were particularly damaging. Jones threw two interceptions, both costly negative plays, giving him one of the highest turnover rates of the week. ( 4th TO% ) He was below average at generating successful plays and the combination of sacks and two interceptions didn’t dropped his overall efficiency even further. ( 18th QBSR; 20th EPA/P ) mouseover definitions: ay< , dp% , ay/c , yac , yd/c , ac% , aypa , drp% , aypa , ta% , ypa , sck% , ny/a , scr% , ny/d , car% , ny/p , 1st% , any/p , td% , any/p , to% , any/p , epa/p , opd , adj/p Jones had decent yardage efficiency on a per-completion basis, largely thanks to strong production after the catch. However, just like last week, his poor completion rate brought his overall yardage efficiency back below average. From there, his efficiency was mostly impacted by sacks and turnovers, both of which caused significant declines. Jones started the game fairly well, generating several positive plays before an interception wiped out much of that early production. He rebounded with some productive passing in the second quarter, including a touchdown, but his performance became increasingly inconsistent as sacks and incompletions piled up. Overall, the costly negative plays outweighed his positive production, leaving him at -0.09 EPA per play. Jones was below average in all top 4 measures. He has been trending downward, with his performance becoming increasingly inconsistent. After a strong Week 2, his overall efficiency and yardage production have fallen considerably, while his success rate and first-down production have also slipped below average. Despite a modest rebound in Week 5, all four measures remain below league average, suggesting a broader decline rather than just one bad game. HOW FAR? Jones started with some productive completions, but his passing became increasingly inconsistent, with two interceptions and frequent incompletions interrupting his rhythm. He had another productive stretch in the fourth quarter, but finished the game going 1 for 8. His throws were generally aggressive downfield, averaging 11.5 yards beyond the line of scrimmage, but he completed just 53.7% of his passes (adjusted). Again this week, passing was particularly aggressive, averaging 11.5 air yards per attempt. However, his completed passes came at a much more ordinary depth, continuing the gap between where he targets receivers and where he actually completes passes. Jones has generated below-average yardage per attempt this season, ranking 26th in the league oof of the 7th shortest attempts. TO WHO? Keenan Allen led the Colts in receiving yards and air yards, catching 8 of 11 targets. Jonathan Taylor was the other major contributor to receiving yardage, with most of his production coming after the catch on just two receptions. Josh Downs leads the Colts in receiving yards, followed by Keenan Allen. Tyler Warren is a close 3rd with Jonathan Taylor beating out Treadwell for the 4th spot. Keenan Allen was Jones’s most productive regular target, generating positive EPA on relatively deep throws, while Josh Downs was only below average target value. Treadwell and Mallory had the deepest targets but were significantly below average value. Josh Downs and Alec Pierce have been Jones’s most efficient downfield targets this season, both generating well-above-average EPA per target. Tyler Warren has also provided solid value on shorter throws, while Jonathan Taylor has been roughly average. Keenan Allen has been a disappointment relative to his target depth, generating very little positive EPA, while Laquon Treadwell is also on the team. HOW ACCURATE? Jones’s completion rate has fallen sharply over the past two weeks, dropping well below league average along with his CPOE, which means his incompletions aren’t just because they are long throws. On the season, he has struggled at nearly every depth, other than screen passes. HOW FAST? Jones took considerably longer to throw this week, reversing the quicker passing rhythm he had established over the previous several games. However, his season-long time to throw is still below average for his target depth. TO WHERE? Within 10 yards, he did well. However, passes over the middle and deeper shots were a dumpster fire. Jones has struggled throwing the ball downfield throughout the season, with below-average efficiency at just about every depth and across all areas of the field.

summary: The Indianapolis Colts today’s released their Wednesday injury report for week 7 of the NFL season against the Minnesota Vikings. Wide receiver Keenan Allen, running back Jonathan Taylor and cornerback Charvarius Ward were all unable to practice at full capacity today. Taylor was limited and both Allen and Ward missed practice due to veteran rest […]
full_text: The Indianapolis Colts today’s released their Wednesday injury report for week 7 of the NFL season against the Minnesota Vikings. Wednesday's practice report for #INDvsMIN . pic.twitter.com/jXmLuL7s8n — Indianapolis Colts (@Colts) October 21, 2026 Wide receiver Keenan Allen, running back Jonathan Taylor and cornerback Charvarius Ward were all unable to practice at full capacity today. Taylor was limited and both Allen and Ward missed practice due to veteran rest days. Linebacker Bryce Boettcher (groin) missed practice today. Whilst fellow linebacker Jaylon Carlies (ribs) was limited, he has missed two games through injury. Austin Ajake (concussion) was limited as the team evaluates him to see if he needs to enter the concussion protocol. The Colts linebacker group is getting more and more banged up and there could be a return to the starting line up for Germaine Pratt this week off the practice squad. Cornerbacks Sauce Gardner (calf) and Justin Walley (knee) both missed practice today. Two starting corners missing practice in a Wednesday isn’t a great look for a 2-4 team in need of a big week. Gardner is likely out multiple weeks through injuring his calf. Wallet needs to bounce back tomorrow or could be at rush if missing this week too. Guard Matt Goncalves (ankle) missed practice today. Right ta Joe Jalen Travis (foot) was limited. The right side of the Colts OL being unable to practice fully today is another worry for the Colts heading into a game against the best defense in football this year. Hopefully both can manage to practice tomorrow and Friday. Tight ends Tyler Warren (groin) and Andrew Ogletree (ankle) both missed practice today. Warren is still dealing with a groin injury he sustained at practice last week. Ogletree appears to have picked up a knock to his ankle. Dulin was limited as he works his way back from a hamstring injury he had been dealing with all year. Gould enters the concussion protocol and is likely to be out this week. title: Colts Interim GM Ed Dodds makes first moves by adding pair of veterans to practice squad
summary: Busy day yesterday, so catching up with the Indianapolis Colts, where interim general manager Ed Dodds made his first roster moves in his position with the franchise for the remainder of the 2026 campaign: It’ll be interesting to see how Dodds leaves his fingerprints on the franchise the next few months compared to his longtime […]
full_text: CLEVELAND, OHIO - AUGUST 22: Mecole Hardman Jr. #1 of the Buffalo Bills celebrates after scoring a nine-yard touchdown during the second quarter of a preseason game against the Cleveland Browns at Huntington Bank Field on August 22, 2026 in Cleveland, Ohio. (Photo by Nick Cammett/Diamond Images via Getty Images) | Diamond Images/Getty Images Busy day yesterday, so catching up with the Indianapolis Colts, where interim general manager Ed Dodds made his first roster moves in his position with the franchise for the remainder of the 2026 campaign: We have signed WR Mecole Hardman Jr. and P Thomas Morstead to the practice squad. We have also released WR Eli Pancol from the practice squad. — Indianapolis Colts (@Colts) October 20, 2026 It’ll be interesting to see how Dodds leaves his fingerprints on the franchise the next few months compared to his longtime GM predecessor, Chris Ballard, who was relieved of his duties earlier this week. The 28-year-year old Harman, who was originally a 2019 2nd round pick of the Kansas City Chiefs, is most known for being a deep threat for that franchise. However, he’s bounced a round a bit since then, having also played with the New York Jets, Green Bay Packers, and Buffalo Bills organizations. At 5,’10”, 187 pounds, Hardman has 178 receptions for 2,302 receiving yards (12.9 ypc. avg.) and 16 touchdown receptions during 82 career games (28 starts). He appeared in 2 games for the Bills last season, but didn’t record a catch. He has not appeared in 2026 with an NFL team, but will be looking to continue his professional football career with the Colts. Meanwhile, after punter Colts Rigoberto Sanchez suffered a big hit late on a blocked punt during Sunday’s brutal home loss to the Tennessee Titans, and sustained a foot injury, Indianapolis is bringing in veteran punter Thomas Morstead for insurance, should Sanchez be unavailable for this weekend’s road game against the Minnesota Vikings. The 40-year-old longtime punter has appeared in 272 career games, and was the rookie punter for the New Orleans Saints during their 2009 upset Super Bowl win against the Indianapolis Colts. He actually executed the surprise second-half onside kick, which talk about a bad memory and a blast from the past. Morstead punted for the San Francisco 49ers last year in all 17 games, averaging 43.6 yards per punt on his 44 punts, including 22 pinned within the opponent’s 20-yard line.

title: 1 playoff win, 10 seasons, and 100 reasons why the Colts had to fire Chris Ballard
summary: “I don’t understand how that person still works here.” That is a statement most of us have made at some time or another about that one person who seems to get away with everything despite their poor performance. They’re late. They don’t get all their work done. Others have to pick up the slack, and […]
full_text: “I don’t understand how that person still works here.” That is a statement most of us have made at some time or another about that one person who seems to get away with everything despite their poor performance. They’re late. They don’t get all their work done. Others have to pick up the slack, and they have a bad attitude. Somehow, they keep their job. It’s as if they have something on the boss… When the day finally comes and that person has been released or left, it’s almost unbelievable even though you’ve anticipated it for years. That is exactly how I feel about the Indianapolis Colts finally pulling the trigger and firing Chris Ballard. For the last three years, I have publicly advocated for the Colts to cut ties with Ballard. It’s nothing personal. It’s just business, and business has been bad. It was bad enough to justify a firing before the last three years, but a bad thing has somehow gotten worse. Ballard had some bright spots. This isn’t to say everything he touched turned to dust, but in the NFL, a few bright spots don’t cut it. Winning is all that matters and quite frankly, Ballard didn’t do enough of it. To the Ballard apologists, we can look historically or recently, but the outlook doesn’t change. After ten years at the helm, Ballard’s Colts made the playoffs twice, winning once. They have zero AFC championships during that time. A hat with AFC South Champs would have been in the Goodwill bin during the Manning years because they were a dime a dozen. Nowadays, they would be like discovering buried treasure. Why didn’t the Colts win under Ballard? I’ll give you a hint: it has nothing to do with Andrew Luck retiring. Was that a blow? Certainly, but life is all about how we handle adversity. Ballard had plenty of years and chances to right that ship. There were some fantastic draft picks along the way, but there were way too many failures too. Build the trenches was the motto, but the modern NFL is built on the edges and at quarterback. Even the trenches have struggled mightily over the years. A fresh and more modern approach is needed. If you don’t like history, let’s look at this year. A 2-4 record after having lost to the worst team in football at home was the final straw. A $50 million quarterback who isn’t throwing downfield and when he does, it’s to the other team, and a benched fourth overall pick backing him up is the current situation at the game’s most important position. Receivers are being brought in off the street while the defensive line generates no pressure, resulting in the secondary getting cooked. This isn’t legacy. This is now. In a win now, what have you done for me lately type of league, this doesn’t cut it. Pile on the last decade, and it’s obvious why the Colts cut ties. Honestly, if you’re still on the fence about this move, why? What have you seen that makes you still back Chris Ballard? “Well, you can fire him but that doesn’t mean there is someone better to take his place…” Maybe that’s the case, but most likely not. Does it get much worse? Being too good to rebuild with quality draft selections but not good enough to be in contention is the worst possible place for a sports franchise. Ballard knew the gig was up. He knew he didn’t perform to the required standards, and the Colts were more than patient. There were 100 reasons to fire Ballard. It took the 100th, but the right move was finally made.

title: Jaguars drop in NFL power rankings entering Week 7
summary: The Jacksonville Jaguars enter their Week 7 bye with a sour taste in their mouth after losing to the division rival Houston Texans. Still, the Jags are in the driver’s seat in the AFC South. They’re feeling good about where they’re at through a third of the season. “We strung together some good performances,” safety […]
full_text: LONDON, ENGLAND - OCTOBER 18: Trevor Lawrence of the Jacksonville Jaguars runs with the ball during the NFL London Series match between Houston Texans and Jacksonville Jaguars at Wembley Stadium on October 18, 2026 in London, England. (Photo by Alex Davidson/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Jacksonville Jaguars enter their Week 7 bye with a sour taste in their mouth after losing to the division rival Houston Texans. Still, the Jags are in the driver’s seat in the AFC South. They’re feeling good about where they’re at through a third of the season. “We strung together some good performances,” safety Eric Murray said Tuesday. “I think the biggest thing going forward is just hitting on consistency and getting back to what we do on a more consistent basis. Not necessarily putting ourselves in bad positions where we can’t make plays and going off of that but just being more consistent. We are 4-2 at the bye, it’s nothing to be going crazy about. It’s just lock in and keep going.” As Week 7 approaches, we rounded up the latest NFL power rankings to get a sense of how the Jaguars are viewed nationally. Pro Football Talk: 4 (last week: 3) From Mike Florio : They’re finally getting a return on the Travis Hunter investment. ESPN: 5 (5) From Michael DiRocco : Penalties have cost the Jaguars three touchdowns, including a pair of 3-yard touchdown runs by running back Bhayshul Tuten. It happened again in Sunday’s loss, with a questionable holding call on tight end Brenton Strange. The Jaguars didn’t get points on that possession because QB Trevor Lawrence threw an end zone interception two plays later. Jacksonville did score touchdowns after the other two penalties, against New England and Cincinnati, but it finally caught up to them in a three-point loss to the Texans. NFL.com: 5 (5) From Nick Shook : The Jaguars’ high-scoring loss to the Texans at Wembley Stadium was one of the best games of the season so far. Two division rivals battled for four quarters, and the Jaguars erased a 10-point deficit, but they had to still be irritated as they flew home from their two-week trip after a last-second defeat. Travis Hunter’s emergence should be monitored going forward — his two-way ability is finally adding significant value to the Jaguars’ larger equation. Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android . Bleacher Report: 7 (5) From Kris Knox : Jacksonville features an elite run defense and boasts an offense that can match points with anyone when Trevor Lawrence is taking care of the football. That could be enough for the Jags to control the AFC South and push into the postseason with plenty of momentum. However, it’s fair to wonder if Jacksonville can corral top signal-callers in January. The Athletic: 7 (5) From Josh Kendall and Chad Graff : Fantasy focus: Trevor Lawrence. The Jags quarterback is outperforming his draft position by more than 50 spots. He went off the board an average of 86th, but he’s 22nd in scoring (19.0 ppg) through six games. Lawrence’s EPA per dropback this season (0.20) is nearly twice his career high, and Jacksonville lost Sunday despite a four-touchdown, one-interception performance from its leader on offense. USA Today: 7 (5) From Nate Davis : CB/WR Travis Hunter played a season-high 71 snaps Sunday, quite a few of them impactful, and the Jags lost − through no fault of Hunter, who’s played nearly every defensive snap the past three weeks. Still trying to find his sweet spot, but we may finally be near it. Same can’t be said for WR Brian Thomas Jr. Sports Illustrated: 8 (2) From Conor Orr : It’s hard to penalize the Jaguars that much for a shootout loss to the heating-up Texans. But if Travis Hunter can do this and this in the same game, and we can inch him on the field more after possibly trading Brian Thomas Jr., I like the ceiling for this team. CBS Sports: 8 (5) From Pete Prisco : They have to do a better job rushing the passer if they are to be a deep-playoff team. They have to make a move to get somebody at the trade deadline. Fox Sports: 8 (5) From Ralph Vacchiano : The Jaguars’ offense is finally starting to click, but their 34-31 loss to the Texans in London should be a wake-up call that their defense isn’t everything they thought it was. Maybe they were just tired from a long couple of weeks in London, or maybe the Texans are just starting to roll. But even Houston’s disastrous running game managed to put up 114 yards on the Jags. The good news for them, though, is they have a really soft schedule coming out of the bye week, including games against the Colts and the Giants and two meetings with the Titans. title: Jaguars Trade Deadline Targets: 10 Defensive Players to Watch
summary: At 4-2, the AFC South-leading Jacksonville Jaguars are positioned to be a trade deadline buyer in a market where plenty of teams are early sellers. Winless Miami, a slumping Eagles squad, and a struggling Commanders team have all created an early 2026 where a few surprising veterans may be in play. With the Jacksonville defense […]
full_text: TAMPA, FL - OCTOBER 18: Tampa Bay Buccaneers Defensive Tackle Vita Vea (50) rushes the passer during the regular season game between the Pittsburgh Steelers and the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on October 18, 2026 at Raymond James Stadium in Tampa, Florida.(Photo by Cliff Welch/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images At 4-2, the AFC South-leading Jacksonville Jaguars are positioned to be a trade deadline buyer in a market where plenty of teams are early sellers. Winless Miami, a slumping Eagles squad, and a struggling Commanders team have all created an early 2026 where a few surprising veterans may be in play. With the Jacksonville defense recently putting up a season-high in rushing yards surrendered (114) and points allowed (34), the bye week felt like the perfect time to evaluate where the Jaguars could take a swing via trade after a 2025 season featuring 10 total draft-day and in-season trades. Here are a few potential trade targets for James Gladstone and the Jaguars’ defense, as the November 10th trade deadline approaches. Defensive Tackle (4) Daron Payne, DT, Commanders Projected Trade Value: Brian Thomas Jr for Payne (player for player) Payne (29) has 14 tackles, a sack, and a forced fumble in the six 2026 games played and is currently in the final year of a four-year, $90 million extension he signed in 2023. As he carries a current $27.95 million cap hit, any trade would likely require Washington to eat part of his salary, though sending Brian Thomas Jr. (BTJ) the other way, still on his rookie contract, makes that math work. With Washington’s loss of Terry McLaurin for the year due to a torn patellar tendon, and the team sitting at 1-4-1, just two games out of the division lead, optimism for salvaging the season still exists. While Payne’s 108th-ranked PFF pass rush grade (55.3) doesn’t pop, the Jacksonville appeal for Payne is a possible role change. Since his 11.5-sack season in 2022 playing primarily 3-technique defensive tackle, Washington has mostly used him as a nose tackle who absorbs double teams in recent years. His role in Jacksonville could be more fluid, playing more of that rotational 3T role with Arik Armstead, or in the 2I role on obvious passing downs, with Davon Hamilton off the field. He would also allow Travon Walker to rush exclusively from the edge instead of kicking inside. Zach Sieler, DT, Dolphins Projected Trade Value: Conditional 2027 5th-round pick (that can become a 4th with performance escalators) Sieler has 12 tackles, two sacks, and five tackles for loss, plus 11 quarterback pressures through five starts for the winless, rebuilding Dolphins. Sieler has had a down season in the struggling Miami defense, reflected by his “down” 62nd ranked PFF pass rush win rate of 63.0. He’s under contract through 2029 and only $10 million of his salary becomes guaranteed in March 2027. The ninth-year veteran has said publicly that he wants to stay in Miami and win there. However, an opportunity to remain in the state while playing for a contender could serve just as strong a selling point for the 31-year-old. Moro Ojomo, DT, Eagles Projected Trade Value: 2027 4th-Round Pick Ojomo, 25, has 13 tackles, 12 quarterback hurries, three hits, and no sacks through six games. Though his pass-rush numbers are somewhat better than that suggests, his 10.6% pressure rate leads Eagles defensive tackles and is well above the 7.9% league average for the position. However, PFF rates his pass rush grade 114th of 129 qualified interior defensive linemen at 54.0. He’s in the last year of his rookie deal at a $3.67 million base salary, and he posted six sacks last season. With Jalen Carter and Jordan Davis now extended and Philadelphia sitting at 2-4, he looks like he could be the obvious odd man out. With quarterback Jalen Hurts on IR for the remainder of the year and a playoff berth seemingly out of play, a move for future capital makes sense here. DeForest Buckner, DT, Colts Projected Trade Value: 2027 3rd-Round Pick + Brian Thomas Jr. At 32, Buckner is still producing like the elite defensive tackle we’ve seen since 2016. He has started all six games in 2026 with 26 tackles, four sacks, three passes defended, and nine pressures. His contract expires after this season, and a new team would take on his $8.7 million cap hit. He has also been openly frustrated with the Colts’ direction, and Indianapolis recently fired its general manager, signaling a change of guard. Buckner could be a cornerstone in that future rebuild. However, it seems more likely that the team would use the picks gained in his trade in a future roster build. A team trading an elite player to a divisional rival makes this the toughest sell. Two teams trading players in a swap to divisional rivals feels highly unlikely. But with the Colts still in need of receiver help, with Alec Pierce still nursing his offseason heel injury that was re-injured in Week 2, the win-win for both teams clearly exists. Buckner’s 2026 75.3 pass rush grade (13th) reflects a significant upgrade to Arik Armstead’s 56.1 (103rd of 129 qualified edges). Edge (3) Will McDonald IV, DE, Jets Projected Trade Value: 2027 3rd-Round pick (can become a 2nd with sack escalators) The biggest benefit in trading for McDonald is that he wouldn’t have to carry Jacksonville’s pass rush. He would be free to just win his one-on-one matchups. With his burst and closing speed, the Jaguars could employ a heavier rush-four approach. McDonald had 10.5 sacks in 2024 and eight sacks and 42 pressures last season. This year he has two sacks and 12 pressures in five games, a 14.1% pressure rate. PFF currently grades McDonald with a 71.5 pass rush grade (26th). The Jets picked up his $14.4 million fifth-year option for 2027, so he comes with another year of team control. He’s clearly a good player and still under team control for 2027, but at 2-4 and in a division with the Bills and Patriots, the Jets are obviously looking at another rebuilding year. But they may think they have a legitimate shot at the playoffs in 2027 and choose to hold onto him. A pick that could become a second-rounder could move them closer to the trade deadline. Josh Sweat, DE, Cardinals Projected Trade Value: Conditional 2027 4th-Round Pick Sweat is through the guarantees on his four-year, $76.4 million deal he signed in 2025, which gives any buyers flexibility. He’s 29 and in the middle of his prime. But this year has seen a slight dip in his production. He has just two sacks, 6 hurries, three tackles for loss, and 10 pressures, well below his 12-sack, 13-tackle-for-loss 2025. PFF grades Sweat with a 2026 59.2 pass rush grade, 75th among the 115 qualified edges. Khalil Mack, DE, Chargers Projected Trade Value: 2027 4th-Round Pick At 35, Mack is on an expiring deal on a team that sits at 0-6. He has started every game with 19 tackles, three sacks, five tackles for loss, and 11 pressures. The Bears have frequently been mentioned as a potential landing spot for him, though I think Jacksonville could be just as likely. L.A. has reportedly told teams it isn’t interested in dealing, but that stance may not survive many more losses. PFF currently rates Mack with a 75.2 overall grade, 25th among all qualified edges. His 66.1 pass rush grade (40th) is also higher than both Josh Hines-Allen (64.5; 46th) and Travon Walker (62.8; 57th). Cornerback (2) Zyon McCollum, CB, Buccaneers Projected Trade Value: 2027 3rd-Round Pick McCollum’s 2025 season was a disappointment, but the early returns in 2026 are mixed, despite the team’s 1-5 record. PFF has him at a 63.4 coverage grade (44th), with opposing passers posting a 75.0 rating when targeting him in coverage. But he also has three passes defended, a fumble recovery, a quarterback pressure, and two run stuffs through six games. Given McCollum’s superior man coverage (69.4 PFF coverage grade) paired with his 2024 and 2025 resume, where he was better in zone, he could be a piece that soundly fits in…

title: Jaguars Reacts Survey: Will Jacksonville win the AFC South this season?
summary: Welcome to SB Nation Reacts, a survey of fans across the NFL. Throughout the year we ask questions of the most plugged-in Jaguars fans and fans across the country. The Jacksonville Jaguars just can’t seem to get past the Houston Texans. The Jags have a 13-3 record in their last 16 regular season games, but […]
full_text: Football - NFL - Houston Texans v Jacksonville Jaguars - Wembley Stadium, London, Britain - October 18, 2026 Jacksonville Jaguars head coach Liam Coen looks on Action Images via Reuters/Paul Childs | Action Images via Reuters Welcome to SB Nation Reacts, a survey of fans across the NFL. Throughout the year we ask questions of the most plugged-in Jaguars fans and fans across the country. The Jacksonville Jaguars just can’t seem to get past the Houston Texans. The Jags have a 13-3 record in their last 16 regular season games, but two of those three losses came against the Texans, including Sunday’s 31-34 stunner . “That was not the result that you hunt up each week,” head coach Liam Coen said Monday. “You never want to lose, but I am glad that we’re able to respond in terms of the mental toughness of the group when it’s not perfect or everything’s not going exactly according to plan, and they just keep playing their tails off.” The Week 6 loss to Houston was a bummer, as was Jacksonville’s 10-point blown lead to Denver in Week 2. At the end of the day, though, the Jaguars have a 4-2 record going into their bye. They lead the AFC South by two games over the Texans (2-4), Indianapolis Colts (2-4), and Tennessee Titans (1-5). And it’s not fraudulent at all. The top four teams in point differential this year are the Jaguars (+50) and the three remaining undefeated teams: the San Francisco 49ers (+67), Kansas City Chiefs (+57), and Minnesota Vikings (+45). Jacksonville has performed like one of the best teams in the NFL — despite facing the league’s seventh-toughest schedule so far this season, per Sharp Football Analysis . They’re projected to have the single easiest schedule the rest of the way. “To be six weeks in and to feel confident that your team’s going to respond, that we’re made of the right stuff to respond, and we have so much football left that you’re excited about,” Coen said. “You’re excited about getting things corrected; you’re excited about being able to be in those moments again and maybe do it right or do it better the next time, as much as it hurts in the moment, in the aftermath. But I have a lot of confidence in this football team. Trevor [Lawrence] gives me so much confidence on a weekly basis as a play caller and the way that I think he’s seeing it right now and playing. I’m very excited about this football team.” Did the latest loss to Houston make you worried about Jacksonville’s lead in the division? Or do you feel comfortable predicting them to win the AFC South for a second straight season? Will the Jaguars win the AFC South? Are you confident in the Jaguars? Sign up here to participate in the weekly emailed surveys: Let us know your thoughts in the comments below!

title: Chiefs News: Seahawks to wear 90s-inspired uniforms Sunday night
summary: The Kansas City Chiefs will face a former AFC West foe in Week 7: the Seattle Seahawks were a division rival from 1977-2002, when the expansion Houston Texans and Cleveland Browns joined the NFL and the league adjusted to its current four-division format. Seattle moved conferences, and the teams have matched up only seven times […]
full_text: (Photo by DAN LEVINE / AFP) (Photo by DAN LEVINE/AFP via Getty Images) | AFP via Getty Images The Kansas City Chiefs will face a former AFC West foe in Week 7: the Seattle Seahawks were a division rival from 1977-2002, when the expansion Houston Texans and Cleveland Browns joined the NFL and the league adjusted to its current four-division format. Seattle moved conferences, and the teams have matched up only seven times since. On Sunday evening, the franchises will square off again, and Seattle will wear uniforms that may bring back memories of the twice-annual matchups in the 1990s. If you’re like me, you’ll hope the Chiefs match it with their best kit: white-on-white uniforms. Chiefs Kingdom, bring the noise to the SB Nation app! Download the SB Nation app on your mobile device! For Apple devices, click here . For Android devices, click here . The latest Kansas City Chiefs news Seahawks To Wear Throwback Uniforms On Sunday Night Football vs. Chiefs | Seahawks Official Website The Seattle Seahawks are set to return home to Lumen Field for a Sunday Night Football showdown against the undefeated Kansas City Chiefs in Week 7, and they will wear their 90s-inspired threads for the second time in as many weeks. Seattle will wear its fan-favorite royal blue and silver throwback uniforms for the ninth time since the team debuted them in the 2023 regular season. The team wore these uniforms three times last season with one game being played in prime time, a 38-14 road win over the Commanders on Sunday Night Football in Week 9. Kansas City Chiefs WR Xavier Worthy thriving in expanded role as Seahawks loom | ESPN “People look at him because he’s a little bit smaller and he’s real fast, so they think of him as just a deep threat,” Reid said of Worthy, who is listed at 5-foot-11 and 165 pounds. “We’ve always looked at him like he can run shallow crosses, deep crosses. He can do all that stuff and [is] very good at it. He’s tough and he’s smart, so you can move him around a lot in a lot of different spots.” In Sunday’s game, Worthy caught the ball on crossing routes, beating zone and man-to-man coverage on different snaps. When the Chiefs asked him to work in the intermediate area of the field, he was able to create proper separation. All told, he led the team with 28 routes. Kansas City Chiefs trade acquisition in line for his first start as offensive line injuries linger into first practice for Week 7 vs. Seahawks | A to Z Sports That leaves trade acquisition Joshua Ezeudu as the next man up at right tackle. The Chiefs acquired Ezeudu from the New York Giants during 53-man roster cuts. Ezeudu filled in for Moore on Sunday after he suffered a concussion against the Chargers. He played just 17 pass-blocking snaps in Week 6 and allowed a single hurry. He also played well in the run game. Kansas City put him in a good spot to succeed, since he hadn’t taken starting snaps that week. With a full week of practice at right tackle and preparation as the starter, it stands to reason that he could deliver an even better performance against the Seahawks. Who knows, perhaps he outshines Jaylon Moore, who has been rather underwhelming at right tackle this season. Kenneth Walker III returns to Seattle as Chiefs face Seahawks in Super Bowl MVP’s homecoming | KMBC “Off to a tremendous start. Stats back it up; tape definitely backs it up. He’s playing great football,” Macdonald said Wednesday. While Macdonald would probably prefer Walker wasn’t coming back to town with the Chiefs, he’s happy to see him doing well. “I love Ken. I thoroughly enjoyed him being on our football team,” Macdonald said. “I respect the heck out of him. I’m happy for him.” Chiefs’ Kenneth Walker III wins FedEx Air & Ground NFL Player of the Week for 2nd time this season | KSHB Walker now has his second Player of the Week award of this season and fourth overall of his career. He earned his first honor of the season after a 177-yard, two-touchdown performance in a narrow 30-27 win against the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 4. As a result of Walker’s most recent award, a $2,000 donation was made to Kansas City’s local food bank, Harvesters — The Community Food Network. Around the NFL Cornell Green, Cowboys cornerback part of ‘Doomsday Defense,’ dies at 86 | The Athletic “We are sad to share news of the passing of Cowboys Legend Cornell Green this morning,” the Cowboys said in a statement released Wednesday. “Cornell was a true trailblazer, having never played football in college, yet becoming a multi-time Pro Bowler, All Pro and NFL Super Bowl Champion with the Cowboys, playing defensive back from 1962 to 1974. That said, the league will have heightened security in the wake of these demonstrations. In their SoFi Stadium incident, Troy Aikman’s position to Joe Buck was: “You f—ked me over!” | Pro Football Talk “There had been weeks of Troy becoming increasingly cold, difficult, short, making comments,” a source with direct knowledge of the situation told Byers. “Joe finally snapped,” the source told Byers, in reference to the Week 5 incident at the Bills-Rams game. “He basically said, ‘Dude, are we really going to do this?’ And Troy’s position was: You fucked me over!” Said another unnamed source to Byers, “They exchanged some very direct and honest feelings.” In case you missed it on Arrowhead Pride Chiefs second-year linebacker designated to return from the IR Last year, after making the team as a rookie minicamp tryout from TCU, McDonald played the third-most special-teams snaps on the Chiefs.
