title: Chiefs-Seahawks Week 7 Wednesday injury report: Josh Simmons misses practice
summary: Each practice day this season, the Kansas City Chiefs release an official injury report ahead of the next game. In Week 7, the Chiefs play the Seattle Seahawks on “Sunday Night Football.” Here is the Chiefs’ first official injury report of the week, courtesy of the team’s official website: Chiefs “First of all, he’s played before; […]
full_text: DENVER, CO - NOVEMBER 16: Josh Simmons #71 of the Kansas City Chiefs exits the field at halftime during an NFL football game against the Denver Broncos at Empower Field at Mile High on November 16, 2025 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images Each practice day this season, the Kansas City Chiefs release an official injury report ahead of the next game. In Week 7, the Chiefs play the Seattle Seahawks on “Sunday Night Football.” #Chiefs at #Seahawks Injury Report – Wednesday pic.twitter.com/mFTIPlH277 — Nick Jacobs (@Jacobs71) October 21, 2026 Here is the Chiefs’ first official injury report of the week, courtesy of the team’s official website: Chiefs On Monday, head coach Andy Reid told reporters that left tackle Josh Simmons — who returned to practice last week from a back injury that has sidelined him since the second half of training camp — would still be “ramping up” this week. That ramp up period is apparently happening off the field. Simmons was listed on Wednesday as did not participate . Simmons initial absence for this week also had a designation of “Non-injury related (personal).” We will see if he is on the field on Thursday. Reid will next address the media on Friday. Wide receiver Rashee Rice (Hamstring) did not participate in practice. He tweaked his hamstring during the first quarter of the Week 4 win over the Las Vegas Raiders . Reid said Rice is “getting better as we go, by the day, so that helps” on Wednesday. Right tackle Jaylon Moore (Concussion) did not participate in practice after entering the concussion protocol during the Week 6 win over the Los Angeles Chargers . Moore’s participation going forward is dependent on the contracted independent neurologist and completely out of the team and player’s hands. Backup Joshua Ezeudu stepped in for Moore, and Reid acknowledged the reserve’s opportunity to fill in on Wednesday. “First of all, he’s played before; when we brought him in, we knew that. We knew he was a good player; now he potentially has an opportunity to be in there. I thought he did a nice job when he was in there this past weekend. I think everyone around him has confidence in him, too.” Cornerback L’Jarius Sneed (Knee) was a limited participant in practice. His time on the field is regularly managed due to a lingering knee issue. Tight end Travis Kelce (ankle) was a limited participant in practice. Kelce briefly left in Week 6 against the Chargers and was seen multiple times having his ankle taped. Linebacker Cooper McDonald (knee) was a limited participant in practice. McDonald was placed on the team’s Reserve/Injured list after suffering a knee injury in Week 1. Although he has been “designated to return,” McDonald must be officially added to the active roster by Saturday in order to play against Seattle. The Chiefs seemingly opened a roster spot for McDonald by waiving linebacker Cam Jones on Tuesday. Wide receiver Cyrus Allen (knee), safety Chamarri Conner (knee), guard Trey Smith (hip) and quarterback Patrick Mahomes (knee) were full participants in practice. Seahawks The notable news for the Seahawks is an upgrade for running back Zach Charbonnet — now Chiefs’ running back Kenneth Walker’s backfield partner for the previous three seasons in Seattle. Charbonnet tore his ACL during the postseason and remains on the team’s Reserve/Physically-Unable-to-Perform (PUP) list. Charbonnet returned to practice on October 1 and was listed as a full participant for the first time on Wednesday. He is highly likely to make his return against the Chiefs. Pass rusher Demarcus Lawrence (non-injury related – rest), linebacker Connor O’Toole (hamstring), linebacker Chazz Surratt (calf), and linebacker Drake Thomas (ankle) did not participate . Linebacker Tyrice Knight, former Missouri quarterback Drew Lock, wide receiver Rasheed Shaheed (hip) and guards Anthony Bradford (knee) and Beau Stephens (knee) were limited particpants .

title: ‘One of my favorite players’ Chiefs remember the late Allen Bailey
summary: On Wednesday, the Kansas City Chiefs acknowledged the passing of former player Allen Bailey, who tragically passed away on Tuesday evening at 37 years old. The former NFL defensive lineman who played eight seasons in Kansas City was found dead by his wife, with no official cause of death as of this writing. Chiefs head […]
full_text: (Photo by Tom Szczerbowski/Getty Images) | Getty Images On Wednesday, the Kansas City Chiefs acknowledged the passing of former player Allen Bailey, who tragically passed away on Tuesday evening at 37 years old. The former NFL defensive lineman who played eight seasons in Kansas City was found dead by his wife, with no official cause of death as of this writing. Allen Bailey was an excellent teammate, generous man, and kind soul. We're deeply saddened to hear of his passing, and our thoughts and prayers are with his family and friends. pic.twitter.com/gdeSp5AxDX — Kansas City Chiefs (@Chiefs) October 21, 2026 Chiefs head coach Andy Reid coached Bailey from 2013 to 2018, and remembered him fondly when he began his weekly press conference on Wednesday. “Sad news: the passing of Allen Bailey. Our hearts go out to his family, and prayers are with them,” Reid said. “Way too young, obviously. One of my favorite players. Great kid, just sorry to see that happen to him.” Bailey was born on Sapelo Island, an island off the George coastline “that is accessible only by boat,” according to Men’s Journal . He learned football through pickup games with family, but didn’t play it in an organized way until the seventh grade. The Chiefs produced a video about Bailey’s hometown, “Allen Bailey: Pride of Sapelo Island.” You can watch it here . Bailey’s humble beginnings came across in his personality. “A good guy,” Reid remembered. “I drive in every morning… I’ll see a possum. He was a big hunter; I’ll say, ‘I saw a possum out there.’ He goes, ‘Don’t eat those possums. They eat garbage. You have to get the ones that eat the chestnuts,‘” Reid shared with a laugh. “He was that kind of guy: an outdoorsman, and then he was dirty tough. Talk about giving you an honest down, he gave you an honest down every snap.” He was eventually recruited by the University of Miami, committed to play for the Hurricanes, and became a first-team all-conference player before the Chiefs drafted him in the third round of the 2011 NFL Draft. He finished his 10-year professional career with 70 starts, 22 sacks, 40 tackles for loss and four forced fumbles. By the time quarterback Patrick Mahomes arrived in Kansas City, the 6-foot-3-inch, 288-pound Bailey — nicknamed “The Hulk” as a freshman at Miami — was an established 28-year-old veteran who left an early mark on the young gunslinger from Texas Tech. “I tell this story kind of every year; he was the first person I saw when I stepped into the locker room,” Mahomes shared with local media on Wednesday. “I think it was after one of the drafts, they were in OTAs, and I step into the locker room and see Allen Bailey, and I’m like, ‘This isn’t the Big 12 anymore.‘ It was surreal to see him, and so I tell that story every single year.” Bailey finished his career with two seasons on the Atlanta Falcons , the closest team to his birthplace, Sapelo Island. “It’s terrible to hear the news that we heard,” Mahomes continued. “He was a great teammate, one of those glue guys on the team. He makes plays, but not necessarily the superstar, but the guy that kind of makes everything go.”

title: Chiefs’ Andy Reid calls Seahawks defense ‘The best in the business’
summary: The Kansas City Chiefs have taken care of business through six weeks of the regular season, but the seventh week may feature the toughest test yet. A road trip to face the Seattle Seahawks at Lumen Field is a tall task for any NFL team, especially when the reigning Super Bowl champions have something to […]
full_text: (Photo by Soobum Im/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Kansas City Chiefs have taken care of business through six weeks of the regular season, but the seventh week may feature the toughest test yet. A road trip to face the Seattle Seahawk s at Lumen Field is a tall task for any NFL team, especially when the reigning Super Bowl champions have something to prove to stay above .500 on “Sunday Night Football.” Head coach Andy Reid previewed the Week 7 matchup at his Wednesday press conference. “We know they’ve got a good team, obviously, World Champs,” Reid said. “We know the environment of the 12th man… great atmosphere for football, great venue all the way around, and two good teams playing each other.” Last year, the Seahawks beat the New England Patriots in Super Bowl LX with the help of Super Bowl MVP Kenneth Walker, now arguably the Chiefs’ most valuable player, but Seattle’s championship foundation was clearly the defense. Head coach Mike Macdonald has built one of the league’s best units, including leading the NFL in yards allowed (237 yards per game) so far this year. “They’re the best in the business right now,” Reid emphasized. “Mike does a nice job with the defense, and they have a good scheme; then they fly around. They believe in it, and they fly around. They aren’t a lot of hiccups on the back end. You see some teams where something goes on, and suddenly someone is popping free. You don’t see that with these guys.” The Seahawks have seven interceptions this season, led by a defensive backfield featuring two players with multiple interceptions: safety Julian Love and cornerback Nehemiah Pritchett. Macdonald’s scheme plays into that. His pre-snap disguises put defenders in position to take advantage of predetermined throws. Reid acknowledged that and pointed to what quarterback Patrick Mahomes must do to avoid those game-flipping turnovers. “You have to see it on your drop,” Reid said. “That’s all part of it. They do a good job of disguising and holding their looks; that’s being comfortable with the scheme. “They also have a good front,” Reid continued. “It kind of starts up there. They’re going to give you an honest look every snap.” Seattle has plenty of playmaking from its back seven, including linebacker Ernest Jones, who is tied for the team lead in sacks (3), but Reid is pointing out a talented group up front. Whether it’s veteran defensive end Leonard Williams or prodigal defensive tackle Byron Murphy — the other two sack leaders — the Chiefs’ offensive line will have its hands full. Whichever level of the unit you want to highlight, Seattle’s likely the best group Mahomes has seen this season. He acknowledged the talent at the podium on Wednesday. “They’re good at every single level of the defense,” Mahomes said. “Defensive line, linebackers, secondary, everybody, and they have a great scheme. They’re going to make you earn it every single drive, and it’s not always going to be pretty, but you have to be consistent and not push it too far, but push it enough to make plays happen.” Mahomes’ history against Macdonald — the former defensive coordinator for the Baltimore Ravens in 2022 and 2023 — is something he can draw on to prepare for the ambigiously disruptive scheme. “Going up against Coach Macdonald whenever he was with the Ravens, I learned that,” Mahomes remembered. “So this will be a great challenge for us. We have to go out there and match their energy and match their passion and execute at a high level.”
author: Ron Kopp Jr.

title: Chiefs second-year linebacker designated to return from the IR
summary: On Tuesday, we learned that the Kansas City Chiefs were adding to the depth of the linebacker position with the addition of rookie Aiden Fisher to the practice squad. However, he wasn’t the only reserve linebacker entering the mix at Chiefs practice. Second-year linebacker Cooper McDonald has been designated to return to practice after spending […]
full_text: (Photo by Scott Winters/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images On Tuesday, we learned that the Kansas City Chiefs were adding to the depth of the linebacker position with the addition of rookie Aiden Fisher to the practice squad. However, he wasn’t the only reserve linebacker entering the mix at Chiefs practice. We have designated LB Cooper McDonald to return to practice. We have signed LB Aiden Fisher to the Practice Squad. We have waived LB Cam Jones. We have terminated the Practice Squad contract of RB Nate Carter. pic.twitter.com/U6O61Nvfy6 — Kansas City Chiefs (@Chiefs) October 21, 2026 Second-year linebacker Cooper McDonald has been designated to return to practice after spending Weeks 2-6 on the Reserve/Injured list; the team will still need to activate him to the 53-man roster before he can return to the game field and has a 21-day window to do so. The Chiefs waived backup linebacker Cam Jones, who has been on and off the team in recent seasons, on Tuesday. The team also terminated the practice-squad contract of running back Nate Carter. McDonald played only two snaps against the Denver Broncos in Week 1 — both on special teams — but he recorded one tackle in his short time on the field this season. Last year, after making the team as a rookie minicamp tryout from TCU, McDonald played the third-most special-teams snaps on the Chiefs. Over the final two games of the season, he saw more defensive snaps and totaled 10 tackles (1 for loss) over 47 snaps in Weeks 17 and 18. He made his first career start in the season finale against the Las Vegas Raiders . Heading into this season, after 25 tackles as a rookie, McDonald was projected as the starting SAM linebacker in the base defense, a role that former Chiefs linebacker Leo Chenal excelled in. It remains to be seen whether the 6-foot-3-inch, 240-pound linebacker will step back into that role in defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo’s system, taking the spot back from veteran Jack Cochrane, but Chiefs Kingdom can expect No. 44 to fly around the field on special teams whenever he is ready to play.

title: The Chiefs’ wide receivers stepped up against the Chargers
summary: The Kansas City Chiefs improved to 5-0 on Sunday with a 22-6 victory over the Los Angeles Chargers at Arrowhead Stadium. The Chiefs’ offense was far from perfect, but their depleted wide receiver room still contributed significantly. With Rashee Rice (hamstring) out and Tyquan Thornton (dislocated ankle) set to miss extensive time, the Chiefs needed […]
full_text: (Photo by David Eulitt/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Kansas City Chiefs improved to 5-0 on Sunday with a 22-6 victory over the Los Angeles Chargers at Arrowhead Stadium. The Chiefs’ offense was far from perfect, but their depleted wide receiver room still contributed significantly. With Rashee Rice (hamstring) out and Tyquan Thornton (dislocated ankle) set to miss extensive time, the Chiefs needed veterans and young players to step up. Throughout the week, much of the discourse around Kansas City focused on adding talent at wide receiver to bolster the position ahead of a deep run. A move for more talent could be in the works, but this week, the Chiefs gave their in-house talent a chance to show what they could do against a divisional rival. A look at the numbers Quarterback Patrick Mahomes threw for 272 yards, with 137 coming between four wide receivers. Xavier Worthy led the way with seven receptions on seven targets for 72 yards. Rookie Cyrus Allen followed with two receptions on two targets for 27 yards. Second-year player Jalen Royals caught two of four targets for 24 yards, and journeyman Andrew Armstrong caught one pass for 13 yards. Xavier Worthy The Chiefs emphasized putting the ball in Worthy’s hands early, and he was a major focal point of the opening script. The offense took advantage of Worthy’s speed out of condensed sets, with plays designed to use him in space. After a pre-snap motion, Patrick Mahomes’ run-sell steals the defense’s eyes, and Worthy flares quickly to the flat before working a route across the middle of the field. The Chargers play zone coverage, and Worthy finds open space behind the linebackers and in front of the secondary. A questionable block in the back erases a thirty-plus-yard game, but the Chiefs would keep going Worthy’s direction. From under center, Mahmes takes a quick drop and rifles the ball to Worthy, who hauls in the missile. Walker’s motion out of the backfield draws the corner with him, and the safety gravitates toward Travis Kelce, leaving Worthy alone. It is hard to tell whether this is a break by the Chargers’ defense or a Chiefs design, but the only thing preventing a touchdown was Mahomes’ high pass. Just before halftime, the Chiefs would once again look to get Worthy involved with shallow patterns in space. Out of the bunch, the offense runs a mesh look to take advantage of the Chargers’ man defense. Off the snap, Worthy runs a shallow drag, not getting much depth past the line of scrimmage, but he has the speed on the corner covering him. His man gets lost in the “trash,” and Worthy ends up free on the other end. Mahomes delivers a good ball, and Worthy gets out of bounds to stop the clock and give his team a chance at a last-second field goal. Jalen Royals The Chiefs found ways to get the ball to Royals that incorporated aspects of their play-action game and the newer condensed sets they have been using this season. Royals has proven this season to be a quality blocking wide receiver and has lined up on multiple snaps around the line of scrimmage. Royals has made his impact on the roster this season with blocking and effort, but on critical downs and distances, he is quickly becoming the Chiefs’ “secret weapon” out of these traditionally heavy formations. This is the kind of play that can leave defenses guessing and lead to bigger plays for Royals down the line. Cyrus Allen Allen was a hot commodity during the preseason, but his impact this season has been minimal until this game. Allen saw only nine snaps, but he made the most of his opportunities. Lined up in the slot, Allen attacks the heart of the defense and immediately creates a mismatch for the linebacker trying to pick him up. With outstanding acceleration, Allen gets past the linebacker level and finds the spot between the two high safeties. Mahomes delivers a missile, and Allen catches the pass in stride before being tackled. The timing and precision required to pull this play off shouldn’t be overlooked, and it’s even more impressive that he and Mahomes have had so few live snaps together in games. If Allen keeps making plays like this, he should earn a bigger role in the offense. Andrew Armstrong Journeyman Andrew Armstrong played 42 snaps on Sunday, and he took advantage of his opportunities. While he mostly blocked, he made the most of his chances. The Chiefs are Armstrong’s third team since joining the league as an undrafted free agent last season. On his first two teams, he didn’t see the field; Sunday marked his NFL regular-season debut. In the red zone, he made his first career catch on a nice route to beat the coverage. On the snap, Armstrong gets out of his stance and works the in-cut after beating his coverage to the spot in the middle of the field. Mahomes throws a good pass, and Armstrong focuses and hauls it in. The play was basic, but Armstrong will never forget it. The bottom line The Chiefs’ wide receivers made the most of their opportunities on Sunday. Worthy showed he can take on a larger role in the room, while Allen, Royals, and Armstrong all made their case for more playing time. It is still uncertain whether the team will add more firepower ahead of the trade deadline, but the current unit is doing what it can to earn more playing time.
author: Caleb James

title: Week 7 AP NFL Power Rankings: Rams and Eagles are in a free fall
summary: The NFL’s contenders and pretenders are beginning to take shape. It appears we are heading toward the familiar reunion of Kansas City Chiefs–Buffalo Bills in the postseason. Meanwhile in the NFC, the San Francisco 49ers remain undefeated while postseason regulars the Los Angeles Rams and Philadelphia Eagles are seeing their seasons slip through their fingers. […]
full_text: (Photo by Jevone Moore/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The NFL’s contenders and pretenders are beginning to take shape. It appears we are heading toward the familiar reunion of Kansas City Chiefs – Buffalo Bills in the postseason. Meanwhile in the NFC, the San Francisco 49ers remain undefeated while postseason regulars the Los Angeles Rams and Philadelphia Eagles are seeing their seasons slip through their fingers. Let’s take a look at all eight divisions a third of the way through the season: The NFC East is pathetic, with no team winning a game in the past two weeks (including when two teams played each other). The NFC North is loaded, with all four teams potentially making the postseason. Likewise, all AFC North teams have a winning record. The 49ers and Chiefs appear to be pulling away from the other teams in both western divisions. You never know what you’ll get from the AFC or NFC South on a week-to-week basis, while the AFC East appears to be a two-horse race with the resurgence of the New England Patriots on the heels of the Bills. There’s plenty of football still to be played. No doubt there are teams currently slated to make the postseason who will see their hopes shattered by January. Until then, let’s take a look at how the Arrowhead Pride Power Rankings shook out this week. Biggest risers: Cleveland Browns and Houston Texans +6 Biggest fallers: Los Angeles Rams and Philadelphia Eagles -9 This week, along with myself, staff voters were: Caleb James, Ron Kopp Jr., Rocky Magana, and Jared Sapp . 1. San Francisco 49ers (1st) Great teams take care of business in games against weaker opponents. Even when Washington was mounting a comeback, the 49ers finished out the game with the W. 2. Kansas City Chiefs (2nd) Not even the most optimistic Chiefs fan could have predicted the impact running back Kenneth Walker III would have. 3. Buffalo Bills (4th) Another week where they snatch victory from the jaws of defeat. 4. Minnesota Vikings (6th) We’ll find out who this team really is in the next month: Colts, Lions, Bills, Packers, 49ers are on the docket. 5. Chicago Bears (10th) Petty Caleb Williams might be the answer. I suspect Bears fans love that version of Caleb, just like I love petty Patrick Mahomes. 6. Baltimore Ravens (3rd) Lamar would have won that football game. Snoop is a fine backup, but if Lamar can’t be relied upon, then I don’t realistically see the Ravens as a legitimate threat in the AFC. 7. New England Patriots (11th) AJ Brown made his return, and the Patriots won. But the Maye-Brown connection still wasn’t there. 8. Jacksonville Jaguars (5th) Win on a walk-off field goal one week. Lose in the same fashion the next. 9. Cincinnati Bengals (9th) The bye week pushed them into last place in the AFC North—still with a winning record. 10. Seattle Seahawks (7th) Halloween is coming up. Sam Darnold is already seeing ghosts again. 11. Denver Broncos (12th) Inconceivably, this team continues to win football games, despite the less-than-elite play from the quarterback position. 12. Green Bay Packers (16th) Matthew Golden and Christian Watson are becoming an elite tandem at wide receiver. Jordan Love is taking full advantage. 13. title: Chiefs Mailbag: Is Kansas City’s current approach sustainable?
summary: Welcome back to the Arrowhead Pride Mailbag! Throughout the season, keep watching The Feed for an opportunity to submit your questions about the Kansas City Chiefs! The Chiefs are 5-0 after a 22-6 victory over the Los Angeles Chargers that left many fans wondering why the team didn’t look more dominant in a divisional victory […]
full_text: (Photo by Jamie Squire/Getty Images) | Getty Images Welcome back to the Arrowhead Pride Mailbag ! Throughout the season, keep watching The Feed for an opportunity to submit your questions about the Kansas City Chiefs ! The Chiefs are 5-0 after a 22-6 victory over the Los Angeles Chargers that left many fans wondering why the team didn’t look more dominant in a divisional victory that never truly seemed in doubt. Let’s see what’s on our readers’ minds. FoxBox2021 asks: If wide receiver Rashee Rice stays out longer, and Xavier Worthy has more performances like he did against the Chargers, would it be likely the Chiefs would be comfortable in letting Rice walk in free agency? I think Rice’s first taste of free agency after the season is going to be complicated. Beyond demonstrating that his off-field issues are behind him, Rice entered 2026 needing to prove that he can stay healthy. Other than six offensive snaps in Week 4, he has now missed two games. Worthy has played well in the last two games. One thing that always frustrates me about the third-year pro is that he was drafted to provide a vertical element to complement what the Chiefs have in Rice. However, some of Worthy’s best games have come in essentially Rice’s catch-and-run role when the troubled wideout has missed. It was definitely encouraging to see Worthy reel in seven passes for 73 yards against the Chargers. However, he also finished the game with a 4.3-yard average depth of target (ADoT). That is not the player he was drafted to be. Ultimately, I still expect Rice to somehow still be a Chief in 2027, even if it is on an incentive-laden “prove it” deal. Should a bidding war unexpectedly open for his services, however, the Chiefs should feel pretty confident they can get much of the production from Worthy, who will likely be entering his own contract season in 2027 unless the Chiefs exercise an expensive fifth-year option for 2028. TheSovereign1587 asks: It seems rookie pass rusher R Mason Thomas is beating blockers regularly, creating pressures but can’t seem to close the deal with sacks. From a coaching/technical standpoint, what does he need to do to take the next step and start getting sacks? I am very confident that as Thomas gets more time in the film room with a veteran coaching staff, he will hone his craft. His first five games should provide some good experience to build on. Though Kirk Cousins and Justin Herbert take more than their share of sacks, both are crafty veterans who know how to get the ball off quickly to thwart a rookie pass-rushing technique. He also has film to study of going against a mobile quarterback in Malik Willis. Sacks can sometimes come in bunches, and I won’t be surprised if there is a stretch where Thomas turns his high pressure rate into prettier results on the stat sheet. Most rookie pass rushers take time getting acclimated. The player Thomas is most often compared to is Nik Bonitto of the Denver Broncos , who ended his rookie season with only 1.5 sacks and six pressures. Thomas already has more pressures through five games (nine) than a player considered with the league’s best had as a rookie. BuckeyeChief asks: Is what the Chiefs are doing sustainable for a deep playoff run and will they trade for help at WR before the Nov. 10 deadline? I think Kansas City’s defense is playing well, but I think they will be playing even better as the playoffs near. I expect the young talent will be a more well-rounded unit than the famous 2022 squad that boasted multiple rookie starters. I am not sure what the offense is doing through five games is sustainable. Perhaps Kenneth Walker really is just a Derrick Henry-level running back that is ready to hold up to extreme usage. However, I think the team has to find a way to involve rookie Emmett Johnson more in the run game. Johnson’s potential on screen passes is also one of the most feasible ways for Kansas City to raise the floor and ceiling of the offense. In the receiving game, I think the Chiefs can win a lot of games with the current group, but the depth is already being tested. Not having Tyquan Thornton to take the top off of defenses is also an issue that now must be worked around. The floor of the current receiving room also depends on tight end Travis Kelce continuing a high snap count and remaining a top focus of opposing defenders. A month from now, I do predict that there will be at least one wide receiver added. I am not sure if that will come via trade or a reunion with the ever-controversial Tyreek Hill. Unless the Chiefs find an opportunity to add a cost-controlled talent with high upside, I suspect the focus will be on adding a situational deep threat, rather than someone to replace any of the current starters. da’Monk asks: What dead money sits on kicker Harrison Butker’s contract and is there an upside, financially, to cutting him now? There is no financial benefit to the Chiefs were they to release Butker during the season. They would still owe the remainder of his $5.8 million base salary for 2026. Because he cannot be replaced with an unpaid intern, the move would cost salary cap space as his hypothetical replacement’s salary is added. I do not expect Butker to be released during the season. If his struggles become too much for the Chiefs to work through, my guess is you would see a mystery placement on Reserve/Injured. NFL players truly enter contract seasons in the last year that their salary is guaranteed. Although Butker is nominally signed for two more seasons, I do not expect him to be brought back at his current non-guaranteed $5.7 million salary for 2027. The Chiefs will be able to save $4.4 million against the 2027 cap by moving on while leaving a $2.8 million deal money charge. Otis#89 asks: What needs to be done to fix the short yardage issues? The Chiefs have not run a quarterback sneak since the night the world saw Patrick Mahomes’ kneecap put back into place on the field in Denver in 2019. Once again, opposing defenses knowing that Mahomes is not going to push forward for a first down seems to limit what the Chiefs can do. We have seen Kansas City use tight ends for quarterback sneaks with Blake Bell and Noah Gray in the past. Every time that has been used, however, it seems to be something defenses solve very quickly. One possible path would be to have quarterback Justin Fields situationally on the field for short yardage. I wonder if that is something we will see in the weeks to come. With third-string running back Brashard Smith seeming to have no role on either offense or special teams, I have seen some thoughts of replacing him with veteran Kareem Hunt, who was unstoppable on short conversions in 2025. It would still seem difficult to use a roster spot on a running back who would only be used in one specific case. The Chiefs have a very veteran offensive staff, and their offensive coordinator and running backs coach played a combined 241 games in NFL backfields. This is a clear weakness of the team that they have to find the solution to before it is too late. Thank you for reading this week’s Arrowhead Pride Mailbag ! We will be back after the Chiefs to face the Seattle Seahawks on next week’s “Sunday Night Football.” Keep watching The Feed for an opportunity to ask your questions.

title: Report: Rams exploring trade market for receivers
summary: In the wake of Davante Adams’ hamstring injury that will sideline him for at least six weeks, the Los Angeles Rams are reportedly exploring the wide receiver trade market, according to ESPN’s Dan Graziano. Finding a legitimate downfield threat could be exactly what their offense needs to regain consistency with the trade deadline now a […]
full_text: In the wake of Davante Adams’ hamstring injury that will sideline him for at least six weeks , the Los Angeles Rams are reportedly exploring the wide receiver trade market, according to ESPN’s Dan Graziano. Finding a legitimate downfield threat could be exactly what their offense needs to regain consistency with the trade deadline now a few weeks away. The Rams are expected to pursue a WR trade before the Nov 10 deadline. With Davante Adams sidelined 6-10 weeks by a ruptured hamstring, Los Angeles is looking for help despite having limited draft capital. Puka Nacua remains the centerpiece of the passing attack, while Tutu… pic.twitter.com/QubVPH53OK — The Goal Line Grind (@theGLgrind) October 21, 2026 Los Angeles needs a receiver who can consistently win one-on-one matchups and force opposing defenses to respect the deep ball. With defenses capable of crowding the intermediate areas of the field, adding another explosive playmaker could create more opportunities for Matthew Stafford, Davante Adams and Puka Nacua. Three potential trade targets stand out: Brian Thomas Jr. of the Jacksonville Jaguars , Josh Downs of the Indianapolis Colts, and George Pickens of the Dallas Cowboys. Thomas would be an intriguing option because of his combination of size, speed and vertical ability. The former first-round pick has the physical tools to stretch defenses and win contested catches, giving Stafford another weapon capable of turning a routine completion into a significant gain. Downs offers a different skill set. The Colts receiver is particularly dangerous working underneath and through the middle of the field, where his quickness and route-running ability can create separation. While he may not provide the same vertical threat as Thomas, he could give the Rams another reliable option against man coverage. Pickens might be the most established big-play threat of the group. His ability to win contested catches, separate downfield and capitalize on isolated coverage would address a major need in Los Angeles. However, acquiring him could come with a higher asking price, depending on Dallas’ willingness to move him. Ultimately, the Rams need another receiver for their starting lineup with the long term injury of Davante Adams. They need someone who can consistently beat defensive backs without help. If general manager Les Snead finds the right deal, a receiver trade could give Los Angeles’ offense another dimension for the second half of the season.

title: The Rams’ real MVP this season hasn’t been Stafford or Puka
summary: The Los Angeles Rams have desperately needed Kyren Williams to be at his best this season. So far, he has been. Williams has been the most valuable player for the Rams so far this season, putting together one of his most productive campaigns while the offense is in a state of flux and upheaval. His […]
full_text: The Los Angeles Rams have desperately needed Kyren Williams to be at his best this season. So far, he has been. Williams has been the most valuable player for the Rams so far this season, putting together one of his most productive campaigns while the offense is in a state of flux and upheaval. His efficiency on the ground and increased usage through the air has been one of the lone bright spots in L.A.’s 2-4 start to the 2026 season. Kyren Williams – notoriously horrible fantasy pick – on pace for another double-digit TD season. Rough start to the season for the haters. pic.twitter.com/w3yrqFSzL1 — Drew Davenport (@DrewDavenportFF) September 22, 2026 Rams running game Through six weeks, Williams is eighth in the NFL in yards from scrimmage (seventh among running backs). Puka Nacua has missed time, Davante Adams might miss the rest of the season and tight ends room hasn’t exploded in production like the offseason hype projected it would. But then there’s Williams, who has been as consistent as nearly any running back in the NFL. He’s eighth among running backs in yards per carry this season at 4.9 yards a pop, leading the way for a rushing attack that is still one of the best in the league despite the myriad issues the franchise is currently facing. In fact, NFL analyst Nate Tice took out any doubt about the quality of the rushing attack when recapping Sunday’s Rams loss to the Cardinals on a recent podcast . Referring to L.A.’s lack of play-action passing, Tice said, “That’s a big part of their offense, especially if you have the best run game in the NFL. Again, no caveats there, the best run game in the NFL.” Sean McVay knows how to design a running game, but it wouldn’t be the engine of this offense like it currently is if not for Williams’s high-level play. When Kyren Williams is on the field, the Rams gain +0.075 EPA/Play and a +5.1% Success Rate When Blake Corum is on the field, the Rams lose -0.016 EPA/Play and -5.9% Success Rate Just some food for thought 🤷‍♂️ Metrics per @FantasyPtsData https://t.co/bJZyuwTLtb — Kyle (@KyleM_FF) October 19, 2026 Kyren Williams as a pass catcher But for as good as he’s been on the ground, Williams has taken another step forward in the passing attack as well. Per Pro-Football-Reference’s parameters, among running backs, Williams is 13th in success rate as a pass catcher. However, he has a higher target share than any of the 12 players ahead of him in that stat, including some of the most lauded pass-catching backs in the NFL like Christian McCaffrey and Jahmyr Gibbs. As previously outlined here on TST , Williams is a key part of some staple passing concepts in McVay’s offense, which has helped him become an even more dangerous red zone weapon. That increase in passing-game effectiveness would be great on its own. But when you consider how much less the Rams and quarterback Matthew Stafford are pushing the ball down the field this season, as highlighted in the aforementioned and linked episode of “Football 301,” his impact underneath has been downright vital. It doesn’t hurt that he packs a punch in pass protection, too. Kyren Williams hit a legit Arn Anderson spinebuster on the blitzing LB pic.twitter.com/upiQIOv1Y0 — Bill Barnwell (@billbarnwell) October 14, 2026 We’re a third of the way through this season and things are looking dire for Los Angeles with just two wins so far. But not all news is bad; in fact, Williams and his growth have been a legitimate positive and strength. On a team that entered the year with high expectations, multiple superstars and last year’s actual MVP, it’s Kyren Williams who has been the most impactful performer for the Rams this season.

title: The Rams worked out 42-year old Matt Prater
summary: Matt Prater is one of the best NFL kickers viewers have had the privilege to watch for years. He maybe almost joined the Los Angeles Rams. Now, Prater has been in the league since 2006 so with that longevity comes experience, but age. Age equating to diminished performance can be the end of an NFL […]
full_text: GLENDALE, ARIZONA - SEPTEMBER 25: Matt Prater #5 and Markus Golden #44 of the Arizona Cardinals interact with Matthew Stafford #9 of the Los Angeles Rams after their game at State Farm Stadium on September 25, 2022 in Glendale, Arizona. (Photo by Mike Christy/Getty Images) | Getty Images Matt Prater is one of the best NFL kickers viewers have had the privilege to watch for years. He maybe almost joined the Los Angeles Rams. Now, Prater has been in the league since 2006 so with that longevity comes experience, but age. Age equating to diminished performance can be the end of an NFL career. Prater specialized as a long-distance kicker with the most 50+ yard field goals made in NFL history . Prime Prater with Sean McVay would’ve been a cheat code for points. McVay did somewhat have this type of kicker with Greg Zuerlein , he was great when he was great, but Prater was a bit better. All that aside, the Rams are going with Brandon McManus. You could say I buried the lede down here , but how desperate are the Rams for a kicker? Very desperate. As their dream turned nightmare season rolls along. Brandon McManus is latest signing in Rams’ kicker carousel (clutchpoints) “The Los Angeles Rams are signing veteran kicker Brandon McManus , their third kicker of the 2026 NFL season. The move follows Blake Grupe’s torn ACL during Sunday’s 18-16 loss to the Arizona Cardinals at SoFi Stadium. McManus, 35, worked out Tuesday alongside free-agent kicker Matt Prater as Los Angeles addressed its special-teams problems. The Rams are 2-4 after six games and hope the veteran can bring stability to the position. NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport shared details of the agreement Tuesday on X, formerly Twitter, citing information gathered alongside fellow insider Mike Garafolo.“ NFC West standings: Rams fall to last place, 4 games behind 49ers (ramswire) “It doesn’t help that the Rams have already lost to the 49ers, too, so they can’t sweep San Francisco and clinch that tiebreaker in the event that they finish with the same record. They’ll have to finish with a better divisional record than the 49ers in that case, which seems unlikely considering San Francisco is 3-0 and the Rams are 0-2. The Rams have to go on a run before their Week 11 bye. They’ve got four winnable games coming up, one of which is a rematch against the Cardinals in Week 10. Their other opponents are the Raiders , Chargers and Commanders, who are all at or below .500.“ Past NFC Champ Takes Swipe at Rams for Losing to Mike LaFleur, Cardinals (heavy.com) “Cardinals veteran wide receiver Kendrick Bourne blasted LA via Instagram in a post that surfaced after the 18-16 victory. He believes the Rams haven’t looked efficient on offense without LaFleur there. “Them boys ain’t the same wit out LaFleur,” Bourne posted on his personal IG page. LaFleur worked under McVay as offensive coordinator before accepting the Cardinals head coaching opening in the 2026 offseason. He became the latest past McVay OC to land a head coaching gig; following the path of brother Matt LaFleur, Zac Taylor, and Kevin O’Connell. The latter three have guided playoff runs or, in the case of the Cincinnati Bengals head coach Taylor, a Super Bowl appearance against the Rams in 2021.“ Rams put 2 players on IR, officially sign new kicker (ramswire) “The Los Angeles Rams made a trio of roster moves on Tuesday, all of which were expected. They placed Davante Adams and Poona Ford on injured reserve and signed kicker Brandon McManus to replace Blake Grupe. Interestingly, they did not put Kobie Turner on IR yet, though Sean McVay said on Monday that the team will likely move him there at some point; he’s expected to miss a “handful of weeks,” as McVay put it. Adams will be out 6-10 weeks with a ruptured hamstring, while Ford will miss the rest of the season with a torn triceps. Turner injured his groin in Sunday’s loss but McVay didn’t have an exact timetable for his return.“ Rams are gambling on Brandon McManus being past his Packers collapse (ramblinfan) “Last season, McManus ranked 43rd out 43 kickers as measured by FanSided’s Kick Value Added metric. he names directly above him? Ironically enough, LA’s Joshua Karty and Grupe. Hopefully McManus can keep those gargoyles at bay for as long as the Rams must rely on him. Brandon McManus isn’t dependable, but he’ll have to do for the Rams McManus did, at least, beat out an ancient Matt Prater in Tuesday’s audition. If you’re looking for more robust reassurance, well, there really isn’t any, but McManus was highly effective in 2024, his first Packers season.“ NFL Power Rankings Week 7: Rams Fall 12 Spots, Steelers Up 5 (nfl.com) “Check out Nick Shook’s Power Rankings for Week 7 of the 2026 NFL Season.” 49ers fans can laugh at the Rams (but it would be foolish to count them out) (ninernoise) “While it is more than fair, and probably even encouraged, to laugh at the Rams right now, it would be silly to count them out entirely. Yes, they have been really bad and have had some key injuries, but they still have a lot of talent on the roster, and it would be surprising if head coach Sean McVay isn’t able to figure something out by the end of the season. The Myles Garrett trade has not worked out as planned, and Davante Adams is going to be out for a while. But the Rams’ upcoming schedule is not especially scary, and if they get some of their guys back late in the season and start to peak for the playoffs, then they will definitely be a team no one wants to face in the playoffs.“ Jaguars could gift LA Rams a WR spark with Brian Thomas Jr. trade (blackandteal) “The Washington Commanders most definitely make sense because of Thomas’ LSU connection with quarterback Jayden Daniels . However, there’s another club in the NFC that would make a push for him. The Jaguars could trade Brian Thomas Jr. to the LA Rams in return for a 2nd-round pick Like other teams that are dealing with injuries at receiver, Los Angeles would be a realistic landing spot for Brian Thomas Jr. While Puka Nacua is back in the fold after sitting out two contests with a groin and a core muscle injury, teammate Davante Adams will tentatively miss six to 10 games after sustaining a hamstring rupture . Brian Thomas Jr. would be a more than capable replacement, as Michel Haney at Ramblin Fan suggests. Here’s the skinny.“ 5 things to know about new Rams kicker Brandon McManus (ramswire) “Here are five things to know about the Rams’ new kicker. He’s a Super Bowl champion Before the Broncos went on a decade-long playoff drought that lasted after McManus’ departure, he won Super Bowl 50 with the team. During that playoff run, McManus hit all 10 field goal attempts and was perfect in point-after attempts.“ Raiders Won’t Face Former Star Davante Adams as Rams Lose Key Players (sports.yahoo) “Adams, 33, spent parts of three seasons with the Raiders after arriving in a blockbuster trade with the Green Bay Packers in 2022. He was traded to the New York Jets during the 2024 season before joining the Rams. Sunday’s game would have marked his first appearance against the Raiders since leaving Las Vegas. Adams had been one of the Rams’ most productive offensive players this season, catching 30 passes for 480 yards and four touchdowns through six games. His absence is another significant setback for Los Angeles, which has struggled to a 2-4 start.“ Comment of the Day: “McManus is an experienced kicker in the NFL unlike Tanner whose glory came in the UFL. Rams obviously looking for someone with experience based off of who they brought in. I’ll go with the Rams in this one.” -TonyT828 Feed post of the day:

title: Raiders injury report: Tonka Hemingway is still out
summary: The Las Vegas Raiders are beginning he practice week for Sunday’s home game against the Los Angeles Rams without starting defensive tackle Tonka Hemingway. Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak said the 2025 fourth-round is still in the NFL’s concussion protocol. He was hurt in Week 5 and he didn’t play in a Week 6 loss […]
full_text: (Photo by Jordon Kelly/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Las Vegas Raiders are beginning he practice week for Sunday’s home game against the Los Angeles Rams without starting defensive tackle Tonka Hemingway. Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak said the 2025 fourth-round is still in the NFL’s concussion protocol. He was hurt in Week 5 and he didn’t play in a Week 6 loss to the Buffalo Bills. Monday, Kubiak said he was expecting Hemingway back in practice this week. If he returns to practice by Friday, he can still have a chance to face the Rams. Hemingway has been the Raiders’ snap leader at defensive tackle. He averaged playing 62 percent of the snaps in the four games he was fully healthy for. Foley Fatukasi started in place of Hemingway against the Bills. Meanwhile, Kubiak said second-year wide receiver Dont’e Thornton has a chance to be activated from the injured reserve this week, but the coach indicated Thornton has to show he’s ready. He must be activated by next week or he would be out for the season. Kubiak also said there will be competition on the offensive line again this week. Caleb Rogers replaced Jackson Powers-Johnson in Week 6. According to NFL.com, several Raiders were limited in practice Wednesday. They included tight end Brock Bowers (hamstring/calf), running back Mike Washington (foot/back), tackle Kolton Miller (shoulder) and linebacker Quay Walker (chest). Often, players are limited on Wednesdays, but progress through the week.

title: How James Cook ran right through Las Vegas Raiders’ defense in Week 6 loss to Buffalo Bills
summary: To be fair, the Las Vegas Raiders’ run defense against Buffalo Bills running back James Cook was a mismatch heading into the Week 6 contest. Cook came into the matchup averaging more than 11 yards per game than he did while winning the 2025 rushing title, and the Raiders’ run defense ranks 18th with a […]
full_text: (Photo by Ethan Miller/Getty Images) | Getty Images To be fair, the Las Vegas Raiders’ run defense against Buffalo Bills running back James Cook was a mismatch heading into the Week 6 contest. Cook came into the matchup averaging more than 11 yards per game than he did while winning the 2025 rushing title , and the Raiders’ run defense ranks 18th with a negative 0.07 EPA per rush this year, according to Sumer Sports . So, it shouldn’t come as much of a surprise that Cook had 22 carries for 95 yards and a touchdown in Las Vegas. However, the breakdown of his production via Sumer Sports is mind-boggling. Vs. light box (6 or fewer defenders): 2 carries, 5 yards (2.5 YPC) Vs. standard box (7 defenders): 5 carries, 16 yards (3.2 YPC) Vs. heavy box (8 or more defenders): 15 carries, 74 yards (4.9 YPC) and 1 TD In other words, the Silver and Black had more success stopping the running back when they had fewer defenders dedicated to him. How does that happen? For good measure, Cook’s yards per carry against a heavy box is in line with his average for the entire season (4.9), but the two other figures above were well below his production in the first five games: 6.8 ypc versus a light box and 5.5 versus standard . Also, his avoided tackle rate was about 10 percent lower on Sunday: 14.6 percent to 4.5 percent . These numbers simply don’t make sense, so let’s flip on the tape to answer the question above. Starting with the positive -6 man box vs 11 personnel in the gun -LBs cross with Dean crashing downhill, throws off LT's angle -Dean sinks hips and redirects to make a nice tackle fo r 1-yard gain #RaiderNation pic.twitter.com/wYkQrBmBPM — Matt Holder (@MHolder95) October 19, 2026 We’ll start with a couple of positive reps to help add some context into why the Raiders were successful using a light box against Cook. Buffalo comes out in 11 personnel and in the shotgun with back offset on the weak side, while Las Vegas is in nickel and has just six defenders in the box. Defensive coordinator Rob Leonard gets creative with his play call by having the linebackers cross paths, where Dean crashes downhill and attacks the strong side A-gap while Quay Walker wraps around and replaces Dean on the weak side B-gap. That action throws off left tackle Dion Dawkins’ angle climbing to the second level, and Dean does a great job of sinking his hips to redirect and make the tackle for a short gain. A well-timed play call by the coordinator and well-executed by the linebacker. -Nickel and a 7-man box vs 12 personnel and Toss OZ -Quay Walker sets the edge, Maxx Crosby beats combo from RT & TE, Adam Butler reset LOS to force cutback -Nakobe Dean mirrors RB while Foley Fatuaski wins back side for a tackle at the LOS #Raiders pic.twitter.com/ih4PzUKcIF — Matt Holder (@MHolder95) October 19, 2026 Another big factor in the Raiders’ run defense on Sunday was that Maxx Crosby was fairly hot and cold throughout the game. For example, Pro Football Focus had him accounting for four ‘ defensive stops ’ against the run but a season-low 55.6 grade as a run defender. He doesn’t make the tackle/stop here, but he does have a really good rep that helps set up Dean and defensive tackle Foley Fatuaski to make the play. The Bills are in 12 personnel and run toss outside zone to the two-tight end side of the formation, while the Raiders are in nickel personnel with safety Jeremy Chinn in the box as the weakside linebacker and Walker on the line of scrimmage as the outside linebacker on the strong side edge. Walker manages to set the edge, and Crosby (who is playing as a 6-technique defensive end) manages to split and defeat the combo block between the right tackle and tight end to take away the C- and D-gaps. Also, Adam Butler has a nice rep as the 3-technique defensive tackle, where he gets some push against the right guard and runs his feet to eliminate the B-gap. All of that forces Cook to cut back side. Meanwhile, Dean does an excellent job of mirroring Cook, and Foley Fatukasi (as the back side one-technique) has a similar rep as Butler, resetting the line of scrimmage and running his feet to beat the left guard’s block. As a result, Dean and Fatukasi meet the running back in the hole for a short gain. -8-man box vs. 13 personnel but #Raiders stay in nickel -Taron Johnson ends up at MIKE & flows too hard to the playside -Jonah Laulu gets shoulders turned & washed inside vs RG/RT combo -Crosby gets pancaked by TE/TE combo -Backside cutback is open for easy 5 yards pic.twitter.com/2VIP7iryE4 — Matt Holder (@MHolder95) October 19, 2026 On the opposite end of the spectrum, this is an example of a negative rep from Crosby’s afternoon. Buffalo tries to run inside zone to the weak side of the formation. However, the back side cutback lane is open for Cook, partially because Crosby gets pancaked by a combo block from two tight ends. But the defensive end is far from the only problem the Raiders have on this rep. For some reason, Leonard wasn’t matching personnel on Sunday. To his credit, that didn’t come back to bite Las Vegas in the running game too much throughout the game, but it did on this play. With Las Vegas in nickel against this three-tight-end formation, Chinn is the weak-side edge defender and defensive back Taron Johnson is in the box as the MIKE linebacker. That’s two defensive backs playing out of position and in spots where they’ll have to take on or defeat blocks in the running game. Post-snap, Johnson crashes too far downhill and abandons the back side A-gap that he’s responsible for. That’s likely a result of lacking linebacker instincts since he’s out of position, and could also be symptomatic of Chinn trying to set the edge against an offensive tackle. Granted, with Malcolm Koonce and Thomas Booker IV plugging up their gaps, Chinn doesn’t become much of a factor on this play despite struggling to anchor. The problem is, no one is in the back side A-gap until 3-technique defensive tackle Jonah Laulu gets his shoulders turned and washed inside by the combo block from the right guard and right tackle. In other words, Laulu is in a bad position, too. Combine that with Crosby getting taken out of the equation, and Cook gets an easy five yards on the ground. Bills are in 11 personnel but in a condensed formation and run weak side mid zone w/ #Raiders in nickel -2nd level adjusts to motion but the strength doesn't change, leaving too many defenders on the weak side -Both DTs get pushed and no one is there to fill back side A-gap pic.twitter.com/EhiLIsDSKT — Matt Holder (@MHolder95) October 19, 2026 This is a similar play call from Buffalo, only they come out in 11 personnel and a condensed formation with two wide receivers next to the tight end on the strong side instead of two more tight ends. But the Bills still call a weak-side inside- or mid-zone run that Cook hits on the back side. That being said, one tweak really throws the Raiders for a loop: one of the wide receivers motioning across the formation. Initially, Las Vegas is in a great front to stop Cook. Focusing on the second level and Johnson: Chinn has the weak-side B-gap, Walker is in the strong-side A-gap, Dean can account for strong C, and Johnson can either fit inside the outside receiver’s block or close the gap with the receiver and stay on the edge. However, instead of having cornerback Hezekiah Masses follow the outside receiver across the formation, the second level of the defense shifts to the weak side so that Chinn can cover the receiver if it’s a pass play. As a result, the Raiders have four defenders on the weak side, including two (Chinn and Walker) who are covering the B-gap, allowing the Bills to get a hat on a hat with their backside blocks. Additionally, JJ Pegues (the one-technique nose tackle) gets widened by the center, Booker gets pushed into the second level as the strong-side 3-technique, and Dean fits to the wrong side of his block. That gives Cook a cutback lane right up the gut for a nine-yard gain.…

title: The Las Vegas Raiders should trade for Quenton Nelson
summary: The Las Vegas Raiders are 3-3 and need to make a move to give not only the offense, but the team a shot in the arm. In previous weeks, the chatter centered on Marvin Harrison Jr., Brian Thomas Jr., and any other wide receiver. However, there is a need that will fix far more than […]
full_text: (Photo by Jeffrey Brown/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Las Vegas Raiders are 3-3 and need to make a move to give not only the offense, but the team a shot in the arm. In previous weeks, the chatter centered on Marvin Harrison Jr., Brian Thomas Jr., and any other wide receiver. However, there is a need that will fix far more than just the passing game. Carlie Irsay-Gordon, the owner of the Indianapolis Colts fired her general manager of 10 years, Chris Ballard. Many speculate an oncoming fire sale as the Colts look to potentially dump salary and begin the tear down phase of a rebuild. One of the players rumored to be available is Guard Quenton Nelson. Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak has cited a need to get better production across the offensive line. Nelson is 30 years old, an 8-time Pro Bowler and a 6-time All-Pro. Nelson has the unique set of skills that can make the entire offense better overnight. Instant impact With Nelson, the run blocking becomes 20% better and takes some of the stress off center Tyler Linderbaum, so he can focus on his blocking assignment instead of being a help blocker. Maybe even help him out so that running backs stop getting hit in the backfield. Combine that with a switch to Mike Washington Jr. as the number one back and suddenly the Raiders are controlling the clock on the ground, allowing the defense to rest and not be overextended. Against the Buffalo Bills in the waning moments of the game, we saw a beautiful deep ball to Tre Tucker who came up with a diving catch in the end zone. Nelson’s pass blocking provides interior protection for the quarterbacks, be it Kirk Cousins now and/or Fernando Mendoza later. Giving receivers more time to get open and get deep, making all of the existing pass catchers better. The fallout Kubiak may profess a healthy respect for Spencer Burford but we can be honest in this safe space. Burford has been a liability. There is not good, and there is what Burford has been. For someone with experience in Kubiak’s system it’s inexcusable how he isn’t obtaining larger amounts of success. Nelson erases that issue outright, helps both Kolton Miller and Linderbaum. Potentially allows for Trey Zuhn to be slid out to left tackle, if need be and keeps continuity in the better performing right side of the line. The question is, what will it cost? Would the Colts be interested in a cheaper veteran cornerback such as Eric Stokes and a second- or third-round draft pick? If so, the deal should be done posthaste. Or perhaps a young defensive end like Malcolm Koonce? That’s where the Raiders general manager John Spytek will have to be willing to make a splash that will help his team for years to come.
author: Philip Robinson

title: 5 things about the Rams
summary: The 3-3 Las Vegas Raiders host the 2-4 Los Angeles Rams on Sunday at Allegiant Stadium. Kickoff is 1:25 p.m. PT. Here are some things to consider about the Rams: They can move the ball: The Rams have their problems, but the numbers say they are doing some things right. They have outgained their opponents […]
full_text: The 3-3 Las Vegas Raiders host the 2-4 Los Angeles Rams on Sunday at Allegiant Stadium. Kickoff is 1:25 p.m. PT. Here are some things to consider about the Rams: They can move the ball: The Rams have their problems, but the numbers say they are doing some things right. They have outgained their opponents by 644 yards this season. That’s an average of 107.3 yards a game. That is a testament to both sides of the ball. It shows the Rams are playing well in some areas. They’re losing close games: In their last three losses, the Rams have been outscored by a total of nine points with the biggest deficit being four points. They are 2-4 with a total points deficit of three points. Defensive line decimated: In addition to playing with starting wide receiver, former Raider, Davante Adams, the Rams’ defensive front, an expected NFL force, has been ravaged by injuries. They are without star defensive end Myles Garrett and standout defensive tackle Poona Ford and Kobie Turner. The Raiders might be able to get the ground game going Sunday. Aaron Donald snap counts: With Turner and Ford out, Aaron Donald may see more playing time. He has averaged playing 58.6 percent of the Rams’ defensive snaps in the four games he has played this season after he returned from retiring for the past two seasons. So the Raiders may see a lot of the 35-year-old future Hall of Famer. New quarterbacks coming: While this game will feature veteran quarterbacks Matthew Stafford and Kirk Cousins, the next time these two teams play will likely feature 2026 first-round picks Fernando Mendoza and Ty Simpson, the No. 1 and No. 13 overall draft picks. Both players did well in the preseason. Mendoza has mopped up in one game, while Simpson hasn’t played this season.
author: Bill Williamson

title: Darien Porter definitely a starter again
summary: Here is a look at how the Las Vegas Raiders’ 2025 draft class fared in a 33-30 home loss to the Buffalo Bills on Sunday and what to look for Sunday at home against the Los Angeles Rams: Ashton Jeanty: The No. 6 overall draft pick played 58 percent of snaps Sunday (well below his […]
full_text: (Photo by Ethan Miller/Getty Images) | Getty Images Here is a look at how the Las Vegas Raiders’ 2025 draft class fared in a 33-30 home loss to the Buffalo Bills on Sunday and what to look for Sunday at home against the Los Angeles Rams: Ashton Jeanty: The No. 6 overall draft pick played 58 percent of snaps Sunday (well below his season average) even though he proclaimed himself healthy as he’s been all this season. Still, Jeanty continued to struggled on the ground as he had 10 carries for 22 yards. His drop issues in the passing game continued. He did have some nice moments, but overall his impact continues to be lacking. Jack Bech: The second-round pick is on the injured reserve with a fractured forearm and will likely be out for several more weeks. Darien Porter: The third-round pick played 79 percent of the defensive snaps and he continued to play much more than rookie Zeke Masses. So, Porter has regained his starting job. This can be a fluid situation and Porter has to prove he deserves to keep the starting gig. Coach Klint Kubiak said he likes Proter’s makuop. Caleb Rogers: The third-round pick took over for the benched Jackson Powers-Johnson and Rogers played every snap in his second straight of the season. Kubiak said Monday there was good and bad from Rogers’ performance against Buffalo, but the coach noted Rogers was prepared. It remains to be seen if this shakeup will continue. Charles Grant: The offensive lineman, taken in the third round, didn’t play on offense as usual, but he did log six snaps on special teams. Dont’e Thornton: The wide receiver, taken in the fourth round, is in the 21-day practice window to return from the injured reserve. Thornton is coming back from a hamstring injury and helps he could be activated this week. Tonka Hemingway: The fourth-round pick did not play in Week 6 because of a concussion he suffered in Week 5. He could return to play against the Rams and he would resume his starting role. JJ Pegues: The defensive tackle, taken in the sixth round, was active for the second time this season, partly because Hemingway was out. He played three snaps against Buffalo. Cody Lindenberg: The seventh-round pick played 19 snaps on special teams.

title: Bills had a 2nd spitter in Las Vegas
summary: In a bizarre and disturbing twist, the NFL announced Wednesday morning that it has suspended another Buffalo Bills’ defensive back for spitting at a Las Vegas Raiders’ player in the Bills’ 33-30 victory. The league suspended defensive back/special teamer Sam Franklin for spitting. He will serve a one-game suspension against the Baltimore Ravens when the […]
full_text: (Photo by Candice Ward/Getty Images) | Getty Images In a bizarre and disturbing twist, the NFL announced Wednesday morning that it has suspended another Buffalo Bills’ defensive back for spitting at a Las Vegas Raiders’ player in the Bills’ 33-30 victory. The league suspended defensive back/special teamer Sam Franklin for spitting. He will serve a one-game suspension against the Baltimore Ravens when the Bills returner from their by after Week 7. Monday, the NFL suspended Buffalo defensive back C.J. Gardner-Johnson for spitting. Gardner-Johnson eject before halftime for spitting in the direction of Raiders’ tight end Brock Bowers. Gardner-Johnson was also suspended for the Baltimore game. Bills S Sam Franklin has been suspended for a game for spitting on a Raiders player. He is appealing. pic.twitter.com/pwplhfiNd4 — Albert Breer (@AlbertBreer) October 21, 2026 Franklin’s incident occurred with 1:32 remaining in the game after a Raiders’ extra point on their final touchdown. Franklin is reportedly denying the act and will appeal the suspension. Video shows Franklin and Raiders’ tackle D.J. Glaze having a confrontation after the kick. So here’s the alleged spitting incident. #Bills DB Sam Franklin Jr. (28) takes a shot below the belt from #Raiders T DJ Glaze (71). Franklin confronts Glaze, who then signals to an official. Franklin is adamant there was no spitting. Too tough to see anything clearly here. pic.twitter.com/RzK6M2WY9q — Mike Garafolo (@MikeGarafolo) October 21, 2026 The NFL is cracking down on such incidents, but it is highly unusual for two players from the same team to get such suspensions.

title: Kyle Louis returns to Miami Dolphins practice
summary: The Miami Dolphins welcomed rookie defender Kyle Louis back to practice today after a lengthy injury absence. His 21-day window was opened, giving the player the chance to work himself back into shape during practice before being activated for his first game since injuring his knee in the season opener against the Las Vegas Raiders. […]
full_text: LAS VEGAS, NEVADA - SEPTEMBER 13: Kyle Louis #19 of the Miami Dolphins warms up prior to an NFL football game against the Las Vegas Raiders at Allegiant Stadium on September 13, 2026 in Las Vegas, Nevada. (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Miami Dolphins welcomed rookie defender Kyle Louis back to practice today after a lengthy injury absence. His 21-day window was opened, giving the player the chance to work himself back into shape during practice before being activated for his first game since injuring his knee in the season opener against the Las Vegas Raiders. Louis was selected with the 138th pick in the 4th round of the 2026 NFL Draft after a decorated college career at Pittsburgh where he was a two-year starter. He has experience playing both as a linebacker and as a safety. Speaking with the South Florida media today, Miami’s head coach, Jeff Hafley, tempered immediate expectations by noting Louis needs time to get back into football shape following his MCL injury. “[Louis] hasn’t played real football in quite awhile. It’s his first practice back [today]. As excited as I am to have him back, I think I got to kind of temper that and see how he practices today and then how does he feel after he practices — and getting through Thursday and Friday. Then we’ll see where he’s at physically and mentally and if he’s ready to play in the game. I’m glad to have him back out there. He’s very eager.”

(Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images Tuesday was a busy day for the Miami Dolphins, with the front office making several roster moves. The Dolphins swapped kickers on Tuesday, bring back Zane Gonzalez and waiving Riley Patterson. Patterson was 7-for-0 on field goals this season and 5-for-6 on extra point attempts. After connecting on 93.1 percent of this field goal attempts, including 3-of-4 from over 50 yards, last year, Patterson’s accuracy seem to fall off this year, but a bigger issue seemed to be on kickoffs. “We did try to kick them out of the end zone; that was discussed and just not executed the way that we wanted it to be…yeah, several of them were supposed to be touchbacks and weren’t,” head coach Jeff Hafley explained on Monday when asked about the team’s special teams issues and lack of simply kicking the ball for touchbacks rather than relying on the coverage unit. The Dolphins held a tryout for kickers on Tuesday, including former seven-time Pro Bowl selection Justin Tucker, and ultimately brought back Gonzalez. The Cleveland Browns’ 2017 seventh-round draft pick, Gonzalez landed on injured reserve during the preseason with Miami this past summer. He was released with an injury settlement and now returns to to the Dolphins, signing with the practice squad. Miami was not done with their roster moves. They also promoted rookie edge rusher Rodney McGraw from the practice squad and waived edge rusher Andre Jones Jr. The potentially surprise move of the day came with the news the Dolphins were waiving cornerback Storm Duck. A 2024 undrafted free agent out of Louisville, Duck was on the physically unable to perform list this year as he recovered from a knee injury sustained last year. He returned to practice three weeks ago, and the team has until today to decide whether to add him to the active 53-man roster or keep him on the PUP for the rest of the year. summary: The Minnesota Vikings and Indianapolis Colts released their first injury reports in advance of their Sunday afternoon matchup at U.S. Bank Stadium. Here they are. full_text: PITTSBURGH, PENNSYLVANIA - OCTOBER 11: Sauce Gardner #1 of the Indianapolis Colts warms up prior to a game against the Pittsburgh Steelers at Acrisure Stadium on October 11, 2026 in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Lauren Leigh Bacho/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Minnesota Vikings and Indianapolis Colts released their first injury reports in advance of their Sunday afternoon matchup at U.S. Bank Stadium. Here they are. Minnesota Vikings Player Name Position Injury Wednesday Thursday Friday Injury Designation Donovan Jackson* LG Knee DNP DNP DNP IR-OUT Jordan Addison* WR Hamstring FP Christian Darrisaw* LT Concussion FP Charles Demmings CB Hamstring FP T.J. Hockenson* TE Concussion FP Justin Jefferson* WR Ankle LP Jordan Mason* RB Thumb FP Brian O’Neill* RT Knee LP James Pierre CB Foot LP Indianapolis Colts Player Name Position Injury Wednesday Thursday Friday Injury Designation Arden Key* DE Hamstring DNP DNP DNP IR-OUT Alec Pierce* WR Foot DNP DNP DNP IR-OUT Austin Ajaike LB Concussion LP Keenan Allen* WR NIR-Rest DNP Bryce Boettcher* LB Groin DNP Jaylon Carlies LB Ribs LP Ashton Dulin WR Hamstring LP Sauce Gardner* CB Calf DNP Matt Gonglaves* RG Ankle DNP Anthony Gould WR Concussion DNP Drew Ogletree TE Ankle DNP Rigoberto Sanchez* P Foot DNP Jonathan Taylor* RB NIR-Rest LP Jerry Tillery DT NIR-Personal DNP Jalen Travis* RT Foot LP Justin Walley* SCB Knee DNP Charvarious Ward* CB NIR-Rest DNP Tyler Warren* TE Groin DNP Injury Report Terms and Glossary FP = Full participant in practice. LP = Limited participant in practice. DNP = Did not participate in practice. NIR = Not injury related. PUP = Physically unable to participate list. IR = Injured reserve. Note: only starters on IR are listed. Player Name* = Starter. Injury designation definitions: Probable = the league defines a Probable injury designation as a 75% or greater chance of playing. Historically, 95% of players designated probable are active and played on game day. Questionable = the league defines a Questionable injury designation as being ‘uncertain’ of whether the player will play or not. This replaces the former definition of having a 50% chance of playing. Historically, 70-75% of players with a Questionable injury designation were active and played on game day. Doubtful = The league defines a Doubtful injury designation to mean the player is unlikely to participate in the game. In practical terms, teams use the designation when a player has less than a 50% chance to suit up, and active game appearances from this designation remain rare. Historically only around 6% of players with a Doubtful designation are active and played on game day. Out = will not play. Players with this designation are not active on game day and league rules prohibit them from playing. Notes on Injured Players For the Vikings, lots of good news on the injury front after their bye week. First, both Christian Darrisaw and T.J. Hockenson are in the last phase of the concussion protocol, which is practicing, and they are both expected to clear the protocol and play on Sunday. Jordan Mason is also back practicing and is expected to be removed from IR and play on Sunday. Jordan Addison and Charles Demmings are also back practicing after missing time with hamstring injuries and are expected to play on Sunday as well. Justin Jefferson and Brian O’Neill are still working through their minor injuries, as is James Pierre, but all are expected to play on Sunday. So, apart from those on IR, it should be all hands on deck for the Vikings on Sunday after some R&R during their bye week. For the Colts, they have seven starters who did not practice Wednesday due to injury. They include linebacker Bryce Boettcher, cornerback Sauce Gardner, right guard Matt Gonglaves, punter Rigoberto Sanchez, right tackle Jalen Travis, slot cornerback Justin Walley, and tight end Tyler Warren. Sauce Gardner is their best cornerback, who they traded two first round picks to acquire, and is expected to miss the Vikings game with a calf injury. He is considered week-to-week but expected to miss some time. Tight End Tyler Warren missed the Colts last game with the same groin injury so his still not practicing doesn’t bode well at this point for his playing Sunday. Punter Rigoberto Sanchez injured his foot last weekend and the Colts added a punter to their roster so that isn’t a good sign for his availability on Sunday either. Slot Cornerback Justin Walley’s injury is new. Not much else is known at this point, but his not practicing and Sauce Gardner already likely out on Sunday could leave the Colts’ struggling secondary pretty thin at cornerback. Linebacker is another concerning position with three linebackers on the injury report including starter Bryce Boettcher, who didn’t practice Wednesday with a groin injury. This injury is also new and not much else is known at the moment. And lastly, two starting offensive linemen for the Colts are on the injury report including right guard Matt Gonglaves who didn’t practice Wednesday with an ankle injury, which is new. Bottom line for the Colts, who fired their general manager after losing to the previously winless Tennessee Titans last weekend and falling to 2-4 on the season, this feels like an injury report for a team later in the season that was just eliminated from playoff contention. Rumor is the Colts may start trading away players to get a head start on a multi-year rebuild. These are the conditions where more guys on the injury report end up not playing. We’ll see how it plays out with injury updates tomorrow and Friday. Follow me on X/Bluesky @wludford
