Since the Colts look to be in free fall, speculation abounds about them moving some of their top players like Quentin Nelson and DeForest Buckner. Both would be fabulous pickups for the Vikings. I like Jonathan Taylor myself due to the fact that Aaron Jones and Jordan Mason are both free agents next year and, more importantly, Taylor would be under contract for two more years with none guaranteed, He would be due 16 & 18M the next two years. Nelson and Buckner will be free agents and will get paid well is my guess. Some folks have speculated about the Vikings trying to trade for Ben Bredeson of the Bucs but he is their starter so it is hard to see that happening. They need to protect Baker. It is hard to find a decent guard that might be available. Nelson would be the crown jewel but that would mean an immediate extension and moving Jackson to right guard. Not sure about that. Buckner could be the extra squeeze to get the defense more juice that the team needs. He has a 74.9 pass-rushing pff grade which ranks 12th overall showing he still has elite pass-rush efficiency. He has already racked up 4 sacks and 18 total pressures (including 3 hits and 9 hurries). If the Colts are sellers, they probably are going to move Nelson and Buckner who likely want to go to a team that has a chance to get into the dance no? Who do you think the team could and will sign? Minnesota Vikings News and Links NFL Power Rankings: Vikings Status After Week 6 Bye https://www.vikings.com/news/nfl-power-rankings-week-7-status-bye-week No. 3 (no change): Gary Davenport – Bleacher Report There isn’t a more surprising team in the NFL this year (at least in a positive way) than the undefeated Minnesota Vikings. Naysayers will point to a relatively easy schedule and offensive inconsistency as reasons why they aren’t as good their record. But Minnesota’s ultra-aggressive defense is legit: second in yards allowed, third against the pass, fifth against the run and first in points allowed. Edge-rusher Andrew Van Ginkel told reporters the defense’s strength lies in its versatility. “Things are constantly changing,” he said. “It could be changing game to game. It could be changing from series to series. It could be changing from play to play. It could be changing within the play.” That defense is going to be tested coming up — after facing the struggling Colts at home in Week 7, the Vikings take on two of the league’s best offenses in the Lions and Bills. No. 3 (up 1 spot): Vinnie Iyer – Sporting News The Vikings defense has been the foundation of their undefeated start through their Week 6 bye. They have impressive pressure and takeaway stats in Brian Flores’ aggressive, blitz-happy attack, but there’s one simple number for why they haven’t lost. Their defense allows opponents to convert only a league-best 22 percent of third-down attempts. No. 5 (up 2 spots): Frank Schwab – Yahoo! Sports Jordan Mason’s return from a broken thumb, which should happen in Week 7, won’t create big headlines, but it’s important for the Vikings. Aaron Jones, Sr., filled in well, but he’s 31 years old, and asking him to handle almost all of the running back duties was not a long-term plan. Mason and Jones form a good committee, and they can resume their roles. The Vikings face the reeling Colts this weekend before a four-game stretch that will define their season: at Lions, vs. Bills, at Packers, vs. 49ers (in Mexico City). If they beat the Colts and go 2-2 in the four games that follow, they’ll be in great shape. Vikings Gets Major Injury News on Addison, 3 Other Key Starters Ahead of Colts Game https://heavy.com/sports/nfl/minnesota-vikings/addison-mason-hockenson-darrisaw-injuries-colts-nfl-news/ “Jordan Mason, TJ Hockenson, Christian Darrisaw and Jordan Addison are all expected to return to practice tomorrow for the #Vikings, KOC mentioned via @KFAN1003,” the VikingzFanPage X account reported. “Bye week came at the right time.” Vikings OC Wes Phillips sends firm message about Kyler Murray’s growth and how he’s adapted to the offense https://atozsports.com/nfl/minnesota-vikings-news/vikings-oc-wes-phillips-sends-firm-message-kyler-murray-kevin-oconnell-relationship/ Kyler Murray has adapted well to the system One thing that was interesting when we went into the season was how much each side would adapt to the other? Offensive coordinator Wes Phillips talked about that coming out of the bye week and was open about how much Murray tried to acclimate. “There wasn’t any like resistance or like, ‘Hey, I don’t want to do any of this stuff’; it was, it was more like, ‘Hey, I want to do what you guys, your offense is,’ and us trying to adjust some to make sure that he’s comfortable, but he was very open right from the start,” said Phillips. You can see how that’s evolved over the last few weeks, especially with how much Murray was under center against the Buccaneers. They have significantly increased the shotgun percentage with the offense, and it’s done a lot for how successful they’ve been able to be. To Murray’s credit, it’s not as if he can’t play under center; he did that with the Cardinals the last three years under Drew Petzing. He has played under center. I mean, he’s done things under center,” said Phillips. “I think that’s why you go through off-season training camp, and you put a lot of install, or at least we do, on the guys,” continued Phillips. “You come in sometimes [early on], and you’re not asking a lot of questions necessarily right away because you need to learn you need to learn enough about what you’re doing to ask the questions, and so I think that’s just part of a new player as well. They’re trying to figure out our system, and then they start opening up and saying, okay, have you ever done it this way? Or I’m not as comfortable doing this, you know, or I haven’t done this before. And the communication with him and the play caller, Kevin, has just grown and grown as we’ve gone, as you’d expect it to, you know, as we get through our first year with him.” Vikings Trade Rumors Hint at Potential Moves Before Deadline https://sports.yahoo.com/articles/vikings-trade-rumors-hint-potential-032756253.html “On The Alec Lewis Show, he tripled down on his reports from KFAN and The Athletic earlier in the week, telling his YouTube and podcast audience that the MN Vikings will be ‘very active and aggressive’ in trying to find trade partners before the deadline.. title: Patriots mailbag: What’s the formula against the Bears defense?
summary: The New England Patriots are looking to keep their winning streak alive on a short week. They travel to the Midwest to take on the Chicago Bears in a prime time matchup. So, let’s get into a Thursday edition of this week’s #PostPulpit Mailbag. What do you make of the Bears’ pass rush? Their overall […]
full_text: The New England Patriots are looking to keep their winning streak alive on a short week. They travel to the Midwest to take on the Chicago Bears in a prime time matchup. So, let’s get into a Thursday edition of this week’s #PostPulpit Mailbag. What do you make of the Bears’ pass rush? Their overall pressure rate is strong, but I’ve seen their D-line ranked 20th in pressure rate, while their blitz rate is the league’s 7th highest at 39.3%. Does that suggest they struggle to generate pressure with four and rely on sending extra rushers? Maye has been excellent against the blitz, but the Pats are down to backups at three OL spots, including their fourth-string guard. On paper, the Bears’ defensive scheme seems tailor-made for Maye to exploit, with plenty of single-high, man coverage and blitzing. Do you expect Chicago to blitz aggressively, trust its front four to win, or lean more on two-high zone to limit Maye’s big plays? – Maye The Force Be With You The Bears’ defensive line is a solid group. They’ll be without Montez Sweat due to a PED suspension, but speed rusher Austin Booker, someone we liked and discussed in the 2024 NFL Draft , has gotten off to a strong start this season. From this point of view, Chicago’s pressure numbers are driven by defensive coordinator Dennis Allen’s third-down pressure packages. The Bears have the second-best third-down conversion rate in football at 26%, fueled by those blitzes. They helped scheme up cornerback Kyler Gordon for three sacks last week against Atlanta. As Maye said this week, the Patriots will need to be efficient on first and second down to avoid third-and-long situations and obvious passing downs. Chicago has struggled on early downs this season and when it comes to stopping the run and play-action passing game. That could give New England a formula for staying ahead of the chains and creating explosive plays. Meanwhile, the Bears’ heavy reliance on man coverage and struggles at cornerback should give Maye opportunities to take shots downfield as well. LT- Will Campbell Center- Jared Wilson RT- Caleb Lomu Who mans the Guard spots against the Bears? – For Pats Sake It’s trending towards Morgan Moses being ready to go at right tackle. On the inside, Mike Vrabel said Walter Rouse will start at left guard and Matt Pryor at right , just like they finished Sunday’s game. Rouse has flashed some intriguing tools in limited action, while the 6-foot-7 Pryor is a massive body who can move people in the run game. The real question was if New England would kick Caleb Lomu inside to get their most talented five on the field. He might be forced to if the injuries continue, but it seems like the team would prefer him to stick at offensive tackle for the time being. How can you explain substitutes guards supposed to be second or even third stringers were able to play very efficiently when called upon vs Jets ferocious front seven ? – 7i165 Credit to a number of people. First off, the players themselves for preparing like starters and taking advantage of their opportunities. Doug Marrone and the coaching staff also deserve credit for getting these players ready to go, as does the player personnel department for finding them. Matt Pryor was sitting on the Cardinals practice squad only a few weeks ago before signing here while Walter Rouse was at the bottom of the Vikings roster and eventually brought aboard via trade in late August. Good finds as depth options. Who gets more snaps/targets on Thursday, Chism or Williams? – slunkywontergreen As he did last week, Efton Chism will continue to see more snaps as he fulfills the Mack Hollins role. Targets is a more interesting question, as Chism ran just 10 routes on 42 snaps last week leading to just one target. Williams, meanwhile, ran 21 routes after Doubs left the game with injury. I might still lean Chism seeing more targets due to the nature of a higher-volume role. With only 4 wideouts is there any chance we call up someone from the practice squad? – jpd985 Assuming they need to use their elevations on at least one offensive lineman, I don’t see another wide receiver joining the mix. It’s possible as no other spot on the roster is in desperate need of more depth, but they played the Raiders game with just four wide receivers, so should be set with Brown, Chism, Williams, and Douglas for Thursday night. It will provide a good opportunity for the second-year players. With the amount of injuries we have to the receiving group, can we expect more of a double TE set (especially since Raridon seems to be coming into his own over the past few weeks)? Also, when should we officially start worrying about AJ? I’m not too worried as of now, but should we start panicking if he continues his drops against the Bears? – Mayilman10 The Patriots already run roughly 20% of their offensive plays in 12 personnel, and upped their rate of 13 personnel (three tight ends) last weekend. I’d imagine they continue to lean more on that group with the wide receiver injuries. As for Brown, there is no concern here. As we wrote after the game, the fact that he looked explosive and was getting open was encouraging. It’s be more worrisome if he was wearing coverage all game. If the drops continue in Chicago, however, maybe we start to have a different conversation. With all our injuries this season. Do you think we leave Bryce Baringer on IR and roll with Mitch Wishnowsky for the rest of the season? Are they so far apart in ability/execution that bringing back Bryce would be a substantial upgrade? – Wally242 Baringer isn’t currently ready to return from injury in the first place, so that decision is not yet needed to be made. But, it’s tough to see the Patriots using one of their limited return spots on the position as Wishnowsky has been solid filling in. It’s unfortunate for Baringer, who is in a contract year and had a very strong summer. That’s all for this week’s #PostPulpit mailbag. If you have questions you’d liked to be answered next week, submit them online in our weekly submission post on the Feed. Make sure to follow @iambrianhines and @PatsPulpit as well.

full_text: The New England Patriots’ game against the Chicago Bears on Thursday night will also be a matchup between two of the best young quarterbacks in the NFL: Drake Maye and Caleb Williams, who both entered the league within the first three selections of the 2024 draft. Williams was chosen first overall by the Bears out of USC, through a pick they originally obtained the previous year in a trade with Carolina. Maye came off the board two selections later, moving from North Carolina to New England as the No. 3 pick. They have since started their pro careers apart from one another — one in the AFC, the other in the NFC — but will now cross paths for a second time in three seasons. This gives us an opportunity to take a closer look at how they stack up midway through Year 3. Statistical comparison Despite entering the NFL the same year, Maye and Williams began on different trajectories. Maye was a backup at first, while Williams began as a Day 1 starter. And yet, they are entering Thursday with the same number of combined regular season and playoff starts under their respective belts. Drake Maye Caleb Williams Games (starts) 40 (39) 39 (39) Snaps 2,390 2,640 Attempts 1,133 1,311 Completions 766 794 Completion % 67.6% 60.6% Yards 8,961 8,813 TDs 63 54 INTs 29 19 Yards/attempt 7.9 6.7 CPOE 6.0 -1.4 AdoT 9.1 8.5 Drops 31 55 Throwaways 54 91 Pressure % 38.3% 36.1% Sacks 113 102 Carries 180 168 Rush yards 1,186 1,028 Yards/run 6.6 6.1 Rushing TDs 8 5 Fumbles (lost) 29 (15) 22 (6) EPA/play 0.153 0.055 From a statistical perspective, Maye has been the superior player thus far from an efficiency perspective. He has completed passes at a higher rate, is willing and able to push the ball downfield, and is more dangerous as a runner. He also has scored more often and contributed more yards despite playing 250 fewer snaps. That said, Williams has been better at taking care of the football. He has turned it over 25 times in 39 games compared to Maye’s 44 giveaways. Both have also been hampered at times by uneven support, with Maye finding himself under pressure and on the ground more often. Williams, on the other hand, has seen his receivers drop 24 more passes in two and a half seasons so far. Career accomplishments Maye and Williams developed on a similar trajectory, and from a similar starting point. Their rookie seasons were plagued by organizational turmoil — both their head coaches were not retained after 2024 — and rosters not at a stage to help first-year quarterbacks to consistent success. Since 2024, with Mike Vrabel and Ben Johnson arriving in Foxborough and Chicago, respectively, their outlooks have changed. Maye made one of the most impressive second-year leaps in NFL history, and finished 2025 as a Pro Bowler, second-team All-Pro selections, as well as the MVP runner-up to eventual winner Matthew Stafford. He also led the Patriots to their first Super Bowl appearance in seven years. Williams has not enjoyed the same level of individual or team success yet. That said, with him at the helm Chicago won its first playoff game since 2010 last season. In total, the Patriots are 21-14 with Maye as their starter in the regular season and 3-1 in the playoffs. The Bears are 18-19 and 1-1 when led by Williams. Head-to-head Maye and Williams met once before in their careers, in Week 10 of their respective rookie campaigns. New England, then led by head coach Jerod Mayo, traveled to Chicago to take on the Matt Eberflus-led Bears in a matchup between a 2-7 and a 4-4 team. Despite the Bears being favored by six points entering the contest, it was the visiting Patriots that came a way victoriously. Their 19-3 victory was mostly a defensive one: their defense sacked Williams nine times, forced two turnovers on downs, and allowed the Bears to convert only one of 14 third downs. Their QB went 16-for-30 for 120 yards — one of the least productive outings of his career. Drake Maye fared marginally better, going 15-for-25 for 184 yards with a touchdown and interception each. The score was a 2-yard connection with Ja’Lynn Polk in the late second quarter, and the only time New England found the end zone that day. All their other points came courtesy of kicker Joey Slye. Outlook Maye has been the more successful of the two quarterbacks so far, which is a testament to his own abilities and the support he enjoys in New England. That doesn’t mean Williams is not equally supported in Chicago, but coaching experience does matter: Mike Vrabel and Josh McDaniels have a combined nine Super Bowl rings between them, and are both accomplished and well-proven in their positions as head coach and offensive coordinator. Williams has one of the NFL’s best young head coaches and most creative offensive play-callers and play-designers by his site in Ben Johnson, but Johnson is only in his second season as an NFL head coach. Looking forward, Johnson and Williams will continue developing together, as will Maye alongside his own support staff on and off the field. And after this season, both are in contract extension territory. The expectation is that both will be signed to multi-year deals near the top of the market; depending on what happens down the stretch in 2026, both could reset the market altogether and become the highest-paid quarterbacks in NFL history. Even if they don’t, however, both the Patriots and Bears seem committed to their young quarterbacks in the long term. Accordingly, they will likely be locked up sooner rather than later.

title: Patriots vs. Bears: Who has the edge in Week 7?
summary: The New England Patriots are off to Chicago for their second prime time game of the season. The Bears will present a formidable challenge, not only because the game is taking place at Soldier Field on a short week: they have played some impressive football this season en route to their 4-2 record. That being […]
full_text: The New England Patriots are off to Chicago for their second prime time game of the season. The Bears will present a formidable challenge, not only because the game is taking place at Soldier Field on a short week: they have played some impressive football this season en route to their 4-2 record. That being said, we are — no pun intended — a bit bearish on the team particularly on defense. Likewise, even with their current injury questions we can see the Patriots emerge victoriously. A look at our weekly head-to-head comparison shows why. Passing game Patriots pass offense vs. Bears pass defense: Yes, the Patriots will be without their starting guards . Yes, Morgan Moses is questionable. Yes, the Patriots just placed Romeo Doubs on injured reserve. We still feel confident in the Patriots’ ability to find success against a Bears pass defense missing its two most disruptive and likely one of its starting linebackers as well. The middle of the field is an area that can be attacked, A.J. Brown should be better than he was last week, and as long as New England’s blocking holds up against the blitz and ageless wonder Grady Jarrett, we do believe the team can scheme around its personnel shortcomings and continue to operate at a winning level. Of course, having Drake Maye helps as well. | Edge: Patriots Patriots pass defense vs. Bears pass offense: Caleb Williams is a pretty good quarterback, and he has some talented players around him to throw to. And yet, we like the Patriots pass defense in this matchup. It starts up front, with an offensive line that has had its ups and downs in pass protection and will go up against an aggressive unit anchored by the likes of Milton Williams and Christian Barmore. In the secondary, a lot will depend on how New England defends tight end Colston Loveland and if Charles Woods can continue his hot streak as a replacement starter. We do believe Loveland will be kept in check, and Woods not exploited. Make no mistake, though, the Bears pass offense will win its battles. The war, however, should be won by the visitors. | Edge: Patriots Patriots fans, join the game-day huddle! Follow every snap and discuss every decision with fellow fans on the SB Nation app. Connect through our live game chat Browse with fewer ads Seamlessly move between communities Enjoy faster commenting and posting Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android . Running game Patriots rushing offense vs. Bears run defense: On paper, this reads like a battle between a very stoppable force and an immensely movable object. And it very well might turn out that way: neither unit has stood out so far this season, and one’s edge might be more the result of the other’s shortcomings. With that said, we think the Patriots do have a chance to perform well in the run game even with Walter Rouse and Matt Pryor as their new starting guard duo . Chicago simply doesn’t have the quality in the middle outside of the aforementioned Grady Jarrett, particularly if focused heavily on stopping Drake Maye. | Edge: Patriots Patriots run defense vs. Bears rushing offense: Chicago will be without its No. 2 running back, Kyle Monangai, but D’Andre Swift is more than capable of creating problems on his own. And problems, the Patriots run defense has had this season. And it doesn’t look like there will be a quick or easy fix either, which in turn means that the Bears could be able to put pressure on New England. Lapses similar to the ones Zak Kuhr’s unit had against the Jets — missed tackles, insufficient angles — won’t cut it against a team that ranks first in rushing attempts this season and is certain to keep pounding the rock, and in creative ways. | Edge: Bears Special teams The Patriots and Bears are both entering Thursday night among the best kicking game performers so far this season. They also are facing the same questions, with both teams’ kickers having missed three of their attempts thus far. So, who gets the edge? Statistically, Chicago has been slightly better this year so far in categories such as coverage and return. That being said, New England’s numbers are impacted by not having Brenden Schooler on the active roster for four of six games and by teams trying to neutralize Marcus Jones. No team has a clear edge in this matchup. | Edge: N/A Coaching The Jets (and their own injury situation) turned out to be quite the challenge for the Patriots last week. At the end of the day, though, they still found a way to emerge victoriously. The coaching staff’s ability to adapt and adjust its plans along the way played a big role in that, and it is also why we feel confident in Mike Vrabel and company on a short week as well. Even with the questions along the offensive line, New England has shown the ability to work around potential vulnerabilities already this season. | Edge: Patriots Verdict Even though we give the Patriots an edge in four of six categories, we do not automatically think this will be a clear-cut New England victory. Far from it: all those picks can be disputed, and we actually feel most confident in the one going to the home team (Patriots run defense vs. Bears rushing offense). We do see a path to victory for Mike Vrabel’s team even if the circumstances make for a difficult assignment this week, but it will need high-level performances especially from the backups inserted into the lineup and a coaching staff responsible for not putting them in disadvantageous situations.

title: Patriots to start Walter Rouse, Matt Pryor at guard against Bears
summary: The New England Patriots will be without both of their starting guards on Thursday against the Chicago Bears, but they have already decided on who will replace them. As head coach Mike Vrabel announced on Wednesday, Walter Rouse and Matt Pryor will fill the two vacant spots in the lineup. “We have a lot of […]
full_text: The New England Patriots will be without both of their starting guards on Thursday against the Chicago Bears, but they have already decided on who will replace them. As head coach Mike Vrabel announced on Wednesday, Walter Rouse and Matt Pryor will fill the two vacant spots in the lineup. “We have a lot of consideration. We go through things, different scenarios,” Vrabel explained during a press conference at Gillette Stadium. “We’re going to go with where we finished on Sunday and see what that looks like, and then have everybody else ready to go.” Rouse and Pryor started Sunday’s game against the New York Jets on the bench, but were forced into action due to the injuries suffered higher up on the depth chart. Pryor was first up, entering at right guard in the second quarter after Alijah Vera-Tucker left with a hamstring injury. With Ben Brown sliding over to Vera-Tucker’s spot, the 31-year-old took the field for his first offensive snaps since arriving in Foxborough. He finished the game with 46 snaps . Rouse entered the mix in the fourth quarter, after Brown went out with a knee injury. He played the final 14 offensive snaps of the day. The 25-year-old had previously played extended snaps albeit at right guard during the Patriots’ Week 3 loss in Jacksonville; in that game, Rouse was the backup at that particular position and called upon after Greg Van Roten — himself an injury replacement for regular starter Mike Onwenu — was lost to injury. Now, the two will be part of the starting lineup against the Bears. The group will also consist of left tackle Will Campbell and center Jared Wilson. Right tackle Morgan Moses is officially questionable because of a foot injury, with first-round rookie Caleb Lomu a candidate to enter the lineup if need be. Earlier this week, Mike Vrabel said that the Patriots need Lomu to be “ready to go at multiple positions” versus the Bears. Kickoff between the two teams is scheduled for 8:15 p.m. ET on Thursday.

Alijah Vera-Tucker and Ben Brown have been ruled out for Thursday night’s matchup against the Chicago Bears, as head coach Mike Vrabel announced during his final press conference of the short week. A hamstring injury and a knee injury , respectively, kept the two offensive linemen sidelined throughout preparations. Cornerbacks Carlton Davis III, Karon Prunty and Channing Canada will also be missing in the Midwest, while four members of the active roster stand as questionable. Here’s the rest of the game statuses leading up to the 8:15 p.m. ET kickoff. OUT Patriots G Alijah Vera-Tucker (hamstring) G Ben Brown (knee) CB Carlton Davis III (neck) CB Karon Prunty (hamstring) CB Channing Canada (hamstring) Bears RB Kyle Monangai (thumb, toe) LB Jack Sanborn (concussion) New England’s left guard and right guard had been ruled out on the way to what became a 26-19 win last Sunday. The musical chairs sent Matt Pryor and Walter Rouse in along the interior. No sacks nor penalties followed for what remained of the front five against the New York Jets. The October signing as well as the August trade acquisition that stepped in for 46 and 14 offensive downs, respectively, are now set to start over the shoulders of center Jared Wilson . There were three cornerbacks among the inactives for the AFC East meeting at Gillette Stadium. And despite recently returning as a limited participant , the Patriots’ secondary will be again without Davis for a third consecutive game. The veteran outside starter has dealt with a neck issue dating back to September and had missed the previous two full weeks of practice. That leaves 2025 waiver claim Charles Woods and team captain Marcus Jones on deck for expanded roles alongside All-Pro Christian Gonzalez. Hamstring injuries will also keep a pair of rookies who have combined for 76 snaps on special teams out for Thursday night. DOUBTFUL Patriots No players listed Bears LB T.J. Edwards (hamstring) No Patriots check in with a doubtful designation, but the Bears will likely be without two linebackers under the lights at Soldier Field after one was already ruled out. The doubtful Edwards was a partial participant on Wednesday while working through a hamstring injury. He stands with 16 tackles and one interception through five starts this fall for Chicago’s front. QUESTIONABLE Patriots OT Morgan Moses (foot) LB Christian Elliss (chest) S Kevin Byard III (chest) S Craig Woodson (shoulder) Bears CB Tyrique Stevenson Sr. (hip) The lone questionable Patriot not to practice in full on kickoff’s eve was Moses, who has been listed as limited since the initial estimation . The 35-year-old captain had exited just nine offensive downs into last weekend’s start at right tackle. In his absence due to a foot injury, rookie No. 28 overall pick Caleb Lomu went from reporting as an eligible tight end to stepping in as the bookend opposite blindside starter Will Campbell. New England could elect to activate swing tackle Marcus Bryant from injured reserve before Thursday’s 4 p.m. ET deadline for roster moves. The 2025 seventh-rounder’s 21-day practice window opened midway through October. He has since ramped up to full participation as well as no game designation. With two offensive linemen officially ruled out, the 53-man roster currently includes seven options available. The organization brought back blockers Jacob Rizy and Andrew Rupcich on the practice squad amid the attrition.

title: Patriots vs. Bears series history ahead of Week 7 game
summary: Following a game against their division rival Jets, the New England Patriots are up against a relatively unfamiliar opponent. They will travel to Chicago this week to take on the Bears on Thursday Night Football. It will be only the 17th meeting between the two storied franchises. Let’s take a look back at the most […]
full_text: Following a game against their division rival Jets, the New England Patriots are up against a relatively unfamiliar opponent. They will travel to Chicago this week to take on the Bears on Thursday Night Football. It will be only the 17th meeting between the two storied franchises. Let’s take a look back at the most important moments from the first 16. Patriots vs. Bears series history Overall history: Even though the most memorable game of the series is a Bears win, it is the Patriots who have won the majority of the first 16 contests between the two organizations. New England holds an 11-5 edge after winning six of eight games since 2000. Those include a come-from-behind victory in 2002 that saw Tom Brady and company erase a 27-6 deficit in the late third quarter to ultimately win 33-30, as well as a lopsided 51-23 win during the 2014 season that was dominated by Rob Gronkowski and his three touchdowns. Chicago, as we will discuss shortly, is 1-0 against the Patriots in the playoffs. First game: Three years after the AFL-NFL merger, the Patriots and Bears met for the first time. The game at Soldier Field was a defensive affair that saw the two teams combine for only 98 net passing yards as well as six turnovers. Five of those were forced by New England, putting the team on the path to success. The winning points were scored in the fourth quarter, when quarterback Jim Plunkett found the end zone on a 5-yard quarterback keeper to give the Patriots a 13-10 win. Neither they nor the Bears were overly successful as a whole in 1973, though. | Highlights Most memorable game: Unfortunately for the Patriots, the most memorable out of their meetings with the Bears is Super Bowl XX. New England did manage to take a 3-0 lead and by doing so score the first points of the playoffs against Chicago’s famous 46 defense, but it ultimately was unable to hang on: the NFC champions scored 44 unanswered points, including the famous 1-yard rushing touchdown by defensive tackle William “Refrigerator” Perry in the third quarter. When all was said and done, the team of head coach Raymond Berry finished with just 123 net yards and turned the ball over six times en route to a 46-10 blowout that was the most lopsided defeat in a Super Bowl at the time. | Highlights Most recent game: The Patriots’ most recent matchup with the Bears brought more pleasant memories than the 1986 defeat, albeit at a smaller scale. Meeting at Soldier Field in 2024, the team led by then-head coach Jerod Mayo and then-rookie quarterback Drake Maye celebrated a 19-3 win. Maye was solid, but the defense was the story of the day: led by Deatrich Wise Jr. and Anfernee Jennings, who each registered two takedowns, the Patriots sacked Caleb Williams nine times and limited Chicago to 142 yards. | Highlights The Patriots and Bears will add to their series history on Thursday at 8:20 p.m. ET.

full_text: Winners of three straight games, the New England Patriots had little time to enjoy their victory over the New York Jets on Sunday. They quickly turned their attention to their upcoming Week 7 game on Thursday Night Football. The quick turnaround is not the only challenge this week, though. Even though they are ranked only third in the NFC North at the moment, the Bears look like one of the best teams in football right now: good on offense, good on defense, solid in the return game. Sounds familiar? Well, let’s take a closer look. Bears key stats The Patriots and Bears are entering their prime time meeting with identical 4-2 records, and similar numbers across the board. What those go to show is that the Bears in Year 2 under head coach Ben Johnson are a legitimate contender — and quite similar to their opponent this week. Like its Patriots counterpart, however, it also has had its issues with finishing: the Bears are tied for 22nd with a 50.0% red zone rate and tied for sixth-worst in the NFL in total giveaways (11) and turnover rate (16.2%). Defensively, the unit has performed very well especially against the pass — another similarity with the Patriots, who, like the Bears, have had issues against the run. Bears 2026 season As noted above, Caleb Williams has not been able to play the entirety of Chicago’s season. He hurt his hamstring late in Week 2, and subsequently had to sit out the next three games as well. During that span, the Bears did go 2-1 — a testament to their backup quarterbacks and the team’s overall talent (and the fact that the Eagles and Jets are both beatable teams in 2026). Week 1: 59-37 win at Carolina Panthers (1-0) Week 2: 9-3 loss vs. Minnesota Vikings (1-1) Week 3: 27-7 win vs. Philadelphia Eagles (2-1) Week 4: 23-12 win vs. New York Jets (3-1) Week 5: 31-7 loss at Green Bay Packers (3-2) Week 6: 31-23 win at Atlanta Falcons (4-2) The Bears started their campaign with a shootout win over the Panthers, but just a week later found themselves on the wrong end of a 9-3 loss. Their 56-point swing between those two games was the biggest in since 1973. Chicago rebounded with those two wins over the Eagles and Jets, followed by a lopsided loss in Green Bay. Their 0-2 record in a competitive division is why the Bears are only third in the NFC North right despite still being sixth in the NFC playoff picture. On Sunday against the Falcons, Chicago rebounded in style. With Williams back in the lineup, the team jumped to a 31-7 lead before surrendering two late touchdowns. The Bears dominated time of possession and ran 73 plays compared to Atlanta’s 50. The first overall selection in the 2024 NFL Draft is the prototypical modern-era quarterback due to his immense arm talent and physical skill combined with the ability to keep plays alive and stress defenses with his legs if need be. In his three starts this season, Williams completed a league-leading 72.5% of his passes for 712 yards with three touchdowns and an interception. He also scored on a pair of rushes, contributing to a combined EPA per play of 0.247 — fifth-highest among all qualifying quarterbacks right now. If there are any negatives, it’s Williams taking nine sacks thus far and fumbling the ball twice. His supporting cast is talented across the board, even with left tackle Braxton Jones out due to injury. It starts at running back, where D’Andre Swift is the main man and a dangerous player as a runner and receiver: he has carried the ball 94 times for 398 yards and six touchdowns, averaging 4.2 yards per carry. Kyle Monangai has also produced at a high level, though, gaining 324 yards and scoring three times on 60 carries for an average of 5.4 yards per run — impressive numbers. The receiving corps mainly consists of five players, with some alternating as starters. The core guys are Rome Odunze and Colston Loveland, whose catches/yards/touchdowns stat lines are solid — 20/312/0 and 19/175/1 — but naturally impacted by Williams’ absence. Atop of the list, meanwhile, are Luther Burden (31/361/1) and Kalif Raymond (26/244/1), who rank first and second on the team in receptions. Also part of the mix is Cole Kmet (7/59/1), whose statistics are mediocre but who plays an important role as a blocker. The offensive line, as noted above, has been forced to replace its left tackle with backup Theo Benedet. It still has one of the best left guards in the game, ageless wonder and future Pro Football Hall of Famer Joe Thuney, as well as another ex-Patriot, Garrett Bradbury, manning the center position. The right side led by Jonah Jackson and Darnell Wright has been quite solid as well; in fact, it is where the Bears have done their most damage on the ground. On defense, Chicago will be without starting edges Dayo Odeyingbo and Montez Sweat, who are ranked first and second on the team with 14 and 13 quarterback pressures, respectively. As can be seen, the personnel questions are another similarity with the Patriots, even though the Bears have not had to deal with the same volume of injuries this year. With Odeyingbo and Sweat out, a mix of Austin Booker, James Lynch and Shemar Turner will man the edge. title: State of the NFC South: Week 6
summary: A week of blown leads, close games, and two NFC South teams winning. What an exciting week of football! Here is how each team did in Week 6: Tampa Bay Buccaneers After entering the fourth quarter with a 16-3 home lead, the Buccaneers and rookie QB Jalon Daniels looked set for their second win of […]
full_text: A week of blown leads, close games, and two NFC South teams winning. What an exciting week of football! Here is how each team did in Week 6: Tampa Bay Buccaneers After entering the fourth quarter with a 16-3 home lead, the Buccaneers and rookie QB Jalon Daniels looked set for their second win of the season, but instead head coach Todd Bowles’ seat got even hotter. The Pittsburgh Steelers scored 16 points in the fourth quarter, and Aaron Rodgers was impossible to stop. It didn’t help that the Bucs kept turning the ball over. The game went to overtime, and the Steelers won. It’s only a matter of time before Bowles gets fired, and with the team back at the bottom of the NFC South, the clock is ticking. Carolina Panthers Atop the NFC South, the Panthers had a really good chance to extend their lead with Jalen Hurts being out for the Eagles. That’s exactly what happened, and although it was a bit closer than Carolina would have likely wanted, Bryce Young and Chuba Hubbard had really great games. This offense continues to be one to watch in the NFC, but the pass defense is a major worry. Next week, Carolina faces the Bucs in an NFC South battle, so they’ll likely get another win. Atlanta Falcons One team in the division that had to make their own comeback was the Falcons, and they nearly did it with Bijan Robinson having under 70 yards running the ball. At one point in the fourth quarter, the Chicago Bears led 31-7, but the Falcons cut the lead to 31-23 with 5 minutes left. Penix was sacked after getting the ball back again, which led to a fumble, and the Bears never looked back at that point. If the Falcons played as well as they did in that fourth quarter all game, we may be talking about a different result, and it would have been a big win against a potential playoff team. Next week, the Falcons must play better as they face the undefeated San Francisco 49ers. New Orleans Saints Of course, another almost-comeback in the NFC South, but the Saints were nearly victims of it. After dominating the third quarter, Kellen Moore pulled starters early in the fourth quarter, and that was way too early. Momentum shifted once CJ Donaldson fumbled, and all of a sudden, the Saints needed their starters back in, and the defense that had kept the Saints in this game had to defend an entirely new QB. If the Saints kept their significant lead and maybe even extended it, we would be having a different conversation, but the doubt around Moore has not subsided after the near comeback by the Giants. Now, if the game even happens in Paris, a blowout loss to the Steelers may end Moore’s time in New Orleans. NFC South standings: Carolina Panthers (3-2) Atlanta Falcons (2-4) New Orleans Saints (2-4) Tampa Bay Buccaneers (1-5)

title: Saints Rookie Report: Week 7 preview vs. the Steelers
summary: After a nearly disastrous loss to the New York Giants, the New Orleans Saints are facing another must-win situation against the Pittsburgh Steelers, and the game will be played overseas in Paris. In that Week 6 game, the Saints’ rookies put on some nice performances, and Week 7 may be the breakout game for this […]
full_text: BALTIMORE, MARYLAND - SEPTEMBER 20: Jeremiah Wright #65 of the New Orleans Saints reacts against the Baltimore Ravens during an NFL football game at M&T Bank Stadium on September 20, 2026 in Baltimore, Maryland. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images After a nearly disastrous loss to the New York Giants, the New Orleans Saints are facing another must-win situation against the Pittsburgh Steelers, and the game will be played overseas in Paris. In that Week 6 game, the Saints’ rookies put on some nice performances, and Week 7 may be the breakout game for this class. WR Jordyn Tyson Finally, we can talk about Jordyn Tyson. Although his availability for Sunday’s game is up in the air, he did travel with the team, which means there’s a chance he plays. The Saints’ offense has had a number of issues this season, and although Tyson will not fix everything, he is a massive upgrade over Bryce Lance. The injuries have been demoralizing, to say the least, but Tyson is an extremely talented player who can be one of the best WRs in the NFL. Although I would expect a small sample size if he does play, we may finally see him on the field. DT Christen Miller Although this was another game where the Saints went with other DT options over Miller, he did get on the field and helped shut down New York’s running game. In Week 7, the Saints face a much better rushing attack led by Jaylen Warren, so they will have to rely on Miller a bit more. TE Oscar Delp Against the Giants, Delp had his best game so far. He made some really important blocks that significantly helped the run game and had two catches. It wasn’t an incredible performance by any means, but one that could lead to more snaps for Delp. Delp is likely going to be in the same exact role for Week 7. OG Jeremiah Wright Here we go! After Cesar Ruiz left the game with an injury, rookie Jeremiah Wright was thrown into the lineup, and suddenly the run game looked great. Could this be a coincidence? Maybe. But it was clear that lanes were being opened up that the running backs could easily take advantage of. He got pushed back and beat at times, any rookie would, but overall, it was exactly what you wanted to see in his first real game. Now with Ruiz’s health in question, and the fact Wright’s debut was positve, the Saints must start him in Week 7. Might as well see what you have with Wright in a full game. WR Bryce Lance This was an up-and-down game for Lance. He once again had some head-scratching moments, including a drop, but he also scored the first touchdown of his young career. With Tyson’s return, Lance may be demoted to a more blocking role, but that may be better for now, especially as he develops. WR Barion Brown I thought Barion Brown had the best game of his career as well. He had some really nice returns and made a nice contested catch that may have been an interception if he didn’t get to the ball. Brown will likely fall to WR5 on the depth chart, but just like Lance, that’s perfectly fine. RB CJ Donaldson Another up-and-down game, Donaldson had some really nice runs to begin the game and fought for some tough yards. He nearly scored the first touchdown of his career, but was called back after his knee was down short. His blocking was also good, which was needed against the blitzes. Then we get to the fumble. The Giants’ comeback started after Donaldson fumbled, and that put a stain on this performance. Not sure if Donaldson will see fewer snaps in Week 7, but it’s something to monitor. OT Mason Murphy Murphy did not come into this game like last week, but after Asim Richards clear struggles against the Giants, it may be time for New Orleans to try something new. DB Lorenzo Styles Jr. Styles Jr. was once again an impact player on special teams, which is exactly why the Saints drafted him.

title: NY Giants QB Jameis Winston on benching: ‘My week has been the same’
summary: New York Giants quarterback Jameis Winston is heading back to the sidelines after it was announced that J.J. McCarthy would start the team’s Week 7 matchup against the Houston Texans. Winston isn’t changing his routine much even after the announcement. “My week has been the same. You move forward by continuing to focus on what […]
full_text: Jameis Winston | Getty Images New York Giants quarterback Jameis Winston is heading back to the sidelines after it was announced that J.J. McCarthy would start the team’s Week 7 matchup against the Houston Texans. Winston isn’t changing his routine much even after the announcement. “My week has been the same. You move forward by continuing to focus on what you love, and that’s my desire is being the starting quarterback for the New York Football Giants. And that’s also pointing to those around me and impacting them the best way that I can. Because like I always say, what I want for myself, I want for everyone. So, when I say that, I mean it. So, I go out there and apply it,” Winston said. Winston knows that his number can be called at any moment, just like it was in Week 2 against the Los Angeles Rams. He’s preparing for that opportunity while simultaneously supporting McCarthy in his stint as the team starter. “By being my very best,” Winston said in how he is supporting McCarthy. “That’s how you support a young man, by coming to work, being the same person every single day, by showing respect and gratitude for the opportunity that he’s presented with and the opportunity that I had and understanding that gratitude is the key to abundance in all of this. So, when you come to work and you approach it from a grateful mindset, it kind of leads out to the entire building and nothing really changed but the role itself.” Winston has been through the ups and downs of being a quarterback in the NFL. He’s been on the mountaintop as the No. 1 overall pick in the 2015 draft, and he’s also experienced plenty of lows. Winston is still why he is viewed as a valuable piece of the puzzle for the Giants. His ability to accept decisions like this is part of the reason why. “Just focusing on one day at a time is the biggest thing. I’m extremely grateful that I still get to do what I love, and that’s play football at a high level for the New York Football Giants. And being able to accept roles and understand what is your significant role, how can I be the best at my role with this team, is one of the things that you have to adjust to in this league,” Winston said. Big Blue View community, what do you make of Winston’s comments in regards to his benching? Let us know in the comments section below.

Carroll: The ultimate question this time of year, and the division-leading Giants will have a nicely timed bye week to evaluate their future. If they remain atop the NFC East, there’s a strong argument to be made to add pieces and try to take advantage of a weak division. But will that really be useful in a season they’re operating with backup quarterbacks? The Giants only own six picks in the upcoming draft, so trading away draft assets, particularly premium picks, for short-term gains might be shortsighted. And while John Harbaugh has been aggressive in trying to plug the holes on this team, he values draft capital. There’s no doubt the Giants could use help along the defensive line and at running back — especially after they just released Najee Harris — but a blockbuster move still feels like it’d be a surprise. That said, it’s been a season full of those, so perhaps we’re in for a few more. Of all the lucrative chips in Indianapolis, none would surpass Taylor. It is worth mentioning that Taylor has been less dynamic in 2026, with his 67.3 rushing grade sitting 16th out of 27 qualified backs and averaging just 2.79 yards after contact per attempt. John Harbaugh’s offense has not found sustainable production on the ground through six games. title: J.J. McCarthy is honored to have the opportunity to start for the NY Giants
summary: The New York Giants named third-year quarterback J.J. McCarthy their starter against the Houston Texans on Wednesday. It’s a decision that felt inevitable since the Giants traded for the former 10th overall pick less than a month ago. But it also sudden considering McCarthy hadn’t thrown a pass for the Giants before coming in for […]
full_text: J.J McCarthy nearly led the Giants to an incredible come-from-behind victory on Sunday. | Getty Images The New York Giants named third-year quarterback J.J. McCarthy their starter against the Houston Texans on Wednesday. It’s a decision that felt inevitable since the Giants traded for the former 10th overall pick less than a month ago. But it also sudden considering McCarthy hadn’t thrown a pass for the Giants before coming in for a struggling Jameis Winston in the fourth quarter last week against the New Orleans Saints. “Honored to be a quarterback for the New York Football Giants,” McCarthy said. “To be able to get an opportunity to go against a great Houston Texans team, and thrilled to get out there tomorrow, really get in the film room and just evaluate today’s practice to get better and go from there.” McCarthy doesn’t have long to adapt to being named the starter. After all, the Giants travel to Houston after just three days of practice. Still, McCarthy says that the Giants have felt like a good fit since he arrived, and he’s getting comfortable. “I feel like just being around a new group of guys, new system, new coaching staff, just a new culture. Everything about this place, it feels very fitting for me.” McCarthy added that while the offensive system is a good fit for his skill set, it’s the culture in Giants’ facilities that’s the best fit. That, he says, reminds him of winning teams he’s been a part of in the past. “Being in this system where they use the quarterback’s legs and a multitude of things,” he said. “But the personalities, the culture of just grinding every single day to get better and everyone helping each other to progress towards one goal. It’s been fantastic. A lot of successful buildings have similar qualities, and this building definitely has that.” In a round-about way, it feels somewhat fitting that the McCarthy has become the Giants’ starting quarterback. He was widely linked to the Giants prior to the 2024 NFL Draft, and even expected to be a Giant before the selected Malik Nabers and Vikings traded up for him. “There’s definitely a point where I wanted to be here,” McCarthy said. “It’s the second I got in here and the second I left. There’s something special about this building, this state, this football program, been around for 101 years. It’s got so much passion, so much tradition. Nothing about this place really gives you the kind of irk feeling to it. It’s just welcomed me with open arms since the first second I got in these doors. And it’s done the same since I got here this year. I’m extremely grateful to this organization for just welcoming me.” The ‘point’ McCarthy was talking about was likely when McCarthy visited the Giants twice in the pre-draft process. He said at the time that he spent more time with the Giants than any other team before the draft. Adding another layer is that the Giants are traveling to Houston, where McCarthy won the National Championship with Jim Harbaugh’s Michigan Wolverines in 2024, a fact that isn’t lost on McCarthy. “It is really special, it’s awesome,” he said. “But each game, each rep is an independent event. And going in there and just focusing on that first play and executing those six seconds within that play, that’s really the main focus. But it’s going to be really cool to be in Houston and I think we’re staying in the same hotel that we stayed in when we were there in 2024.” McCarthy doesn’t have time to get caught up in sentimentality, however. He has a game against the Houston Texans to get get ready for, adding more tumult to a month-long whirlwind. “A lot of change of scenery, a lot of change of language, and meeting so many great, new people,” McCarthy said, when describing the whirlwind change when the was traded from Minnesota to New York. “Just a lot of things you have to forget and move on. It’s tough when you don’t see your family for a long time. It’s easier to do that while you’re learning a whole new offense, and you have that distraction of just always being busy.” And that’s been the biggest thing for McCarthy — learning the Giants’ offense. First he had to learn it well enough to back up Jameis Winston, and now he needs to be able to command the offense as a starter. Fortunately, he says, the Giants have a building full of excellent teachers. “I mean, great teachers in this building,” McCarthy said. “Jameis has helped me out from the get go since I got here. Coach Nags (OC Matt Nagy), Coach Callahan (Quarterbacks Coach Brian Callahan), they’ve been doing a tremendous job of just making sure I’m up to speed.” McCarthy also looks forward to getting help from the Giants’ intended starting quarterback, Jaxson Dart. “I talked to him (Dart) today,” McCarthy said. “Just normal conversation. We’re both just rooting for each other. “And like I told him, I want the same thing that you want, to help win the football games for this organization and do everything we can and be the best versions of ourselves every day to help the collective. It’s been great conversation. I love Jaxson. We’ve worked with the same QB coach out in California for a long time, so we have a prior relationship. “I think he’s coming back this week to really dive into the game plan and be that sounding board for me. It’s going to be great because he is such a smart player and obviously very well-rounded in this offense. It’s going to be awesome to just ask him really anything and pick his brain about anything.” Speaking of the offense, McCarthy adds an element of athleticism to the quarterback position that was lost with Dart against the Los Angeles Rams. He also adds a speed contrast to the Giants’ more power-oriented backfield. McCarthy has excellent agility for the quarterback position running an elite 6.82-second 3-cone and a very good 4.23-second short shuttle at the 2024 NFL Scouting Combine, as well as a very good 4.48-second 40-yard dash at Michigan’s Pro Day. That athleticism opens up — or re-opens — a world of plays that the Giants had to shelve with Winston as the starter. “I feel like it just adds multiplicity to where you can attack the defense,” McCarthy said. “It’s always doing my job of holding the backside player and making sure that you get that split second to the running back to split that crease and make it a 15-yard gain instead of a six-yard gain. So, there’s a lot of different factors that come with things, not just QB run specific, it adds a lot of elements to just the backside stuff, carrying out your keeper fakes on wide zone stuff. “Yeah, I definitely feel like that’s an element that attacks defenses very well.” Ultimately, this is a econd chance for McCarthy, who had fallen all the way to QB3 in Minnesota. But that’s also where he saw former New York Jets quarterback Sam Darnold revive his career when he stepped in for McCarthy when he tore his meniscus as a rookie. He understands the magnitude of the opportunity before him. “Every time you step on the field, it’s an opportunity,” McCarthy said. “Whether you’re the starting guy, whether you’re not, you have a chance to prove yourself, prove it to your peers, and prove it to everyone around you. And at the end of the day, I approach it the same way. How can I attack that next rep, how can I win this day and go from there.”
author: Chris Pflum

title: Is starting J.J. McCarthy the right choice? BBV staff weighs in
summary: Did New York Giants coach John Harbaugh make the right decision, announcing that J.J. McCarthy will replace Jameis Winston as the starting quarterback beginning Sunday against the Houston Texans? Tony Del Genio For the players? No. John Harbaugh is quickly creating an impression of having an outward persona as a good guy but an actual […]
full_text: J.J. McCarthy | Getty Images Did New York Giants coach John Harbaugh make the right decision, announcing that J.J. McCarthy will replace Jameis Winston as the starting quarterback beginning Sunday against the Houston Texans? Tony Del Genio For the players? No. John Harbaugh is quickly creating an impression of having an outward persona as a good guy but an actual personality as a coach who considers his players little more than fungible quantities. (See: Running back rotation and Harris release – not that Harris was playing well, but you should be able to express frustration to reporters without losing your job.) Did Jameis Winston play poorly against the Saints? Yes. Did he play well in the two wins and a tie before that? Yes. If I’m a Giants player now I’m thinking one bad game and I’m benched. Tom Coughlin at least waited until Game 10 in 2004 before he sat Kurt Warner for Eli Manning. I would have started Jameis on Sunday, gone to J.J. McCarthy after halftime if the first half was a disaster, and waited until after the bye week to name J.J. the starter, with two bad Jameis starts as my evidence. If my only consideration is the short-term “let’s win today” goal, then starting J.J. is understandable. I’ve had this game circled as a loss for the Giants since the summer. The Giants’ IOLs are playing poorly and the team may have to call a couple of Giants fans who travel to Houston out of the stands to play LT and RT. Whoever plays QB is likely to be running for his life, especially from the outside where Will Anderson Jr., the best edge defender in the NFL, and Danielle Hunter will be hunting the QB. The more mobile J.J. has a much better chance of avoiding that pressure, and with a skill set that is somewhat more like Jaxson Dart’s, that may allow Matt Nagy to use more of the playbook he had developed for Dart in the off-season. If J.J. pulls out a win, Harbaugh will look prescient. Finally, if the long-term goal is not to develop J.J. to compete with Dart as starter next season, but rather to showcase him and then flip him to a contender at the trade deadline for a much bigger draft haul than the 5th rounder they gave up to get him, then I can see that making him starter sooner rather than later is the best way to do that. So there are reasons to start J.J. now. The issue is whether Harbaugh risks losing the locker room by doing so after one bad half of football from his previous starter. Chris Pflum It felt like this move was coming at some point after the Giants traded for McCarthy, and the only question was how long Jameis Winston would hold out and hold onto the starting job. It was a bit of a surprise that the move came before the bye week, but the Giants decided to rip off the band-aid. And the fact remains that the Giants’ offensive brain trust have long enjoyed having mobile quarterbacks and built the offense with a certain skill set in mind at the quarterback position — a skill set that Winston just doesn’t have. McCarthy was far from perfect against the New Orleans Saints, but we saw how the threat of the quarterback run slowed down the Saints’ defense and sparked the Giants’ offense. The Giants will still have to use a pared down version of their offense with McCarthy and add concepts as he gets more comfortable. However, the fact that McCarthy’s athleticism enables designed quarterback runs, zone-read or read-option plays, and package plays, he’ll have a wider variety of plays available. McCarthy’s mobility and arm strength also add a level of explosiveness that could help unlock the Giants’ run game — or make teams pay for playing downhill too hard. I’m not going to expect that the Giants will have the same kind of suffocating offense that we saw in Week 1. But I am interested to see what happens with the Giants once again planning their offense around the type of quarterback for which it was built. Nick Falato This was coming sooner rather than later. The Giants traded a round-five selection to acquire the 10th overall pick from two years ago. McCarthy shined in his opportunity, throwing for 243 yards in less than a quarter and sparking an improbable comeback that ultimately failed. Under Jameis Winston, the Giants’ offense was one-dimensional, with a stale run game. The Jameis Winston experience is full of peaks and valleys, and McCarthy seized the opportunity when Winston was in a valley. McCarthy’s success on Sunday wasn’t just against prevent defenses—his accomplishments were impressive—but it’s also fair to acknowledge the fortune of two dropped near-interceptions and the one he threw on what looked like a miscommunication with Malachi Fields. Communication is my reason for hesitation on the move; can McCarthy effectively relay the calls and get the offense on the same page to allow post-alignment adjustments within the Matt Nagy scheme? Communicating in Houston with a young quarterback Jeremy Brener I think this has to be the right move for the Giants at this time. They traded for McCarthy a few weeks ago, not just to stash him on the bench. Eventually, this move was coming, and it comes at a time when the Giants are still in first place, which puts them in the proper position to compete. Moving to McCarthy gives them the best chance to win in Week 7 against the Texans, and that’s what the decision should be based on first and foremost. Over the course of the season, McCarthy has a higher ceiling than Winston. Given that the Giants are competing for the division crown among a gaggle of teams that don’t look very promising, this move is happening at the right time. David Hartman The Giants will turn to J.J. McCarthy as their starting QB in Houston on Sunday. It’s not an ideal spot for the switch. Although their defense has been way worse than expected this season, the Texans are on a two-game winning streak and they’ve got a ton of talent on the defensive line and in the secondary. Still, they’ve been carved up by multiple QBs in the early going. McCarthy acquitted himself well in mop-up duty last Sunday. But that was at home, and mostly against the Saints’ second string, in what started out as garbage time. This will be a much sterner test. And with New York’s top three tackles all ailing, and Will Anderson on the other side, some mobility at the position will help. But I do worry about a disaster performance, and then what? That said, I don’t disagree with giving this a shot. New York needs to see if McCarthy is a potential reclamation project like Sam Darnold or Baker Mayfield. They know what they have with Jameis. They don’t know what they have with McCarthy, although the 2025 tape and results are dreadful. Let’s see what happens. My gut says it won’t be pretty. Valentine’s View It feels like the move to McCarthy was inevitable since the Giants surrendered a fifth-round draft pick to acquire him. In an ideal world, Harbaugh might have waited until after the BYE week to make this move. Then again, the Giants have not been living in an ideal world since the moment Jaxson Dart was lost for the season. Fact is, the Giants have been in survival mode. They are going to be in survival mode all season, doing the best they can with backup quarterbacks they did not plan on playing. McCarthy is not Dart. He does, though, give the Giants the opportunity to be the offense they want to be rather than the offense they have to be with Winston. There is more upside there, though nobody knows if McCarthy will be better or worse than Winston has been. It is still going to be a wild ride. I get it, though.
author: Ed Valentine

title: NY Giants make roster move with top three offensive tackles missing practice
summary: The New York Giants on Wednesday signed offensive tackle Josh Sills off the Indianapolis Colts practice squad, head coach John Harbaugh announced during his post-practice media session. Sills, 28, has played in 21 games for the Colts and Philadelphia Eagles since 2022. He is a former undrafted free agent. Sills has played 41 offensive and […]
full_text: Josh Sills | Getty Images The New York Giants on Wednesday signed offensive tackle Josh Sills off the Indianapolis Colts practice squad, head coach John Harbaugh announced during his post-practice media session. Sills, 28, has played in 21 games for the Colts and Philadelphia Eagles since 2022. He is a former undrafted free agent. Sills has played 41 offensive and 79 special teams snaps. The move was necessitated by injuries at the tackle position. The team’s top three tackles — Andrew Thomas (groin), Jermaine Eluemunor (calf), and Marcus Mbow missed practice on Wednesday. Thomas has been managing his groin injury since Week 2. He has played in each game since despite practicing sparingly. Eluemunor missed last week’s game. Mbow, Eluemunor’s replacement, appeared to suffer an injury late in Sunday’s game against the New Orleans Saints. He is on the injury report with a knee issue. Other than Sills, the only healthy tackle on the roster is rookie J.C. Davis. Davis saw his first game action last Sunday in relief of Thomas during the fourth quarter. Also of concern on the injury report, starting safety Jevon Holland and starting cornerback Greg Newsome II have concussions, and starting inside linebacker Tremaine Edmunds missed Wednesday’s practice with a shoulder injury. Cornerback Colton Hood was a limited participant as he is still in concussion protocol. Punter Jordan Stout (right knee) was also limited. The Giants let running back Najee Harris and outside linebacker Jihad Ward go on Tuesday. They added only outside linebacker Trace Ford, so they still had a space on their 53-man roster. title: John Harbaugh explains Giants switch to J.J. McCarthy at quarterback
summary: J.J. McCarthy “gives us the best chance to play the best offense we can,” New York Giants head coach John Harbaugh said on Wednesday, explaining his decision to start McCarthy over Jameis Winston this Sunday against the Houston Texans. “I thought Jameis has done a tremendous job, won us games, played well,” Harbaugh said. “As […]
full_text: J.J McCarthy nearly led the Giants to an incredible come-from-behind victory on Sunday. | Getty Images J.J. McCarthy “gives us the best chance to play the best offense we can,” New York Giants head coach John Harbaugh said on Wednesday, explaining his decision to start McCarthy over Jameis Winston this Sunday against the Houston Texans. “I thought Jameis has done a tremendous job, won us games, played well,” Harbaugh said. “As we go forward here, this is going to be our direction. We think it gives us some good options on offense.” "I thought Jameis has done a tremendous job, won us games, played well. As we go forward here, this is going to be our direction. We think it gives us some good options on offense." John Harbaugh talks about the Giants' quarterback change from Jameis Winston to J.J. McCarthy: pic.twitter.com/3n2ge4O0ym — SNY Giants (@SNYGiants) October 21, 2026 The Giants went 2-1-1 in four games with Winston starting after Jaxson Dart was lost for the season with a knee injury, McCarthy, though, closer approximates Dart’s skill set than the immobile, 32-year-old Winston. The Giants spent the offseason building an offense that would incorporate Dart’s running ability. That was lost with Winston. McCarthy, 23, is not the runner Dart is, but does give offensive coordinator Matt Nagy the ability to access that portion of the playbook. Harbaugh is not worried about how much of the offense McCarthy can run. “He’s got the gameplan down,” Harbaugh said. “I think he had it down last week pretty fully, even more so this week. It has been tailored a little more toward his direction, probably. He’ll be ready to go.” Harbaugh would not commit to McCarthy being the starter for the remainder of the season. “Life is day-to-day, minute-to-minute. There’s really no guarantees,” Harbaugh said. “I would never say that anything is permanent in football or life. That’s the plan going forward.”
