title: 49ers vs. Falcons odds: The most difficult game on the schedule yet
summary: The San Francisco 49ers are 6-0 heading into Week 6. For the first time in a few weeks, they “lost” against the spread on Monday. The Niners are still 5-2 against the spread, with the NFL’s second-highest margin of victory at 11.2. They’re also tied for a league-high average margin of victory. So, when media […]
full_text: (Photo by Logan Bowles/Getty Images) | Getty Images The San Francisco 49ers are 6-0 heading into Week 6. For the first time in a few weeks, they “lost” against the spread on Monday. The Niners are still 5-2 against the spread, with the NFL’s second-highest margin of victory at 11.2. They’re also tied for a league-high average margin of victory. So, when media members ask this: Are we crowning the #49ers early? — JosinaAnderson (@JosinaAnderson) October 20, 2026 I would say the answer is no. Faithful, take 49ers game day wherever you go! Stay connected to the action and share every reaction with fellow 49ers fans on the SB Nation app. Join the live game-day chat Browse with fewer ads Seamlessly jump between communities Enjoy faster commenting and posting Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android . The matchup against the Atlanta Falcons always looked like a scheduled loss, if there ever was one. The 49ers are 3-point road favorites, with the total on the game sitting at 49.5 on FanDuel Sportsbook . A high total and a low spread hint at a coin-flip game. We’ll see if Mike Evans plays. On the outside, it makes more sense to give Evans two weeks off so the Achilles soreness goes away and allows Evans to complete a game. But Kyle Shanahan seems to be putting the ball in Evans’s court. If the veteran feels healthy enough to play, he’ll play, even if the team knows they could lose him mid-game. There’s familiarity here, as Raheem Morris takes on his old team. Falcons defensive coordinator Jeff Ulbrich is one of the best in the league and worked with Shanahan in Atlanta a decade ago, not to mention as Morris’s defensive coordinator. Morris will need to find a way to limit Drake London, who has the 8th-highest target share among all NFL receivers. The Falcons throw it to London over 28% of the time. London is 11th in EPA per target. Not far behind London is his teammate Jahan Dotson, who is 14th in EPA per target. Tight end Kyle Pitts is fifth in EPA per target among tight ends. Atlanta is not short on weapons, and we haven’t even gotten to their biggest threat. Bijan Robinson is second in the NFL, averaging 5.77 yards per carry. He averages more yards after contact (4.64) than a good chunk of running backs do per carry. Robinson is a walking highlight who is heavily involved in Atlanta’s passing attack. Michael Penix is limited when it comes to being mobile, so that should work in the Niners favor. If there’s one person you’d want to attempt to slow down the Falcons, it’s the coach who drafted most of these players and watched them practice for the past few years: Raheem Morris. On the other side of the ball, no team has been better against the run than the Falcons defense. They’re first in EPA per rush and sixth in rushing success rate. Atlanta has allowed the third-fewest 10+ yard runs and is seventh in the percentage of runs they stuff. They make teams one-dimensional. This will be a Brock Purdy game. The Falcons won’t blitz Purdy nearly as often as Washington does, but they get pressure with four. That’s a big difference. Atlanta is fourth in pressure rate despite blitzing 23.7% of the time (26th in the NFL). You can throw on this defense. Atlanta is 20th and 21st in EPA per pass and passing success rate. Caleb Williams carved up the Dirty Birds for over 300 passing yards a week ago. A good chunk of those came in the first half. Luther Burden and Colston Loveland had him a day. Tyler Huntley was efficient in Week 5 at Atlanta. He threw for only 201 yards, but completed 75% of his passes and threw two touchdowns. Huntley was efficient in Week 5 at Atlanta. He only threw for 201 yards, but completed 75% of his passes and threw for two touchdowns. Rashod Bateman and Zay Flowers combined for 13 receptions for 115 yards. The week before, Tyler Shough threw the ball 48 times for 286 yards. Chris Olave had 116 yards. Of course, it’s far-fetched to imagine the Niners having a 100-yard receiver without Evans, but Shanahan has a full week to scheme up the non-Evans wideouts. A short road week with an early start on the East Coast, potentially without your leading receiver, against a team that has lost back-to-back games where they feel like they should have won. And the familiarity, paired with the weapons the Falcons have, makes this an intriguing game and a difficult schedule spot for a 6-0 team that could be feeling fat and happy a week away from the bye.

title: 49ers in review: The honeymoon phase with Eddy Pineiro is over
summary: The San Francisco 49ers have an opportunity to go into the bye week undefeated with a win over the Atlanta Falcons on Sunday. San Francisco almost lost that opportunity on Monday night with a shaky fourth quarter, allowing the lesser Washington Commanders to nearly come back from a 20-point deficit, holding on to a 23-17 […]
full_text: Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images The San Francisco 49ers have an opportunity to go into the bye week undefeated with a win over the Atlanta Falcons on Sunday. San Francisco almost lost that opportunity on Monday night with a shaky fourth quarter, allowing the lesser Washington Commanders to nearly come back from a 20-point deficit, holding on to a 23-17 win. Let’s take one last look at the win before moving our attention to Week 7 in Atlanta: The 49ers suddenly have a solid defensive line The ascension of Gracen Halton has done wonders for the 49ers’ defensive line outlook. Halton continued his good form with a one-sack, one-tackle-for-loss performance to aid what might have been the best game from the 49ers’ defensive front this season. Of the 49ers’ 25 pressures, 21 came from the defensive line, with Halton’s fellow rookie Romello Height leading the way with five. Height was one of five pass rushers to record at least half a sack on Monday night, sharing a sack with Keion White to close the game. White was right behind Height with four pressures of his own. Height and White weren’t the only two players on the ends to record a sack, as Mykel Williams joined the party in a solid performance in his second game back from an ACL tear. Williams had three pressures of his own while recording a sack of his own to end the Commanders’ opening drive of the second half. Veteran Osa Odighizuwa saw the younger members collect sacks and turned in a solid pass-rushing performance from the interior. Odighizuwa matched Height with five pressures, sacking Daniels once. Oh, and that’s not to mention the defensive line and linebackers holding Washington to 53 rushing yards on 17 attempts, with Daniels rushing for 10 yards on four attempts. With Nick Bosa’s return nearing, the defensive line can only get better. And who knows, maybe a deadline trade (Khalil Mack? DeForest Buckner?) will make the group even deeper. Same dance, different song The honeymoon phase is over. The 49ers have an issue at kicker once again. Eddy Pineiro stole the hearts of 49ers fans last season, replacing Jake Moody by missing only five kicks in 14 games, converting 28-of-29 field goals and making 34-of-38 PATs. In six games this season, Pineiro has already missed six kicks, missing at least one in each of his last four games. After missing one field goal in 2025, Pineiro has already missed three, going six-for-nine with his most recent miss coming against Seattle. But the missed PATs have been a concern, with Pineiro missing his third of the season on Monday night, and that miss almost cost San Francisco. At first it seemed like an innocuous miss, San Francisco having just scored their second touchdown in as many drives, but Pineiro’s missed PAT would keep San Francisco at 13 points. The 49ers’ lead would only extend, as late in the third, San Francisco would be up 23-3, making Pineiro’s miss a mere footnote. But then Washington came back, first cutting the deficit to 13 before the start of the fourth quarter and then cutting it to six early in the fourth. In an instant, Pineiro’s missed PAT loomed large as the Commanders offense neared the red zone late in the fourth quarter, but Malik Mustapha’s heroics prevented Washington’s chance to take the lead. We aren’t in Moody territory yet with Pineiro, but the misses have become all too common. Pineiro needs to start making kicks soon, or he will cost the 49ers a game, as was almost the case on Monday night. An alarming increase in usage One of the more impressive things about the 49ers’ 30.8 points per game over the first five games of the season was how well-managed Christian McCaffrey touches have been. In 2025, Christian McCaffrey was the 49ers’ offense. He finished with a league-high 413 touches in what was his highest-usage season since 2019. In 17 games last season, McCaffrey had 20 or more touches in 13, averaging just under 25 touches per game. Through the first five games of the season, McCaffrey already had more games with fewer than 20 touches than he did all of last season. But Monday night saw McCaffrey’s most active game of the season. And the high usage started even before the Mike Evans injury. With Deebo Samuel out, McCaffrey seemed to be his replacement, finishing the first half with 16 touches, just three shy of his season-high 19. But then Evans went down, and the high usage continued. After touching the ball on 39 percent of the 49ers’ 41 first-half plays, McCaffrey got nine more touches on 19 second-half plays, a whopping 47 percent of the 49ers’ offense. McCaffrey returned the favor in usage with a pair of touchdowns, but he finished with a season-high 25 touches to do so. Kyle Shanahan did a good job managing McCaffrey’s workload in the first five games of the season. But as the offense’s weapons dwindle from injury, Shanahan may be forced to bring McCaffrey closer to his 2025 usage.
author: Andrew Pasquini

title: Kyle Shanahan explains playcalling at end of Commanders win
summary: The San Francisco 49ers managed to pull off the 23-17 victory over the Washington Commanders on Monday night, but it ended up being closer than expected after the Niners dominated the first half and held a 23-3 lead at one point. The 49ers were cruising through three quarters, as they had scored on four of […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - OCTOBER 04: Head coach Kyle Shanahan of the San Francisco 49ers looks on before the game against the Denver Broncosat Levi's Stadium on October 04, 2026 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Lachlan Cunningham/Getty Images) | Getty Images The San Francisco 49ers managed to pull off the 23-17 victory over the Washington Commanders on Monday night, but it ended up being closer than expected after the Niners dominated the first half and held a 23-3 lead at one point. The 49ers were cruising through three quarters, as they had scored on four of their six drives, while sustaining a couple of long possessions. However, in the fourth quarter, their defense was on the field for most of the quarter as the offense went three-and-out on three straight possessions. On the first two, San Francisco called six straight pass plays. With the first set of downs, the 49ers dropped back on first down, and Brock Purdy took a sack. That forced them to throw out of long distances on second and third down, and the 49ers punted on 4th & 11. On the second possession, Purdy scrambled for six on a first-down dropback, but took a sack on 2nd & 4, setting up another third-and-long and a punt. The quick possessions didn’t hurt them, as the 49ers forced a turnover on downs and ended a different drive on a sack to end the game, but there were questions about Shanahan’s playcalling down the stretch. What was going on in the head coach’s mind? “It was a frustrating end there, just going three-and-out those last three drives on offense, having a chance to put them away,” Shanahan said. “Thinking we did a couple of times and then having those penalties kept those drives going. Yeah, you’re not always happy exactly with how it [went]. some of the stuff was frustrating. But, real proud of the guys for just the competitive stamina to keep it going all game. “First half obviously looked like we were going to run away with it, especially that opening drive in the third quarter. They made a big play. I thought we had a touchdown. I think it was number four (Frankie Luvu) tipped the ball, held us to a field goal. They got some big plays going. But just the perseverance of the defense, just putting them back out there those three drives in a row. Losing a couple of key guys. Jalen Graham having to get in there with losing [Luke] Gifford, played a lot in the base stuff. Losing [Upton] Stout there where we had Ashtyn Davis come in and play some big pivotal roles there in the fourth quarter. I was just really proud of the defense for finding a way to overcome all those penalties and us not helping them out on O in the fourth.” The offense had started the second half on a high note, going 11 plays for 65 yards on a six-minute drive and nearly scoring a touchdown before settling for a field goal to extend the lead to 23-3. “I thought we had an awesome drive to start it out,” Shanahan said of the team’s offense in the second half. “I think we were going to score. I think Brock ripped that ball, just got a tip. Then the next three drives were just frustrating. We got sacked on the first one on first-and-10, got us into second-and-20. Couldn’t overcome second-and-20. The next time up, we got to second-and-four. Probably should have called a run, but I was anticipating a run blitz and we did get that and our hot route just got caught up. We couldn’t get rid of it, so we took another sack. Then the third time was just four minute. We were trying to eat up their timeouts. So, it’s frustrating we couldn’t get a first down after that opening drive.” How big was the loss of Mike Evans with the offense’s struggles in the second half? “It’s definitely a big deal when you lose a player like Mike, but our first drive [in the second half] I thought was one of our better drives of the game,” Shanahan added. “We ran the ball real well, we just got a ball tipped on third down that would have been a score and we got a field goal. The next two drives really, we got a sack on first down, got us into second-and-20. We went three-and-out both times and then the fourth time was a four-minute drill. We were trying to run the clock out. “So just the way it ended up being, Mike wouldn’t have had a chance to have much of an effect there in the second half. Now, if we would’ve gotten some first downs and stuff and got driving, then you would’ve felt the lack of presence of him. But, we didn’t get enough first downs to really show where we would miss him.” Following the game, Brock Purdy took responsibility for the sacks, while acknowledging he could’ve been better in the second half. “Obviously offensively and for myself, in the second half, it’s tough just to do what we did, three-and-outs,” Purdy said. “I think there’s some plays where I could have been better for sure in getting the ball out and whatnot instead of taking some sacks. But, for our defense to do what they did, obviously I know it sounds cheesy, but I mean it’s true, it’s a team win. It takes a whole team collectively for four quarters. And so, for our defense to do what they did at the end, that was really impressive.” “I think we were ready for it with our plan,” the quarterback added. “First half, obviously didn’t feel like they did it as much. Second half, I just thought they did a good job with just being a little disruptive and taking checkdowns away, sort of making me hold onto the ball. So that’s still on me on some certain plays to get the ball out. But overall, really good scheme. I respect the heck out of them.” Despite some of the offensive struggles to end the game, San Francisco’s defense kept the Commanders at bay. As a result, the 49ers are 6-0, and they’ll get a chance to clean things up with Mike Evans potentially out against the Falcons next weekend.
author: Rohan Chakravarthi

title: Week 7 NFL Power Rankings: Does close scare drop 49ers this week?
summary: The San Francisco 49ers have been sitting atop the NFL’s power rankings for a few weeks now, as they remain just one of three unbeaten teams in the league. That remained true after Week 6, as the 49ers escaped by the Washington Commanders 23-17 in a game that went down to the final plays as […]
full_text: San Francisco 49ers running back Christian McCaffrey (23) rushes for a touchdown during the first half of a NFL football game against the Washington Commanders in Santa Clara, Calif., Monday, Oct. 19, 2026. (Photo by Stephen Lam/San Francisco Chronicle via Getty Images) The San Francisco 49ers have been sitting atop the NFL’s power rankings for a few weeks now, as they remain just one of three unbeaten teams in the league. That remained true after Week 6, as the 49ers escaped by the Washington Commanders 23-17 in a game that went down to the final plays as the defense made a stand. San Francisco really struggled to generate offense without Mike Evans, while Jayden Daniels threw for 300 yards against the 49ers defense, leading to a closer game. Nonetheless, San Francisco is 6-0, becoming the lone team in the NFL to win six games thus far. Given how close the game was and how other teams fared this weekend, did the 49ers get docked in the power rankings this week? Let’s look at several Week 7 power rankings to see the consensus. ESPN: No. 1 The 49ers remained the top team here as they remain one of the teams without many actual flaws with their play. When highlighting the team’s biggest issue on offense so far, the answer was clear: receiver injuries. “The Niners haven’t had many problems in terms of production, but they have had a significant amount of attrition at wideout,” ESPN’s Nick Wagoner wrote. Ricky Pearsall (knee), De’Zhaun Stribling (ankle), Christian Kirk (calf) and Demarcus Robinson (ankle) were supposed to be four of the team’s top five receivers and all landed on IR before Week 3. “That doesn’t account for Deebo Samuel Sr.’s multiweek hamstring injury or the various bumps and bruises Mike Evans played through before departing Monday night’s game with Achilles tendinitis. The good news? Most of them are expected back this season, but the 49ers have had to scramble in the meantime.” Behind the 49ers were the Kansas City Chiefs, who improved to 5-0 off a dominant win over the Los Angeles Chargers. Rounding out the top five were the Buffalo Bills, Minnesota Vikings, and the Jacksonville Jaguars. NFL.com: No. 1 NFL.com’s Nick Shook did note that there could be some question to San Francisco’s standing atop the rankings after the win, but kept them at No. 1 still after six weeks over the Chiefs. “San Francisco flirted with an epic collapse, but the same battered defensive line came through again in the final moments, sacking Jayden Daniels to bury Washington’s comeback bid,” Shook said. “The fashion in which this game ended might cause some to question the 49ers’ standing atop the Power Rankings; we often fail to remember, however, that there are professional football players on both sides (and the Commanders feature a dynamic quarterback in Daniels). “Kyle Shanahan’s propensity for letting things get a little too close for comfort reared its unwelcome head again, but San Francisco finished the job like a proven winner usually does. Let’s not allow the anxiety-inducing fourth quarter to overshadow how dominant the Niners were earlier in the game. They’re undefeated and keeping the throne.” Behind the 49ers were the Chiefs, Bills, Vikings, and Jaguars. Complete unity here with ESPN’s list with the exact same top five. CBS Sports: No. 1 It was simple here for CBS’s Pete Prisco, as the 49ers found a way to win again. “They made it interesting against the Commanders, but they still found a way,” Prisco wrote. “Now they face a long road trip to play the Falcons on a short week.” There was a slightly different top five here, as the Chiefs, Vikings, Bills, and Denver Broncos followed. The Broncos offense has been a big story, but they’re 4-2 after facing one of the tougher schedules in the NFL to start the season. FOX Sports: No. 1 The Niners remained at No. 1 here as well, with FOX Sports’s Ralph Vacciano lauding the team’s depth following the injuries, while pointing out they’re clearly the best team in the NFL so far. “The 49ers are held together at times by Band-Aids and gauze tape, but there’s no question they’re the best team in football a third of the way through the season,” Vacciano wrote. “They need a rest, especially after WR Mike Evans reinjured his Achilles on Monday night, joining WR Deebo Samuel, WR Christian Kirk, edge rusher Nick Bosa and more on the sideline. “But they’re so deep and so good, they can sleepwalk through wins — like they seemed to do at times in the second half Monday night when they nearly blew their game against the Commanders. Now they just have to get through Atlanta to hit their bye week undefeated and see if they can get some of their walking wounded back after that. The Niners will be favored again this week on the road against the Atlanta Falcons, giving them a chance to go 7-0 entering their bye week, where they can get healthier and acquire reinforcements through the trade market. So far, so good here for San Francisco.

title: Could the Titans trade CB Alontae Taylor?
summary: The Tennessee Titans gave cornerback Alontae Taylor a massive 3-year, $58-millon deal in free agency. He was supposed to be a cornerstone in the defensive resurgence under new head coach Robert Saleh. That hasn’t been the way things have played out to this point. Taylor has struggled to the point that he was a healthy […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - AUGUST 13: Alontae Taylor #24 of the Tennessee Titans looks on during warm ups prior to the start of the game against the San Francisco 49ers at Levi's Stadium on August 13, 2026 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Thearon W. Henderson/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Tennessee Titans gave cornerback Alontae Taylor a massive 3-year, $58-millon deal in free agency. He was supposed to be a cornerstone in the defensive resurgence under new head coach Robert Saleh. That hasn’t been the way things have played out to this point. Taylor has struggled to the point that he was a healthy scratch in the Titans’ Week 6 win over the Indianapolis Colts. A benching of a player of Taylor’s magnitude is naturally going to start trade rumors. Some rando tweeted out on Sunday that the Titans are considering trading Taylor. I didn’t give that much credence, but this morning at ESPN, Jeremy Fowler mentioned Taylor as a name to watch at the NFL trade deadline . The biggest hurdle, as Fowler mentions, is the money Taylor is owed over the next couple of years. The Titans would likely have to eat some of the $20.5 million that is guaranteed next season. If the Titans can get a day two pick for Taylor, they should absolutely do it. Otherwise, it would be best for Saleh and the team to work through whatever issues Taylor has had to this point so this defense can continue to get better.

title: Can Robert Saleh’s defense continue leading Titans to victory?
summary: The Tennessee Titans finally won a football game in Week 6, defeating the Indianapolis Colts 26-20. Robert Saleh’s defense undeniably powered the Nashville-based club to victory. The question goes begging, can Saleh’s defense continue carrying the Titans? Saleh’s defense forced three turnovers through an Amani Hooker interception, a Jeffery Simmons strip, and a Cor’Dale Flott […]
full_text: BALTIMORE, MARYLAND - OCTOBER 04: Head coach Robert Saleh of the Tennessee Titans looks on against the Baltimore Ravens at M&T Bank Stadium on October 04, 2026 in Baltimore, Maryland. (Photo by Patrick Smith/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Tennessee Titans finally won a football game in Week 6 , defeating the Indianapolis Colts 26-20. Robert Saleh’s defense undeniably powered the Nashville-based club to victory. The question goes begging, can Saleh’s defense continue carrying the Titans? Saleh’s defense forced three turnovers through an Amani Hooker interception, a Jeffery Simmons strip, and a Cor’Dale Flott interception. Flott’s INT was the perfect example of Saleh’s scheme beginning to pay dividends. The cover-man passed off a Colts receiver smoothly and stepped in front of an ill-advised Jones throw. The Titans also forced a fourth turnover via special teams. James Williams Sr. and Julius Chestnut combined to block a fourth-quarter punt. It was scooped up by Femi Oladejo and returned for a 14-yard touchdown that completed the comeback, making it 20 unanswered points in a then 20-13 Titans lead. They never trailed again. Simmons sacked Jones twice. So did Jermaine Johnson II. Tony Adams and Jacob Martin contributed one sack apiece to round out the Titans’ six sacks. Saleh’s defense covered for another mediocre offensive performance. Quarterback Cam Ward was 11-of-22 for 102 yards, one touchdown, and one interception. The Titans began three second-half offensive possessions from Colts territory. The offense only scored one touchdown. Brian Daboll’s unit was outgained 399-186. Despite being 1-5, the Titans are now allowing the 13th-fewest points per game. They are tied for ninth in sacks despite lacking elite defensive line talent outside of Jeffery Simmons. You’re really beginning to see the Saleh defense come together. Saleh’s defense will receive another opportunity to spearhead a victory versus a rather average Cleveland Browns offense in Week 7. The Browns are playing excellent on defense, so we probably shouldn’t expect the Titans offense to get on track against this opponent. No, it’ll take another big-time showing from Saleh’s unit to execute an upset.

He was placed on injured reserve on Oct. 5, after suffering a fracture and dislocation of the ankle. Such an injury normally requires surgery, and the Washington Post’s […]
full_text: Commanders receiver and return man Jaylin Lane had surgery to repair a season-ending ankle injury that he suffered during a Week 4 loss to the Indianapolis Colts. He was placed on injured reserve on Oct. 5, after suffering a fracture and dislocation of the ankle. Such an injury normally requires surgery, and the Washington Post ’s Tashan Reed reported on Wednesday that it has now taken place. #Commanders WR Jaylin Lane had surgery to repair his fractured and dislocated ankle on Oct. 9, per source. The procedure was successful and he's expected to be cleared for football activities just before OTAs. — Tashan Reed (@tashanreed) October 21, 2026 Reed also reports that Lane should be ready to return before the Commanders begin OTAs next spring. The injury is a significant one and typically requires an extensive rehab and acclimation to football activities. Lane is a second-year pro who is already considered among the NFL’s top returners, with two punts returned for a touchdown during his rookie season in 2024. He was also improving as a receiver, so this injury was a real setback to that progress. The Commanders have been using Luke McCaffrey and, at times, Rachaad White or Antonio Williams to help with the return duties.

title: How Washington Commanders can make up for loss of Terry McLaurin
summary: Dan Quinn said that the Commanders have faced “a season’s worth of adversity” in their first six games. The beleaguered head coach is correct.   They lost Laremy Tunsil in training camp. Jayden Daniels suffered an elbow dislocation in Week 2 and missed some time. They were down to seventh-round rookie quarterback Athan Kaliakmanis against the […]
full_text: Dan Quinn said that the Commanders have faced “ a season’s worth of adversity ” in their first six games. The beleaguered head coach is correct. They lost Laremy Tunsil in training camp. Jayden Daniels suffered an elbow dislocation in Week 2 and missed some time. They were down to seventh-round rookie quarterback Athan Kaliakmanis against the Colts. There was also the Week 5 debacle against the New York Giants that turned Quinn’s seat into a five-alarm fire. And the sting of being a failed two-point conversion away from sending Philly to overtime and two fateful failed fourth downs from beating the 49ers. Then came the latest knuckle sandwich. Terry McLaurin’s knee was placed in an air cast and he was carted off the field against San Francisco after suffering a season-ending torn patellar tendon . I mean, come on. “He brings a lot on and off the field,” Quinn said. “I felt him in so many unique ways this season from training camp to in-season. We do have a deep crew at that position and we’ll lean on several guys to fill the unique role that Terry does.” There’s no replacing a player like McLaurin. There are special players in this league and he is one. The Commanders must triage, evaluate and then decide how to keep the passing game going strong without McLaurin in the pattern. Here’s what they’ll need to make that happen: Stefon Diggs to play like a true No. 1 Stefon Diggs was an elite, frontline receiver is his younger days and remains an effective and impactful presence in the passing game. His career numbers illustrate that with 1,000-yard seasons in each year since 2018 , save two impacted by injury. He understands coverage as well as anyone and always finds ways to get open. Diggs is a rabid competitor and solid leader of the position group and can carry that mantle he was previously sharing with McLaurin. Game days will be key, especially as coverage starts to devote significant effort to stopping him. He should still be able to operate in those settings as he has so many times before. His target share will surely go up. While he’s not as dynamic as he once and he has had some uncharacteristic drops early on, Diggs is the type to step up and assume a major role in this Commanders offense. Reserves must form a McLaurin Voltron McLaurin does so many things well that his deep skill set can’t be replicated by one individual. McLaurin has deep speed. He’s good creating separation. And, as Quinn put it, his “superpower” is making contested catches. The Commanders have a little bit of that in different options, which is why they’ll have to form a McLaurin Voltron. For those not alive in the 1980s, you’ll have to Google that reference. They can do so with Dyami Brown and Luke McCaffrey stretching the field. Rookie Antonio Williams is excellent creating separation. And Treylon Burks has the contested catch ability you’re looking for. Washington must deploy them correctly and scheme towards their strengths. If those guys can do that, the Commanders should be fine. If Burks is healthy and available, it’s fair to assume he’ll start and play a ton. Williams can work from anywhere but becomes a weapon inside and should see more targets as well. Chig Okonkwo’s involvement goes (way) up Chig Okonkwo took some time to get revved up in the Commanders offense. An early hamstring set him back and kept him out of Weeks 2-3 . He wasn’t super involved in Week 4 but has been far better since then, with 11 catches for 129 yards on 13 targets over the last two weeks. That’s efficient and explosive production that simply must continue now, to keep some attention off Diggs and be a weapon in the middle of the field. Considering John Bates’ presence as a stout blocker and in-line player allows Okonkwo to work from almost anywhere, giving offensive coordinator David Blough to treat him as a receiver at times. Okonkwo has excellent potential. Now’s the time to realize it. No trades!!!! We’re already seen fans discuss the prospect of adding Brian Thomas Jr. or another talent before the trade deadline to make up for McLaurin’s loss. Absolutely not. This team is not in position to be dealing Day 2 or even higher Day 3 pick right now. They need as many assets as possible to fortify their foundation. As a matter of fact, the Commanders could be sellers if the losing continues after the bye. There’s enough talent on the roster and practice squad to keep going. And, just so we’re on the record here, it’s hard pass on Tyreek Hill (no matter where’s he’s at in his rehab) and Brandon Aiyuk. This team doesn’t need that. Promote Van Jefferson or Jaden Bradley off the practice squad and work with what you’ve got. How can the Commanders keep the passing game going with Terry McLaurin now lost for the season? Let us know in the article comments below .

Enjoy! Commanders links Articles NFL.com Commanders WR Terry McLaurin out for rest of season with torn patellar tendon [T]ests on Tuesday showed that he suffered a torn patellar tendon that will sideline him for the remainder of the 2026 season, Quinn told reporters. McLaurin will need to undergo surgery that will shelve him for the rest of his eighth NFL year. Having already missed one game this season due to a hamstring injury, the 31-year-old has now been struck the most severe injury of his career. He missed seven games in 2025, but that was due to a host of injuries: quad, core muscle and groin issues. Now, Diggs will presumably be quarterback Jayden Daniels’ top target with Dyami Brown, rookie Antonio Williams and Treylon Burks being forced into larger roles. McLaurin, a five-time 1,000-yard receiver, finished the season with 15 receptions for 230 yards and one touchdown. To read more of this article, CLICK HERE Commanders Roundtable How Commanders can adjust to loss of Terry McLaurin It’s next man up. Tight end Chig Okonkwo is starting to develop a solid connection with quarterback Jayden Daniels . Against the 49ers, Okonkwo recorded seven receptions for 69 yards, both of which were team highs. Last week against the New York Giants, he caught four passes for 60 yards, just two yards shy of McLaurin’s team-high total. After a rough start to the season, the former Tennessee Titan is beginning to find his groove and could become an even bigger part of Washington’s passing attack. Another player Daniels needs to continue feeding is wide receiver Stefon Diggs. He leads the team in receptions with 24 and ranks second in receiving yards with 214. In three of the five games Diggs has played, he has recorded the second-most receiving yards on the team. With McLaurin potentially sidelined for an extended period, Diggs could become Washington’s top option at wide receiver. The Commanders also have an under-the-radar weapon in their arsenal is wide receiver Antonio Williams. He ranks second on the team in receptions with 18 and third in receiving yards with 205. Time for Antonio Williams to be treated like 1A in the passing game. That needs to be a thing after the bye. For the short term and long term payoff. https://t.co/BwLA2vFcvs — Marshall (@MarshW_7) October 20, 2026 Williams made an immediate impact in Week 1 against the Philadelphia Eagles, leading the team with 64 receiving yards on just four catches. He also had an 87-yard touchdown against the Indianapolis Colts that was nullified because of an illegal shift penalty. Against San Francisco, Williams finished third on the team in receiving with 50 yards. To read more of this article, CLICK HERE NFL.com Bad news, good news for Commanders It has not been a good start to the season for Washington. The Commanders have managed only one win in six games — although it did come against the defending Super Bowl champions — and just fell short in a blowout-turned-nailbiter to the 49ers to fall to 1-4-1. Luckily, that’s not a death sentence in this year’s NFC East, especially if the defense can maintain the form it found in the second half after allowing the most points in the league over the first five games. No one in the division has won a game since Week 4, marking the first time in league history every team in a division has played consecutive weeks without a victory , per NFL Research. It’s a feat made more (un)impressive by the fact that the Commanders and Giants went head-to-head in Week 5, a game that ended in a tie after disastrous overtime mistakes by both squads. So, the Commanders are simultaneously at the bottom of the NFC East and in OK shape. They have the same number of losses as the Cowboys (2-4) and Eagles (2-4) and are by no means an impossible distance behind the first-place Giants (3-2-1). Only blind optimists would bank on Washington rebounding for a wild-card spot at this point, but there’s a path to the playoffs through the division. Moore III/Getty Images) | Getty Images What an unpredictable week in college football. #1 Georgia lost to an unranked Auburn team, and #2 Notre Dame lost late to #8 BYU. #3 Miami needed overtime to beat in-state rival Florida State. #4 Ohio State won a competitive matchup over #5 Indiana, handing them their first loss at home under head coach Curt Cignetti. #6 Alabama lost by a wide margin in Knoxville to #14 Tennessee, and #7 Texas gave up a lead and lost to unranked Florida. Week 8 will see one of those unbeaten teams in the Big 12, #10 Utah, facing off against #14 Houston. A new entrant into the top 10, #9 UCLA will host Michigan State. Both #13 Alabama and #17 Texas will try to avoid three losses in a row. The Crimson Tide will play Texas A&M while the Longhorns play #7 Ole Miss. Let me know what you think about these prospects and feel free to post players that stood out to you. Ashton Daniels | QB | Senior | Florida State As a developmental quarterback prospect, Ashton Daniels could be a fit in Washington. He’s got the size for the position at 6’2”, 225 pounds. He’s not the most creative runner at the position, but he can run away from, and at that size, even over defenders. As a passer, Daniels has shown the ability to make NFL-level throws between defenders and into tight windows. He also can put touch on his passes and allow receivers to run underneath them. He can get himself into trouble when he tries to force throws thinking he can beat defenders. Daniels has thrown 8 interceptions this season. If the Commanders think they can help him improve his decision making, he might be worth investing in. In an overtime loss to Miami, Daniels went 15 of 28 for 298 yards, four touchdowns, and one interception on the last play of the game which any Florida State fan will argue was a catch. He also added 31 yards and a touchdown on the ground. As a bonus for those who want a big receiver, check out Daniels’ teammate, the 6’6”, 230 pound wide receiver Duce Robinson, in the clip below. What Bishop is at 5’10”, 215 pounds is a rugged back that will deliver consistent punishment to a defense, wearing them down as the game progresses. His superpower is his ability to run through tackles and gain tough yardage, a role the Commanders need filled desperately. As a former walk-on, it is easy to root for Bishop’s success at the next level. Bishop rushed 32 times for 159 yards and two touchdows in the Volunteers’ victory over Alabama. title: 2027 NFL mock draft: Yates' early predictions for top 10 picks, QB landing spots
summary: We're two months into the college football season, and Field Yates is projecting which prospects could go in the top 10 picks of the 2027 NFL draft -- including three QBs.
full_text:
The 2027 NFL draft is six months away, but it's never too early to project what's going to happen! Plus, we have six weeks of NFL play and two months of college football games  to fuel our educated guesses for prospect landing spots.

 But ... since there's plenty of football still ahead, I'm only going through the top 10 picks, with the order based on the inverse of the standings through Week 6  of the NFL season. There's plenty of intrigue in these limited selections, including two picks for the Jets that they acquired via trades. And there will be plenty of quarterbacks coming off the board early.

 As we say before every mock draft, it's important to remember that some prospects could decide to head back to school and others could surprisingly declare early. And every NFL team's needs will change amid injuries, breakouts, trades, free agency moves and coaching changes before the draft starts April 29.

 Here are my early projections for the top 10 picks in 2027, starting with the reeling Chargers.

 

 

 1. Los Angeles Chargers (0-6) 
 Jeremiah Smith , WR, Ohio State 

 A pathetic season so far for the Chargers can be traced to several factors, one of which is that the team has no difference-makers among its pass catchers. The Chargers don't have a single receiver in the top 50 for receiving yards per game, and they're 29th in yards after the catch.

 Smith is the most decorated wideout in Ohio State's rich history, and he could be the Big Ten's all-time leader in receiving yards and receiving TDs as soon as Halloween against USC . He has 984 yards and 12 touchdowns this season alone. His combination of size (6-foot-4, 222 pounds), speed and force should immediately translate to the NFL. It has been 30 years since a wide receiver was taken No. 1 (Keyshawn Johnson in 1996). That is very much in play in 2027.

 
 

 

 2. Miami Dolphins (0-5) 
 Drew Mestemaker , QB, Oklahoma State 

 Miami has needs everywhere, but its modest investment in Malik Willis (whose three-year, $67.5 million contract has no guaranteed money beyond 2027) puts quarterback in play. The 20-year-old Mestemaker oozes upside, as the 6-3 215-pounder is a legitimate dual-threat player with exceptional creativity inside and outside of the pocket. I'm giving him the early lead as the top QB in the class, which aligns with Mel Kiper Jr.'s Big Board and Jordan Reid's QB rankings .

 Despite not starting at quarterback in high school, Mestemaker has shown enough in just two college seasons -- one at North Texas -- to contend for the No. 1 pick. He is a fearless playmaker who can impact nearly every blade of grass on the field with his mobility and off-platform throwing skills.

 
 

 3. Tennessee Titans (1-5) 
 Leonard Moore , CB, Notre Dame 

 In this scenario, the Titans have to consider a question on defensive philosophy: Do you build from the front to the back, or just take a surefire cornerback?

 Ultimately, I landed on Moore over someone like Texas'  Colin Simmons  at this early point of the process, as he is off to another exceptional start with just six receptions allowed on 153 coverage snaps. Moore has size (6-2, 197 pounds), a fierce mentality to covet tough matchups, excellent ball skills and solid overall anticipation. He is a true shutdown cornerback, which warrants a selection this high. But the Titans also need young edge rushers, so Simmons was nearly my pick here.

 
 

 4. Tampa Bay Buccaneers (1-5) 
 Colin Simmons , Edge, Texas 

 Tampa Bay is looking for more impact pass rushers -- a way too familiar spot for the team. The Bucs selected Rueben Bain Jr . in April and are getting strong play from 2025 draftee David Walker , but 11 total sacks through six games just won't cut it.

 Simmons is a hyper-charged playmaker who is a massive mismatch for offensive tackles because of his acceleration and overall twitchiness. Though he is listed at just 246 pounds, somewhat light for an NFL edge rusher, his production is off the charts. He's up to 31.5 sacks and eight forced fumbles since the start of the 2024 season.

 
 

 5. Washington Commanders (1-5) 
 Dylan Stewart , Edge, South Carolina 

 The Commanders spent big in free agency to land edge rusher Odafe Oweh , but they are still struggling to impact opposing quarterbacks. So far in 2026, they're 25th in sacks per dropback (4.5%) and 20th in pass rush win rate (48.2%).

 The best version of Stewart has a case for the top pass rusher in the class, as he's incredibly explosive, powerful, long and hell on wheels to try to block. But teams will have some questions about a recent one-game suspension for punching an Alabama player in the helmet and arguing with coaches on the sideline.

 Stewart is immensely talented, but he must harness that skill and find a way for those physical traits to translate into straight production. He has one sack this season and 12 over the past three years.

 

 
 

 6. Philadelphia Eagles (2-4) 
 Charlie Becker , WR, Indiana 

 This Eagles season has not completely gone by the wayside because of the overall NFC East struggles, but it's clear this team has a lot of roster work to do in the offseason. After filling out their slot position with rookie first-round pick Makai Lemon , adding another dynamic perimeter playmaker opposite  DeVonta Smith would be a big boost for the offense.

 Becker has flourished into a megastar in his first season as a full-time starter, ranking 11th nationally in receiving yards per game (99.1). He's 6-4 and 208 pounds with exceptional speed, terrific hands and a unique ability to beat man coverage on the outside.

 
 

 7. New York Jets ( via 2-4 DAL ) 
 CJ Carr , QB, Notre Dame 

 The early returns suggest the Jets went 3-for-3 with their trio of first-rounders in 2026 (edge rusher  David Bailey , tight end  Kenyon Sadiq and receiver  Omar Cooper Jr .), allowing those players to take a massive step forward in 2027. Carr would be their attempt to solve the biggest long-term problem, which is finding a solution under center -- 36-year-old  Geno Smith is currently on a one-year deal .

 In two seasons at Notre Dame, Carr has shown a strong ability to handle pre-snap duties and process quickly, while also being a mechanically sound and talented thrower. He's at his best operating from the pocket, but he's dangerous enough with his legs to keep a defense honest (six rushing touchdowns since the start of last season).

 
 

 8. Houston Texans (2-4) 
 Trevor Goosby , OT, Texas 

 It's important to say that I am bullish on the Texans picking much later than this, as they're coming off back-to-back wins against AFC South opponents. But you are what your record says you are, and this is how it presently shakes out.

 Houston's offensive line has been a multiyear project to get right, which included selecting LT Aireontae Ersery and LG Keylan Rutledge early in the past two drafts. Goosby and LSU's  Jordan Seaton  are among the top offensive tackles in this class. But I'm giving Goosby a narrow edge in this scenario for his standout run blocking and overall power.

 
 

 9. Arizona Cardinals (2-4) 
 Trinidad Chambliss , QB, Ole Miss 

 The Cardinals made enough of an investment in Carson Beck this April (65th overall) to suggest he could be the long-term starter, but I'm not sold on that being the case. Enter the dynamic Chambliss, who makes up for below-average size (6-foot, 205 pounds) with playmaking, clutch production, experience and craftiness.

 No quarterback in this class has played better in big games than Chambliss, who averaged 307 passing yards and accounted for six touchdowns in three College Football Playoff games last season. He has led Ole Miss to three wins over AP Top 25 teams in 2026.

title: Ravens' Lamar Jackson returns to practice but status remains unclear vs. Bengals
summary: After practice, Jackson was favoring his injured left ankle, walking into the team facility with a noticeable limp.
full_text:
OWINGS MILLS, Md. -- Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson returned to practice Wednesday, but it remains uncertain whether the two-time NFL Most Valuable Player will play in Sunday's game against the Cincinnati Bengals . 
 
 After practice, Jackson was favoring his injured left ankle, walking into the team facility with a noticeable limp. He also walked with a limp inside the locker room. 
 
 Jackson wasn't present during the media availability portion of practice, but he later came out onto the practice field. This marked the first time that Jackson has had any on-field work since spraining his ankle 17 days ago. 
 
 Ravens coach Jesse Minter described Jackson as a limited participant, saying he "was able to get in a little bit of work and be involved in preparation." Minter also indicated Jackson participated in some team drills. 
 
 
 "There's nobody that wants to be out there more than Lamar," Minter said. "Lamar wants to play. But at the same time, you got to be healthy enough to play." 
 
 Jackson sprained his left ankle late in the first half of a 24-18 win over the Tennessee Titans on Oct. 4. He had missed the past two games and the past six practices before returning Wednesday. 
 
 Tyler Huntley has filled in for Jackson, leading the Ravens to a comeback win at the Atlanta Falcons before struggling Sunday in a loss at the Cleveland Browns . 
 
 In 14 quarters with Jackson this season, the Ravens have scored 116 points and 14 offensive touchdowns. In 10 quarters without him, Baltimore has totaled 40 points and four touchdowns. 
 
 "He is working to get back," Ravens wide receiver Zay Flowers said. "He is working every day, doing what he needs to do to get back on the field. That's all you can do when you're injured, just do everything you can to get back on the field."  
 
 If Jackson can play Sunday, it would be a timely return. The Ravens (4-2) and the Bengals (3-2) are considered the top two teams in the AFC North. 
 
 Since Jackson became the starter midway through the 2018 season, the Ravens are 11-2 against the Bengals with Jackson, who has thrown 24 touchdowns and six interceptions against Cincinnati. Without Jackson over that span, Baltimore is 0-3, including the playoffs, against the Bengals, losing by an average margin of 12 points. 
 
 "I know this, that when it's ready for him to be able to play and we feel like that's the best thing to do, that's what we'll do," Minter said.

title: Why the Bills have been historically good, and bad, through six weeks
summary: As Buffalo heads into its Week 7 bye, quarterback Josh Allen and the offense have thrived, while the defense has not.
full_text:
ORCHARD PARK, N.Y. -- The  Buffalo Bills ' path forward is pretty simple: Keep scoring.

 Having completed a little more than a third of their games, the Bills head into their bye week with a 5-1 record, primarily because they're scoring a league-leading 32.8 points per game. Let's put that in perspective. Only 14 teams in NFL history have scored at that pace for a full season. Those teams won an average of 13 games per year, with nine making it to a conference championship game and six earning their way into a Super Bowl.

 These are "Greatest Show On Turf" numbers. These are Peyton Manning, Tom Brady, Drew Brees and Aaron Rodgers in their best season numbers. Score like this and your worst-case scenario is 10 wins and a playoff berth, no matter how bad your defense and special teams are.

 

 That the Bills are producing to this eye-popping degree in spite of No. 1 receiver DJ Moore essentially missing four games is hard to fathom. That the Bills have produced to this degree despite facing the NFL's fifth-toughest schedule according to ESPN's Football Power Index , and that the Bills' remaining schedule dips to 24th in difficulty by the same metric, is even harder to ignore.

 Still, this Bills team is hardly perfect. The defense ranks 28th in points allowed and 31st in yards and first downs allowed. Quarterback  Josh Allen and  James Cook III  have fumbled four times apiece (with Cook losing two and Allen losing one), to go along with Allen's four interceptions.

 This adds up to a Bills team that's barely skating by with its wins; out of the 63 teams that have started 5-1 in the past two decades, the 2026 Bills rank bottom 10 in point differential. Despite their hot starts, the other teams in that bottom 10 combined to go 3-8 in the postseason with zero conference championship appearances between them.

 It's just as tough to ignore the bad as it is the good. So with coach Joe Brady's squad on break for the week, let's take some time to evaluate where the Bills are, what they're good at, what they need to be better at and just how achievable this team's Super Bowl aspirations are.

 What's working 

 Put simply, the Bills have Allen -- the current MVP favorite (+200). He has led four game-winning drives and three fourth-quarter comebacks in six games. He's the NFL's leader in rushing touchdowns (eight) while ranking top five in QBR (76.2). Cook leads the NFL in carries of 10 yards or more in large part because Allen's dual-threat reputation means opponents are only stacking the box with eight or more defenders for a quarter of Cook's carries.

 But Allen has been a supernova for years. What's different this year?

 Essentially, the Bills are driving until it's automatic. More than 40% of Bills drives are reaching the red zone, the first time any Bills team can say that since Brian Daboll's final year as offensive coordinator in 2021. Also, 21% of Bills drives include a play from inside their opponent's 5-yard line, the best mark of Allen's career. And since Allen is a red zone battering ram, all but one of those drives has ended in a touchdown.

 Combine that with an offensive line and running game that's top three in the league in yards gained before contact, a defense that's top five in total quarterback pressures and special teams units that rank No. 1 in field goal accuracy and net yards per punt, and it's easy to see why the Bills are winning.

 "There's going to be games where we might try to find a way to win 10-7," Brady told reporters Monday. "There's going to be games like [Sunday versus the  Las Vegas Raiders ] where we've got to find a way to win in the 30s, but as long as we find a way and we don't start pointing fingers at each other, I'm not concerned about the sustaining or anything like that."

 

 What's not working? 

 The Bills have surrendered the league's most passing yards and second-most passing touchdowns through six weeks. The defense is allowing conversions on 45% of third downs, fifth worst in the NFL, and has been even worse on second downs when opponents are gaining nearly 6 yards per play and completing more than 70% of their passes. Greg Rousseau  has six of the team's sacks 11 sacks, and he hasn't brought down a quarterback since Week 3.

 What's most alarming is how much more severe these issues present themselves in the fourth quarter. The Bills are allowing 1.5 touchdowns per fourth quarter this year. That's the worst rate for any defense in any season dating back to at least 1977.

 "Teams get their back against the wall, they're going to be aggressive," defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard says. "We have to close it out, right? We have a number of situations where you either get them to third down, or again, [when] you make teams one dimensional, you have to take advantage of it, right? You have to take advantage of it. We're not necessarily doing that."

 The Bills have also committed 58 accepted penalties, fourth most in the NFL, and been assessed 439 penalty yards, fifth most in the NFL. That includes 21 defensive penalties that have resulted in first downs and six offensive penalties that contributed to a drive stalling. So 4.5 times per game, the Bills commit a penalty that either ends a drive or extends an opponent's drive.

 "We're not a very good defense at overcoming adversity in the form of penalties right now," Leonhard said. "So that's a really bad combination when you're struggling to stop the bleeding."

 Are the Bills' Super Bowl hopes valid? 

 When asked if he thinks this version of the Bills as they're playing now can make it to the Super Bowl, Brady offered a nonanswer that's still fairly telling.

 "I hope," Brady said. "I told the guys this: Our best football has to be ahead of us, whatever that means. You never want to peak early in the season. If you're playing your best football in September, there's a problem. And so how do we continue to improve?

 

 "How do we continue to learn, coaches and players, how the game's being played, how teams are playing us? How do we learn how we're playing with one another with the newness and moving parts? And if we're playing our best football right now, it's not going to look good as the season goes. And so I hope better is ahead, and that's what we're chasing."

 Brady says he hasn't had discussions with general manager Brandon Beane about how the team will handle the Nov. 10 trade deadline. With injury and depth concerns at receiver and across the defense, it's plausible these Bills could be looking to add players in the coming weeks.

 Ask Brady about the Bills' successes and failures and 99 times out of 100 he'll tell you he doesn't get caught up in high highs or low lows. He's said several times the Bills' record doesn't dictate how he prepares, how he views the team or the level of belief he has in individual players and assistants.

 But on the matters of the trade deadline, the overall roster health and the last-minute needs that could better help the team achieve its goals, Brady broke type and deferred to wins and losses.

 "I'm always going to trust Brandon with any decisions that he has with the roster," Brady said. "He's put together a roster right now that's 5-1. He's always going to be looking to find ways to improve. That's in him. But he's helped put us in the position that we're in right now."

title: Proposing NFL trade deadline offers: Moves for Saquon Barkley, Khalil Mack, more
summary: Saquon Barkley joining a contender? Brian Thomas Jr. headed out west? Khalil Mack and Donte Jackson boosting a defense? Let's build 11 win-win trades.
full_text:
NFL trade season is about to heat up -- the deadline is less than three weeks away (Nov. 10 at 4 p.m. ET). We've already seen receiver  Marvin Harrison Jr . dealt to the Texans , quarterback  J.J. McCarthy moved to the Giants , cornerback Joey Porter Jr . sent to the Cowboys and center Cam Jurgens traded to Baltimore . And in the weeks to come, more trades will follow. Let's project some of them with 11 proposals that make sense for both teams involved.

 While deadline deals across all sports don't always have a dramatic impact on the games that play out afterward, 2025 was a clear case when moves in the NFL mattered. The Seahawks might not beat the Rams in the regular season without the addition of Rashid Shaheed , who kicked off their comeback victory with a punt return touchdown. That win pushed the Seahawks into position to land the top seed in the NFC, which gave them home-field advantage in the rubber match against the Rams -- and that might have made the difference in the NFC title game . Not a bad return for a pair of Day 3 picks.

 Teams with Super Bowl aspirations will be hoping to follow in Seattle's footsteps as the 2026 deadline approaches. If anything, I was a little concerned that there might not be many teams ready to trade away talent, given that 27 of the league's 32 teams still have at least a 9% chance of making it to the postseason after six weeks of football, per ESPN's Football Power Index .

 Then two things happened this week to shake up the trade market. One was the firing of Colts general manager Chris Ballard , which came after the Colts blew a 13-0 halftime lead to the Titans at home Sunday and lost 26-20 . Ballard endured some unfortunate luck given that his franchise quarterback (Andrew Luck) and one of his best draft picks ( Shaquille Leonard ) retired prematurely because of serious injuries, but the two big swings Ballard took toward the end of his tenure didn't work out, with QB  Anthony Richardson Sr . and cornerback  Sauce Gardner both failing to live up to expectations (so far) during their time with the Colts.

 Firing Ballard doesn't mean that the Colts are about to trade off every veteran on their roster, especially given that the rest of the front office staff and head coach Shane Steichen still remain, but there's less of a mandate to try to win this season than there would have been with Ballard at the helm. Indy has several pending free agents who could be appealing to opposing teams, and there might be a scenario in which the 2027 version of this franchise has Mannings in the front office and on the football field.

 
 Subscribe: 'The Bill Barnwell Show' 

 
 And then in Philadelphia, we found out that quarterback  Jalen Hurts is expected to miss the rest of the season because of deep vein thrombosis. This was already beginning to feel like a lost season for the Eagles, who were missing as many as nine potential starters in Sunday's loss to the Panthers , but the news that Hurts won't be returning anytime soon only reaffirms that the Eagles need to start thinking about 2027. Barring a stunning turn from Tanner McKee , who struggled badly against Carolina, the Eagles don't have any sort of meaningful ceiling this season beyond potentially competing to win a moribund NFC East with a seven- or eight-win season.

 This is typically the time of year when GM Howie Roseman calls around on veterans to add to his roster in advance of a playoff push. This season, he's more likely to be the one fielding those calls, and he can't afford to be timid or unrealistic. This Eagles team was flawed even before the Hurts injury. The offensive line, which has long been at the core of so many great Philly teams, has fallen apart. With Lane Johnson retired , Jurgens traded and questions about the future of Landon Dickerson and Tyler Steen , the Eagles could need at least two and as many as four new starting linemen next offseason.

 They'll also need to work on contracts for young defensive standouts such as  Quinyon Mitchell , Jalyx Hunt  and Cooper DeJean , which will cause the Eagles to skew far more heavily toward spending on defense after going in the opposite direction. And factoring in the players we already expect not to be back on the roster in 2027, the Eagles could be at $80 million in dead money on next season's cap. Roseman could push money into the future to avoid problems there, but as he did in 2021, it wouldn't be a surprise to see the Eagles take a year to reset their cap to create an advantageous situation in 2028 and beyond.

 With a need to address multiple spots along the O-line, add depth on defense and potentially line up a long-term replacement for Hurts, Roseman has his work cut out for him over the next 12 months. Adding draft capital would help that process. It wouldn't be a surprise to see the Eagles listen to offers for their pending free agents, and we'll have a trade or two in that direction later in the column. I just wouldn't expect them to move cornerstone players such as Mitchell,  DeVonta Smith , Jordan Mailata  or Jalen Carter .

 I have to start today, though, with a player whose status on the 2027 roster is still up for grabs. Adding him was a masterstroke that elevated the roster and sank the hearts of Philly's division rivals. He was the perfect addition to the team in 2024. But ... is Saquon Barkley going to be on the Eagles in 2027? And if not, would Roseman consider trading his star RB in lieu of losing him for nothing as a cap casualty next offseason?

 Barkley was a deserving Offensive Player of the Year candidate in 2024, but he wasn't anywhere near as effective as a runner behind a much worse offensive line in 2025, averaging 4.1 yards per carry (down from 5.8). He has been in and out of the lineup in 2026 because of injuries and turns 30 in February. He's not likely to carry the Eagles very far over the rest of the 2026 season, given that the line is missing multiple starters and the Eagles won't have their starting quarterback the rest of the way.

 Barkley is owed $16 million next year, $2.5 million of which is fully guaranteed. That's not an exorbitant sum for a great running back, but I'm not sure the Eagles as constructed in 2027 are going to be in position to get the most out of his talents in the way they were in 2024. Roseman might prefer to use that $16 million to fix what has gone wrong at the line of scrimmage and trust his ability to find a useful back in free agency or in the middle rounds of the draft, as the Eagles did for many years before the Barkley addition.

 I wouldn't fault the Eagles for holding on to Barkley, but Roseman won't hesitate to be aggressive if the right deal is out there. And while there aren't a ton of teams in the running back market, there's one that would make sense as a potential Barkley trade partner -- which is where I'll begin our annual list of pre-deadline trade proposals.

 

 
 Jump to a deal: 
 MIN-PHI | CAR-PHI | DET-LAC 
 PIT-LV | SF-IND | LAR-IND 
 LV-JAX | CHI-TB | NYG-LAC 
 KC-PHI | NE-WSH 

 
 

 

 Vikings land an impact RB 
 Vikings get: RB  Saquon Barkley 
 Eagles get: 2027 third-round pick (with conditions)

 At 5-0, the Vikings might very well be the team that's actually in position to benefit from adding a star back in his prime. Minnesota has a 90.9% chance of making it to the postseason, per ESPN's FPI, but it'll need the run game and a healthy back once it gets there. Jordan Mason  has already hit injured reserve this season and has battled injuries in each of the past three years.  Aaron Jones Sr . is 32 years old, has already left at least one game because of a knee issue and is on pace for 330 carries.

 

 The Vikings are 22nd in explosive play rate on designed runs, which is a reality of life with Jones in the fold. Adding Barkley would allow the Vikings to use him as their primary back while making Jones a complementary player, which is probably the right role for the veteran at this point of his career.…

title: How to bet Patriots-Bears: Analysis, tips and top prop plays for the game
summary: Odds, bets and analysis to help you bet New England Patriots at Chicago Bears on "Thursday Night Football."
full_text:
Caleb Williams returned for the Chicago Bears ' Week 6 win over the Atlanta Falcons , and he played his most efficient game as a pro, completing 24 of 26 throws from inside the pocket. He was seeing it fast, playing as a ball distributor. Tight end Colston Loveland saw a boost in volume and the Bears controlled the tempo with running backs D'Andre Swift and Roschon Johnson . This is how Ben Johnson wants his offense to operate, using the run-pass balance while mixing in high-percentage throws for the quarterback with the screen package.

 

 Defensively, look for the Bears to keep the blitz rate up versus New England Patriots quarterback Drake Maye . With limited depth at cornerback and defensive end, coordinator Dennis Allen blitzed at a rate of better than 50% versus Atlanta, and his schemed fronts and coverages complement the pressure.

 New England heads into Week 7 with a banged-up offensive line. Wide receiver Romeo Doubs (shoulder) is now on IR, too. The positive here is the play of Maye, who has bounced back from a rough start to the season to throw 10 touchdown passes over his last three games while also showcasing his running ability (103 rushing yards during this stretch). Maye's decision-making has improved, and he's throwing with better location. A.J. Brown returned in Week 6, and his presence will impact the Bears' coverage plans, while slot receiver DeMario Douglas can provide an outlet for Maye. The Patriots used a three-man rotation in the backfield last week, but expect Rhamondre Stevenson to still see the most volume and TreVeyon Henderson to be used as a change-of-pace runner versus a Bears defense allowing 4.5 YPC (25th).

 Mike Vrabel's defense has to play a critical role here against Williams. The Patriots are allowing only 209 passing yards per game (11th), majoring in both single-high and split-safety zone coverage.

 

 

 

 Betting outlook 
 The short week -- and a matchup between nonconference opponents -- gives me some pause when looking at the total. And I feel the same about the Patriots' recent backfield rotation. Does Stevenson get his 15-18 touches? It's something to think about if you are betting on the New England running backs. Maye's props as a runner are worth looking into, though. Maye has rushed for at least 24 yards in three straight games.

 

 Above, I mentioned Williams playing as a ball distributor, which is a positive for the Bears offense, but it also can limit his receivers in terms of seeing heavy volume. However, the recent deployment of Loveland (seven targets last week) works here, as he also saw two end zone targets against Atlanta. Meanwhile, the Bears running backs will see volume, and the screen package we saw in Week 6 creates more opportunities for Luther Burden III and Swift.

 Bets: Total points UNDER 50.5, Patriots +3 

 The Patriots and the Bears both rank in the top 10 in scoring defense. I like the under to hit. I'm leaning toward the Bears moneyline right now, but I'll take the Patriots to cover. Vrabel's team is 3-2-1 against the spread this season, and he has the defense to win third downs and red zone situations.

 

 Notable player props, bets 
 

 Note: Odds by DraftKings   and subject to change.

 Loveland has produced at least 57 yards receiving in two of his last three games, and he has seen 21 targets over that stretch. Plus, Johnson is scheming throws to his tight end.

title: Inside Caleb Williams' group of famous Chicago sports friends
summary: Bears QB Caleb Williams is part of a trio of young Chicago athletes whose friendship transcends sports.
full_text:
Matas Buzelis started his postgame treatment the night of Jan. 10 shortly after the Chicago Bulls beat the Dallas Mavericks . Less than five miles away from the training room inside the United Center, the blustery conditions on the lakefront were the backdrop for the  Chicago Bears ' fourth-quarter fight in a wild-card playoff thriller. Buzelis had a special interest in the game.

 As the 22-year-old small forward lowered himself into a cold tub filled with ice water, Buzelis watched his friend  Caleb Williams  go to work.

 Buzelis, the Bulls' 2024 first-round pick, doesn't claim to be much of a football fan, but he understood the significance of what he was witnessing as a Chicago native. Williams, one of Buzelis' closest confidants, was in the midst of a career-defining moment when he led the Bears back from a 21-3 halftime deficit to beat the Green Bay Packers  31-27.

 Buzelis recalls celebrating "that crazy throw" Williams made on fourth-and-8 to Rome Odunze that kept a touchdown drive alive. Inside a suite at Soldier Field, Chicago Cubs center fielder Pete Crow-Armstrong erupted as Odunze made the catch.

 "My head was about touching the ceiling," Crow-Armstrong told ESPN. "We were all jumping up and down. I feel like that's something you can't really [describe]. Maybe a walk-off homer or something like that evokes sort of a similar feeling, but that one's tough to beat."

 That game helped transform Williams from an ascending, young quarterback into national stardom. The play -- specifically Williams' jump pass -- was commemorated on the cover of Madden NFL '27. Williams' "Ice Man" nickname started generating national buzz, and he emerged as the most recognizable star in Chicago sports. But he has company. And the Williams-PCA-Buzelis group text chat should be popping Thursday after the Bears host the New England Patriots (8:15 p.m., ET, Prime Video).

 

 The increased visibility and expectations for the Bears (4-2, 0-2 NFC North) in Williams' third season is what he has been primed to manage his whole career. At every juncture, from winning the Heisman Trophy at USC to becoming the No. 1 pick, the quarterback has followed a curated plan to keep grounded. A big part of that includes the people he welcomes into his circle.

 In Chicago, the place where Williams says he wants to be forever, he does so in close proximity to others who hold an intimate understanding of the type of demands he encounters daily. Because they, too, navigate a similar burden of success.

 "This isn't even about us going against each other, but that's how we look at it," Buzelis said. "We want to one-up each other every time.

 "We see Pete hit three home runs in one game. Now we want to do something in our sport that's that outstanding in that type of manner, but it's all about us competing against each other. I'd say Caleb had a great game. Now I'm looking forward to my season, and that's the excitement it brings of all of us knowing each other."

 What it's like hanging out with Caleb Williams 

 The three-member group chat lights up multiple times a week. It's the way these 20-somethings with hectic, conflicting schedules stay connected, whether to offer words of encouragement, share TikToks and memes or plan an outing.

 "We just talk a bunch of s--- and also love on each other as well," said Crow-Armstrong, who's expected to be named the National League MVP on Nov. 12.

 The Cubs slugger made his major league debut in September 2023, more than two years after the New York Mets traded him to Chicago. In the spring of 2024, Williams became the first quarterback selected by the Bears with the top pick in the draft. In June 2024, the Bulls drafted Buzelis 11th.

 The foundation of Williams and Buzelis' friendship was set during the quarterback's junior season at USC, where the former NBA G Leaguer's team trained. The two snapped a photo after one of Buzelis' practices and stayed in touch as they both made their way to Chicago.

 

 Crow-Armstrong and Williams were a more traditional Gen-Z match by following each other on social media and trading direct messages back and forth.

 When plans make it out of the chat, the group expands to include Odunze and Cole Bennett, the Illinois native and Lyrical Lemonade founder who has directed over 500 music videos for the industry's biggest artists, from Eminem to Future.

 Bennett met Williams the year after his Heisman campaign when the quarterback asked him to direct an eventual documentary on his life and career.

 "I left the first time we ever met feeling like, oh no, he's a superstar and he knows it," Bennett said. "It's a really unique trait because it's really hard to walk that line of being incredibly confident and not being arrogant but being uniquely yourself and knowing the path that you're on. And he's figured it out."

 Conversations about shared passions, sports and music are held over s'mores and bonfires at Bennett's Chicago-area home. These are sacred occurrences because of how difficult it can be aligning schedules; evenings that hold special meaning for the space they create for vulnerability away from the spotlight.

 "We just sit, talk, we get to vent if we need to about anything that's on our minds," Buzelis said. "Everyone's understanding in that group, and they know the caliber of what we're talking about."

 Other nights it's bowling, showing up at each other's games or attempting to move inconspicuously as they leave restaurants whose reservations are nearly impossible to snag.

 Lately, it's no surprise who among the group gets recognized the fastest.

 

 "When I go out with him, it's always about Caleb, and personally I kind of like that," Crow-Armstrong said. "It's a different kind of night out when he's around just because people f---ing love the dude."

 Williams had "no room to breathe" when he and Crow-Armstrong sat on the glass for the  Chicago Blackhawks - Winnipeg Jets  game in January, one day removed from the Bears' season ending in the divisional round of the playoffs.

 Like Williams, Blackhawks' captain  Connor Bedard  was also drafted No. 1 and carries the mantle of a franchise savior. The night before the Bears- Los Angeles Rams  divisional playoff game on Jan. 18, Bedard arrived at the United Center for the Blackhawks game against the Bruins wearing Williams' orange Bears jersey.

 "I wanted to order one, but obviously it wouldn't get there the day of, so I DoorDashed that [the night before the game]," Bedard told reporters.

 Williams returned the show of support on Jan. 19, donning Bedard's No. 98 sweater as he and Crow-Armstrong were mobbed by fans as they climbed the aisle from their seats.

 It was a similar scene the following night as Williams and Crow-Armstrong's offseason tour de Chicago sports continued. Buzelis was reminded that his friends were in attendance by the loud ovation Williams and Crow-Armstrong received when shown on the jumbotron.

 Sitting on the baseline for Bulls- LA Clippers , the two cheered as Buzelis dropped 21 points in the win.

 "Once I hear them coming, I want to put on a show," said Buzelis, who made All-Rookie second team last season. "And that's something I've been approaching in every game, not just when they show up, but them showing up shows how real they are and what kind of friendship we have."

 When Williams went incognito at a Kanye West concert 

 As the Bears broke training camp in early September and were given four days off, Williams hauled it from Halas Hall to Wrigley Field through heavy Chicago traffic to take advantage of the only respite he would get until after the season.
